docs.title: ModeDecompositionAnalysis(variables=None, *, rank=None, dictionary=None, validation=0.2, horizon=0, dt=1.0, label='surrogate')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Linear system fitted to series by dynamic mode decomposition, computed with PyDMD.

The decomposition fits the exact DMD of the one-sample map g(t + dt) = A g(t) to the pairs of consecutive samples of every run. With a dictionary, g holds the observables the dictionary computes from the variables, which is extended DMD, and the dictionary should keep the variables among its observables. The fitted system follows the rate law dg/dt = L g with L = Phi diag(ln(mu) / dt) Phi^+ under continuous time and starts at the first sample of the first run. The forecast sums the modes from the last sample of the last run.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default variables Sequence[str] | None

The variables of trajectories, or None for every scalar state or observable.

None rank float | None

The rank of the truncated singular value decomposition: a number of modes, 0 for the optimal hard threshold, a share of the energy below 1, or None to keep every singular value.

None dictionary TransformerMixin | None

A scikit-learn transformer that computes the observables, such as PolynomialFeatures(2), or None for the variables themselves.

None validation float

The share of the samples of every run held out at its end to measure the validation error.

0.2 horizon int

The number of samples to forecast after the last sample of the last run.

0 dt float

The time between the rows of an array.

1.0 label str

The label of the surrogate element.

'surrogate'

Attributes:

Name Type Description samples_

The series of every run, the names of the variables, and the step, set by prepare.

system_

The system of one surrogate element under continuous time, whose states follow dg/dt = L g.

labels_

The variables, or the observables of the dictionary, in the order of the states.

states_

The names of the states of the surrogate element.

last_state_

The values of the states at the last sample of the last run, where the forecast starts.

dt_

The time between the samples it was fitted to.

training_error_

The relative error of the predicted increments over one sample on the training samples.

validation_error_

The relative error on the held-out samples, NaN when none are held out.

eigenvalues_

The continuous eigenvalues ln(mu) / dt of the modes, from the eigenvalues mu of the one-sample map.

modes_

The modes, one column per mode and one row per state.

amplitudes_

The amplitudes of the modes at the last sample of the last run.

generator_

The matrix L of the rate law, one row and one column per state.

forecast_

The states at the horizon samples after the last one, one row per sample.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.analysis import ModeDecompositionAnalysis
>>> times = np.arange(0.0, 10.0, 0.1)
>>> values = np.column_stack([np.cos(times), np.sin(times)])
>>> analysis = ModeDecompositionAnalysis(['x', 'y'], horizon=5, dt=0.1).check().prepare(values).run()
>>> np.sort(analysis.eigenvalues_.imag).round(6).tolist()
[-1.0, 1.0]

docs.title: NeighborAnalysis(kind='distances', group=None, *, variables=None, box=None, bins=100, r_max=None, attribute='state', empty=None, diagonal=True)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Neighbours of agents in space, or of cells of a grid or nodes of a network, of one kind.

The kinds read positions, or states on grids and networks:

  • 'distances': the distance from every agent to its nearest neighbour, across periodic edges in a box.
  • 'clark-evans': the mean nearest-neighbour distance over its value for uniform random points in a periodic box, 1 for random points, below 1 for clustered ones, and up to 2.15 for a triangular lattice in a plane.
  • 'radial-distribution': the radial distribution function g(r) in a periodic box, averaged over frames, 1 for an ideal gas.
  • 'like-share': the mean share of an agent's occupied neighbours that share its state, on a periodic grid or along the edges of a network, near 1 when segregated.

An array of positions holds one snapshot, one row per agent, or one snapshot per frame along its first axis. A trajectory gives the positions of an agent group with the sides of its periodic space as the box, or its lattice frames for 'like-share'. A grid array is one frame of states, and a graph carries the states on its nodes.

Parameters:

The neighbour statistic to compute, one of the kinds above.

'distances' group str | None

The path of the agent group of a trajectory, or None for the first one.

None variables Sequence[str] | None

None box Sequence[float] | None

The sides of a periodic box, or None for the periodic space of a trajectory or for open space.

None bins int

The number of distance bins of g(r).

100 r_max float | None

The largest distance of g(r), or None for half the smallest side.

None attribute str

The node attribute of the states of a graph.

'state' empty float | None

The state of empty cells, left out as agents and as neighbours, or None when every cell is occupied.

None diagonal bool

Whether grid cells that share only a corner are neighbours, as in Schelling's Moore neighbourhood.

True

Attributes:

Name Type Description positions_

The positions, frames by agents by dimensions, for the agent kinds.

box_

The sides of the periodic box, or None for open space.

frames_

The grids of states, or the graphs, of 'like-share'.

distances_

The nearest-neighbour distances, frames by agents, of 'distances'.

ratio_

One Clark-Evans ratio per frame.

radii_

The bin centres of g(r).

distribution_

g(r) at every bin centre.

share_

One like share per frame.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.analysis import NeighborAnalysis
>>> positions = [[0.5, 0.0], [9.5, 0.0]]
>>> NeighborAnalysis(box=[10.0, 10.0]).check().prepare(positions).run().distances_.tolist()
[[1.0, 1.0]]
>>> points = np.random.default_rng(0).random((5000, 2))
>>> NeighborAnalysis('clark-evans', box=[1.0, 1.0]).check().prepare(points).run().ratio_.round(1).tolist()

docs.title: NetworkAnalysis(kind='summary', *, orders=(1, 2), attribute=None, numeric=False, measure='degree', method='louvain', reference=None, random_state=None)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Measures of the network of every frame of a trajectory, or of a graph, of one kind.

The kinds read the graph of every frame:

  • 'degrees': the degree of every node, the moments <k^n> of the degree distribution for every order of orders, and the fitted exponent of a heavy-tailed degree distribution, nan below 50 nodes or for a narrow one.
  • 'assortativity': the assortativity by degree, or by a node attribute, positive when linked nodes are alike.
  • 'centrality': the degree, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector, or PageRank centrality of every node.
  • 'communities': the communities by Louvain modularity maximization or label propagation, their modularity, and their agreement with a reference partition.
  • 'neighbor-degree': the mean degree of the neighbours of nodes against their degree, rising in assortative networks.
  • 'summary': the size, mean degree, clustering, path length, diameter, and components, with the path measures on the largest component.

Parameters:

The measure to compute, one of the kinds above.

The orders n of the degree moments.

None numeric bool

False measure str

'degree' method str

'louvain' reference Sequence[object] | str | None

None random_state int | None

The seed of the Louvain method.

None

Name Type Description graphs_

The graph of every frame.

degrees_

The degree of every node of every frame.

moments_

The degree moments, frames by orders.

exponent_

The fitted degree exponent of every frame.

assortativity_

The assortativity of every frame.

centrality_

A mapping from node to its centrality for every frame.

labels_

The community of every node of every frame.

modularity_

The modularity of every frame.

agreement_

The normalized mutual information with the reference of every frame, or None without a reference.

distinct_degrees_

The distinct degrees of every frame.

neighbor_degree_

The mean neighbour degree of the nodes of every distinct degree of every frame.

The sizes of the connected components of every frame, largest first.

docs.title: OperatorAnalysis(kind='spectrum', *, n_states=6, parameters=None, sector=None, subsystems=None)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Spectrum and ground state of an operator system, or the purity and entanglement of the states of its trajectory.

The kinds read a system or a trajectory:

  • 'spectrum': the lowest eigenvalues and eigenstates of the generator, by exact diagonalisation. QuTiP diagonalises small spaces densely and larger ones with a sparse eigensolver. A sector restricts the basis to the states with a given eigenvalue of a conserved operator that is diagonal in the product basis, such as the total magnetisation.
  • 'ground-state': the lowest eigenvalue and eigenstate of the generator.
  • 'purity': the purity Tr(rho^2) of the state of a trajectory at every frame, 1 for pure states.
  • 'entanglement': the von Neumann entropy of the reduced state of some subsystems at every frame of a trajectory, in nats.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind str

The quantity to compute, one of the kinds above.

'spectrum' n_states int

The number of eigenvalues of the spectrum.

6 parameters Mapping[str, object] | None

Parameter values by dotted name that replace the initial ones.

None sector SectorSpec | None

The sector of a conserved diagonal operator whose basis states the spectrum keeps, or None for every basis state.

None subsystems Sequence[str] | None

The keys of the subsystems to keep, such as chain[0], or the path of a whole element or group.

None

Attributes:

Name Type Description problem_

The compiled operator problem.

trajectory_

The trajectory of 'purity' and 'entanglement'.

energies_

The eigenvalues of the spectrum in increasing order.

states_

The eigenstates of the spectrum as columns over the whole space.

energy_

The ground state energy.

state_

The ground state vector.

purity_

The purity at every frame.

entropy_

The entanglement entropy at every frame.

Raises:

Type Description AnalysisError

The system or the trajectory holds no operators, the sector operator is not diagonal or lacks the eigenvalue, or a subsystem is not part of the trajectory.

ParameterError

A parameter name is not part of the system.

Examples:

>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import CC, SR
>>> from skcomplex.analysis import OperatorAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws import GeneratorLaw
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import local_operator
>>> from skcomplex.specs import HilbertSpec, StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.engine.compile import OperatorCompiler
>>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
>>> operators = {'z': (np.diag([1, -1]), True), 'minus': (np.array([[0, 0], [1, 0]]), False)}
>>> QUBIT = HilbertSpec(2, operators, basis={'up': 0, 'down': 1})
>>> class TwoLevelElement(Element):
...     def __init__(
...         self, label, psi: Annotated[object, StateSpec(domain=CC**2)] = 'up', hilbert=QUBIT
...     ):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.psi = psi
...         self.hilbert = hilbert
...
...     def _get_laws(self, s):
...         return [GeneratorLaw(local_operator(s.psi, SR.symbol('z')))]
>>> system = System(elements=[TwoLevelElement('q')])
>>> OperatorAnalysis(n_states=2).check().prepare(system).run().energies_.round(6).tolist()
[-1.0, 1.0]
>>> singlet = np.array([0, 1, -1, 0]) / np.sqrt(2)
>>> pair = System(elements=[GroupElement('pair', element=TwoLevelElement, size=2)])
>>> trajectory = Simulation(
...     pair, compiler=OperatorCompiler(), dt=1.0, initial_state={'system.state': singlet},
... ).check().prepare().run(until=1.0).trajectory_
>>> analysis = OperatorAnalysis('entanglement', subsystems=['pair[0]']).check().prepare(trajectory).run()
>>> bool(np.allclose(analysis.entropy_, np.log(2)))
True

docs.title: PassageAnalysis(kind='first-passage', variables=None, *, threshold=None, target=None, origin=None, direction='up', level=0.0, lag=1, dt=1.0)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Passages of paths to a level or a set of states, or of a Markov chain between two sets, of one kind.

The kinds read paths, one row per path on common times, or a transition matrix:

  • 'first-passage': the first time every path reaches threshold, from below for direction='up' and from above for 'down', or enters the target states.
  • 'hitting': the share of paths that reach each of the absorbing target states before the others.
  • 'return-times': the times between successive returns of a series to level, by visit or by crossing.
  • 'committor': the forward committor of a transition matrix, the probability that the chain reaches the target states before the origin states.
  • 'mean-first-passage': the mean first-passage time of a transition matrix at lag from the origin states, started in their stationary weights, to the target states.

The matrix kinds estimate the transition matrix at lag of the jump path of a trajectory.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind str

The passage to measure, one of the kinds above.

'first-passage' variables Sequence[str] | None

The discrete state of a trajectory to read, or the series for 'return-times', or None for the first.

None threshold float | None

The level a first passage reaches.

None target Sequence[float] | None

The states that end a passage, the absorbing states, or the target set of the chain.

None origin Sequence[float] | None

The origin set of the chain.

None direction str

'up' to reach values at or above the threshold, 'down' at or below it.

'up' level float

The level of the returns.

0.0 lag int

The lag of the transition matrix in steps.

1 dt float

The time of one step of an array, while a trajectory gives its own times.

1.0

Attributes:

Name Type Description values_

The paths, one row per path, or the series of 'return-times'.

times_

The common times of the steps.

matrix_

The transition matrix of the matrix kinds.

passage_times_

The time from the start to the first passage of every path, nan for paths that never pass, of 'first-passage'.

hitting_probabilities_

The share of paths that hit every target state first, of 'hitting'.

return_times_

The time between every return and the next, of 'return-times'.

committor_

The committor of every state, 0 on the origin and 1 on the target, of 'committor'.

mean_first_passage_time_

The mean first-passage time, of 'mean-first-passage'.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.analysis import PassageAnalysis
>>> passage = PassageAnalysis(threshold=2).check().prepare([[0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 0, 0, 0]]).run()
>>> passage.passage_times_.tolist()
[2.0, nan]
>>> PassageAnalysis('return-times').check().prepare([0, 1, 0, -1, -2, -1, 0]).run().return_times_.tolist()
[2.0, 4.0]
>>> walk = [[0.5, 0.5, 0.0], [0.25, 0.5, 0.25], [0.0, 0.5, 0.5]]

docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Reservoir system whose ridge readout gives the increments of the variables over one sample, from ReservoirPy.

The reservoir is driven by the standardized variables, and a ridge regression from its features to the increments of the variables over one sample is fitted on the training samples. A next-generation reservoir takes as features the variables at delay consecutive samples and their monomials of degree order. An echo state network takes the activities of units leaky tanh units with random recurrent weights. The fitted system runs under discrete time, one step per sample, and starts at the last sample of the last run with the memory the runs left, so a run of the system is the autonomous forecast.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default variables Sequence[str] | None

The variables of trajectories, or None for every scalar state or observable.

None kind str

The reservoir, 'next_generation' or 'echo_state'.

2 order int

The degree of the monomials of a next-generation reservoir.

2 units int

300 spectral_radius float

0.9 leak float

The leak rate of the units of an echo state network, 1 for no leak.

1.0 input_scaling float

The scale of the input weights of an echo state network.

0.5 ridge float

The strength of the ridge penalty of the readout.

0.0001 warmup int | None

None validation float

The share of the samples of every run held out at its end to measure the validation error.

0.2 horizon int

The number of samples to forecast after the last sample of the last run.

0 dt float

1.0 random_state int | None

docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Statistic of every series of a source in rolling windows, of one kind, and its trend.

Every window holds the window values that end at a sample, possibly with a linear trend removed first, and the statistic of the window is set at that sample. The trend of the statistic is Kendall's tau against time.

  • 'variance': the variance of the window.
  • 'autocorrelation': the lag-one autocorrelation of the window.
  • 'skewness': the skewness of the window.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind str

The statistic to compute, one of the kinds above.

'variance' variables Sequence[str] | None

The variables of a trajectory to read, or None for every scalar series.

None window int | None

The number of values in every rolling window.

None detrend bool

Whether to remove a linear trend in every window first.

False

Attributes:

Name Type Description values_

The series, one per column.

labels_

The label of every series.

statistic_

The statistic of every series in every window, one row per series, nan before the first full window.

trend_

Kendall's tau of the statistic of every series against time, positive when it rises.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.analysis import RollingAnalysis
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> x = np.zeros(2000)
>>> for t in range(1, 2000):
...     x[t] = (0.2 + 0.79 * t / 2000) * x[t - 1] + rng.standard_normal()
>>> rolling = RollingAnalysis('autocorrelation', window=200, detrend=True).check().prepare(x).run()
>>> bool(rolling.trend_[0] > 0.5)
True

docs.title: ScalingAnalysis(kind='detrended-fluctuation', variables=None, *, scales=None, order=1, fit_sums=(0.0001, 0.01), random_state=0, against='mean', parameters=None, critical=None, above=False)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Scaling exponent of every series of a source, fractal dimension of a set of cells or points, or scaling law.

The kinds read series, fields, points, or samples at several sizes:

  • 'detrended-fluctuation': the slope of the log fluctuation of the integrated series, detrended in windows by a polynomial of degree order, against the log window size. It is 0.5 for white noise, the Hurst exponent H for fractional Gaussian noise, and H + 1 for its integral, such as 1.5 for a random walk.
  • 'rescaled-range': the Hurst exponent by the rescaled range, 0.5 for uncorrelated noise, above 0.5 for persistent and below 0.5 for anti-persistent noise.
  • 'box-counting': the box-counting dimension of the occupied cells of a field, the slope of the log box count against the log box size, read from the last frame of a trajectory.
  • 'correlation-dimension': the Grassberger-Procaccia correlation dimension of a point set, one row per point, such as the columns of an embedded series, from tree counts of close pairs.
  • 'variance-mean': the mean and the standard deviation of a quantity at every scale, and the slope of log deviation against log mean with against='mean', or of log (deviation / mean) against log size with against='size'. It reads the counts of a density field in square boxes of growing side over every frame, where the slope against the mean is 1/2 for independent particles and above for giant fluctuations, or a mapping from size to samples, where the slope against the size is -1/2 for the sums of independent parts.
  • 'power': the exponent b of the power law y ~ |p - p_c|^b of every series against the distance of the control parameters to the critical value, fitted on the side above or below it where y is positive, such as the exponent beta of an order parameter.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind str

The scaling to measure, one of the kinds above.

'detrended-fluctuation' variables Sequence[str] | None

The variables of a trajectory to read, or None for every scalar series, or the first field for a field.

None scales Sequence[float] | None

The window sizes, the box sides in cells, or the radii, or None for windows spaced logarithmically up to a tenth of the series, powers of 2 up to an eighth of the smallest side, or a quarter of it for 'variance-mean', or 30 radii spaced logarithmically over the range of pair distances.

None order int

The order of the detrending polynomial.

1 fit_sums tuple[float, float]

The smallest and largest correlation sums of the scaling region the slope is fitted in.

(0.0001, 0.01) random_state int | None

The seed of the sample of pairs that sets the default radii.

0 against str

What the variance-mean law is fitted against, 'mean' or 'size'.

'mean' parameters Sequence[float] | None

The control parameter value of every row of the series of 'power'.

None critical float | None

The value of the control parameter the distance is measured to.

None above bool

Whether the fit uses the values above the critical value, as for couplings, rather than below it, as for temperatures.

False

Attributes:

Name Type Description values_

The series, one per column, the field or its frames, or the points, and an empty array for samples by size.

samples_

The samples by size, or None for a source of series, points, or a field.

labels_

The label of every series, of the field, or of every size.

scales_

The window sizes, the box sides, the radii, or the sizes.

fluctuations_

The fluctuation, or the rescaled range, of every series at every window size.

counts_

The number of occupied boxes of every side.

sums_

The share of pairs of points closer than every radius.

means_

The mean of the quantity at every scale.

deviations_

The standard deviation of the quantity at every scale.

fit_range_

The smallest and largest radii of the fit of the correlation dimension.

exponent_ float | Array

The exponent of every series for the fluctuation kinds and 'power', the slope of the variance-mean law, and the dimension for the other kinds.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.analysis import ScalingAnalysis
>>> walk = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(5000))
>>> ScalingAnalysis().check().prepare(walk).run().exponent_.round(1).tolist()
[1.5]
>>> round(ScalingAnalysis('box-counting').check().prepare(np.ones((256, 256))).run().exponent_, 2)
2.0
>>> points = np.random.default_rng(0).random((5000, 2))
>>> round(ScalingAnalysis('correlation-dimension').check().prepare(points).run().exponent_, 1)
2.0
>>> counts = np.random.default_rng(0).poisson(5.0, (20, 64, 64))
>>> round(ScalingAnalysis('variance-mean').check().prepare(counts).run().exponent_, 1)
0.5
>>> power = ScalingAnalysis('power', parameters=[0.9, 0.99], critical=1.0)
>>> power.check().prepare([0.1**0.5, 0.01**0.5]).run().exponent_.round(6).tolist()
[0.5]

docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Default analysis of every kind of data of a trajectory, with its curves, axis labels, title, and values.

A series gives its power spectrum with the autocorrelation time, or its return map for a map. A jump path gives the survival function of its waiting times with the dispersion index of jumps per frame. A field gives the structure factor of its last frame with the peak wavelength or the correlation length. Agents give their polar and milling orders over time, or their nearest-neighbour distances against the Poisson law. A network gives its degree distribution.

docs.title: SparseIdentificationAnalysis(variables=None, *, degree=2, threshold=0.1, alpha=0.05, validation=0.2, horizon=0, dt=1.0, label='surrogate')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Sparse symbolic system fitted to series by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics, computed with PySINDy.

SINDy writes the derivative of every variable as a sparse sum of the monomials of the variables up to a degree. It estimates the derivatives by centred finite differences and selects the terms by sequentially thresholded least squares. The fitted system holds one rate law per variable under continuous time and starts at the first sample of the first run, and the forecast simulates it from the last sample of the last run.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default variables Sequence[str] | None

The variables of trajectories, or None for every scalar state or observable.

None degree int

The highest degree of the candidate monomials.

2 threshold float

The smallest magnitude of a kept coefficient.

0.1 alpha float

The strength of the ridge penalty of every least-squares fit.

0.05 validation float

The share of the samples of every run held out at its end to measure the validation error.

0.2 horizon int

The number of samples to forecast after the last sample of the last run.

0 dt float

The time between the rows of an array.

1.0 label str

The label of the surrogate element.

'surrogate'

Attributes:

Name Type Description samples_

The series of every run, the names of the variables, and the step, set by prepare.

system_

The system of one surrogate element under continuous time, with one rate law per variable.

labels_

The variables the system was fitted to, in the order of its states.

states_

The names of the states of the surrogate element.

last_state_

The values of the states at the last sample of the last run, where the forecast starts.

dt_

The time between the samples it was fitted to.

training_error_

The relative error of the predicted derivatives on the training samples.

validation_error_

The relative error on the held-out samples, NaN when none are held out.

features_

The candidate monomials of the states, such as x y.

coefficients_

The coefficient of every monomial in the rate of every state, one row per state and one column per monomial, zero where the term is absent.

forecast_

The variables at the horizon samples after the last one, one row per sample.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.analysis import SparseIdentificationAnalysis
>>> times = np.arange(0.0, 2.0, 0.001)
>>> analysis = SparseIdentificationAnalysis(['x'], degree=1, dt=0.001)
>>> analysis = analysis.check().prepare(np.exp(-2 * times)).run()
>>> analysis.features_, analysis.coefficients_.round(3).tolist()
(['1', 'x'], [[0.0, -2.0]])

docs.title: StabilityAnalysis(kind='fixed-points', parameters=None, points=None, *, at=None)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Linear stability of a system, of one kind.

  • 'fixed-points': the fixed points of a flow or a map, their linear stability, and the Jacobian, nullclines, and divergence.
  • 'dispersion': the growth rate of every Fourier mode of a system of one field, a site group on a periodic lattice whose laws are rate laws. The laws are linearised symbolically around a uniform state, and every Laplacian, nested ones included, becomes its eigenvalue on a Fourier mode of the lattice, Σ (2 cos(k h) - 2) / h² for finite differences and -|k|² for a spectral field. Without at, the uniform state is the fixed point of the laws nearest the mean initial values.

The fixed points of a flow are where every rate is 0, and those of a map where every state equals its next value. Sage solves the equations symbolically, and when it finds no closed form, roots are searched numerically from a grid of starting points with the parameters at their values. The stability of every point comes from the eigenvalues of the Jacobian there, evaluated at the parameter values.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind str

The stability to derive, one of the kinds above.

'fixed-points' parameters Mapping[str, float] | None

Values of parameters by dotted path that replace the system's values. They are substituted before solving, and without them the symbolic fixed points keep the parameters as symbols.

None points Sequence[Point] | None

The points whose stability to analyse, each a mapping from state component name to its value, symbolic or numeric, or None for every fixed point found.

None at Mapping[str, float] | None

The uniform state of the dispersion relation by state name, or None for the nearest fixed point.

None

Attributes:

Name Type Description problem_

The compiled problem.

names_

The state component names, in the order of the rows of the Jacobian.

jacobian_

The Sage matrix of the partial derivatives of the right sides by the states.

divergence_

The trace of the Jacobian, 0 for volume-preserving flows.

nullclines_

A mapping from state component name to its nullcline as a Sage relation, where its rate is 0 or where it is its own next value.

fixed_points_

One mapping from state component name to its value per point, the fixed points found or the given points.

eigenvalues_

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian at every point.

classifications_

The class of every point: stable node, stable focus, unstable node, unstable focus, saddle, centre, or marginal for flows, and stable, unstable, saddle, or marginal for maps.

system_

The system of one field, for 'dispersion'.

wavenumbers_

The wave vector of every mode, one row per mode, for 'dispersion'.

magnitudes_

The length of every wave vector.

growth_rates_

The largest real part of the eigenvalues of the linearisation at every mode.

frequencies_

The imaginary part of the leading eigenvalue at every mode, nonzero for travelling or oscillating modes.

uniform_

The uniform state the model is linearised around, by state name.

band_

The lengths of the wave vectors whose modes grow.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.analysis import StabilityAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.models.biology.ecology import logistic_growth
>>> analysis = StabilityAnalysis().check().prepare(logistic_growth()).run()
>>> sorted(str(point['population.n']) for point in analysis.fixed_points_)
['0', 'K_growth']
>>> analysis = StabilityAnalysis(points=[{'population.n': 100.0}]).check().prepare(logistic_growth())
>>> analysis.run().classifications_
['stable node']
>>> from skcomplex.models.chemistry.pattern_formation import brusselator
>>> relation = StabilityAnalysis('dispersion').check().prepare(brusselator((64,), b=1.9, Dv=8.0)).run()
>>> bool(relation.growth_rates_.max() > 0), bool(relation.growth_rates_[0] < 0)

docs.title: SymbolicAnalysis(kind='equations', *, use_initial_state=False)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAnalysis

Symbolic form of a system: its equations, their exact solution, its Hamiltonian, or its boundary flows.

The kinds read the equations of a system:

  • 'equations': one equation per state component, a Sage relation. Each state component is a function of time t. Continuous forms give its time derivative, the drift for stochastic systems, and discrete maps give its value at t + 1. States of higher order give their highest derivative, diff(x(t), t, k), with their companions written as derivatives, and lagged states read their past values as x(t - j). The equations of a group hold for every member and are named with the member index i. Components driven by a callable law or by a sum over members or pairs are left out.
  • 'solve': the exact solution of the equations of an ODE system as functions of time, with Maxima through Sage. One equation of order 1 or 2 is solved with desolve, one of higher order with desolve_laplace, and several with desolve_system after reduction to first order, which solves linear systems with constant coefficients. A result that still contains unevaluated transforms, integrals, or the unknown functions is not a solution, and raises the error. Parameters give Maxima their sign from their domain, or from their value when their domain is real. One linear fractional relaxation D^alpha x = c x has the solution x(0) E_alpha(c t^alpha), written with the symbolic function mittag_leffler(alpha, beta, z).
  • 'hamiltonian': the Hamiltonian of an operator system, the sum of the operators of its generator laws, whose subsystems are the symbols of the states of the elements, named <state>_<path>, and whose parameters are named <parameter>_<path>.
  • 'conservation': the net inflow from the environment of every quantity of a system with a transfer network, after checking that its internal flows cancel, so the total changes only through the boundary.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind str

The symbolic form to derive, one of the kinds above.

'equations' use_initial_state bool

Whether 'solve' uses the initial state of the system, with the initial values of every derivative of states of higher order, as initial conditions at t = 0. Without them, the solution keeps its integration constants.

False

Attributes:

Name Type Description problem_

The compiled problem.

equations_

A mapping from state component name to its equation.

solutions_

A mapping from state component name to its solution, a relation f(t) == solution. States of higher order appear once, without their derivatives.

hamiltonian_

The Hamiltonian, a Sage expression of local operators.

inflows_

The symbolic rate, or amount per step, at which each quantity enters the system from the environment.

Raises:

Type Description AnalysisError

The system has no form of the kind, Maxima cannot solve its equations, or needs the sign of a parameter.

ConservationError

The internal flows of a quantity do not cancel.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.analysis import SymbolicAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.models.biology.common.populations import ExponentialGrowthInteraction, PopulationElement
>>> system = System(
...     elements=[PopulationElement('a', n=2)],
...     interactions=[ExponentialGrowthInteraction('g', target='a', r=0.5)],
... )

docs.title: Core
docs.text: What a system is: elements, interactions, laws, space and the system itself.

docs.title: Base
docs.text: Define the base of the parts of a system.

docs.title: BasePart(label)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseConfig[ContextT, InputT]

Base of every part of a system: its elements, its interactions, the laws they return, and the system itself.

Every part has a label, returns the laws it contributes from _get_laws, and implements three hooks that the verbs check, prepare, and run call:

  • _check() validates the arguments of the part, after check validates the label.
  • _prepare(context) prepares the part against its context and sets its attributes that end in _.
  • _run(inputs) sets what the part contributes: laws_, the laws of an element, an interaction, or a system, or value_, the value of a law.

A part is generic in the context of prepare and the input of run, which every base of parts names: a law is prepared against the path of its owner, an element against the space of its system.

A part declares which arguments of its constructor are states, parameters, or roles by annotating them with Annotated and a StateSpec, a ParameterSpec, or a RoleSpec, and check validates every declared spec. A part must be checked before it is prepared or run.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.base import BasePart
>>> class DoublingPart(BasePart):
...     def __init__(self, label, factor=2):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.factor = factor
...
...     def _check(self):
...         pass
...
...     def _prepare(self, context=None):
...         pass
...
...     def _get_laws(self, namespace):
...         return []
...
...     def _run(self, value):
...         self.doubled_ = self.factor * value
>>> DoublingPart('doubling').check().prepare().run(3).doubled_
6

def check(self) -> Self:
    """Validate the label and the arguments of the part and mark it as checked.

    Returns:
        part:
            The part itself.

docs.title: System
docs.text: Define systems, which compose elements, interactions, and nested systems on a space, in a time.

docs.title: System(label='system', *, elements=(), interactions=(), systems=(), space=None, time=None)
docs.text:
Bases: BasePart[BaseSpace, SimpleNamespace]

Composition of elements and the interactions between them, with nested systems, on a space, in a time.

A system is defined by its parts and by nothing about how it runs. An interaction refers to an element by its path relative to the system that holds the interaction, so forest/foxes names the element foxes of the nested system forest. Groups and nested systems without a space of their own live on the space of the system.

Attributes:

Name Type Description laws_ Sequence[BasePart]

The laws the system contributes for the namespace of its last run.

Examples:

>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
>>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws import RateLaw
>>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
>>> class DecayElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.x = x
...
...     def _get_laws(self, namespace):
...         return [RateLaw(namespace.x, -namespace.x)]
>>> system = System(elements=[DecayElement('decay')]).check().prepare()
>>> namespace = SimpleNamespace(decay=SimpleNamespace(x=var('x')))
>>> [type(law).__name__ for law in system.run(namespace).laws_]
['RateLaw']

def __init__(
    self,
    label: str = 'system',
    *,
    elements: Sequence[BaseElement] = (),
    interactions: Sequence[BaseInteraction] = (),
    systems: Sequence[System] = (),
    space: BaseSpace | None = None,
    time: BaseTime | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Store the label and the parts of the system.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

        elements:
            The elements and groups.

            The interactions between the elements.

        systems:
            The nested systems.

            The space the elements live on, which gives vector states their dimension, or `None` for none.

Bases: BaseElement

Base class of entities that carry state, such as particles, populations, agents, or firms.

A subclass takes its states, its parameters, and visual as arguments of its own __init__, annotating each state with a StateSpec and each parameter with a ParameterSpec inside Annotated, and returns its intrinsic dynamics from _get_laws, which returns no laws by default. A subclass drawn in its own way gives visual a default in its signature.

An element whose laws have the agent trait, such as rules, alone or in a group, is an agent: under discrete time it runs on the agent stepper, whose rules receive every member as an agent with its states as attributes. Its states then hold any value, not only numbers. A member is removed only when its states tagged with a quantity are settled to zero, and its states and parameters cannot take the names of the agent view, such as location or alive, or of the attributes Mesa reads, such as position or model.

docs.title: FieldElement(label, *, element, space, boundary=None, values=None, visual=None, discretization='finite-difference', symmetry=None)
docs.text:
Bases: LatticeElement

Group of members of one element type at the sites of a lattice, the nodes of a network, or a mesh.

The states of the members are fields, with one value per site, and the laws of the element type are written for one site, with laplacian, gradient, divergence, and advection reading the neighbouring sites. Every state takes a boundary condition at the edges of a lattice: 'periodic', 'zero-flux', or ('fixed', value), where the value can be a function of the node coordinates on a mesh.

The discretization turns the operators into numbers. 'finite-difference' uses stencils on lattices and the graph Laplacian on networks. 'spectral' multiplies Fourier modes on periodic lattices, with the two-thirds rule removing aliasing. 'finite-volume' updates cell averages by the differences of the FluxLaws of the states. 'finite-element' assembles stiffness and mass matrices on a MeshSpace.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the field.

required element type[BaseElement]

The element type of the members.

required space LatticeSpace | NetworkSpace | MeshSpace

The lattice, the network, or the mesh.

required boundary Mapping[str, object] | None

A mapping from state name to its boundary condition, which overrides the edges of the lattice. The value of ('fixed', value) for a tensor state may be a matrix of the symmetry of the state.

None values Mapping[str, object] | None

None visual VisualSpec | None

'finite-difference' symmetry Mapping[str, Sequence[object]] | None

A mapping from state name to its parity along every axis of a periodic lattice, 'odd', 'even', or None, which the rates keep exactly. A lattice twice as long as a domain along an axis, with states odd or even about its middle, represents walls there, such as the free-slip walls of convection. A vector or a tensor state takes one such sequence for its first component, or one sequence per component.

None

docs.text:
Bases: ConservationInteraction

Advection du/dt + divergence(a u) = source(ns) of a state u of a field by a drift field a(ns).

The flux of the conservation law is the drift times the state, written in conservative form, so the total of the state on a periodic field stays constant and, on a spectral field, the dealiasing of products applies to it. The drift is one expression for a field of one dimension, or one per dimension, of the states and parameters of the field, and may read other states than the one it carries, such as the flow of a fluid derived from a streamfunction, or the drift of a probability density in a Fokker-Planck equation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the field whose state is carried.

required state str

The name of the carried state of the field.

'u' drift Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns the drift, or one drift per dimension.

None source Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns the source, or None for none.

None limiter str | None

The slope limiter of the reconstruction of a finite-volume field, 'minmod', 'van-leer', or None.

'minmod' riemann str | None

The numerical flux of a finite-volume field, 'rusanov' or 'godunov', or None for the divergence of the flux on a field of another discretization.

'rusanov' sources Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)]

The paths of other elements the drift and the source read, as the namespaces sources. A field over the position lattice of a target on a phase space is read broadcast along the class axes.

>>> space = LatticeSpace((50,), spacing=0.1, boundary='periodic')
>>> values = {'u': np.exp(-((np.arange(50) - 25) / 5.0) ** 2)}
>>> volumes = 'finite-volume'
>>> field = FieldElement('tracer', element=CellElement, space=space, values=values, discretization=volumes)
>>> drift = AdvectionInteraction('drift', target='tracer', state='u', drift=lambda s: 1.0)

Bases: BasePart[BaseSpace, SimpleNamespace]

Base of every interaction, a part of a system whose laws couple elements to each other or to the environment.

A subclass takes its roles and parameters as arguments of its own __init__, annotated with Annotated and the spec RoleSpec or ParameterSpec, and stores each under its own name, as in scikit-learn. It returns its laws from _get_laws, where namespace.<role> is the namespace of the element bound to the role and namespace.<parameter> is a symbol. Interactions hold no state: state on couplings lives in groups on the edges or hyperedges of a network space. A general interaction reads the members of its roles, such as 'source' or 'target', by the name _get_role returns for them, the role itself by default, so a subclass that names its roles otherwise returns its own names, in the agent forms and, through _get_member, in the symbolic forms. It reads its parameters by the name _get_parameter returns for them, and a parameter the class does not declare reads the plain attribute, so a subclass renames a parameter or fixes its value by setting the attribute.

docs.text:
Bases: NeighborInteraction

Cascade of the members whose state reaches a threshold, which relax and pass shares to their neighbours.

At every step the drive changes the state, and then every member whose state reaches threshold relaxes, all at once, until no member does. In the mode 'redistribute' a relaxing member loses threshold and each of its neighbours gains share. In the mode 'reset' a relaxing member falls to 0 and each of its neighbours gains share times the state it relaxed from. In the mode 'random' a relaxing member loses threshold in parcels of share, and every parcel goes to one of its neighbours drawn at random. Neighbours outside a fixed boundary take no share, so it leaves the system, and the mode 'random' treats every lattice as bounded. Every cascade is recorded as an event with its size, the number of relaxations, its duration, and its area.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The name of the state of the members.

'x' threshold float

The value of the state at which a member relaxes, fixed during a run.

1.0 share float

What a neighbour of a relaxing member gains, an amount, a fraction of the state in the mode 'reset', or the amount of one parcel in the mode 'random', fixed during a run.

0.0 mode str

A function f(values, *, random) of the array of the states and the random generator of the simulation that returns the states after the drive of a step, or None for no drive.

None neighborhood BaseNeighborhood | None

The neighbourhood of the member itself first and its neighbours, or None for the von Neumann neighbourhood of a square lattice with its centre. A network takes AdjacencyNeighborhood(center=True), and the mode 'random' takes a lattice neighbourhood.

None layer str | None

The layer of the network whose edges the interaction runs on, or None for the graph of the network.

docs.title: ChoiceInteraction(label, *, target, state, options, utility, rule='logit', intensity=1.0, schedule='synchronous', activity=1.0, form='symbolic', phase=None, proposal='others', ties='random')
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Choice of every member of a group among options, drawn every step from the utilities of the options by a rule.

The rule 'logit', which is the heat-bath rule, draws option k of utility u_k with probability exp(beta u_k) / sum_j exp(beta u_j), where beta is the intensity of choice. The rules 'metropolis' and 'fermi' propose one of the other options uniformly, or with the proposal 'all' one of all the options including the current one, and accept it with probability min(1, exp(beta (u_new - u_old))) or 1 / (1 + exp(-beta (u_new - u_old))), so the rule 'fermi' with the proposal 'all' is the heat-bath rule of a uniform proposal. The rule 'best' draws uniformly among the options of largest utility under the ties 'random', and takes the first of them under 'first'. Every step, each member revises its choice with probability activity and keeps it otherwise.

In the 'symbolic' form, utility(namespace, option) returns the utility as a symbolic expression, where namespace.target holds the states and parameters of the group, and every member draws at once. In the 'agent' form, the group is an agent group and utility(agent, model, option) returns the utility as a number, so it can read the agent, its neighbours, and the history and storage of the model view. Its members draw at once, from the choices of the last step, under the 'synchronous' schedule, one after the other in their order or in a new random order, each seeing the choices made before it, under the 'sequential' or 'random-sequential' schedule, and each in its own activation under the 'member' schedule, together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them. An option of utility -inf is never drawn in the agent form.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the element or group whose members choose.

required state str

The name of the discrete state of the members that holds the chosen option.

required options Sequence[float]

The values the state can take, at least two.

required utility Callable[..., float | Expression]

The function utility(namespace, option) in the symbolic form, or utility(agent, model, option) in the agent form, that returns the utility of an option.

required rule str

The rule of the draw, 'logit', 'metropolis', 'fermi', or 'best'.

'logit' intensity Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

The intensity of choice beta, zero for uniform choice.

1.0 schedule str

The order in which the members revise, 'synchronous' or, in the agent form, 'sequential', 'random-sequential', or 'member'.

'synchronous' activity Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed(0, 1))]

The probability that a member revises its choice in a step.

1.0 form str

'symbolic' for update laws of the states of a group, or 'agent' for a rule over an agent group.

'symbolic' phase str | None

The phase of the step the agent form runs in, or None for the default phase.

None proposal str

The options the rules 'metropolis' and 'fermi' propose from, 'others' for the options other than the current one, or 'all' for every option.

'others' ties str

The option the rule 'best' takes among options of equal largest utility, 'random' for one drawn uniformly or 'first' for the first in the order of the options.

'random'

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The rule, the schedule, the form, the proposal, or the ties are unknown, the schedule is not synchronous in the symbolic form, there are fewer than two options, or the utility is not callable.

>>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import mean
>>> choice = ChoiceInteraction(
...     'choice', target='spins', state='spin', options=(-1, 1), utility=lambda s, o: o * mean(s.target.spin)
... )
>>> choice.check().rule
'logit'
>>> agents = ChoiceInteraction(
...     'choice', target='traders', state='plan', options=(0, 1), utility=lambda a, m, o: o, form='agent'
... )
>>> type(agents.check().prepare().run(SimpleNamespace()).laws_[0]).__name__
'RuleLaw'
>>> ChoiceInteraction(
...     'heat-bath', target='spins', state='spin', options=(-1, 0, 1), utility=lambda s, o: o, rule='fermi',
...     proposal='all'
... ).check().proposal

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Conservation law du/dt + divergence(flux(ns)) = source(ns) of a state u of a field.

The flux is one expression for a field of one dimension, or one expression per dimension, of the states of the field, and the interaction lowers it to a finite-volume flux law with a slope limiter and a numerical flux, or, without a numerical flux, to the rate -divergence(flux) that the field discretizes by its own operators, as a spectral or finite-difference field does. Without a source the total of the state on a periodic field stays constant. The conservation laws of several states of one field form one system, whose numerical flux reads the wave speeds of all of them, and a flux may read parameters that vary across the cells. A flux or a source function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespace target of the field, the time t, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares.

docs.text:
Bases: NeighborInteraction

Coupling of every member to other members, through a reduction over them of a function of both members.

Every member i gets the reduction over other members j of function(namespace), where namespace.member reads the states of i, namespace.other those of j, namespace.edge the member of the edge group that joins them, or None, and the namespace also holds the parameters and the time t. The function is the difference x_j - x_i of the state read by default. The members j are, by mode:

  • 'edges': the neighbours of i along the edges of its lattice or network, or within the neighborhood.
  • 'group': every other member of the group, or every member of the group source when it is given.

In the mode 'group' the roles may also bind separate elements. A target that lists elements couples every element to the other elements of the list, a single target element is a hub that reduces over every member of the group source, and a source that is one element or a list of elements couples every member of the target to them. The reduction over separate elements is written out term by term. - 'next': the next member of the group in member order, the first after the last. - 'hyperedges': the other members of every hyperedge around i of size members, or of every size, on a network with hyperedges. The function then reads namespace.member, namespace.others, the other members of one hyperedge in its order, and namespace.members, all its members, which reductions over them read, and the reduction runs over the hyperedges around i. The default function is the sum over the other members of the difference of read.

With include_self, the reduction also runs over j = i. Every term f_ij has a weight w_ij: on edges, the state weights of the edge group, which a subclass binds with a second role, over the group, the entry W_ij of the matrix weights or of the shaped parameter of the interaction that weights names, which a subclass declares, and in every mode a callable weights(namespace) of the namespace of the term, such as an indicator of the states of both members. The reductions are 'sum', sum_j w_ij f_ij, 'mean', the sum divided by the number of members j, 'max' and 'min', the largest and smallest w_ij f_ij, 'normalized-mean', sum_j w_ij f_ij / sum_j w_ij, and 'circular-mean', the angle arctan2(sum_j w_ij sin f_ij, sum_j w_ij cos f_ij). The state read of j is read delay earlier, and the one of i shifted by the phase lag lag, when they are not 0.

In the form 'rate' the reduction adds to the rate of the state write, and in the form 'map' it sets the next value of write every step of discrete time to combine(namespace, reduction), where namespace.member reads the states of i and the namespace holds the parameters and the time, or to the reduction itself by default. The sum and the mean of the rate on the edges of a lattice or network run once per edge along both directions, and every other coupling runs once per member. On a FieldElement, a rate that is a constant times the difference of the ends becomes that constant times the field's Laplacian times its squared spacing, and on a lattice the other end is read across the field's boundary conditions, so beyond fixed edges it reads the fixed value.

In the form 'agent' the target is a group of agents, and every agent runs the coupling in its own activation in the phase phase. Every RadiusSpec of radii gives the vector function(agent, other, model) of every other agent of the source group, or of the target group, within its radius, reduced by its sum or mean. Only the radii of the highest priority that hold another agent count, and their reductions add up. The states write of the agent form a vector v, which becomes combine(agent, model, reduction, priority), or v plus the reduction by default, where reduction and priority are None when no radius holds another agent. clamp then bounds the angle the vector turns and its norm.

docs.title: CrossingInteraction(label, *, target, guard, reset=None, direction=0, terminal=False)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Event at the crossing of zero by a guard, which sets states of the target to new values or ends the run.

The guard and the new values are functions of the namespace, which holds namespace.target, the states and parameters of the target, and the time namespace.t. A guard that reads the members of a group gives every member its own event, which sets the states of that member alone. Solvers locate the crossing within their tolerance, and the trajectory records every crossing among its events, under the label of the interaction and with the member.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

required guard Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]

The function guard(namespace) of the expression whose crossing of zero triggers the event.

required reset Mapping[str, Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]] | None

A mapping from the name of a state of the target to the function f(namespace) of its new value, applied all at once, or None to keep the states.

None direction int

1 for crossings from negative to positive, -1 for the opposite, and 0 for both.

0 terminal bool

Whether the crossing ends the run.

False

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The direction is not -1, 0, or 1, or the guard or a new value is not a function.

>>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec

docs.title: EncounterInteraction(label, *, candidate, field=None, rate=None, kernel=None, outcome='conservative', state='f', cross_section=None, factor=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Encounters of a candidate density with a field density over activity classes, which move, remove, or create.

The candidate and the field are groups of DensityElement on the sites of lattices of activity classes, one member per class. A candidate at class h meets a field at class k at the rate eta[h, k]. In the outcome 'conservative' the candidate moves to class i with the probability kernel[h, k, i], in the outcome 'destructive' it is removed, and in the outcome 'proliferative' it creates a new candidate at class i with the probability kernel[h, k, i], or at its own class without a kernel. The rate and the kernel are functions of the namespace, which holds namespace.candidate, namespace.field, and the parameters of the interaction.

On a PhaseSpace the classes are the points of the class axes, and encounters pair classes at the same position. A rate that is one expression may read the coordinate of the class of the candidate. Without a field the encounter is a linear redistribution: a conservative candidate at class h moves to class i at the rate eta[h] with the probability kernel[h, i].

With a cross_section the candidate is a field on a PhaseSpace with two interval class axes, and its rate at every position is the binary collision integral over those axes, evaluated by the fast spectral method on a padded grid. The density is conserved exactly, and the momentum and the energy within the spectral accuracy of the method.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required candidate Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the group of the candidate density.

required field Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True)]

The path of the group of the field density, or None for a linear redistribution.

None rate Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

The function rate(namespace) of the encounter rate, a number or an expression, or an array eta[h, k] of them, or eta[h] without a field, or None with a cross-section.

None kernel Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

The function kernel(namespace) of the array kernel[h, k, i] of the probabilities of the class of the moved or created candidate, or kernel[h, i] without a field, or None for a destructive encounter or the candidate's own class.

None outcome str

'conservative', 'destructive', or 'proliferative'.

'conservative' state str

The name of the state of the densities.

'f' cross_section Callable[..., object] | None

The function B(speed, cosine) of arrays of the relative speed and the cosine of the deflection angle, or None for encounters at a rate.

None factor Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns a factor of the collision frequency, such as a function of the density moment, or None for none.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The outcome is unknown, the state is no name, a function is not callable, a conservative encounter has no kernel, an encounter without a field is not conservative, an encounter has neither a rate nor a cross-section, or a cross-section comes with a rate, a kernel, a field, or an outcome.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import EncounterInteraction
>>> kernel = np.full((3, 3, 3), 1 / 3)
>>> mixing = EncounterInteraction(
...     'mixing', candidate='population', field='population', rate=lambda s: 1.0, kernel=lambda s: kernel
... )
>>> mixing.check().outcome
'conservative'
>>> collide = EncounterInteraction('collide', candidate='gas', cross_section=lambda speed, cosine: 1.0)
>>> collide.check().rate is None
True

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Equations of motion d/dt dL/dq' - dL/dq = Q - dR/dq' of the coordinates q of a Lagrangian L(ns).

The coordinates are states of order 2, and the Lagrangian, the Rayleigh dissipation function R, and the generalized forcing Q read them and their first derivatives derivative(q, 1). The interaction returns one equation law per coordinate, which the compiler solves jointly for the second derivatives, so a Lagrangian with a mass matrix, such as a double pendulum's, needs no inversion by hand. The equations of one coordinate from several interactions add, so their Lagrangians, dissipations, and forcings sum: a coupling, such as a spring between two pendulums, is an interaction of its own whose Lagrangian holds only the coupling energy. The coordinates are the states of every role that binds one element or group, target by default, and every component of a vector state is a coordinate.

A Lagrangian, dissipation, or forcing function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces of the roles, the time t, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares. The forcing returns one generalized force per coordinate, in the order of the roles and of the states, or one expression for a single coordinate.

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the element or group whose states are the coordinates.

A function of the namespace that returns the Lagrangian.

None dissipation Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns the Rayleigh dissipation function, or None for none.

A function of the namespace that returns the generalized forces, or None for none.

docs.title: EvolutionInteraction(label, *, target, strategy='strategy', fitness='fitness', selection='tournament', replacement='generational', crossover=0.7, mutation=0.01, elite=0, tournament=2, alphabet=2, scale=0.1, death=0.1, change='other', parents='survivors', fraction=0.1, period=1, evaluate=None, reset=None, phase=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Replacement of the strategies of an agent group by offspring selected on a fitness, with crossover and mutation.

Every period steps, or rounds of its phase, the interaction selects parents by tournaments of tournament entrants, by roulette with weights of the fitness minus its minimum, in proportion to the fitness itself ('proportional'), or by rank with weights 1 for the least fit to n for the fittest of n members. The 'generational' replacement selects as many parents as there are members, each pair of which exchanges the tails after a random cut with probability crossover, and passes the elite fittest strategies unchanged. The 'moran' replacement runs as many birth-death events as there are members, one after the other, each copying a selected parent onto a member drawn uniformly, and the copy takes the fitness of its parent for the later events of the step. The 'death-birth' replacement removes every member with probability death and fills its place with the offspring of a parent selected among the survivors, or among all members when none survives or parents is 'all'. The 'truncation' replacement fills the places of the fraction least fit members with the offspring of parents selected among the others. The 'best-mutant' replacement lets every member draw a mutant of its strategy, and every member takes the fittest mutant when it is fitter than the fittest strategy, or when every member mutated, so a population of one strategy climbs a landscape as a whole.

Offspring mutate: each gene with probability mutation changes by the rule change, to another symbol of an alphabet of alphabet symbols ('other'), to a symbol drawn anew from the alphabet ('any'), one step up or down ('step'), or to a label one above the largest the members hold ('new'), or with probability mutation one gene drawn at random of every offspring changes to another symbol ('one'). When alphabet is None, the 'other' and 'any' rules add Gaussian noise of deviation scale. A function mutation(strategy, rng) returns the mutated copy of a strategy instead. The fitness is a state of the members, or the function evaluate(strategies, model) of the strategies, one row per member, which the replacement then writes into the fitness state. The probabilities are parameters of the model when a subclass declares them with a ParameterSpec, as the base does for crossover, death, and fraction. The draws come from the random stream of the model.

docs.title: GradientInteraction(label, *, target, states='x', potential=None, sources=(), divisor=None, variational=False, conserved=False)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Motion of states down the gradient of a potential U(ns), as a gradient flow or as Newtonian motion.

Every state x the interaction moves gets the rate -dU/dx / d on its highest time derivative, with d the divisor of its member: a state or parameter of the member, an expression of them such as a moment of inertia m l^2, or one divisor per state, such as the masses of two coordinates of one element. On a state of order 1 this is the gradient flow x' = -dU/dx / d, with d a friction, and on a state of order 2 it is Newton's law x'' = -dU/dx / d, with d an inertia. A vector state gets the gradient of every component, and a tensor state the matrix gradient, the projection of the derivative onto the matrices of its symmetry.

On a field the potential is the density f of a functional F = integral f, which may read the field, its derivatives partial(x, k) or gradient(x), and its laplacian(x). A variational interaction moves the field by the functional derivative dF/dx = df/dx - sum_k partial(df/dx_k, k) + laplacian(df/d laplacian(x)), as in the Allen-Cahn equation, and a conserved interaction gives the rate laplacian(dF/dx) / d instead, as in the Cahn-Hilliard equation, so the total of the field stays constant.

The interaction moves the states of every role that binds one element or group, target by default. A subclass may bind several such roles instead, such as both members of a pair potential, and every one of them moves. The potential function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces of the roles and of the sources, the time t, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the element or group whose states move.

required states str | Sequence[str]

The name of the state that moves, or the names of several states.

'x' potential Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

A function of the namespace that returns the potential, or the density of the functional of a field.

None sources Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)]

The paths of the elements or groups the potential reads but does not move.

() divisor str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | Mapping[str, str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]] | None

The name of the state or parameter of every moving member that divides its rate, a function of the namespace of the member that returns the divisor, a mapping from the name of every moving state to its own divisor, or None.

None variational bool

Whether the potential is the density of a functional of a field, moved by its functional derivative.

False conserved bool

Whether the rate is the Laplacian of the derivative of the potential, which conserves the total of a field.

False

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

A state or the divisor is not a name, or the potential is not callable.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.elements import CompartmentElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import GradientInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
>>> well = GradientInteraction('well', target='walker', states='n', potential=lambda s: s.target.n**2 / 2)
>>> system = System(elements=[CompartmentElement('walker', n=1.0)], interactions=[well])
>>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=1.0).trajectory_
>>> round(float(trajectory.values('walker.n')[-1]), 4)
0.3679

docs.title: GroupingInteraction(label, *, target, groups='pairs', act=None, size=2, by=None, capacity=None, phase=None, form='agent', write=None, function=None, reduce='sum')
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Grouping of the members of a group into groups drawn every step, with an action on every group.

The groups are one of four kinds:

  • 'pairs' draws disjoint random pairs, and an odd member out forms no group.
  • 'partition' draws a random partition into groups of size members, the last group holding the remainder.
  • 'neighborhood' forms one group per member, the member first and then the members in the cells or nodes around it.
  • 'state' forms one group per value of the state by, of at most capacity agents drawn at random among those that hold the value in the agent form.

In the agent form the groups act in random order, each through act(members, model), a function of the list of agent views and the model view, or the method act_on a subclass overrides. The grouping is an agent rule, so the system runs in discrete time.

In the symbolic form every member of a group takes the value of function(namespace) for the state write in the next step, reduced by reduce over the groups that hold it, and a member in no group keeps its value. The namespace of a group holds member, the member the value is for, others, the other members in the order of the group, members, which total, mean, count, maximum, and minimum reduce with over=namespace.members, the time t, and the parameters of the interaction. Pairs and partitions are drawn again at every step from the random stream of the simulation, and neighbourhoods are those of the space. The groups by state hold no others, and their reductions over the members are keyed by the state. Within a step, the grouping runs in its phase and reads the states the phases before it set.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the group whose members are grouped.

required groups str

The kind of groups, 'pairs', 'partition', 'neighborhood', or 'state', or in the agent form a PartnerSpec or a function pairing(members, members, rng, capacity) that returns pairs, which group every member with its partners. 'pairs' is a shorthand of PartnerSpec('all', 'uniform', capacity=1).

'pairs' act Act | None

The function of the members of a group and the model view that acts on the group in the agent form, used when a subclass does not override act_on.

None size int

The number of members of a group of a partition.

2 by str | None

The name of the state whose values the groups 'state' share.

None capacity int | None

The largest number of agents of a group 'state' in the agent form, or None for no limit.

None phase str | None

The phase of the step the grouping runs in, or None for the default phase.

None form str

'agent' for an action on the agents of every group, or 'symbolic' for a function of every group.

'agent' write str | None

The name of the state that the symbolic form sets.

None function GroupFunction | None

The function of the namespace of one group that returns the value of write for its member, in the symbolic form.

None reduce str

'sum' or 'mean', how the symbolic form combines the values of the groups that hold a member.

'sum'

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The kind of groups, the form, or the reduction is unknown, the size is below two, the groups 'state' have no state, the capacity is not positive, the symbolic form has no state or function, or a setting of one form is given to the other, raised by check.

Examples:

>>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import GroupingInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
>>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
>>> class VoterElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, visual=None, *, s: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
...         self.s = s
>>> def adopt_majority(members, model):
...     majority = float(2 * sum(member.s for member in members) > len(members))
...     for member in members:
...         member.s = majority
>>> voters = GroupElement('voters', element=VoterElement, size=3, values={'s': [1.0, 1.0, 0.0]})
>>> galam = GroupingInteraction('galam', target='voters', groups='partition', size=3, act=adopt_majority)
>>> trajectory = Simulation(System(elements=[voters], interactions=[galam])).check().prepare().run(until=1)
>>> trajectory.trajectory_.agents('voters', 1).values['s'].tolist()
[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]

In the symbolic form every group of the partition takes the opinion of its majority:

>>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import mean, where
>>> galam = GroupingInteraction(
...     'galam',
...     target='voters',
...     groups='partition',
...     size=3,
...     form='symbolic',
...     write='s',
...     function=lambda g: where(mean(g.members.s, over=g.members) > 1 / 2, 1, 0),
... )
>>> simulation = Simulation(System(elements=[voters], interactions=[galam]), random_state=0)
>>> simulation.check().prepare().run(until=1).trajectory_.values('voters.s')[-1].tolist()
[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Hamilton's equations q' = dH/dp and p' = -dH/dq of the canonical pairs (q, p) of a Hamiltonian H(ns).

The coordinates and the momenta are states of order 1, which may be angles, of every role that binds one element or group, target by default, and the coordinates pair with the momenta in order. Every component of a vector state is a coordinate or a momentum. The interaction returns one rate law per coordinate and per momentum, and the rates of one state add, so the Hamiltonians of separate interactions sum: a coupling between two oscillators is an interaction of its own whose Hamiltonian holds only the coupling energy. Dissipation or forcing is a rate interaction on the momenta.

A Hamiltonian function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces of the roles, the time t, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseInteraction

Base class of interactions whose laws run once for every hyperedge of the network of the nodes a role binds.

The first role binds a group with one member per node of a network space with hyperedges. A second role may bind a group on the hyperedges of the same network, or a group on the edges of one of its layers. The laws are written for one hyperedge of size members and read:

  • namespace.member, the focal member, whose states rate, noise, and jump laws change;
  • namespace.others, the other members in the order of the hyperedge, a tuple of namespaces;
  • namespace.members, the members of the hyperedge, which total, mean, count, maximum, and minimum reduce with over=namespace.members;
  • namespace.hyperedge, the member of the group on hyperedges;
  • namespace.edge, the member of the group on edges that joins the first two members of the hyperedge;
  • the parameters of the interaction.

A law of the focal member runs once per member of every hyperedge and adds into that member. A law that targets the member of the group on hyperedges or on edges runs once per hyperedge, with the first member of the hyperedge as the focal member. Without a size, the laws run on the hyperedges of every size, one size at a time.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required size int | None

The number of members of the hyperedges the laws run on, or None for every size.

Raises:

The size is not a whole number of at least two.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import HyperedgeInteraction

>>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import mean
>>> from skcomplex.specs import RoleSpec
>>> class ConsensusInteraction(HyperedgeInteraction):
...     def __init__(self, label, voters: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()], size=None):
...         super().__init__(label, size=size)
...         self.voters = voters
...
...     def _get_laws(self, s):
...         return [RateLaw(s.member.x, mean(s.members.x, over=s.members) - s.member.x)]
>>> ConsensusInteraction('consensus', voters='voters', size=3).check().size
