docs.text:
Bases: NeighborInteraction

Imitation of a discrete state of the neighbours of every member, at a rate or with a probability per step.

By the rule 'random' a member copies a neighbour chosen at random, by 'majority' it takes the option that more of its neighbours hold than any other, and by 'best' it copies the neighbour whose payoff is largest, when that payoff is larger than its own. By 'better' it picks a neighbour at random and copies it when the neighbour's payoff is larger than its own. By 'fermi' it picks a neighbour at random and copies it with probability 1 / (1 + exp(-beta (P_j - P_i))), where P_j and P_i are the payoffs of the neighbour and of the member and beta is the intensity. A member without such a neighbour keeps its state. The rules read the neighbourhood of the space, the graph of a network or the neighbourhood of a lattice.

In the 'rate' form every member imitates at the rate rate, by jumps between every pair of options in continuous time. In the 'probability' form every member imitates with probability probability in every step of a discrete-time system, all members at once in its phase, reading the states the phases before it set. In the 'agent' form the target is an agent group, and every agent imitates its neighbours in the space with probability probability in its phase. The agents imitate at once, reading the states of the step before, under the schedule 'synchronous', one after the other in their order or in a new random order every step under 'sequential' or 'random-sequential', each reading the states the agents before it set, or each in its own activation under 'member'. The rule 'better' runs in the agent form only. Among neighbours of equal largest payoff, the rule 'best' of the agent form copies the first under the ties 'first' and one drawn uniformly under 'random'.

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Random event that changes states of the target by signed amounts, at a rate, by a probability, or after a wait.

With a rate, the event fires at the times of a Poisson process of that propensity in continuous time. With a probability, it fires in a step of discrete time with that probability. With a waiting time, usually a draw from a distribution with nonnegative support, it fires after a time drawn anew at every firing, as in renewal processes, and every member of a bound group fires on its own clock. When the event fires it adds the changes to the states and, with a waiting time, sets the states of reset to their new values. Every function reads namespace.target, the states and parameters of the target, and the time namespace.t.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the element or group whose states the event changes.

required changes Mapping[str, float] | None

A mapping from the name of a state of the target to the signed amount the event adds to it.

None rate Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

The function rate(namespace) of the propensity of the event, or None.

None probability Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

The function probability(namespace) of the probability that the event fires in a step, or None.

None waiting Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None

The function waiting(namespace) of the time until the next firing, or None.

None reset Mapping[str, Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]] | None

With a waiting time, a mapping from the name of a state of the target to the function f(namespace) of its new value, one value per component of a vector state, or None.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The event has not exactly one clock, changes nothing, or resets states without a waiting time, or a function is not callable.

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.elements import CompartmentElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import JumpInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
>>> arrivals = JumpInteraction('arrivals', target='queue', changes={'n': 1}, rate=lambda s: 2.0)
>>> system = System(elements=[CompartmentElement('queue')], interactions=[arrivals])
>>> simulation = Simulation(system, dt=1.0, random_state=0).check().prepare()
>>> counts = simulation.run(until=5).trajectory_.values('queue.n')
>>> bool(all(count == round(count) for count in counts))
True

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Life cycle of the agents of a group, which give birth to offspring and die, every step of discrete time.

Every step the agents act once each, in their order under the schedule 'sequential', in a new random order under 'random-sequential', or each in its own activation under 'member', together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them, without the reports of the step and without arrivals. An agent dies with the probability death, and an agent that survives gives birth with the probability birth, or as many times as a Poisson number of the mean rate. A probability is a number or a function of the agent and the model view, and a function that returns a condition gives probability one where it holds. Every birth creates offspring new agents, a number or a function of the parent and the model view, such as a Poisson draw, of the group group, or of the parent's group without one. A new agent stands in the cell of its parent, with the placement 'here', in a neighbouring cell that no agent of the group holds, with the placement 'neighbor', or at the location a function of the parent and the model view returns, where None means no place, and a birth without a place creates fewer agents.

A new agent copies the states inherit of its parent and takes the values that values(parent, model) returns, such as a generation one higher or drawn states. The parent splits each state of split with its offspring, keeping the share keep, a number or a function of the parent and the model view such as a random cut, or else an equal share, and the offspring share the rest equally. Then mutate(values, model) returns the values of a new agent from those it would get, and the other states take their defaults. A parent that gave birth takes the values reset, and with replace it is removed, so its offspring replace it, also when the birth created none. With renew an agent that dies is renewed in place instead of removed: it keeps its identity, its place, and the states the new values leave out, and takes the values of an offspring of its own. With the probability cull an agent that does not die removes, after its births, one member of group, or of the target without a group, for which kin(agent, member) holds, the first in the order of the group under the pick 'first', such as one it owns, or a random one under 'random'. Every step a Poisson number of the mean arrival, a number or a function of the model view, of new agents arrive without a parent, at the location of the placement function or else at a random place, with the values values(None, model). The life cycle reports the births, deaths, and arrivals of every step. It is an agent rule, so the system runs in discrete time.

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

required birth Chance | None

None death Chance | None

The probability that an agent dies in a step, or None for no deaths.

None rate Chance | None

None offspring Count

The number of new agents of a birth.

1 placement Placement

Where a new agent stands, 'here', 'neighbor', or a function of the parent, None for an arrival, and the model view that returns its location.

'here' inherit Sequence[str]

The names of the states a new agent copies from its parent.

() split Sequence[str]

() mutate Mutation | None

None schedule str

The order of the agents, 'sequential', 'random-sequential', or 'member'.

'random-sequential' phase str | None

The phase of the step the life cycle runs in, or None for the default phase.

None group Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True)]

None values Values | None

None keep Chance | None

None reset Mapping[str, object] | None

None replace bool

False renew bool

Whether an agent that dies is renewed in place instead of removed.

False cull Chance | None

The probability that an agent removes one member of group, or of the target without a group, in a step, or None for no removals.

None kin Kinship | None

A function of an agent and a member of group that returns whether the agent may remove the member, or None for every member.

docs.title: MapInteraction(label, *, target, state, function, sources=(), mode='replace', schedule='synchronous', form='symbolic', phase=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Map of a state of discrete time, whose next value is a function, or the state plus it.

In the mode 'replace' the next value of the state is f, and in the mode 'increment' it is the state plus f. Under the 'synchronous' schedule every member of a bound group updates at once, from the states at the start of the step. Under the 'sequential' schedule the members update one after the other, in their order, and under the 'random-sequential' schedule in a new random order every step, each member reading the values the members before it set. Under the 'member' schedule of the agent form, every member updates in its own activation, together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them.

In the 'symbolic' form, function(namespace) returns a symbolic expression, or a vector of them for a vector state, where namespace.target holds the states and parameters of the target, namespace.sources the namespaces of the sources, and namespace.t the time, and may hold draws such as normal('noise'). In the 'agent' form, the target is an agent group and function(agent, model) returns the value as a number, or as an array of the shape of a vector state, so it can read the agent, its neighbours, and the history and storage of the model view.

docs.title: MatchingInteraction(label, *, requesters, providers, rule=RandomSearchSpec(), limit='limit', quantity='quantity', allowance='allowance', transfers=(), phase=None, on_match=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Matching of the members of a group of requesters with those of a group of providers by a rule.

Requesters state the highest clearing value they accept in their limit state, the quantity they want in their quantity state, and the most value they can give in their allowance state, and providers the lowest clearing value they accept and the quantity they offer. A name given as a pair names the state of the requesters first and of the providers second, and a missing state counts as no limit, one unit, and no allowance. The rule is a spec that names the algorithm that pairs the offers and holds its settings: random search, partners, partner switching, a queue, iterative, continuous, batch, or stable matching. The value of a match is its clearing value per unit. Every match lowers the quantities of both sides and moves every state of transfers: a negative sign moves value * quantity from the requester to the provider, and a positive sign moves quantity from the provider to the requester, so the totals stay the same. on_match(match, model) adds any other effect. The matching runs once per round of its phase and reports the quantity-weighted clearing value value, the matched volume, and the unmatched quantity left, as the reporters <label>.value, <label>.volume, and <label>.unmatched.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the matching.

required requesters Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the group of requesters.

required providers Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the group of providers.

required rule MatchingRule | Pairing

The spec of the algorithm that matches the members, such as ContinuousMatchingSpec(), or a function rule(requesters, providers, rng, capacity) of the agents with a positive quantity that returns their pairs, which match at the midpoint of both limits. A PartnerSpec picks among the providers that still offer a quantity at a limit the requester accepts, in random order of the requesters.

RandomSearchSpec() limit str | tuple[str, str]

The state with the limit of both sides, or a pair of the requesters' and the providers' states. An agent without the default state 'limit' has no limit as a requester and the limit 0 as a provider.

'limit' quantity str | tuple[str, str]

The state with the quantity of both sides, or a pair of the requesters' and the providers' states. An agent without the default state 'quantity' offers the quantity 1.

'quantity' allowance str

The state of a requester with the most value it can give. A requester without the default state 'allowance' has no limit on what it gives.

'allowance' transfers Sequence[tuple[str, int]]

The states every match moves, each with the sign -1 for a move from the requester to the provider or 1 for a move from the provider to the requester.

() phase str | None

The phase the matching runs in, or None for the default phase.

def match(self, model: ModelT) -> None:
    """Match the members, settle the matches, and report the value, the volume, and the unmatched quantity.

    Args:
        model:
            The model view of the matching.
    """
    requesters, providers = self._get_offers(model)
    matches = self._get_matches(requesters, providers, model)
    for match in matches:
        self._settle(match, model)
    unmatched = sum(offer.quantity for offer in requesters + providers)
    self._report_matches(matches, unmatched, model)

docs.title: MovementInteraction(label, *, target, step='neighbor', probability=1.0, rate=None, condition=None, accept=None, exclusive=False, score=None, scale=1.0, exponent=1.5, cost=None, vision=None, schedule='random-sequential', phase=None, ties=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Movement of the agents of a group by steps, every step of discrete time.

A step is one of five kinds:

  • 'neighbor' moves an agent to a uniformly drawn cell or node next to its own, on a lattice or a network.
  • 'gaussian' adds to the position of an agent a normal vector whose components have the standard deviation scale, in a continuous space.
  • 'levy' moves an agent in a uniformly drawn direction by a Pareto length, whose least value is scale and whose tail exponent is exponent, in a continuous space.
  • 'best' moves an agent to the cell or node next to its own with the highest score(agent, cell, model). With a vision, a number or a function of the agent and the model view, it looks instead along every direction of the neighbourhood of a lattice up to that many cells, and at the cell of the agent, in the order of the axes, the positive direction first. Among cells of equal highest score, the ties 'random' draw one uniformly, 'first' take the first in that order, and 'nearest' take the nearest, the first of them among equal distances. By default the ties are 'random' without a vision and 'nearest' with one.
  • A function step(agent, model) returns the destination, or None to stay.

An agent for which condition(agent, model) holds attempts one step every step of time, or a Poisson number of steps with the mean rate, and takes each attempt with the probability probability and then with the probability accept(agent, destination, model). An exclusive movement never moves an agent to a cell another agent of the group holds. The agents move one after the other, in their order under the schedule 'sequential', in a new random order every step under 'random-sequential', or each in its own activation under 'member', together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them. Every step taken charges its cost, a TransferInteraction from the agent to itself or a function of the agent and the model view. The movement is an agent rule, so the system runs in discrete time.

1.0 rate float | None

None condition Callable[[AgentViewProtocol, ModelViewProtocol], bool] | None

A function of the agent and the model view that returns whether the agent moves, or None for every agent.

None accept Callable[[AgentViewProtocol, object, ModelViewProtocol], float] | None

None exclusive bool

'random-sequential' phase str | None

docs.text:
Bases: BaseInteraction

Base class of interactions whose laws run once for every edge of the network of the nodes a role binds.

A role binds a group with one member per node or site, and a second role may bind a group on the edges of the same network and layer. The laws are written for one edge and read namespace.source and namespace.target, the members at both ends, namespace.edge, the member of the edge group, and the parameters. On a directed graph the ends follow the direction of the edge, and on an undirected graph the source comes first in node order. Rate, noise, and jump laws may target any of them, and update laws the edge member. delayed reads the past state of either end.

On fixed edges, namespace.source.degree and namespace.target.degree are the degrees of the ends, the number of edges of the layer at every node, both ways on a directed graph. A law that reads no edge member and, outside its reductions, only one end is a law of that end's member, and runs once per member rather than once per edge. Inside its reductions the other end stands for the other members of the group, so mean(f(namespace.source.x, namespace.target.x), over=namespace.source) is the mean of f over every member for the target. Cascade, drive, and local rule laws are laws of the members, and a cascade records its cascades as events.

Instead of a group on the edges, a second role may bind a second group of nodes. The laws then run once per member of the group of the first role, which namespace.target reads, and their reductions run over the members of the second group, which namespace.source reads, without edges. A role declared RoleSpec(optional=True) and bound to None binds nothing.

The roles may also bind separate elements. When the first role binds one element or a list of elements, the laws run once per element, which namespace.target reads. When the second role binds a group, namespace.source reads its members inside reductions, and otherwise namespace.source is the tuple of the namespaces of the elements the second role binds, or of the other elements of the list the first role binds.

The laws read every end under the name _get_role returns for 'source', 'target', and 'edge', the end itself by default, so a subclass that names its roles otherwise reads the ends under its own names.

Parameters:

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required layer str | None

The layer of the network whose edges the interaction runs on, or None for the layer of the edge group it binds, or else the graph of the network.

Bases: Interaction

Move a group of candidates on an objective, one generation of a pymoo algorithm per step of discrete time.

Every candidate holds a vector state in a box, from which the first generation starts. docs.text:
Bases: PairInteraction

Coupling of every pair of members closer than a cutoff, through a function of the pair or a pair potential.

Every member of a pair adds a value to the rate of its state write, which gives the highest derivative of a state of any order. With function, the value is function(namespace), where namespace.first is the member that adds it and namespace.second the other member. With potential, a function potential(namespace, r) of the distance r between the values of the vector state position of the pair, the value is minus the gradient of the potential with respect to the member's own position. A divisor names a state or parameter of the members that divides the value. With several states write, the function returns one value per state, in their order, so one pair couples several states jointly.

required second Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the group whose members are the second of every pair, which may be the first group.

The largest distance between the members of a pair.

1.0 position str

The name of the vector state whose distances select the pairs, and which the potential is a function of.

The name of the state whose rate the coupling adds to, or a sequence of names, one per value of the function.

'x' function NamespaceFunction | None

The value a member adds, or a sequence of values, one per state write, a callable of the namespace of the pair, or None when the potential is given.

None potential PairPotential | None

The pair potential, a callable of the namespace of the pair and the distance, or None when the function is given.

None divisor str | None

Bases: Interaction

Rate rate(ns) and noise noise(ns) dW added to the highest time derivative of a state of a target.

On a state of order 1 the rate is its first derivative, and on a state of order k it adds to the k-th derivative, so rates on one state superpose. With a divisor d the rate and the noise are divided by d, the name of a state or parameter of the target, such as an inertia, a friction, or a capacitance, which backends can read.

A number stands for a constant, and a number on a vector state applies to every component. The noise is a Wiener process per component and member by default, a process of a WienerProcessSpec to share or correlate it across states and members, or a fractional Brownian motion of a Hurst index.

docs.title: ReactionInteraction(label, *, target=None, reactants=None, products=None, k=1.0, propensity=None, modifiers=None, mode='rate', form='symbolic', phase=None, schedule='synchronous')
docs.text:
Bases: JumpInteraction

Reaction that moves units from its reactants to its products at a mass-action or a given propensity.

A reactant, a product, or a modifier is a pair of the path of an element, or of a member of a group such as cells[0], and the name of its state that holds the units, mapped to its stoichiometric coefficient. A coefficient is a positive number, or a function of the namespace of the reaction that returns an expression of its parameters, such as lambda s: 1 / s.target.epsilon. So S + I -> 2 I has the reactants {('S', 'n'): 1, ('I', 'n'): 1} and the products {('I', 'n'): 2}, and two states of one element are ('cell', 'u') and ('cell', 'v'). A species may also be the name of a state of the target alone, such as {'u': 1, 'v': 2}. A target that is a group or a field reacts in every member, with the species of every member its own states, as the reactions at every site of a reaction-diffusion field.

A subclass may bind its species under roles of its own names, such as susceptible and infected: it returns its entries from _get_reactants, _get_products, and _get_modifiers, pairs of the path a role binds and a state name, and the reaction reads every pair from the namespace of the role that binds its path.

The propensity is k times the product of every reactant and modifier state to the power of its coefficient, or the expression the propensity function returns. The reaction changes every state by its coefficient among the products minus its coefficient among the reactants, so it conserves the total of the states whose changes sum to zero, and modifiers enter the propensity but do not change.

In the mode 'rate' the reaction is a rate equation. In the mode 'jump' it is the random event of a JumpInteraction at the propensity that moves the units of the coefficients. In the mode 'langevin' it is the chemical Langevin equation, the rate equation with one Wiener process of amplitude the square root of the propensity driving every state the reaction changes.

In the 'agent' form the target is an agent group and every member reacts on its own states, the species named by state names alone, in every step from the states at its start. The propensity of a member is k times the product of its reactant and modifier states to the power of their coefficients, or the number propensity(agent, model) returns, and a coefficient that is a function is the number coefficient(agent, model) returns. In the mode 'rate' the member adds the changes times its propensity, one unit step of the rate equation, and in the mode 'jump' it adds the changes with the probability 1 - exp(-propensity) that an event fires in the step. The members react at once from the states at the start of the rule under the schedule 'synchronous', one after the other in their order or in a new random order every step under 'sequential' or 'random-sequential', or each in its own activation under 'member'.

docs.title: ReinforcementInteraction(label, *, target, scores, payoff, rate=0.1, rule='average', form='symbolic', phase=None, chosen=None, schedule='synchronous')
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Reinforcement of the scores of options, each moving towards the payoff its option realized in the step.

Every step, the score s_k of option k of every member moves towards the realized payoff P_k at the rate a, s_k <- s_k + a (P_k - s_k), so a score is an exponentially weighted mean of past payoffs, and the last payoff at the rate 1, by the rule 'average'. By the rule 'cumulative' the score adds the payoff, s_k <- s_k + P_k, so it is the sum of past payoffs, such as a virtual score. In the agent form the scores may be the components of one vector state, one per option, and a group of one member holds scores that several groups share. In the 'symbolic' form, payoff(namespace, k) returns the payoff of option k as a symbolic expression, where namespace.target holds the states and parameters of the group. In the 'agent' form, the group is an agent group and payoff(agent, model, k) returns the payoff as a number, so it can read the agent and the history and storage of the model view. With chosen, the name of a state that holds the index of the option a member chose, only the score of that option moves, and the payoff of the other options is not read. In the agent form every agent reinforces at once under the schedule 'synchronous', one after the other in their order or in a new random order every step under 'sequential' or 'random-sequential', and each in its own activation under 'member', together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them, such as after a choice and a transfer in one visit.

required payoff Callable[..., float | Expression]

The function payoff(namespace, k) in the symbolic form, or payoff(agent, model, k) in the agent form, that returns the realized payoff of option k.

required rate Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed(0, 1))]

The rate a at which the scores move towards the payoffs, between 0 and 1, by the rule 'average'.

0.1 rule str

'average' to move the scores towards the payoffs, or 'cumulative' to add the payoffs to the scores.

'average' form str

'symbolic' for update laws of the states of a group, or 'agent' for a rule over an agent group.

'symbolic' phase str | None

The phase of the step the agent form runs in, or None for the default phase.

None chosen str | None

The name of the state that holds the index of the option a member chose, so only its score moves, or None to move every score.

None schedule str

The order of the agent form, 'synchronous' for every agent at once, 'sequential' or 'random-sequential' for one agent after the other, or 'member' for every agent in its own activation.

docs.text:
Bases: RateInteraction

Relaxation (goal(ns) - x) / time(ns) of a state x of a target towards a goal, with optional noise.

With a constant goal and time and an additive noise of amplitude sigma, the state follows the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dx = (goal - x) / time dt + sigma dW, whose stationary variance is sigma**2 time / 2. Without noise it is first-order smoothing, or adaptive expectation, towards the goal. A goal or a time function takes the namespace of the interaction, as for RateInteraction, and a number stands for a constant. A goal that is a number applies to every component of a vector state.

docs.title: SamplingInteraction(label, *, target, state, objective, move='flip', intensity=1.0, rule='metropolis', schedule='checkerboard', neighborhood=None, values=(), width=1.0, cooling=None)
docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Monte Carlo sweeps of a state of the members of a lattice or network group, one sweep per unit of time.

Every sweep proposes a move of the state of every member and accepts it from the change of the local objective of the member, the terms of the objective that involve its value, at the intensity. The local objective is a function of the namespace, which holds namespace.target, the states and parameters of the member, and namespace.target.other, a neighbour, whose values neighbors(...) sums over neighborhood. A move is 'flip', the negative value, 'random-value', a value drawn from values, 'rotate', the value plus a uniform number in [-width, width], 'gaussian', the value plus a normal number of standard deviation width, or a function move(values, random) of the array of the current values of some members and the random generator that returns their proposed values. The move 'cluster' is the Wolff algorithm instead: a sweep flips clusters until the flipped members number as many as the members, each cluster grown from a random member through the bonds to neighbours with probability 1 - exp(min(0, -intensity * (f(-s, n) - f(s, n)))), where f(s, n) is the term of the local objective of a member of value s with a neighbour of value n. It takes an objective of such pair terms that the flip of both values keeps, and ignores the rule and the schedule.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default label str

The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

required target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

The path of the group on the sites of a lattice or the nodes of a network.

required state str

The name of the state the moves change.

required objective Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]

The function objective(namespace) of the local objective of a member.

required move str | Callable[..., object]

'flip', 'random-value', 'rotate', 'gaussian', 'cluster', or a function that proposes values.

'flip' intensity Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

The factor of the change of the objective in the acceptance exp(-intensity * change).

1.0 rule str

The acceptance, 'metropolis', 'glauber', or 'heat-bath', which draws among all values of a discrete move by the weights exp(-intensity * objective).

'metropolis' schedule str

'checkerboard', 'colored', or 'random-sequential'.

'checkerboard' neighborhood BaseNeighborhood | None

The neighbourhood the objective reduces over, or None for the von Neumann neighbourhood of a square lattice. A network takes AdjacencyNeighborhood().

None values Sequence[float]

The values a random-value move draws from.

() width float

The largest change of a rotation, or the standard deviation of a Gaussian move.

1.0 cooling Callable[[Expression], object] | None

The function of the time symbol that multiplies one over the intensity, or None for a constant intensity.

...     def __init__(self, label, s: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.s = s

>>> ising = SamplingInteraction('ising', target='spins', state='s', objective=objective, intensity=1.0)
>>> spins = LatticeElement('spins', element=SpinElement, space=LatticeSpace((8, 8)))
>>> system = System(elements=[spins], interactions=[ising], time=DiscreteTime())
>>> states = Simulation(system, random_state=0).check().prepare().run(until=20).trajectory_.states
>>> bool(abs(states[-1].mean()) > 0.9)

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Step of a state of discrete time by the sign of a signal, kept within bounds.

In the mode 'multiplicative' the next value of the state x is x (1 + step sign(signal)), and in the mode 'additive' it is x + step sign(signal), so the state rises while the signal is positive, falls while it is negative, and stays while it is zero, by trial and error rather than by the size of the signal. The next value is then limited to [lower, upper].

In the 'symbolic' form, the signal, the step, and the bounds are numbers or functions of the namespace, where namespace.target holds the states and parameters of the target. In the 'agent' form, the target is an agent group and they are numbers or functions f(agent, model) that return numbers. The agents step at once from the states at the start of the rule under the schedule 'synchronous', one after the other in their order or in a new random order every step under 'sequential' or 'random-sequential', each reading the states the agents before it set, or each in its own activation under 'member', together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them.

docs.title: TopologyInteraction(label, *, target=None, action='add-edge', rate=None, probability=None, condition=None, toward=None, edges=1, keep='source', values=None, layer=None, hyperedge=None)
docs.text:
Bases: NeighborInteraction

Change of the topology of a network: nodes and edges that are added or removed, and edges that are rewired.

The action runs for every node of the group a role binds, 'add-node', 'remove-node', 'replace-node', which removes the node and adds a new one, and 'add-edge', or for every edge of its network, 'remove-edge' and 'rewire'. Without a target, 'add-node' runs once per step, adding one node from outside the network to the one network whose groups are variable, as in growing networks. It fires at a rate, with a probability per step, or with probability one, and only where the condition holds. The rate, the probability, and the condition are numbers or functions of the namespace of an edge, whose ends are namespace.source and namespace.target, and an action of the nodes reads the node as the source. A new node joins edges other nodes, a node adding edges joins edges other nodes, and a rewiring keeps the end keep of its edge. New ends are drawn with probability proportional to toward(node), a function of the namespace of a candidate node, or uniformly. A new node or edge takes the values, each a value or a function of the random number generator that draws it. The groups on the nodes and the edges of the network are variable. With hyperedge, a new node instead forms a hyperedge of that size with hyperedge - 1 existing nodes and joins each of them by an edge: the first two are the ends of an edge drawn uniformly, so a size of three attaches a triangle along an edge, and further members are drawn by toward. The new hyperedge is a new member of the variable group on the hyperedges of the network.

Parameters:

Bases: Interaction

Training of the adaptive parameters of a nested system by gradient steps on a loss over unrolled runs.

The role model binds the path of a nested system, which the training unrolls over the sequences of a dataset from its initial states, inside one step of the discrete time of the system that holds the interaction. That step is one epoch of shuffled batches, each followed by one update of the optimizer, and the interaction returns the GradientStepLaw that takes it. The hyperparameters of the optimizer are parameters of the interaction, so a schedule or Simulation.update_parameters changes them between epochs. 'sgd' reads the learning rate, 'momentum' also the momentum, 'rmsprop' the learning rate and beta2, the decay of its mean squared gradient, and 'adam' the learning rate, beta1, and beta2. It differs from GradientInteraction, which moves states down the gradient of a potential in the system's own time.

docs.text:
Bases: Interaction

Transfer of amounts of states from the members of a source role to the members of a target role.

A leg moves an amount out of a state of the source member, or out of Source(), into a state of the target member, or into Sink(). The transfer has a first leg, state into into by amount, and any further legs, each (state, into, amount) or (state, into, amount, flow). The amounts of all legs are read before any of them moves, so a leg sees the states as they were before the transfer. A guard skips the transfer where it does not hold.

The symbolic form reports the amount of every leg as a flow. A leg named by its flow is reported under that name: under the element or group, as <path>.<flow>, when the source and the target are one element or group, since the flow then moves a quantity within it like a flow of its own, and under the interaction, as <label>.<flow>, otherwise, as it is for a subclass that names its roles otherwise. A leg without a name is reported under the interaction as <label>.flow_<index>.

The form chooses how the transfer lowers:

  • 'symbolic' lowers to TransferLaws between the source and the target of one element, or member i of both groups. The amounts, the guard, and the rates are numbers or functions of the namespace, and the roles are read as namespace.source and namespace.target. With a rate, the amount is the size of a jump at the rate, and with a reverse_rate jumps also move the amounts back from the target to the source at that rate, so a leg from Source() returns its amount to the environment. With an offset, the source is a group and every member transfers along an edge of the group order, to the member offset places along it, which namespace.target reads. Past the ends of a 'fixed' boundary no member is there, and the edge moves nothing. A draw in an amount is one draw per edge, which both of its ends read, so the amounts of a step move in parallel. A leg end '<role>.<state>' names the state of the element or group another role binds, so one transfer moves amounts between several holders, such as the payments of a circuit of sectors, and a subclass that declares parameters reads them in its amounts. A subclass that names its roles otherwise returns their names from _get_role, or the namespaces of the source and the target of every pair from _get_holders.
  • 'agent' lowers to an agent rule, whose amounts and guard are numbers or functions of the source agent, the target agent, and the model view. The pairing 'members' pairs member i of both groups, 'random' pairs every source member with a random target member, 'pairs' draws disjoint random pairs, 'neighbors' pairs every source member with the target members in the cells or nodes around it, 'neighbor-pairs' draws disjoint random pairs of neighbours, every source member in random order taking a random unpaired target member around it, and 'cell' pairs the source and target members that stand in one cell or node. With a fallback group, the members of that group are the targets of a step in which no target member lives. With the pairing 'site' the target role binds a field, and every source member moves its amounts into the site of the field at its cell or node, so a negative amount takes from the site. The functions of this pairing take the cell of the source agent in place of a target agent. With remove, the source or the target member of every pair that transfers is removed, as an agent eaten whole. The named pairings other than 'members' and 'site' are shorthands of a PartnerSpec, which pairs every source member with partners within a radius, by score, or with a fallback. A settlement receives both partners and the amounts of the legs, read once, and changes the states in place of the legs, so one draw credits both ends. A subclass that names its roles otherwise returns their names from _get_role.

Under the schedule 'random-sequential' the pairs act in random order. Under 'member' every member of the actor role acts in its own activation, together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them: it transfers with its partners, the members of the other role that the pairing 'random', 'neighbors', or 'cell' gives it, or with partners of them drawn at random, and with itself under the pairing 'members' within one group. A leg end of the agent form may name '<reference>.<state>', the state of the member that a reference state of the agent names, such as 'bank.deposits' for the deposits of a customer's bank, declared StateSpec(reference='banks').

def transfer(self, source: AgentViewProtocol, target: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> bool:
    """Move the amounts of every leg from one source agent to one target agent, when the guard holds.

    Args:
        source:
            The agent the amounts leave.

        target:
            The agent the amounts enter.

        model:
            The model view of the rule.

    Returns:
        transferred:
            Whether the guard held, so the amounts moved.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            An amount function returns something other than a number.

        SimulationError:
            A leg end names the state of a referenced member, and the reference state names no member.
    """
    if self.guard is not None and not self.guard(source, target, model):
        return False
    legs = self._get_legs()
    amounts = [self._evaluate(amount, source, target, model) for _, _, amount, _ in legs]
    if self.settlement is not None:
        self.settlement(source, target, amounts, model)
        return True
    ends = [
        (
            self._get_end(source, state) if isinstance(state, str) else None,
            self._get_end(target, into) if isinstance(into, str) else None,
        )
        for state, into, _, _ in legs
    ]
    for (taken, given), amount in zip(ends, amounts, strict=True):
        if taken is not None:
            holder, name = taken
            setattr(holder, name, getattr(holder, name) - amount)
        if given is not None:
            holder, name = given
            setattr(holder, name, getattr(holder, name) + amount)
    return True

Bases: Interaction

Move of a discrete state of the target from one value to another, or between all its values by a matrix.

A member whose state holds source moves to destination at a rate, as a jump in continuous time, with a probability in every step of discrete time, or in the step in which a condition holds. With over='neighbors' the rate and the probability are those of one neighbour, written with namespace.target.other for the neighbour: the rates of the neighbours add up, and their probabilities combine as 1 - prod(1 - p), the probability that at least one of them moves the member. With a matrix instead, the state takes the values 0 to n - 1 and steps by the rows of a transition matrix in discrete time, the row of its current value. An emission matrix then draws the observed state of the target from the row that the next value of the state selects, as a hidden Markov source. With a residence time after, a member moves by a probability or a condition only once it has held the source value for after steps, at the earliest at the end of the step that completes them.

In the 'symbolic' form, every function reads namespace.target, the states and parameters of the target, and the time namespace.t. In the 'agent' form, the target is an agent group and every function takes the agent and the model view, f(agent, model), and returns a number, a truth value, or the rows of a matrix, and a rate r moves an agent with probability 1 - exp(-r) in a step. With over='cell', every member acts on the other members of its cell: it moves each one that holds the source value with the probability, the rate, or the condition f(agent, other, model) of that member agent and the acting member other, each by its own draw.

The schedule of the agent form orders the members. Under 'synchronous' every member decides from the states at the start of the step, under 'sequential' the members act one after the other in their order, and under 'random-sequential' in a new random order every step, each reading the values the members before it set. Under 'member' every member acts in its own activation, together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them, so one rule of a member runs its movement, transfers, transitions, and life cycle.

def move(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
    """Move the state of every agent of the target that moves in this step, by the schedule.

    Args:
        model:
            The model view of the interaction.
    """
    agents = list(model.agents(self._get_role('target')))
    if self.schedule == 'synchronous':
        moves = [move for agent in agents for move in self._get_moves(agent, model)]
        self._apply(moves, model)
        return
    order = model.rng.permutation(len(agents)) if self.schedule == 'random-sequential' else range(len(agents))
    for index in order:
        self._move_member(agents[int(index)], model)

Bases: BaseLaw

Gain or loss of a target density at a signed rate of the product of two densities.

The amount of the first density f in class h that meets the amount of the second density g in class k adds to class i of the target at the rate r[h, k] with probability B[h, k, i], so the law adds sum_hk r[h, k] B[h, k, i] f_h g_k to the rate of the target at i. docs.title: CascadeLaw(drive, relax, stable, max_iterations=100000, activity=None, *, label='')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseLaw

Cascade of a lattice: drive laws once per step, then the laws that relax it until it is stable.

Every cascade that changes the lattice is recorded as an event with its size, the number of site updates, its duration, the number of iterations, and its area, the number of distinct sites updated. A site update is a site that changes in an iteration, or a site that activity marks as active before it, such as a toppling site.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default drive Sequence[BaseLaw]

The laws applied once per step, local rules or drives.

required relax Sequence[BaseLaw]

The laws applied in turn until the lattice is stable.

required stable Callable[..., bool]

A function of the arrays of the targets of the laws that relax the lattice, in lattice shape, that returns whether the lattice is stable.

required max_iterations int

The largest number of iterations in one step.

100000 activity Callable[..., object] | None

A function of the arrays of the targets that returns a boolean array of the active sites of an iteration, or None to count the sites that change.

None label str

The name of the cascade events, or the empty string for the path of the element.

''

Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.laws import CascadeLaw, LocalRuleLaw
>>> from skcomplex.core.spaces import VonNeumannNeighborhood
>>> height = var('height')
>>> topple = LocalRuleLaw(height, VonNeumannNeighborhood(center=True), lambda z, *n: z - 4 * (z >= 4))
>>> CascadeLaw([], [topple], lambda z: bool((z < 4).all())).check().prepare().targets_

docs.title: EncounterLaw(candidate, field, rate, transition, test=None, *, label='')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseLaw

Bilinear transfer of a density between its classes at the rate of its product with a second density.

The amount of the candidate density f in class h meets the amount of the field density g in class k at the rate eta[h, k], and moves to class i with the probability A[h, k, i]. The law adds the gain and the loss

df_i/dt = sum_hk eta[h, k] A[h, k, i] f_h g_k - f_i sum_k eta[i, k] g_k,

where the loss acts on the candidate and the gain on the test density, the candidate itself by default, so the total over the classes is conserved. The candidate, the field, and the test are states of groups on the sites of lattices of classes, one member per class. A field density that no law changes is a fixed external input.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default candidate Expression

The symbol of the candidate density, a state of a group read member by member.

required field Expression | None

The symbol of the field density, or None for a linear redistribution, with one field class of value one.

required rate object

The encounter rate, a number or a parameter expression, or an array eta[h, k] of them.

required transition object

The array A[h, k, i] of transition probabilities, numbers or parameter expressions, which sum to one over i.

required test Expression | None

The symbol of the density the candidate moves into, or None for the candidate's own density.

None label str

The name of the law, or the empty string for a law without one.

''

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws import EncounterLaw
>>> f, g = var('f'), var('g')
>>> rate, transition = EncounterLaw(f, g, 1.0, np.full((2, 2, 2), 0.5)).check().prepare().run({}).value_
>>> rate, np.shape(transition)
(1.0, (2, 2, 2))

docs.title: EquationLaw(lhs, rhs=None, *, target=None, label='')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseLaw

Implicit relation in which the highest time derivatives of states appear, such as Newton's second law.

The states are Sage functions of time, such as function('theta')(t), and their derivatives are Sage derivatives, theta.diff(t, 2). The compiler solves all equations of a system jointly for the highest derivatives, which must appear linearly, and adds the rate laws on the same states to the solution. An equation may name the state whose equation it is, its target, and the equations of one target, from any element or interaction, add into one before the solve, so a term of it may hold no highest derivative, such as the part a coupling Lagrangian adds to the Euler-Lagrange equation of a coordinate.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default lhs object

The left side, or a Sage relation lhs == rhs.

required rhs object

The right side, or None when lhs is a relation.

None target object

The state whose equation this is, so that the equations of one target add, or None for an equation of its own.

None label str

The name of the law, or the empty string for a law without one.

''

Attributes:

Name Type Description lhs_

The left side.

rhs_

The right side.

Examples:

>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import function, sin, var
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws import EquationLaw
>>> t, g, l = var('t g l')
>>> theta = function('theta')(t)
>>> EquationLaw(l * theta.diff(t, 2) == -g * sin(theta)).check().prepare().rhs_

docs.title: GradientStepLaw(trained, loss, data, optimizer, batch_size, *, truncation=None, metrics=(), label='')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseLaw

Optimizer steps on adaptive parameters of a nested system, on the gradient of a loss over unrolled runs.

One step of the discrete time that holds the law is one epoch. In an epoch the sequences of the dataset are shuffled and split into batches, and for every batch the nested system runs from its initial states over every sequence, the loss is averaged over the steps and sequences with the step weights, and the optimizer changes the trained parameters by the gradient of that mean. The gradient is exact, by automatic differentiation of the unrolled runs. The law records the mean batch loss of the epoch and every metric over the whole dataset at the end of the epoch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default trained Sequence[str]

The dotted paths of the adaptive parameters of the nested system that the law trains, such as readout.W.

required loss ObservableSpec

The observable of the nested system whose weighted mean over the steps of a batch is minimized.

required data DatasetSpec

The sequences of the parameters of the nested system that set its inputs and targets at every step.

required optimizer str

The name of the optimizer, 'sgd', 'momentum', 'rmsprop', or 'adam'.

required batch_size int

The number of sequences of a batch. The last batch of an epoch holds the rest.

required truncation int | None

The number of inner steps the gradient flows back through the inner states, or None for the whole run.

None metrics Sequence[ObservableSpec]

The observables of the nested system recorded at the end of every epoch, as weighted means over every sequence.

() label str

The name of the law, or the empty string for a law without one.

''

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws import GradientStepLaw
>>> from skcomplex.specs import DatasetSpec, ObservableSpec
>>> data = DatasetSpec({'inputs.x': np.zeros((4, 3, 1))})
>>> law = GradientStepLaw(['readout.W'], ObservableSpec('error', 0.0), data, 'adam', 2).check()
>>> law.prepare('training').targets_

docs.title: JumpLaw(rate=None, changes=None, waiting=None, reset=None, *, label='')
docs.text:
Bases: BaseLaw

Random event that changes states, on an exponential clock of a given rate or on a clock of drawn waiting times.

With a rate, the event fires at the times of a Poisson process of that propensity and changes states by fixed increments, as in continuous-time Markov chains. With a waiting time instead, it fires after a waiting time drawn anew at every firing, and applies its reset, as in renewal processes such as the jumps of a random walk. Every member of a group then fires on its own clock, and the trajectory records every firing and counts them in <label>.renewals. Jumps combine with rate and noise laws, which evolve the states between firings.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rate object

The propensity of the event, a symbolic expression, a Call, or a callable f(t, values), or None with a waiting time.

None changes Mapping[Expression, object] | None

A mapping from the symbol of a scalar state to its increment when the event fires. In a law of a group, a target may also be a member offset read shift_member(namespace.n, k).

None waiting object

The waiting time until the next firing, usually a draw from a distribution with nonnegative support, such as draw('wait', 'pareto', b=alpha), or None for the exponential clock of rate.

None reset Mapping[Expression, object] | None

With a waiting time, a mapping from state symbol to its new value, which may hold draws, or None.

None label str

With a waiting time, the name of the firings in the trajectory, or the empty string for the path of the element.

''

def get_pairs(
    self,
    left: Sequence[AgentViewProtocol],
    right: Sequence[AgentViewProtocol],
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> list[tuple[object, object]]:
    """Return the pairs of the agents of both sides by the pairing.

    Args:
        left:
            The agents of the first side.

        right:
            The agents of the second side, the same sequence for pairs within one group.

        rng:
            The random generator.

    Returns:
        pairs:
            The pairs of agents, the first of every pair from the first side.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            A selection of partners names a state the agents do not have.
    """
    spec = self.pairing
    if not isinstance(spec, PartnerSpec):
        return (spec or random_pairing)(left, right, rng, self.capacity)
    if (spec.candidates, spec.choice, spec.capacity, spec.fallback) == ('all', 'uniform', 1, None):
        return self._get_disjoint_pairs(left, right, rng)
    return list(self._get_partners(spec, left, right, rng))

def iterate_pairs(
    self,
    left: Sequence[AgentViewProtocol],
    right: Sequence[AgentViewProtocol],
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    feasible: Feasibility,
) -> Iterator[tuple[AgentViewProtocol, AgentViewProtocol]]:
    """Yield the pairs of a selection of partners one at a time, so a caller settles each before the next one.

    The agents act in random order, since the first to act take what the feasibility reads.

    Args:
        left:
            The agents of the first side.

        right:
            The agents of the second side.

        rng:
            The random generator.

        feasible:
            The function `feasible(agent, candidate)` that says whether an agent can pair with a candidate now.

    Returns:
        pairs:
            The pairs of agents, the first of every pair from the first side.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The pairing is not a selection of partners, or it names a state the agents do not have.
    """
    if not isinstance(self.pairing, PartnerSpec):
        error_msg = f'The match {self.label!r} iterates the pairs of a `PartnerSpec`, not {self.pairing!r}.'

    return self._get_partners(self.pairing, left, right, rng, feasible)

docs.text:
Bases: BaseLaw

Amplitude of a Wiener process that drives the highest time derivative of a state.

Without a process, every component of the target and every member of a group gets its own independent Wiener process. Laws of one component, or of one member, that name the same local process share its increment. Laws that name a process of a WienerProcessSpec through a role share it across components and members.

A conserved noise on a state of a field on a lattice adds div(value eta) instead, the finite-difference divergence of a random flux with one Wiener process per link between neighbouring sites, so the total of the field changes only by its rate laws.

Name Type Description Default target Target

required value object

required order int | None

None convention str

The stochastic calculus of the law, 'ito', 'stratonovich', or 'anti-ito'. The compiler adds the drift correction of the convention, so every solver integrates the Itô form.

'ito' process Process

None for independent processes, a label local to the element, a tuple of labels with one per component of a vector target, or the handle namespace.<role>.dW or namespace.<role>.dW[k] of the processes of a WienerProcessSpec.

None conserved bool

Whether the noise is the divergence of a random flux on the links of the lattice of a field.

False label str

''

Bases: BaseLaw

docs.title: UpdateLaw(target, value, *, label='', increment=False, source=None, order=None, phase=None)
docs.text:
Bases: BaseLaw

Next value of a state after one discrete time step.

A state takes one update law, unless each of its update laws declares how it combines with the others. An increment law gives the state plus a change, and a law with a source changes only a state that holds the source value and keeps every other value. Several such laws of one state combine in one step by adding their changes, x + sum_k (f_k - x), all computed from the states at the start of the step, so increments add and moves from distinct source values compose. Two laws with the same source, or a law that declares neither, are an error.

With an order, the members of a group update one after the other, in increasing order of the value of order at the start of the step, ties in the order of the members, and each member reads the values the members before it set. Without one, every member updates at once from the states at the start of the step.

With a phase, the law runs in that phase of the step, which a PhasesScheduleSpec of the discrete time orders. The phases run one after the other, each reading the states the phases before it set, and the laws of one phase update at once. A law without a phase runs in the default phase, first unless the schedule places it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target Target | TopologyRequestSpec

The symbol of a scalar state, the column of symbols of a vector state, or a TopologyRequestSpec, whose value is the probability that the request fires.

required value object

A symbolic expression, a Call, or a callable f(t, values) that gives the next value.

required label str

The name of the law, or the empty string for a law without one.

'' increment bool

Whether the value is the state plus a change that adds to the changes of the other update laws of the state.

False source float | None

The value the law moves the state from, keeping every other value, or None.

None order object

A symbolic expression of the states, parameters, and draws of a member, whose values order the members that update one after the other, or None for members that update at once.

None phase str | None

The name of the phase of the step the law runs in, or None for the default phase.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The value is a NumPy array, or an increment law has a source.

Examples:

>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws import UpdateLaw
>>> x = var('x')
>>> UpdateLaw(x, 4 * x * (1 - x)).check().prepare().run({'x': 0.5}).value_
1.0
>>> UpdateLaw(x, x + 1, increment=True).check().increment
True
>>> UpdateLaw(x, x + 1, phase='imitate').check().phase
'imitate'

def advection(expression: object, velocity: Sequence[object] | FreeModuleElement) -> Expression:
    """Return the advection of a field expression by a velocity, its rate of transport, with upwind differences.

    Args:
        expression:
            An expression of the states and parameters of a field.

        velocity:
            One velocity component per dimension, numbers or expressions.

    Returns:
        advection:
            The advection term, to subtract from the rate of the field.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import advection
        >>> sorted(str(term) for term in advection(var('u'), [1.0, 2.0]).operands())
        ['upwind(u, 0, 1.0)', 'upwind(u, 1, 2.0)']
    """
    return sum((upwind(SR(expression), SR(axis), SR(item)) for axis, item in enumerate(velocity)), SR(0))

def antisymmetric_part(tensor: Matrix) -> Matrix:
    """Return the antisymmetric part of a square matrix, `(M - M^T) / 2`.

    Args:
        tensor:
            A square matrix of expressions.

    Returns:
        part:
            The antisymmetric matrix.

    Raises:
        TensorShapeError:
            The value is not a square matrix.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import SR, matrix, var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import antisymmetric_part
        >>> antisymmetric_part(matrix(SR, [[0, 2 * var('a')], [0, 0]]))
        [ 0  a]
        [-a  0]
    """
    checked = _check_matrix('antisymmetric_part', tensor)
    return (checked - checked.transpose()) / 2

def circular_mean(
    angle: object,
    over: object = None,
    where: object = None,
    weights: object = None,
    by: str | None = None,
) -> Expression:
    """Return the circular mean of an angle over the members of a group, `arctan2(sum_j sin a_j, sum_j cos a_j)`.

    The mean is the direction of the sum of the unit vectors at the angles, 0 when no member is selected.

    Args:
        angle:
            The angle of one member, in radians.

        over:
            The namespace of the group to reduce over, or `None` for the group the angle reads.

        where:
            A condition on the reduced member that selects the members, or `None` for all members.

        weights:
            A constant matrix with one row per reading member and one column per reduced member, or `None`.

        by:
            The name of a state of the group, so every member reduces over the members that share its value of the
            state, or `None` for all members. It needs the namespace of the group as `over`.

    Returns:
        reduction:
            The symbolic circular mean, in `[-pi, pi]`.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The group is not a namespace or a symbol, the weights are not a matrix, or a key has no group namespace.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import circular_mean
        >>> circular_mean(var('theta'))
        arctan2(total(sin(theta)), total(cos(theta)))
    """
    sines = total(sin(SR(angle)), over, where, weights, by)
    cosines = total(cos(SR(angle)), over, where, weights, by)
    return arctan2(sines, cosines)

def clip(x: object, low: object = None, high: object = None) -> Expression:
    """Return an expression limited to an interval, `low` below it, `high` above it, and the expression inside.

    Args:
        x:
            The expression to limit.

        low:
            The lower bound, or `None` for none.

        high:
            The upper bound, or `None` for none.

    Returns:
        value:
            The symbolic limited value.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import clip
        >>> x = var('x')
        >>> clip(x, 0, 1)
        where(x < 0, 0, where(x > 1, 1, x))
        >>> [clip(x, 0, 1).subs(x=value) for value in (-2, 0.5, 3)]
        [0, 0.5, 1]
    """
    value = SR(x)
    if high is not None:
        value = where(SR(x) > high, high, value)
    if low is not None:
        value = where(SR(x) < low, low, value)
    return value

Return a reduction over the connected components of the active links between the members of a group.

The links are the pairs of neighbours of the neighbourhood, the graph of a network space by default, and a link is active when active, written for one link as in neighbors, is not 0. Inside it namespace.other holds the symbols of the neighbour, namespace those of the member, and the states of a group on the edges of the network those of the edge that joins them, so a link is active by a condition, such as edges.state > 0, or by an edge weight that is not 0. Two members are in one component when a path of active links joins them, read without direction on a directed network, and a member without active links is a component of its own.

The reductions are 'label', the smallest index of a member of the component of every member, 'size', the number of members of the component of every member, 'largest', the number of members of the largest component, the same for every member, and 'giant', 1 for the members of the largest component and 0 for the others, the component of the smallest label among components of equal size.

The neighbourhood, or None for the neighbours of the network or lattice the group lives on.

None reduce str

Name Type Description reduction Expression

The unevaluated reduction, one value per member.

Raises:

Type Description ValidationError

The reduction or the neighbourhood is unknown.

>>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import components, neighborhoods_in
>>> components(var('open') > 0, reduce='size')
components(open > 0, reduce='size')
>>> [item.kind for item in neighborhoods_in(1 + components(var('open'), reduce='largest'))]

def components(
    active: object,
    over: BaseNeighborhood | LayerSpec | None = None,
    reduce: str = 'label',
) -> Expression:
    """Return a reduction over the connected components of the active links between the members of a group.

    The links are the pairs of neighbours of the neighbourhood, the graph of a network space by default, and a link is
    active when `active`, written for one link as in `neighbors`, is not 0. Inside it `namespace.other` holds the
    symbols of the neighbour, `namespace` those of the member, and the states of a group on the edges of the network
    those of the edge that joins them, so a link is active by a condition, such as `edges.state > 0`, or by an edge
    weight that is not 0. Two members are in one component when a path of active links joins them, read without
    direction on a directed network, and a member without active links is a component of its own.

    The reductions are `'label'`, the smallest index of a member of the component of every member, `'size'`, the
    number of members of the component of every member, `'largest'`, the number of members of the largest component,
    the same for every member, and `'giant'`, 1 for the members of the largest component and 0 for the others, the
    component of the smallest label among components of equal size.

    Args:
        active:
            The activity of one link, an expression of the symbols of `namespace.other`, `namespace`, and the edge
            between them, whose links are active where it is not 0.

        over:
            The neighbourhood, or `None` for the neighbours of the network or lattice the group lives on.

        reduce:
            `'label'`, `'size'`, `'largest'`, or `'giant'`.

    Returns:
        reduction:
            The unevaluated reduction, one value per member.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The reduction or the neighbourhood is unknown.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import components, neighborhoods_in
        >>> components(var('open') > 0, reduce='size')
        components(open > 0, reduce='size')
        >>> [item.kind for item in neighborhoods_in(1 + components(var('open'), reduce='largest'))]
        ['component-largest']
    """
    if reduce not in COMPONENT_REDUCTIONS:
        error_msg = f'Unknown components reduction {reduce!r}. Use one of {", ".join(COMPONENT_REDUCTIONS)}.'
        raise ValidationError(error_msg)
    return COMPONENTS(SR(active), _neighborhood_symbol(over), COMPONENT_REDUCTIONS.index(reduce))

def contraction(tensor: object, *expressions: object) -> Expression:
    """Return the contraction of a tensor with one expression per index after the first, `sum_jk T_ijk a_j b_k`.

    The tensor is a parameter of an interaction declared `ParameterSpec(shape=(role,) * k)`, whose first index runs
    over the reading members and every other index over the members of a group. Inside the contraction the symbols of
    the expression of an index stand for the member of that index, so `contraction(T, x, x)` reads `x_j` and `x_k`.

    Args:
        tensor:
            The symbol of the shaped parameter of order `k`.

        *expressions:
            The `k - 1` expressions of one member, one per index after the first.

    Returns:
        contraction:
            The unevaluated contraction, one value per reading member, which every backend lowers.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The tensor is not a symbol, or no expression is given.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import contraction, contractions_in
        >>> T, x = var('T x')
        >>> contraction(T, x, x)
        contraction(T, x, x)
        >>> [call.operands()[0] for call in contractions_in(x * contraction(T, x, x))]
        [T]
    """
    if not isinstance(tensor, Expression) or not tensor.is_symbol():
        error_msg = f'The tensor of a contraction must be the symbol of a shaped parameter, not {tensor!r}.'
        raise ValidationError(error_msg)
    if len(expressions) < MIN_FACTORS:
        error_msg = f'The contraction of {tensor} needs one expression per index after the first, but none is given.'
        raise ValidationError(error_msg)
    return CONTRACTION(tensor, *(SR(item) for item in expressions))

def distribute_operators(expression: object) -> Expression:
    """Return an expression with the linear field operators distributed over sums and out of numeric factors.

    Args:
        expression:
            An expression of the states and parameters of a field.

    Returns:
        expression:
            The same field, in which every operator reads a product of symbols, such as `laplacian(-a)` as
            `-laplacian(a)`.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import distribute_operators, laplacian
        >>> a = var('a')
        >>> distribute_operators(laplacian(-a) + laplacian(a))
        0
    """
    item = SR(expression)
    operator = item.operator()
    if operator is None:
        return item
    operands = [distribute_operators(operand) for operand in item.operands()]
    return _distribute_call(item, operands) if _is_linear_call(item) else operator(*operands)

A delay that does not conserve its input smooths it, each stage adjusting to the previous one at gap / (time / order), and its output starts at the value.

required time object

The mean delay time, a positive number or an expression of parameters.

1 conserved bool

True

The order is not a positive integer, or the delay time is a number that is not positive.

>>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import distributed_delay
>>> distributed_delay(var('orders'), 4, order=3)
material_delay3(orders, 4)
>>> distributed_delay(var('sales'), 2, conserved=False)
smoothing_delay1(sales, 2)

def distributed_delay(value: object, time: object, order: int = 1, *, conserved: bool = True) -> Expression:
    """Return the output of a distributed delay of a value: hidden stages in series, each with a share of the time.

    A conserved delay passes its input through the stages like a material, so its output is the outflow of the last
    stage, `stage / (time / order)`, and its response to a pulse is the Erlang distribution of the order with the mean
    `time`. A delay that does not conserve its input smooths it, each stage adjusting to the previous one at
    `gap / (time / order)`, and its output starts at the value.

    Args:
        value:
            The symbolic input.

        time:
            The mean delay time, a positive number or an expression of parameters.

        order:
            The number of stages.

        conserved:
            Whether the delay conserves its input, as a material delay, or smooths it, as an information delay.

    Returns:
        output:
            The symbolic output.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            The order is not a positive integer, or the delay time is a number that is not positive.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import distributed_delay
        >>> distributed_delay(var('orders'), 4, order=3)
        material_delay3(orders, 4)
        >>> distributed_delay(var('sales'), 2, conserved=False)
        smoothing_delay1(sales, 2)
    """
    if isinstance(order, bool) or not isinstance(order, int) or order < 1:
        error_msg = f'A distributed delay has a positive integer order, but got {order!r}.'
        raise ValueError(error_msg)
    name = f'{"material" if conserved else "smoothing"}_delay{order}'
    if SR(time).is_numeric() and float(SR(time)) <= 0:
        error_msg = f'The delay time of {name} must be positive, but got {time}.'
        raise ValueError(error_msg)
    return function(name, nargs=2, eval_func=_eval_delay)(value, time)

Return every draw of an expression with its arguments, including draws in the arguments of other draws.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default expression object

A symbolic expression, a number, a vector of expressions, or a sequence of them.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description draws list[DrawSpec]

The draws, each call listed once, outer draws before the draws in their arguments.

Examples:

>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
>>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import bernoulli, draws_in, uniform
>>> x = var('x')
>>> [item.name for item in draws_in(x * uniform('u') + bernoulli('flip', uniform('u')))]

Source code in src/skcomplex/specs/_draw_spec.py 
def draws_in(expression: object) -> list[DrawSpec]:
    """Return every draw of an expression with its arguments, including draws in the arguments of other draws.

    Args:
        expression:
            A symbolic expression, a number, a vector of expressions, or a sequence of them.

    Returns:
        draws:
            The draws, each call listed once, outer draws before the draws in their arguments.

    Examples:
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import bernoulli, draws_in, uniform
        >>> x = var('x')
        >>> [item.name for item in draws_in(x * uniform('u') + bernoulli('flip', uniform('u')))]
        ['u', 'flip']
    """
    items = list(expression) if isinstance(expression, FreeModuleElement | list | tuple) else [expression]
    stack = [SR(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, Expression | int | float)]
    found: dict[str, DrawSpec] = {}
    while stack:
        item = stack.pop()
        operator = item.operator()
        if operator is None:
            continue
        name = getattr(operator, 'name', lambda: '')()
        if name in DRAWS:
            known = DRAWS[name]
            found.setdefault(
                str(item),
                DrawSpec(known.kind, known.name, known.distribution, known.keywords, tuple(item.operands()), item),
            )
        stack.extend(reversed(item.operands()))
    return list(found.values())
