docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='economics/econophysics',
    tags=('el farol', 'agents', 'inductive reasoning', 'bounded rationality'),
    references=('Arthur 1994', 'Yakovenko and Rosser 2009', 'Carmichael and Hadzikadic 2019 ch. 9'),
    defaults={'until': 200},
    observables=lambda system: [ObservableSpec('attendance', group='patrons', variable='attends', reduce='sum')],
)
def el_farol(
    n_agents: int = 100,
    *,
    capacity: float = 60.0,
    n_predictors: int = 6,
    discount: float = 0.9,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return Arthur's El Farol bar problem, whose attendance self-organizes around the capacity.

    Every patron holds a random set of predictors of next week's attendance, drawn from a pool of 46, and acts on
    its currently most accurate one, going when it forecasts room in the bar. The attendance is random-looking, yet
    its mean settles near the capacity. The patrons read the past attendances from the observable `attendance` of
    the run, which the catalog lists, so a run passes it in `observables`.

    Args:
        n_agents:
            The number of patrons.

        capacity:
            The attendance above which the bar is too crowded to enjoy.

        n_predictors:
            The number of predictors every patron holds.

        discount:
            The weight of past errors in the accuracy of a predictor.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the predictors that every patron holds.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `patrons`, the one-member group `pool` of the forecasts and the errors of the
            predictors, the reinforcement `scoring` of the errors, and the choice `choice` to go when the forecast is
            below the capacity of the patrons.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import el_farol
        >>> el_farol(10).elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        10
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state)
    masks = [
        float(sum(1 << int(index) for index in rng.choice(len(PREDICTORS), n_predictors, replace=False)))
        for _ in range(n_agents)
    ]
    patrons = GroupElement(
        'patrons',
        element=PatronElement,
        size=n_agents,
        values={'predictors': masks, 'capacity': capacity},
    )
    pool = GroupElement(
        'pool',
        element=PredictorPoolElement,
        size=1,
        values={'forecasts': np.zeros((1, len(PREDICTORS))), 'errors': np.zeros((1, len(PREDICTORS)))},
    )
    scoring = ReinforcementInteraction(
        'scoring',
        target='pool',
        scores='errors',
        payoff=PredictorPoolElement.error,
        rate=1 - discount,
        form='agent',
        phase='learn',
    )
    choice = ChoiceInteraction(
        'choice',
        target='patrons',
        state='attends',
        options=(0.0, 1.0),
        utility=lambda agent, model, option: option if agent.forecast < agent.capacity else -option,
        rule='best',
        form='agent',
        phase='decide',
    )
    return System(
        elements=[patrons, pool],
        interactions=[scoring, choice],
        time=DiscreteTime(
            schedule=PhasesScheduleSpec(
                [PhaseSpec(name) for name in ('learn', 'forecast', 'predict', 'decide')],
            ),
        ),
    )

    """Patron of the El Farol bar, who forecasts the attendance with its most accurate predictor.

    Every patron holds a few predictors of the pool, the set bits of `predictors`, and forecasts with the one of
    smallest error in the pool. A choice then sends the patron to the bar when the forecast is below the capacity.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        predictors:
            The bit mask of the predictors of the pool that the patron holds.

        forecast:
            The last forecast of the patron's most accurate predictor.

        attends:
            Whether the patron went to the bar this week, 1 or 0.

        capacity:
            The attendance above which the bar is too crowded to enjoy.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import PatronElement
        >>> GroupElement('patrons', element=PatronElement, size=100, values={'predictors': 7}).size
        100
    """

    pool: ClassVar[str] = 'pool'

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        predictors: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=NN)] = 1,
        forecast: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
        attends: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=FiniteEnumeratedSet([0, 1]))] = 0.0,
        capacity: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 60.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.predictors = predictors
        self.forecast = forecast
        self.attends = attends
        self.capacity = capacity

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[PatronView]:
        """Return the view of the agents of the element."""
        return PatronView

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the predicting rule.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return [RuleLaw(self.predict, phase='predict')]

    def predict(self, agent: PatronView, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Forecast the attendance with the most accurate predictor held.

        Args:
            agent:
                The patron.

            model:
                The model.
        """
        pool = model.agents(self.pool, PredictorPoolView)[0]
        errors, predicted = np.ravel(pool.errors), np.ravel(pool.forecasts)
        mask = int(agent.predictors)
        held = [index for index in range(len(PREDICTORS)) if mask >> index & 1]
        agent.forecast = float(predicted[held[int(np.argmin(errors[held]))]])

class PredictorPoolElement(Element):
    """Pool of Arthur's predictors, with the forecast and the accuracy of every predictor that the patrons share.

    The accuracy of a predictor depends only on the history of attendance, the observable `attendance` of the run,
    so one member holds it for every patron. Every week the pool forecasts the attendance with every predictor, from
    ten random weeks it draws at the first week followed by the observed attendances, and a
    `ReinforcementInteraction` moves the error of every predictor towards its last absolute error, a discounted mean
    of the errors.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        forecasts:
            The forecast of next week's attendance by every predictor of the pool.

        errors:
            The discounted mean absolute error of every predictor of the pool.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import PredictorPoolElement
        >>> GroupElement('pool', element=PredictorPoolElement, size=1).size
        1
    """

    attendance: ClassVar[str] = 'attendance'

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        forecasts: Annotated[npt.ArrayLike, StateSpec(vector=True)] = 0.0,
        errors: Annotated[npt.ArrayLike, StateSpec(vector=True)] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.forecasts = forecasts
        self.errors = errors

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[PredictorPoolView]:
        """Return the view of the pool."""
        return PredictorPoolView

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the forecasting rule.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return [RuleLaw(self.forecast, phase='forecast')]

    def _history(self, model: ModelView) -> Array:
        """Return the attendances, after ten random weeks drawn at the first week."""
        seeded = model.storage.get('seeded')
        if not isinstance(seeded, np.ndarray):
            seeded = model.rng.integers(0, int(MAX_ATTENDANCE) + 1, N_SEEDED_WEEKS).astype(float)
            model.storage['seeded'] = seeded
        return np.concatenate([seeded, model.history(self.attendance)])

    def forecast(self, agent: PredictorPoolView, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Forecast next week's attendance with every predictor of the pool.

        Args:
            agent:
                The pool.

            model:
                The model.
        """
        agent.forecasts = forecasts(self._history(model))

    @staticmethod
    def error(agent: PredictorPoolView, model: ModelView, index: int) -> float:
        """Return the absolute error of a predictor last week, or its error so far before the first attendance.

        Args:
            agent:
                The pool.

            model:
                The model view of the rule that reads the error.

            index:
                The index of the predictor in the pool.

        Returns:
            error:
                The absolute error of the forecast of the predictor.
        """
        attendance = model.history(PredictorPoolElement.attendance)
        if not len(attendance):
            return float(np.ravel(agent.errors)[index])
        return float(abs(np.ravel(agent.forecasts)[index] - attendance[-1]))

class ReinforcementInteraction(Interaction):
    """Reinforcement of the scores of options, each moving towards the payoff its option realized in the step.

    Every step, the score `s_k` of option `k` of every member moves towards the realized payoff `P_k` at the rate `a`,
    `s_k <- s_k + a (P_k - s_k)`, so a score is an exponentially weighted mean of past payoffs, and the last payoff at
    the rate 1, by the rule `'average'`. By the rule `'cumulative'` the score adds the payoff, `s_k <- s_k + P_k`, so
    it is the sum of past payoffs, such as a virtual score. In the agent form the scores may be the components of one
    vector state, one per option, and a group of one member holds scores that several groups share. In the
    `'symbolic'` form, `payoff(namespace, k)` returns the payoff of option `k` as a symbolic
    expression, where `namespace.target` holds the states and parameters of the group. In the `'agent'` form, the
    group is an agent group and `payoff(agent, model, k)` returns the payoff as a number, so it can read the agent and
    the history and storage of the model view. With `chosen`, the name of a state that holds the index of the option a
    member chose, only the score of that option moves, and the payoff of the other options is not read. In the agent
    form every agent reinforces at once under the schedule `'synchronous'`, one after the other in their order or in a
    new random order every step under `'sequential'` or `'random-sequential'`, and each in its own activation under
    `'member'`, together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system
    lists them, such as after a choice and a transfer in one visit.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose members hold the scores.

        scores:
            The names of the states that hold the score of every option, in the order of the options, or in the agent
            form the name of one vector state whose components are the scores.

        payoff:
            The function `payoff(namespace, k)` in the symbolic form, or `payoff(agent, model, k)` in the agent form,
            that returns the realized payoff of option `k`.

        rate:
            The rate `a` at which the scores move towards the payoffs, between 0 and 1, by the rule `'average'`.

        rule:
            `'average'` to move the scores towards the payoffs, or `'cumulative'` to add the payoffs to the scores.

        form:
            `'symbolic'` for update laws of the states of a group, or `'agent'` for a rule over an agent group.

        phase:
            The phase of the step the agent form runs in, or `None` for the default phase.

        chosen:
            The name of the state that holds the index of the option a member chose, so only its score moves, or
            `None` to move every score.

        schedule:
            The order of the agent form, `'synchronous'` for every agent at once, `'sequential'` or
            `'random-sequential'` for one agent after the other, or `'member'` for every agent in its own activation.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The form, the rule, or the schedule is unknown, the symbolic form runs member by member, there are no
            scores, or the payoff is not callable.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import ReinforcementInteraction
        >>> reinforcement = ReinforcementInteraction(
        ...     'reinforcement', target='learners', scores=('first', 'second'), payoff=lambda s, k: k, rate=0.5
        ... )
        >>> reinforcement.check().rate
        0.5
        >>> ReinforcementInteraction(
        ...     'virtual', target='players', scores='scores', payoff=lambda a, m, k: k, rule='cumulative', form='agent'
        ... ).check().rule
        'cumulative'
        >>> ReinforcementInteraction(
        ...     'satisfaction', target='customers', scores=('s1', 's2'), payoff=lambda a, m, k: 1.0, chosen='shop',
        ...     schedule='member', form='agent',
        ... ).check().chosen
        'shop'
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        scores: str | Sequence[str],
        payoff: Callable[..., float | Expression],
        rate: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed(0, 1))] = 0.1,
        rule: str = 'average',
        form: str = 'symbolic',
        phase: str | None = None,
        chosen: str | None = None,
        schedule: str = 'synchronous',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.scores = scores
        self.payoff = payoff
        self.rate = rate
        self.rule = rule
        self.form = form
        self.phase = phase
        self.chosen = chosen
        self.schedule = schedule

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown variant, no scores, or a payoff that cannot be called.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, the form, the rule, or the schedule is unknown, the symbolic form runs member
                by member, there are no scores, or the payoff is not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        for name, value, variants in (
            ('form', self.form, FORMS),
            ('rule', self.rule, RULES),
            ('schedule', self.schedule, SCHEDULES),
        ):
            if value not in variants:
                error_msg = f'Unknown {name} {value!r} of {self.label!r}. Use one of {variants}.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.form == 'symbolic' and self.schedule != 'synchronous':
            error_msg = f'The schedule {self.schedule!r} of {self.label!r} runs agent rules. Use `form="agent"`.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        vector = isinstance(self.scores, str) and bool(self.scores) and self.form == 'agent'
        if not vector and (isinstance(self.scores, str) or not self.scores):
            error_msg = (
                f'{self.label!r} has the scores {self.scores!r}. Give a sequence of state names, one per option, or '
                'in the agent form the name of a vector state.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not callable(self.payoff):
            error_msg = f'The payoff of {self.label!r} must be callable, but it is {self.payoff!r}.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _read(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol) -> Array:
        """Return the scores of an agent, one per option."""
        if isinstance(self.scores, str):
            return np.array(getattr(agent, self.scores), dtype=float).ravel()
        return np.array([getattr(agent, name) for name in self.scores], dtype=float)

    def _get_scores(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> Array:
        """Return the new scores of an agent, every score or only that of its chosen option moved by its payoff."""
        old = self._read(agent)
        options = range(len(old)) if self.chosen is None else [int(getattr(agent, self.chosen))]
        rate = 1.0 if self.rule == 'cumulative' else self._get_parameter_value('rate', model)
        change = np.zeros_like(old)
        for k in options:
            payoff = float(self.payoff(agent, model, k))
            change[k] = payoff if self.rule == 'cumulative' else rate * (payoff - old[k])
        return old + change

    def _write(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, scores: Array) -> None:
        """Set the scores of an agent."""
        if isinstance(self.scores, str):
            setattr(agent, self.scores, scores)
            return
        for name, value in zip(self.scores, scores, strict=True):
            setattr(agent, name, float(value))

    def _reinforce_member(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Move the scores of one agent towards its payoffs, in its own activation."""
        if agent.alive:
            self._write(agent, self._get_scores(agent, model))

    def reinforce(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Move the scores of every agent towards the payoffs of its options, by the schedule.

        Args:
            model:
                The model view of the interaction.
        """
        self._update_agents(model, self.schedule, self._get_scores, self._write)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the update of every score towards its payoff, or the rule of the agent form.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with `namespace.target` and `namespace.rate`.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The update laws of the scores, or the rule that reinforces the scores of the agents.
        """
        if self.form == 'agent' and self.schedule == 'member':
            return [RuleLaw(self._reinforce_member, phase=self.phase, members=self._get_role('target'))]
        if self.form == 'agent':
            return [RuleLaw(self.reinforce, phase=self.phase)]
        laws: list[BasePart] = []
        for index, name in enumerate(self.scores):
            score = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), name)
            payoff = self.payoff(namespace, index)
            change = (
                payoff
                if self.rule == 'cumulative'
                else self._get_parameter_symbol('rate', namespace) * (payoff - score)
            )
            if self.chosen is not None:
                change = where(getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.chosen) == index, change, 0)
            laws.append(UpdateLaw(score, score + change))
        return laws

class ChoiceInteraction(Interaction):
    """Choice of every member of a group among options, drawn every step from the utilities of the options by a rule.

    The rule `'logit'`, which is the heat-bath rule, draws option `k` of utility `u_k` with probability
    `exp(beta u_k) / sum_j exp(beta u_j)`, where `beta` is the intensity of choice. The rules `'metropolis'` and
    `'fermi'` propose one of the other options uniformly, or with the proposal `'all'` one of all the options
    including the current one, and accept it with probability `min(1, exp(beta (u_new - u_old)))` or
    `1 / (1 + exp(-beta (u_new - u_old)))`, so the rule `'fermi'` with the proposal `'all'` is the heat-bath rule of a
    uniform proposal. The rule `'best'` draws uniformly among the options of largest utility under the ties
    `'random'`, and takes the first of them under `'first'`. Every step, each member revises its choice with probability
    `activity` and keeps it otherwise.

    In the `'symbolic'` form, `utility(namespace, option)` returns the utility as a symbolic expression, where
    `namespace.target` holds the states and parameters of the group, and every member draws at once. In the `'agent'`
    form, the group is an agent group and `utility(agent, model, option)` returns the utility as a number, so it can
    read the agent, its neighbours, and the history and storage of the model view. Its members draw at once, from the
    choices of the last step, under the `'synchronous'` schedule, one after the other in their order or in a new random
    order, each seeing the choices made before it, under the `'sequential'` or `'random-sequential'` schedule, and each
    in its own activation under the `'member'` schedule, together with the rules of its element and the other member
    interactions, in the order the system lists them. An option of utility `-inf` is never drawn in the agent form.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose members choose.

        state:
            The name of the discrete state of the members that holds the chosen option.

        options:
            The values the state can take, at least two.

        utility:
            The function `utility(namespace, option)` in the symbolic form, or `utility(agent, model, option)` in the
            agent form, that returns the utility of an option.

        rule:
            The rule of the draw, `'logit'`, `'metropolis'`, `'fermi'`, or `'best'`.

        intensity:
            The intensity of choice `beta`, zero for uniform choice.

        schedule:
            The order in which the members revise, `'synchronous'` or, in the agent form, `'sequential'`,
            `'random-sequential'`, or `'member'`.

        activity:
            The probability that a member revises its choice in a step.

        form:
            `'symbolic'` for update laws of the states of a group, or `'agent'` for a rule over an agent group.

        phase:
            The phase of the step the agent form runs in, or `None` for the default phase.

        proposal:
            The options the rules `'metropolis'` and `'fermi'` propose from, `'others'` for the options other than the
            current one, or `'all'` for every option.

        ties:
            The option the rule `'best'` takes among options of equal largest utility, `'random'` for one drawn
            uniformly or `'first'` for the first in the order of the options.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The rule, the schedule, the form, the proposal, or the ties are unknown, the schedule is not synchronous in
            the symbolic form, there are fewer than two options, or the utility is not callable.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import ChoiceInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import mean
        >>> choice = ChoiceInteraction(
        ...     'choice', target='spins', state='spin', options=(-1, 1), utility=lambda s, o: o * mean(s.target.spin)
        ... )
        >>> choice.check().rule
        'logit'
        >>> agents = ChoiceInteraction(
        ...     'choice', target='traders', state='plan', options=(0, 1), utility=lambda a, m, o: o, form='agent'
        ... )
        >>> type(agents.check().prepare().run(SimpleNamespace()).laws_[0]).__name__
        'RuleLaw'
        >>> ChoiceInteraction(
        ...     'heat-bath', target='spins', state='spin', options=(-1, 0, 1), utility=lambda s, o: o, rule='fermi',
        ...     proposal='all'
        ... ).check().proposal
        'all'
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str,
        options: Sequence[float],
        utility: Callable[..., float | Expression],
        rule: str = 'logit',
        intensity: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        schedule: str = 'synchronous',
        activity: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed(0, 1))] = 1.0,
        form: str = 'symbolic',
        phase: str | None = None,
        proposal: str = 'others',
        ties: str = 'random',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.state = state
        self.options = options
        self.utility = utility
        self.rule = rule
        self.intensity = intensity
        self.schedule = schedule
        self.activity = activity
        self.form = form
        self.phase = phase
        self.proposal = proposal
        self.ties = ties

    def _check_variants(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown variant, or a symbolic choice that is not synchronous."""
        self._check_variant('rule', self.rule, RULES, (BaseSpec,))
        for name, value, variants in (
            ('schedule', self.schedule, SCHEDULES),
            ('form', self.form, FORMS),
            ('proposal', self.proposal, PROPOSALS),
            ('ties', self.ties, TIES),
        ):
            if value not in variants:
                error_msg = f'Unknown {name} {value!r} of {self.label!r}. Use one of {variants}.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.form == 'symbolic' and self.schedule != 'synchronous':
            error_msg = (
                f'{self.label!r} has the schedule {self.schedule!r}, which only the agent form runs. Use '
                "form='agent' or schedule='synchronous'."
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown variant, fewer than two options, or a utility that cannot be called.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, the rule, the schedule, the form, the proposal, or the ties are unknown, the
                schedule is not synchronous in the symbolic form, there are fewer than two options, or the utility is
                not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        self._check_variants()
        if len(self.options) < MIN_OPTIONS:
            error_msg = f'{self.label!r} chooses among {list(self.options)}. Give at least {MIN_OPTIONS} options.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not callable(self.utility):
            error_msg = f'The utility of {self.label!r} must be callable, but it is {self.utility!r}.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _select(self, index: Expression, values: Sequence[Expression]) -> Expression:
        """Return the value at a symbolic index."""
        return sum((where(index == position, value, 0) for position, value in enumerate(values)), SR(0))

    def _draw_softmax(self, state: Expression, utilities: Sequence[Expression], intensity: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return the option drawn with probabilities proportional to `exp(beta u_k)`."""
        index = categorical(f'{state}_option', [exp(intensity * utility) for utility in utilities])
        return self._select(index, [SR(option) for option in self.options])

    def _draw_best(self, state: Expression, utilities: Sequence[Expression]) -> Expression:
        """Return an option drawn uniformly among the options of largest utility."""
        largest = utilities[0]
        for utility in utilities[1:]:
            largest = where(utility > largest, utility, largest)
        weights = [where(utility >= largest, 1, 0) for utility in utilities]
        if self.ties == 'first':
            weights = [
                weight * where(sum(weights[:position], SR(0)) > 0, 0, 1) for position, weight in enumerate(weights)
            ]
        index = categorical(f'{state}_best', weights)
        return self._select(index, [SR(option) for option in self.options])

    def _draw_proposal(self, state: Expression, utilities: Sequence[Expression], intensity: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return a uniform proposal of an option, accepted by the Metropolis or the Fermi probability."""
        weights = [SR(1) if self.proposal == 'all' else where(state == option, 0, 1) for option in self.options]
        index = categorical(f'{state}_proposal', weights)
        proposal = self._select(index, [SR(option) for option in self.options])
        gain = self._select(index, utilities) - sum(
            (where(state == option, utility, 0) for option, utility in zip(self.options, utilities, strict=True)),
            SR(0),
        )
        if self.rule == 'metropolis':
            acceptance = where(gain >= 0, 1, exp(intensity * gain))
        else:
            acceptance = 1 / (1 + exp(-intensity * gain))
        return where(uniform(f'{state}_acceptance') < acceptance, proposal, state)

    def _draw_symbolic(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the option a member draws, as a symbolic expression of the namespace."""
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        utilities = [SR(self.utility(namespace, option)) for option in self.options]
        if self.rule == 'logit':
            return self._draw_softmax(state, utilities, self._get_parameter_symbol('intensity', namespace))
        if self.rule == 'best':
            return self._draw_best(state, utilities)
        if self.rule in ('metropolis', 'fermi'):
            return self._draw_proposal(state, utilities, self._get_parameter_symbol('intensity', namespace))
        raise self._get_variant_error(self.rule, 'rule', '_draw_symbolic')

    def _get_utilities(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return the utility of every option for an agent."""
        return np.array([float(self.utility(agent, model, option)) for option in self.options])

    def _draw_agent_proposal(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol, intensity: float) -> float:
        """Return a uniform proposal of an option of an agent if accepted, or its current option."""
        current = float(getattr(agent, self.state))
        others = [option for option in self.options if self.proposal == 'all' or option != current]
        proposal = float(others[int(model.rng.integers(len(others)))])
        before = float(self.utility(agent, model, current)) if current in self.options else 0.0
        gain = float(self.utility(agent, model, proposal)) - before
        if self.rule == 'metropolis':
            acceptance = 1.0 if gain >= 0 else math.exp(intensity * gain)
        else:
            acceptance = float(expit(intensity * gain))
        return proposal if model.rng.random() < acceptance else current

    def _draw_agent(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol, intensity: float) -> float:
        """Return the option an agent draws by the rule."""
        if self.rule in ('metropolis', 'fermi'):
            return self._draw_agent_proposal(agent, model, intensity)
        utilities = self._get_utilities(agent, model)
        if self.rule == 'best':
            return float(self.options[self._pick_best(utilities, self.ties, model)])
        if self.rule != 'logit':
            raise self._get_variant_error(self.rule, 'rule', '_draw_agent')
        scaled = np.where(np.isneginf(utilities), -np.inf, intensity * utilities)
        probabilities = softmax(scaled)
        return float(self.options[int(model.rng.choice(len(self.options), p=probabilities))])

    def _is_active(self, model: ModelViewProtocol, activity: float) -> bool:
        """Return whether a member revises its choice in this step."""
        return activity >= 1 or bool(model.rng.random() < activity)

    def _get_choice(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> float | None:
        """Return the option an agent draws if it revises in this step, or `None` to keep its own."""
        if not self._is_active(model, self._get_parameter_value('activity', model)):
            return None
        return self._draw_agent(agent, model, self._get_parameter_value('intensity', model))

    def _set_choice(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, option: float | None) -> None:
        """Set the state of an agent to the option it draws, if any."""
        if option is not None:
            setattr(agent, self.state, option)

    def _choose_member(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Set the state of one agent to the option it draws if it revises, in its own activation."""
        if agent.alive:
            self._set_choice(agent, self._get_choice(agent, model))

    def choose(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Set the state of every agent that revises in this step to the option it draws, by the schedule.

        Args:
            model:
                The model view of the interaction.
        """
        self._update_agents(model, self.schedule, self._get_choice, self._set_choice)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the update of the state of every member that revises, or the rule of the agent form.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with `namespace.target`, `namespace.intensity`, and
                `namespace.activity`.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The update law of the state, or the rule that runs the choice of the agents.
        """
        if self.form == 'agent' and self.schedule == 'member':
            return [RuleLaw(self._choose_member, phase=self.phase, members=self._get_role('target'))]
        if self.form == 'agent':
            return [RuleLaw(self.choose, phase=self.phase)]
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        revised = where(
            uniform(f'{state}_activity') < self._get_parameter_symbol('activity', namespace),
            self._draw_symbolic(namespace),
            state,
        )
        return [UpdateLaw(state, revised)]
</code></pre>

docs.text:
A kinetic wealth exchange model with a saving propensity or a debt limit.

  • Name: kinetic_wealth_exchange
  • Field: economics/econophysics
  • Formalism: agent-based model
  • References: Chakraborti and Chakrabarti 2000; Dragulescu and Yakovenko 2000; Yakovenko and Rosser 2009

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='economics/econophysics',
    tags=('wealth', 'agents', 'exchange', 'kinetic'),
    references=('Chakraborti and Chakrabarti 2000', 'Dragulescu and Yakovenko 2000', 'Yakovenko and Rosser 2009'),
    defaults={'until': 200},
    observables=lambda system: [ObservableSpec('variance', group='traders', variable='wealth', reduce='var')],
)
def kinetic_wealth_exchange(
    n_agents: int = 500,
    *,
    saving: float = 0.0,
    debt: float | None = None,
    wealth: float = 1.0,
    amount: float = 0.1,
) -> System:
    """Return a kinetic wealth exchange model with a saving propensity or a debt limit.

    Without a debt limit, agents trade random shares of their pooled wealth after saving a fraction `saving` of it,
    as in Chakraborti and Chakrabarti. With a debt limit, they pay a fixed amount in every trade and may go into debt
    down to the limit, as in Dragulescu and Yakovenko.

    Args:
        n_agents:
            The number of agents.

        saving:
            The saving propensity `lambda`, between 0 and 1, of the trades without a debt limit.

        debt:
            The debt limit of the fixed-amount trades, or `None` for trades of random shares with saving.

        wealth:
            The initial wealth of every agent, the mean wealth.

        amount:
            The amount paid in every fixed-amount trade.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `traders`, the interaction `trades`, and the variance of wealth `variance`.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            Both a saving propensity and a debt limit are given, or the saving propensity is not below 1.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import kinetic_wealth_exchange
        >>> type(kinetic_wealth_exchange(10, debt=2.0).interactions[0]).__name__
        'DebtExchangeInteraction'
    """
    if debt is not None and saving:
        error_msg = 'Give either a saving propensity or a debt limit, not both.'
        raise ValueError(error_msg)
    if not 0 <= saving < 1:
        error_msg = f'The saving propensity must lie in [0, 1), got {saving}.'
        raise ValueError(error_msg)
    trades = (
        SavingExchangeInteraction('trades', source='traders', target='traders', saving=saving)
        if debt is None
        else DebtExchangeInteraction('trades', source='traders', target='traders', debt=debt, amount=amount)
    )
    return System(
        elements=[GroupElement('traders', element=SavingTraderElement, size=n_agents, values={'wealth': wealth})],
        interactions=[trades],
    )

class SavingTraderElement(Element):
    """Agent of the kinetic wealth exchange models, whose wealth changes only in pairwise trades.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        wealth:
            The initial wealth, negative down to the debt limit.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import SavingTraderElement
        >>> group = GroupElement('traders', element=SavingTraderElement, size=10, values={'wealth': 2.0})
        >>> group.label, group.element.__name__, group.size
        ('traders', 'SavingTraderElement', 10)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        wealth: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.wealth = wealth

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[SavingTraderView]:
        """Return the view of a trader, with its wealth."""
        return SavingTraderView

class SavingExchangeInteraction(TransferInteraction):
    """Random pairwise trades of Chakraborti and Chakrabarti, where every agent saves a fraction of its wealth.

    A trade between agents `i` and `j` keeps total wealth and gives `w_i' = lambda w_i + eps (1 - lambda) (w_i + w_j)`
    and `w_j' = lambda w_j + (1 - eps) (1 - lambda) (w_i + w_j)` with `eps` uniform on `[0, 1]`, so `i` transfers
    `(1 - lambda) (w_i - eps (w_i + w_j))` to `j`, an amount of either sign. Every step, every agent trades once with
    another agent drawn at random, in random order. Without saving the stationary wealth distribution is exponential,
    and with saving propensity `lambda` it is close to a Gamma distribution of shape `n = 1 + 3 lambda / (1 - lambda)`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        source:
            The path of the group of traders.

        target:
            The path of the group of traders, the source again.

        saving:
            The saving propensity `lambda`, the fraction of its wealth that an agent keeps out of a trade.

        phase:
            The phase the trades run in, or `None` for the default phase.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import SavingExchangeInteraction
        >>> SavingExchangeInteraction('trades', source='traders', target='traders').check().saving
        0.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        source: str,
        target: str,
        saving: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
        phase: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            source=source,
            target=target,
            state='wealth',
            amount=self._get_amount,
            pairing='random',
            form='agent',
            phase=phase,
        )
        self.saving = saving

    def _get_amount(self, first: SavingTraderView, second: SavingTraderView, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> float:
        """Return the wealth the first trader transfers to the second, of either sign."""
        saving = model.parameter('saving')
        share = float(model.rng.random())
        return (1 - saving) * (first.wealth - share * (first.wealth + second.wealth))

docs.title: Kinetic wealth and welfare dynamics
docs.text:
The kinetic theory of wealth classes, with a welfare policy when the tax is positive.

  • Name: kinetic_wealth_welfare
  • Field: economics/econophysics
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Bellomo et al. 2017; Dolfin and Lachowicz 2014; Bertotti and Delitala 2008

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='economics/econophysics',
    tags=('wealth', 'kinetic', 'distribution', 'welfare'),
    references=WELFARE_REFERENCES,
    defaults={'until': 100, 'dt': 1.0},
    observables=lambda system: wealth_observables(_classes_of(system)),
)
def kinetic_wealth_welfare(
    classes: int = 9,
    *,
    cooperation: float = 0.2,
    competition: float = 0.3,
    eta: float = 1.0,
    tax: float = 0.0,
) -> System:
    """Return the kinetic theory of wealth classes, with a welfare policy when the tax is positive.

    The population is a distribution over wealth classes, a site group on a lattice of the classes. Encounters
    between classes move particles one class up or down, with cooperation narrowing the gaps and competition widening
    them, so the total density stays constant. When competition wins, wealth polarises toward the poorest and the
    richest classes, and the Gini coefficient grows. A welfare policy is an encounter with a group of fixed density,
    which moves the richest third of the classes down and the poorest third up and lowers the stationary Gini
    coefficient.

    Args:
        classes:
            The number of wealth classes.

        cooperation:
            The probability of the move that narrows the gap between the classes of an encounter.

        competition:
            The probability of the move that widens it.

        eta:
            The encounter rate.

        tax:
            The rate of the welfare policy, 0 for none.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the distribution `wealth`, the encounters `exchange`, and with a tax the group `state` and
            the policy `welfare`. Its standard observables are the density, the mean wealth, and the Gini coefficient
            of `wealth`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import kinetic_wealth_welfare
        >>> [item.label for item in kinetic_wealth_welfare(tax=0.2).interactions]
        ['exchange', 'welfare']
    """
    initial = np.exp(-((wealth_classes(classes) - 0.5) ** 2) / 0.05)
    components: list[GroupElement] = [
        GroupElement(
            'wealth',
            element=DensityElement,
            size=classes,
            on='sites',
            values={'f': initial / initial.sum()},
        ),
    ]
    interactions: list[BaseInteraction] = [
        WealthExchangeInteraction(
            'exchange',
            candidate='wealth',
            field='wealth',
            classes=classes,
            eta=eta,
            cooperation=cooperation,
            competition=competition,
        ),
    ]
    if tax > 0:
        components.append(GroupElement('state', element=DensityElement, size=1, values={'f': 1.0}))
        interactions.append(
            WelfarePolicyInteraction('welfare', candidate='wealth', field='state', classes=classes, tax=tax),
        )
    return System(
        elements=components,
        interactions=interactions,
        space=LatticeSpace(classes, boundary='fixed'),
        time=ContinuousTime(),
    )

class DensityElement(Element):
    """Value of a density at one class, a member of a distribution over the classes.

    A distribution is a group of densities on the sites of a lattice of classes, one member per class, and encounter,
    proliferation, and destruction laws change it. A density has no laws of its own.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the density, unique among the parts of its system.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        f:
            The initial density, a nonnegative number.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the element when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import DensityElement, GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.spaces import LatticeSpace
        >>> classes = LatticeSpace(5, boundary='fixed')
        >>> group = GroupElement('distribution', element=DensityElement, space=classes, on='sites', values={'f': 0.2})
        >>> group.check().prepare().size_
        5
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        f: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.f = f

class WealthExchangeInteraction(EncounterInteraction):
    """Conservative encounters between wealth classes, with cooperation and competition.

    A candidate of class `h` meets a field particle of class `k` at the rate `eta` and moves by the transition table
    of `exchange_table`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        candidate:
            The path of the distribution over wealth classes whose particles move.

        field:
            The path of the distribution over wealth classes they meet, the candidate again.

        classes:
            The number of wealth classes.

        eta:
            The encounter rate.

        cooperation:
            The probability of the move that narrows the gap between the classes of an encounter.

        competition:
            The probability of the move that widens it.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import WealthExchangeInteraction
        >>> WealthExchangeInteraction('exchange', candidate='wealth', field='wealth').check().competition
        0.3
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        candidate: str,
        field: str,
        classes: Annotated[int, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 9,
        eta: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        cooperation: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.2,
        competition: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.3,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, candidate=candidate, field=field, rate=self._get_rate, kernel=self._get_kernel)
        self.classes = classes
        self.eta = eta
        self.cooperation = cooperation
        self.competition = competition

    def _get_rate(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the encounter rate `eta`."""
        return s.eta

    def _get_kernel(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> npt.NDArray[np.object_]:
        """Return the transition table of the encounters, with the cooperation and competition parameters."""
        return exchange_table(int(self.classes), s.cooperation, s.competition)

docs.title: Kolkata Paise Restaurant
docs.text:
The Kolkata Paise Restaurant problem, where diners spread over restaurants that serve one meal each.

  • Name: kolkata_restaurant
  • Field: economics/econophysics
  • Formalism: agent-based model
  • References: Chakrabarti et al. 2009; Ghosh et al. 2010; Carmichael and Hadzikadic 2019 ch. 9

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='economics/econophysics',
    tags=('kolkata paise restaurant', 'agents', 'resource allocation', 'minority game'),
    references=('Chakrabarti et al. 2009', 'Ghosh et al. 2010', 'Carmichael and Hadzikadic 2019 ch. 9'),
    defaults={'until': 100},
)
def kolkata_restaurant(
    n_agents: int = 100,
    *,
    n_restaurants: int | None = None,
    strategy: str = 'random',
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return the Kolkata Paise Restaurant problem, where diners spread over restaurants that serve one meal each.

    With random choice the expected utilization of `N` restaurants by `N` diners is `1 - 1/e`, about 0.632, and with
    the stochastic crowd avoiding strategy it settles near 0.8.

    Args:
        n_agents:
            The number of diners.

        n_restaurants:
            The number of restaurants, or `None` for as many as diners.

        strategy:
            `'random'` or `'crowd_avoiding'`.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the first choices.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `diners`, the choice `choice` of a restaurant every evening, uniform or by crowd
            avoidance, and the interaction `restaurants`, which reports the fraction of
            restaurants that serve a meal `restaurants.utilization`.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            The strategy is unknown.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import kolkata_restaurant
        >>> type(kolkata_restaurant(10, strategy='crowd_avoiding').interactions[0]).__name__
        'CrowdAvoidanceInteraction'
    """
    if strategy not in STRATEGIES:
        error_msg = f'Unknown strategy {strategy!r}. Use one of {STRATEGIES}.'
        raise ValueError(error_msg)
    n_restaurants = n_agents if n_restaurants is None else n_restaurants
    options = [float(restaurant) for restaurant in range(n_restaurants)]
    choices = np.random.default_rng(random_state).integers(n_restaurants, size=n_agents).astype(float)
    diners = GroupElement('diners', element=DinerElement, size=n_agents, values={'restaurant': choices})
    choice = (
        CrowdAvoidanceInteraction('choice', target='diners', options=options)
        if strategy == 'crowd_avoiding'
        else ChoiceInteraction(
            'choice',
            target='diners',
            state='restaurant',
            options=options,
            utility=lambda agent, model, option: 0.0,
            intensity=0.0,
            form='agent',
        )
    )
    restaurants = RestaurantsInteraction('restaurants', target='diners', n_restaurants=n_restaurants)
    return System(elements=[diners], interactions=[choice, restaurants])

class DinerElement(Element):
    """Diner of the Kolkata Paise Restaurant problem, who goes to one restaurant every evening.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        restaurant:
            The restaurant chosen last, from 0 to the number of restaurants minus one.

        crowd:
            The number of diners at that restaurant, 0 before the first evening.

        served:
            Whether the diner got a meal, 1 or 0.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import DinerElement
        >>> GroupElement('diners', element=DinerElement, size=10).size
        10
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        restaurant: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=NN)] = 0,
        crowd: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=NN)] = 0,
        served: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=FiniteEnumeratedSet([0, 1]))] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.restaurant = restaurant
        self.crowd = crowd
        self.served = served

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[DinerView]:
        """Return the view of the agents of the element."""
        return DinerView

class ChoiceInteraction(Interaction):
    """Choice of every member of a group among options, drawn every step from the utilities of the options by a rule.

    The rule `'logit'`, which is the heat-bath rule, draws option `k` of utility `u_k` with probability
    `exp(beta u_k) / sum_j exp(beta u_j)`, where `beta` is the intensity of choice. The rules `'metropolis'` and
    `'fermi'` propose one of the other options uniformly, or with the proposal `'all'` one of all the options
    including the current one, and accept it with probability `min(1, exp(beta (u_new - u_old)))` or
    `1 / (1 + exp(-beta (u_new - u_old)))`, so the rule `'fermi'` with the proposal `'all'` is the heat-bath rule of a
    uniform proposal. The rule `'best'` draws uniformly among the options of largest utility under the ties
    `'random'`, and takes the first of them under `'first'`. Every step, each member revises its choice with probability
    `activity` and keeps it otherwise.

    In the `'symbolic'` form, `utility(namespace, option)` returns the utility as a symbolic expression, where
    `namespace.target` holds the states and parameters of the group, and every member draws at once. In the `'agent'`
    form, the group is an agent group and `utility(agent, model, option)` returns the utility as a number, so it can
    read the agent, its neighbours, and the history and storage of the model view. Its members draw at once, from the
    choices of the last step, under the `'synchronous'` schedule, one after the other in their order or in a new random
    order, each seeing the choices made before it, under the `'sequential'` or `'random-sequential'` schedule, and each
    in its own activation under the `'member'` schedule, together with the rules of its element and the other member
    interactions, in the order the system lists them. An option of utility `-inf` is never drawn in the agent form.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose members choose.

        state:
            The name of the discrete state of the members that holds the chosen option.

        options:
            The values the state can take, at least two.

        utility:
            The function `utility(namespace, option)` in the symbolic form, or `utility(agent, model, option)` in the
            agent form, that returns the utility of an option.

        rule:
            The rule of the draw, `'logit'`, `'metropolis'`, `'fermi'`, or `'best'`.

        intensity:
            The intensity of choice `beta`, zero for uniform choice.

        schedule:
            The order in which the members revise, `'synchronous'` or, in the agent form, `'sequential'`,
            `'random-sequential'`, or `'member'`.

        activity:
            The probability that a member revises its choice in a step.

        form:
            `'symbolic'` for update laws of the states of a group, or `'agent'` for a rule over an agent group.

        phase:
            The phase of the step the agent form runs in, or `None` for the default phase.

        proposal:
            The options the rules `'metropolis'` and `'fermi'` propose from, `'others'` for the options other than the
            current one, or `'all'` for every option.

        ties:
            The option the rule `'best'` takes among options of equal largest utility, `'random'` for one drawn
            uniformly or `'first'` for the first in the order of the options.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The rule, the schedule, the form, the proposal, or the ties are unknown, the schedule is not synchronous in
            the symbolic form, there are fewer than two options, or the utility is not callable.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import ChoiceInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import mean
        >>> choice = ChoiceInteraction(
        ...     'choice', target='spins', state='spin', options=(-1, 1), utility=lambda s, o: o * mean(s.target.spin)
        ... )
        >>> choice.check().rule
        'logit'
        >>> agents = ChoiceInteraction(
        ...     'choice', target='traders', state='plan', options=(0, 1), utility=lambda a, m, o: o, form='agent'
        ... )
        >>> type(agents.check().prepare().run(SimpleNamespace()).laws_[0]).__name__
        'RuleLaw'
        >>> ChoiceInteraction(
        ...     'heat-bath', target='spins', state='spin', options=(-1, 0, 1), utility=lambda s, o: o, rule='fermi',
        ...     proposal='all'
        ... ).check().proposal
        'all'
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str,
        options: Sequence[float],
        utility: Callable[..., float | Expression],
        rule: str = 'logit',
        intensity: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        schedule: str = 'synchronous',
        activity: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed(0, 1))] = 1.0,
        form: str = 'symbolic',
        phase: str | None = None,
        proposal: str = 'others',
        ties: str = 'random',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.state = state
        self.options = options
        self.utility = utility
        self.rule = rule
        self.intensity = intensity
        self.schedule = schedule
        self.activity = activity
        self.form = form
        self.phase = phase
        self.proposal = proposal
        self.ties = ties

    def _check_variants(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown variant, or a symbolic choice that is not synchronous."""
        self._check_variant('rule', self.rule, RULES, (BaseSpec,))
        for name, value, variants in (
            ('schedule', self.schedule, SCHEDULES),
            ('form', self.form, FORMS),
            ('proposal', self.proposal, PROPOSALS),
            ('ties', self.ties, TIES),
        ):
            if value not in variants:
                error_msg = f'Unknown {name} {value!r} of {self.label!r}. Use one of {variants}.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.form == 'symbolic' and self.schedule != 'synchronous':
            error_msg = (
                f'{self.label!r} has the schedule {self.schedule!r}, which only the agent form runs. Use '
                "form='agent' or schedule='synchronous'."
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown variant, fewer than two options, or a utility that cannot be called.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, the rule, the schedule, the form, the proposal, or the ties are unknown, the
                schedule is not synchronous in the symbolic form, there are fewer than two options, or the utility is
                not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        self._check_variants()
        if len(self.options) < MIN_OPTIONS:
            error_msg = f'{self.label!r} chooses among {list(self.options)}. Give at least {MIN_OPTIONS} options.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not callable(self.utility):
            error_msg = f'The utility of {self.label!r} must be callable, but it is {self.utility!r}.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _select(self, index: Expression, values: Sequence[Expression]) -> Expression:
        """Return the value at a symbolic index."""
        return sum((where(index == position, value, 0) for position, value in enumerate(values)), SR(0))

    def _draw_softmax(self, state: Expression, utilities: Sequence[Expression], intensity: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return the option drawn with probabilities proportional to `exp(beta u_k)`."""
        index = categorical(f'{state}_option', [exp(intensity * utility) for utility in utilities])
        return self._select(index, [SR(option) for option in self.options])

    def _draw_best(self, state: Expression, utilities: Sequence[Expression]) -> Expression:
        """Return an option drawn uniformly among the options of largest utility."""
        largest = utilities[0]
        for utility in utilities[1:]:
            largest = where(utility > largest, utility, largest)
        weights = [where(utility >= largest, 1, 0) for utility in utilities]
        if self.ties == 'first':
            weights = [
                weight * where(sum(weights[:position], SR(0)) > 0, 0, 1) for position, weight in enumerate(weights)
            ]
        index = categorical(f'{state}_best', weights)
        return self._select(index, [SR(option) for option in self.options])

    def _draw_proposal(self, state: Expression, utilities: Sequence[Expression], intensity: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return a uniform proposal of an option, accepted by the Metropolis or the Fermi probability."""
        weights = [SR(1) if self.proposal == 'all' else where(state == option, 0, 1) for option in self.options]
        index = categorical(f'{state}_proposal', weights)
        proposal = self._select(index, [SR(option) for option in self.options])
        gain = self._select(index, utilities) - sum(
            (where(state == option, utility, 0) for option, utility in zip(self.options, utilities, strict=True)),
            SR(0),
        )
        if self.rule == 'metropolis':
            acceptance = where(gain >= 0, 1, exp(intensity * gain))
        else:
            acceptance = 1 / (1 + exp(-intensity * gain))
        return where(uniform(f'{state}_acceptance') < acceptance, proposal, state)

    def _draw_symbolic(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the option a member draws, as a symbolic expression of the namespace."""
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        utilities = [SR(self.utility(namespace, option)) for option in self.options]
        if self.rule == 'logit':
            return self._draw_softmax(state, utilities, self._get_parameter_symbol('intensity', namespace))
        if self.rule == 'best':
            return self._draw_best(state, utilities)
        if self.rule in ('metropolis', 'fermi'):
            return self._draw_proposal(state, utilities, self._get_parameter_symbol('intensity', namespace))
        raise self._get_variant_error(self.rule, 'rule', '_draw_symbolic')

    def _get_utilities(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return the utility of every option for an agent."""
        return np.array([float(self.utility(agent, model, option)) for option in self.options])

    def _draw_agent_proposal(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol, intensity: float) -> float:
        """Return a uniform proposal of an option of an agent if accepted, or its current option."""
        current = float(getattr(agent, self.state))
        others = [option for option in self.options if self.proposal == 'all' or option != current]
        proposal = float(others[int(model.rng.integers(len(others)))])
        before = float(self.utility(agent, model, current)) if current in self.options else 0.0
        gain = float(self.utility(agent, model, proposal)) - before
        if self.rule == 'metropolis':
            acceptance = 1.0 if gain >= 0 else math.exp(intensity * gain)
        else:
            acceptance = float(expit(intensity * gain))
        return proposal if model.rng.random() < acceptance else current

    def _draw_agent(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol, intensity: float) -> float:
        """Return the option an agent draws by the rule."""
        if self.rule in ('metropolis', 'fermi'):
            return self._draw_agent_proposal(agent, model, intensity)
        utilities = self._get_utilities(agent, model)
        if self.rule == 'best':
            return float(self.options[self._pick_best(utilities, self.ties, model)])
        if self.rule != 'logit':
            raise self._get_variant_error(self.rule, 'rule', '_draw_agent')
        scaled = np.where(np.isneginf(utilities), -np.inf, intensity * utilities)
        probabilities = softmax(scaled)
        return float(self.options[int(model.rng.choice(len(self.options), p=probabilities))])

    def _is_active(self, model: ModelViewProtocol, activity: float) -> bool:
        """Return whether a member revises its choice in this step."""
        return activity >= 1 or bool(model.rng.random() < activity)

    def _get_choice(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> float | None:
        """Return the option an agent draws if it revises in this step, or `None` to keep its own."""
        if not self._is_active(model, self._get_parameter_value('activity', model)):
            return None
        return self._draw_agent(agent, model, self._get_parameter_value('intensity', model))

    def _set_choice(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, option: float | None) -> None:
        """Set the state of an agent to the option it draws, if any."""
        if option is not None:
            setattr(agent, self.state, option)

    def _choose_member(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Set the state of one agent to the option it draws if it revises, in its own activation."""
        if agent.alive:
            self._set_choice(agent, self._get_choice(agent, model))

    def choose(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Set the state of every agent that revises in this step to the option it draws, by the schedule.

        Args:
            model:
                The model view of the interaction.
        """
        self._update_agents(model, self.schedule, self._get_choice, self._set_choice)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the update of the state of every member that revises, or the rule of the agent form.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with `namespace.target`, `namespace.intensity`, and
                `namespace.activity`.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The update law of the state, or the rule that runs the choice of the agents.
        """
        if self.form == 'agent' and self.schedule == 'member':
            return [RuleLaw(self._choose_member, phase=self.phase, members=self._get_role('target'))]
        if self.form == 'agent':
            return [RuleLaw(self.choose, phase=self.phase)]
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        revised = where(
            uniform(f'{state}_activity') < self._get_parameter_symbol('activity', namespace),
            self._draw_symbolic(namespace),
            state,
        )
        return [UpdateLaw(state, revised)]

class RestaurantsInteraction(GroupingInteraction):
    """Restaurants that each serve one meal every evening, to one of the diners who come chosen at random.

    The diners are grouped by their restaurant. Every diner learns the crowd at its restaurant, and the first of the
    group in a random order is served. The interaction reports the fraction of restaurants that serve a meal.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        target:
            The path of the group of diners.

        n_restaurants:
            The number of restaurants.

        by:
            The state of the diners that holds their restaurant.

        phase:
            The phase the restaurants serve in, or `None` for the default phase.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import RestaurantsInteraction
        >>> RestaurantsInteraction('restaurants', target='diners', n_restaurants=5).check().groups
        'state'
    """

    reports: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ('utilization',)

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: str,
        n_restaurants: int = 100,
        by: str = 'restaurant',
        phase: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, groups='state', by=by, phase=phase)
        self.n_restaurants = n_restaurants

    def act_on(self, members: list[AgentViewProtocol], model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Tell every diner of a restaurant its crowd and serve the first diner.

        Args:
            members:
                The diners at one restaurant, in random order.

            model:
                The model view of the restaurants.
        """
        diners = [member for member in members if isinstance(member, DinerView)]
        for position, member in enumerate(diners):
            member.crowd = float(len(diners))
            member.served = float(position == 0)

    def report(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Report the fraction of restaurants with at least one diner.

        Args:
            model:
                The model view of the restaurants.
        """
        visited = {float(getattr(agent, str(self.by))) for agent in model.agents('target')}
        model.report('utilization', len(visited) / self.n_restaurants)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rule that serves the diners and the rule that reports the utilization.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The serving and the reporting rules.
        """
        return [*super()._get_laws(namespace), RuleLaw(self.report, phase=self.phase)]

The minority game of an odd number of agents with two random strategies each.

  • Name: minority_game
  • Field: economics/econophysics
  • Formalism: agent-based model
  • References: Challet and Zhang 1997; Yakovenko and Rosser 2009; Carmichael and Hadzikadic 2019 ch. 9

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='economics/econophysics',
    tags=('minority game', 'agents', 'inductive reasoning', 'evolution'),
    references=('Challet and Zhang 1997', 'Yakovenko and Rosser 2009', 'Carmichael and Hadzikadic 2019 ch. 9'),
    defaults={'until': 500},
)
def minority_game(
    n_agents: int = 101,
    *,
    memory: int = 3,
    evolutionary: bool = False,
    period: int = 50,
    fraction: float = 0.1,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return the minority game of an odd number of agents with two random strategies each.

    Args:
        n_agents:
            The number of agents, odd so that there is always a minority.

        memory:
            The memory `m` of the strategies, so `alpha = 2^m / N`.

        evolutionary:
            Whether every `period` rounds the poorest agents take new random strategies.

        period:
            The number of rounds between two evolutions of the evolutionary version.

        fraction:
            The fraction of poorest agents that take new strategies at an evolution.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the strategies.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `players`, the choice `choice` of the strategy of higher virtual score, the
            interaction `game`, which reports the attendance `game.attendance`, the cumulative reinforcement
            `scoring` of the virtual scores, and in the evolutionary version the truncation `evolution`, which gives
            the poorest agents new random strategies and no wealth every `period` rounds.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            The number of agents is even.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.econophysics import minority_game
        >>> minority_game(11, memory=2).interactions[1].memory
        2
    """
    if n_agents % 2 == 0:
        error_msg = f'The minority game needs an odd number of agents, got {n_agents}.'
        raise ValueError(error_msg)
    codes = np.random.default_rng(random_state).integers(MAX_SEED, size=(2, n_agents)).astype(float)
    players = GroupElement(
        'players',
        element=MinorityPlayerElement,
        size=n_agents,
        values={'first': codes[0], 'second': codes[1]},
    )
    choice = ChoiceInteraction(
        'choice',
        target='players',
        state='strategy',
        options=(0.0, 1.0),
        utility=lambda agent, model, option: agent.second_score if option else agent.first_score,
        rule='best',
        form='agent',
        phase='choose',
    )
    game = MinorityGameInteraction('game', players='players', memory=memory, phase='play')
    scoring = ReinforcementInteraction(
        'scoring',
        target='players',
        scores=('first_score', 'second_score'),
        payoff=game.payoff,
        rule='cumulative',
        form='agent',
        phase='score',
    )
    evolution = EvolutionInteraction(
        'evolution',
        target='players',
        strategy=('first', 'second'),
        fitness='wealth',
        replacement='truncation',
        fraction=fraction,
        mutation=1.0,
        change='any',
        alphabet=MAX_SEED,
        period=period,
        reset={'first_score': 0.0, 'second_score': 0.0, 'wealth': 0.0},
        phase='score',
    )
    return System(
        elements=[players],
        interactions=[choice, game, scoring, *([evolution] if evolutionary else [])],
        time=DiscreteTime(
            schedule=PhasesScheduleSpec([PhaseSpec('choose'), PhaseSpec('play'), PhaseSpec('score')]),
        ),
    )
