class HarvestedResourceElement(Element):
    """Logistic resource whose harvest effort is a bounded control input, after Clark.

    The stock follows `x' = r x (1 - x / K) - q E x` under the effort `E` between 0 and its largest value. The
    harvest earns the price `p` per unit of catch and costs `c` per unit of effort, and the owner maximises the
    discounted profit `∫ exp(-delta t) (p q x - c) E dt`. The profit is linear in the effort, so the optimal effort is
    bang-bang or singular: it takes a bound until the stock reaches the level where the yield net of costs earns the
    discount rate, holds the stock there, and harvests at the largest effort at the end of the horizon.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the resource.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x:
            The initial stock.

        effort:
            The harvest effort, the control input.

        r:
            The intrinsic growth rate.

        K:
            The carrying capacity.

        q:
            The catchability.

        p:
            The price per unit of catch.

        c:
            The cost per unit of effort.

        delta:
            The discount rate.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import HarvestedResourceElement
        >>> HarvestedResourceElement('resource', x=0.5).x
        0.5
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        effort: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(adaptive=True, bounds=(0.0, MAX_EFFORT))] = 0.0,
        r: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        q: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        p: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        c: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.2,
        delta: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.1,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.effort = effort
        self.r = r
        self.K = K
        self.q = q
        self.p = p
        self.c = c
        self.delta = delta

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the regrowth less the catch.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return [RateLaw(s.x, s.r * s.x * (1 - s.x / s.K) - s.q * s.effort * s.x)]

docs.title: Tragedy of the meadow commons
docs.text:
Herders whose cows graze a shared meadow, each adding cows while a cow pays, until the grass collapses.

  • Name: tragedy_of_the_commons
  • Field: economics/resources
  • Formalism: agent-based model
  • References: Hamill and Gilbert 2016 sec. 10.2; Hardin 1968

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='economics/resources',
    tags=('commons', 'agents', 'overgrazing', 'regulation', 'grid'),
    references=('Hamill and Gilbert 2016 sec. 10.2', 'Hardin 1968'),
    defaults={'until': 100},
    observables=_commons_observables,
)
def tragedy_of_the_commons(
    n_herders: int = 20,
    *,
    width: int = 20,
    height: int = 20,
    cows: int = 1,
    quota: float | None = None,
    regrowth: float = 0.2,
    capacity: float = 2.0,
    upkeep: float = 0.3,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return herders whose cows graze a shared meadow, each adding cows while a cow pays, until the grass collapses.

    Every step every cow moves to the richest pasture it can reach, eats, and earns its herder milk, and the grass
    grows back logistically. Every herder adds a cow whenever a cow earned more than its upkeep, since the gain of a
    cow goes to its herder while the cost of the grass it eats falls on all. With more herders than the meadow
    carries, the herd grows past what the grass sustains, the grass collapses below a tenth of its capacity, and the
    cows starve, so the herd shrinks after it. A regulator with an adaptive quota of cows per herder, lowered when the
    grass runs short and raised when it recovers, keeps the meadow from collapse (Hamill and Gilbert 2016 sec. 10.2).

    Args:
        n_herders:
            The number of herders.

        width:
            The number of columns of the meadow.

        height:
            The number of rows of the meadow.

        cows:
            The initial number of cows of every herder.

        quota:
            The initial quota of cows per herder of a regulator that adapts it, or `None` for no regulation.

        regrowth:
            The logistic growth rate of the grass.

        capacity:
            The most grass a cell holds.

        upkeep:
            The cost of keeping a cow for a step.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the cells of the cows.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the groups `meadow`, `cows`, and `herders`, whose adaptive parameter `quota` the regulator
            `regulator` changes, and the grazing `grazing`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import tragedy_of_the_commons
        >>> [group.size for group in tragedy_of_the_commons(4, width=5, height=5).elements]
        [25, 4, 4]
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state)
    cells = [(x, y) for x in range(width) for y in range(height)]
    meadow = GroupElement(
        'meadow',
        element=PastureElement,
        size=len(cells),
        values={'grass': capacity, 'capacity': capacity, 'regrowth': regrowth},
        location=cells,
    )
    herders = GroupElement(
        'herders',
        element=HerderElement,
        size=n_herders,
        values={
            'upkeep': upkeep,
            'quota': UNLIMITED if quota is None else quota,
        },
        location=[cells[0]] * n_herders,
    )
    n_cows = n_herders * cows
    herd = GroupElement(
        'cows',
        element=CowElement,
        size=n_cows,
        values={'owner': np.repeat(np.arange(n_herders, dtype=float), cows)},
        variable=True,
        location=[cells[index] for index in rng.integers(len(cells), size=n_cows)],
    )
    regulator = QuotaRegulatorInteraction('regulator', phase='herding', regulated=float(quota is not None))
    grazing = GrazingInteraction(
        'grazing',
        requesters='cows',
        providers='meadow',
        rule=PartnerSpec('local', 'score', score=GrazingInteraction.score, clearing='provider'),
        herders='herders',
    )
    return System(
        elements=[meadow, herd, herders],
        interactions=[grazing, *_get_investment(), regulator],
        space=LatticeSpace((width, height), boundary='periodic', neighborhood='moore'),
        time=DiscreteTime(
            schedule=PhasesScheduleSpec([PhaseSpec('grazing'), PhaseSpec('growth'), PhaseSpec('herding')]),
        ),
    )

<pre><code>class PastureElement(Element):
    """Cell of the meadow whose grass grows back logistically, from a seed bank when it is grazed bare.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        grass:
            The grass on the cell.

        capacity:
            The most grass the cell holds.

        regrowth:
            The logistic growth rate of the grass.

        seed:
            The share of the capacity that grows back as if it stood on a bare cell.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import PastureElement
        >>> GroupElement('meadow', element=PastureElement, size=4, values={'capacity': 2.0}).size
        4
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = VisualSpec('agents', {'color_by': 'grass', 'color_range': (0.0, 2.0)}),
        *,
        grass: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 2.0,
        capacity: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 2.0,
        regrowth: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.2,
        seed: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.05,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.grass = grass
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.regrowth = regrowth
        self.seed = seed

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[PastureView]:
        """Return the view of the agents of the element."""
        return PastureView

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the regrowth rule of the phase of growth.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return [RuleLaw(self.grow, phase='growth')]

    def grow(self, agent: PastureView, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Grow the grass logistically up to the capacity.

        Args:
            agent:
                The pasture.

            model:
                The model.
        """
        stand = max(agent.grass, model.parameter('seed') * agent.capacity)
        growth = model.parameter('regrowth') * stand * (1 - stand / agent.capacity)
        agent.grass = min(agent.capacity, agent.grass + growth)

class CowElement(Element):
    """Cow of a herder that gains the energy of the grass it eats, burns its metabolism, and starves without food.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        owner:
            The id of the herder that owns the cow, given initially as its position in the group `herders`.

        energy:
            The energy of the cow.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import CowElement
        >>> GroupElement('cows', element=CowElement, size=3, values={'energy': 4.0}).size
        3
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = VisualSpec('agents', {'color_by': 'energy'}),
        *,
        owner: Annotated[float, StateSpec(reference='herders')] = -1.0,
        energy: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 4.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.owner = owner
        self.energy = energy

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[CowView]:
        """Return the view of the agents of the element."""
        return CowView

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return no laws, since the grazing moves the cows and their energy.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return []

class HerderElement(Element):
    """Herder who adds a cow whenever a cow earned more than its upkeep, and sells one when the herd exceeds its quota.

    The life cycle `investment` of the model buys a cow, at a random cell, or sells the first cow the herder owns,
    and two maps clear the income and the herd the grazing tallies, all member interactions in the phase of herding.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        income:
            The milk income of the herder in the last step.

        herd:
            The number of cows of the herder in the last step.

        upkeep:
            The cost of keeping a cow for a step.

        newborn:
            The energy of a new cow.

        quota:
            The largest herd of a herder, an adaptive parameter that a regulator may change.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import HerderElement
        >>> GroupElement('herders', element=HerderElement, size=5).size
        5
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        income: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
        herd: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
        upkeep: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.3,
        newborn: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 4.0,
        quota: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo), adaptive=True)] = UNLIMITED,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.income = income
        self.herd = herd
        self.upkeep = upkeep
        self.newborn = newborn
        self.quota = quota

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[HerderView]:
        """Return the view of the agents of the element."""
        return HerderView

class GrazingInteraction(MatchingInteraction[ModelView]):
    """Grazing of the meadow, a matching of the cows with the pastures, after which every cow eats and burns energy.

    The rule of the matching pairs the cows with the pastures, such as
    `PartnerSpec('local', 'score', score=GrazingInteraction.score, clearing='provider')`, which pairs every cow, in
    random order, with the free pasture of most grass in its cell or the cells around it, ties broken at random. A
    pasture takes one cow, its default quantity of one unit. Every matched cow moves to its pasture and eats up to its
    appetite as a transfer of grass to its energy, and its herder earns milk for what it ate. Then every cow burns
    its metabolism and counts in the herd of its herder, and a cow whose energy runs out dies.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the grazing.

        requesters:
            The path of the group of cows.

        providers:
            The path of the group of pastures.

        rule:
            The spec of the algorithm that pairs the cows with the pastures.

        phase:
            The phase the grazing runs in.

        herders:
            The path of the group of herders.

        appetite:
            The most grass a cow eats in a step.

        metabolism:
            The energy a cow burns in a step.

        milk:
            The income of a herder per unit of grass its cows eat.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import GrazingInteraction
        >>> GrazingInteraction('grazing', requesters='cows', providers='meadow', herders='herders').appetite
        1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        requesters: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        providers: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        rule: MatchingRule = RandomSearchSpec(),
        phase: str | None = 'grazing',
        herders: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        appetite: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        metabolism: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
        milk: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, requesters=requesters, providers=providers, rule=rule, phase=phase)
        self.herders = herders
        self.appetite = appetite
        self.metabolism = metabolism
        self.milk = milk

    @staticmethod
    def score(cow: object, pasture: object) -> float:
        """Return the score of a pasture for a cow, the grass on the pasture.

        Args:
            cow:
                The agent view of the cow.

            pasture:
                The agent view of the pasture.

        Returns:
            score:
                The grass on the pasture, or minus infinity for an agent that is not a pasture.
        """
        del cow
        return float(pasture.grass) if isinstance(pasture, PastureView) else -np.inf

    @staticmethod
    def _get_herder(cow: CowView) -> HerderView:
        """Return the herder that owns a cow, which its reference state `owner` names."""
        herder = cow.referenced('owner')
        if not isinstance(herder, HerderView):
            error_msg = f'Cow {cow.id} names no herder as its owner.'
            raise SimulationError(error_msg)
        return herder

    def _settle(self, match: MatchSpec, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Move the cow of a match to its pasture, feed it, and pay its herder for what it ate.

        Args:
            match:
                The match of a cow with a pasture.

            model:
                The model view of the grazing.
        """
        cow, pasture = match.requester, match.provider
        if not isinstance(cow, CowView) or not isinstance(pasture, PastureView):
            return
        cow.move_to(pasture.location)
        eaten = min(pasture.grass, model.parameter('appetite'))
        transfer(pasture, cow, eaten, 'grass', 'energy')
        self._get_herder(cow).income += model.parameter('milk') * eaten

    def match(self, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Pair and feed the cows, then let every cow burn its metabolism, count it in its herd, and starve.

        Args:
            model:
                The model view of the grazing.
        """
        super().match(model)
        for cow in model.agents('requesters', CowView):
            cow.energy -= model.parameter('metabolism')
            self._get_herder(cow).herd += 1
            if cow.energy < 0:
                cow.remove()

class LifeCycleInteraction(Interaction):
    """Life cycle of the agents of a group, which give birth to offspring and die, every step of discrete time.

    Every step the agents act once each, in their order under the schedule `'sequential'`, in a new random order under
    `'random-sequential'`, or each in its own activation under `'member'`, together with the rules of its element and
    the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them, without the reports of the step and without
    arrivals. An agent dies with the probability `death`, and an agent that survives gives birth with the probability
    `birth`, or as many times as a Poisson number of the mean `rate`. A probability is a number or a function of the
    agent and the model view, and a function that returns a condition gives probability one where it holds. Every birth
    creates `offspring` new agents, a number or a function of the parent and the model view, such as a Poisson draw, of
    the group `group`, or of the parent's group without one. A new agent stands in the cell of its parent, with the
    placement `'here'`, in a neighbouring cell that no agent of the group holds, with the placement `'neighbor'`, or at
    the location a function of the parent and the model view returns, where `None` means no place, and a birth without a
    place creates fewer agents.

    A new agent copies the states `inherit` of its parent and takes the values that `values(parent, model)` returns,
    such as a generation one higher or drawn states. The parent splits each state of `split` with its offspring,
    keeping the share `keep`, a number or a function of the parent and the model view such as a random cut, or else an
    equal share, and the offspring share the rest equally. Then `mutate(values, model)` returns the values of a new
    agent from those it would get, and the other states take their defaults. A parent that gave birth takes the values
    `reset`, and with `replace` it is removed, so its offspring replace it, also when the birth created none. With
    `renew` an agent that dies is renewed in place instead of removed: it keeps its identity, its place, and the states
    the new values leave out, and takes the values of an offspring of its own. With the probability `cull` an agent
    that does not die removes, after its births, one member of `group`, or of the target without a group, for which
    `kin(agent, member)` holds, the first in the order of the group under the pick `'first'`, such as one it owns, or
    a random one under `'random'`. Every
    step a Poisson number of the mean `arrival`, a number or a function of the model view, of new agents arrive without
    a parent, at the location of the placement function or else at a random place, with the values
    `values(None, model)`. The life cycle reports the `births`, `deaths`, and `arrivals` of every step. It is an agent
    rule, so the system runs in discrete time.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the variable group whose agents give birth and die.

        birth:
            The probability that an agent gives birth in a step, or `None` for no births by probability.

        death:
            The probability that an agent dies in a step, or `None` for no deaths.

        rate:
            The mean number of births of an agent in a step, a number or a function, or `None` for no births by rate.

        offspring:
            The number of new agents of a birth.

        placement:
            Where a new agent stands, `'here'`, `'neighbor'`, or a function of the parent, `None` for an arrival, and
            the model view that returns its location.

        inherit:
            The names of the states a new agent copies from its parent.

        split:
            The names of the states the parent shares with its offspring.

        mutate:
            A function of the values of a new agent and the model view that returns its values, or `None`.

        schedule:
            The order of the agents, `'sequential'`, `'random-sequential'`, or `'member'`.

        phase:
            The phase of the step the life cycle runs in, or `None` for the default phase.

        group:
            The path of the variable group the new agents join, or `None` for the group of the target.

        values:
            A function of the parent, `None` for an arrival, and the model view that returns values of a new agent by
            state name, or `None`.

        keep:
            The share of every split state the parent keeps, a number or a function, or `None` for an equal share.

        reset:
            The values a parent takes after it gives birth, by state name, or `None`.

        replace:
            Whether a parent that gives birth is removed.

        renew:
            Whether an agent that dies is renewed in place instead of removed.

        cull:
            The probability that an agent removes one member of `group`, or of the target without a group, in a
            step, or `None` for no removals.

        kin:
            A function of an agent and a member of `group` that returns whether the agent may remove the member, or
            `None` for every member.

        arrival:
            The mean number of new agents that arrive in a step without a parent, or `None` for no arrivals.

        pick:
            Which member of `group` a removal takes among those it may remove, `'first'` or `'random'`.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The placement, the schedule, or the pick is unknown, both a birth probability and a rate are given, a
            function is not callable, or the schedule `'member'` has arrivals, raised by `check`.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element, GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import LifeCycleInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.spaces import LatticeSpace
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> class CellElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, visual=None, *, size: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
        ...         super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        ...         self.size = size
        >>> cells = GroupElement('cells', element=CellElement, size=1, values={'size': 8.0}, variable=True)
        >>> division = LifeCycleInteraction('division', target='cells', birth=1.0, split=('size',))
        >>> system = System(elements=[cells], interactions=[division], space=LatticeSpace((3, 3)))
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, random_state=0).check().prepare().run(until=2).trajectory_
        >>> trajectory.agents('cells', 2).values['size'].tolist()
        [2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0]
    """

    reports: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ('births', 'deaths', 'arrivals')

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        birth: Chance | None = None,
        death: Chance | None = None,
        rate: Chance | None = None,
        offspring: Count = 1,
        placement: Placement = 'here',
        inherit: Sequence[str] = (),
        split: Sequence[str] = (),
        mutate: Mutation | None = None,
        schedule: str = 'random-sequential',
        phase: str | None = None,
        group: Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True)] = None,
        values: Values | None = None,
        keep: Chance | None = None,
        reset: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
        replace: bool = False,
        renew: bool = False,
        cull: Chance | None = None,
        kin: Kinship | None = None,
        arrival: Arrival | None = None,
        pick: str = 'first',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.birth = birth
        self.death = death
        self.rate = rate
        self.offspring = offspring
        self.placement = placement
        self.inherit = inherit
        self.split = split
        self.mutate = mutate
        self.schedule = schedule
        self.phase = phase
        self.group = group
        self.values = values
        self.keep = keep
        self.reset = reset
        self.replace = replace
        self.renew = renew
        self.cull = cull
        self.kin = kin
        self.arrival = arrival
        self.pick = pick

    def _check_variants(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown placement, schedule, or pick, or arrivals of a member schedule."""
        self._check_variant('placement', self.placement, PLACEMENTS, functions=True)
        self._check_variant('schedule', self.schedule, SCHEDULES)
        self._check_variant('pick', self.pick, PICKS)
        if self.schedule == 'member' and self.arrival is not None:
            error_msg = f'{self.label!r} runs member by member, so no agent brings arrivals. Give `arrival=None`.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check_space(self, space: BaseSpace | None) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a placement in a neighbouring cell or node in a continuous space."""
        if self.placement == 'neighbor':
            self._check_grid('placement', self.placement, space, "placement='here', or a placement function")

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown placement, a birth by both probability and rate, or a bad function.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The placement, the schedule, or the pick is unknown, both a birth probability and a rate are given,
                a value is neither a number nor a function, or the schedule `'member'` has arrivals.
        """
        super()._check()
        self._check_variants()
        if self.birth is not None and self.rate is not None:
            error_msg = f'{self.label!r} gives births by a probability and by a rate. Give one of them.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        for name in ('birth', 'death', 'rate', 'offspring', 'keep', 'cull', 'arrival'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and not callable(value) and not isinstance(value, int | float):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a number or a function.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        for name in ('mutate', 'values', 'kin'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and not callable(value):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function, or None.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    @staticmethod
    def _evaluate(value: Chance | Count, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> float:
        """Return a number, or the value of a function of an agent and the model view, as a float."""
        return float(value(agent, model) if callable(value) else value)

    def _happens(self, chance: Chance | None, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> bool:
        """Return whether an event of a probability happens to an agent in this step."""
        if chance is None:
            return False
        probability = self._evaluate(chance, agent, model)
        return probability >= 1.0 or (probability > 0.0 and model.rng.random() < probability)

    def _count_births(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> int:
        """Return the number of births of a parent in this step."""
        if self.rate is not None:
            return int(model.rng.poisson(self._evaluate(self.rate, agent, model)))
        return int(self._happens(self.birth, agent, model))

    def _get_places(
        self,
        agent: AgentViewProtocol,
        count: int,
        occupied: set[object],
        model: ModelViewProtocol,
    ) -> list[object]:
        """Return the locations of the new agents of a parent, fewer when places run out."""
        if callable(self.placement):
            places = [self.placement(agent, model) for _ in range(count)]
            return [place for place in places if place is not None]
        if self.placement == 'here':
            return [agent.location] * count
        free = [cell for cell in agent.neighbor_cells() if cell not in occupied]
        chosen = [free[int(index)] for index in model.rng.permutation(len(free))[:count]]
        occupied.update(chosen)
        return chosen

    def _get_values(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol | None, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Return the inherited and given values of a new agent of a parent, or of an arrival."""
        values: dict[str, object] = {} if agent is None else {name: getattr(agent, name) for name in self.inherit}
        if self.values is not None:
            values.update(self.values(agent, model))
        return values

    def _create(
        self,
        agent: AgentViewProtocol | None,
        place: object,
        values: dict[str, object],
        model: ModelViewProtocol,
    ) -> None:
        """Create a new agent with mutated values at a place, `None` for a random one, in the group of the cycle."""
        if self.mutate is not None:
            values = self.mutate(values, model)
        if self.group is not None:
            model.create(self._get_role('group'), place, **values)
        elif agent is not None:
            agent.create(None, place, **values)
        else:
            model.create(self._get_role('target'), place, **values)

    def _bear(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, places: list[object], model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Create the new agents of a parent at their places, with inherited, given, split, and mutated values."""
        kept = 1 / (len(places) + 1) if self.keep is None else self._evaluate(self.keep, agent, model)
        totals = {name: float(getattr(agent, name)) for name in self.split}
        for name, amount in totals.items():
            setattr(agent, name, amount * kept)
        shares = {name: (amount - amount * kept) / max(len(places), 1) for name, amount in totals.items()}
        for place in places:
            values = self._get_values(agent, model)
            values.update(shares)
            self._create(agent, place, values, model)

    def _renew(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Give an agent that dies the values of an offspring of its own, in place."""
        values = self._get_values(agent, model)
        if self.mutate is not None:
            values = self.mutate(values, model)
        for name, value in values.items():
            setattr(agent, name, value)

    def _remove_kin(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Remove the first or a random member of the group of the cycle that is kin of an agent, if there is one."""
        kin = self.kin
        group = self._get_role('target' if self.group is None else 'group')
        members = (item for item in model.agents(group) if item.alive and (kin is None or kin(agent, item)))
        if self.pick == 'random':
            candidates = list(members)
            if candidates:
                candidates[int(model.rng.integers(len(candidates)))].remove()
            return
        member = next(members, None)
        if member is not None:
            member.remove()

    def _die(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, occupied: set[object], model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Renew an agent in place, or remove it and free its cell."""
        if self.renew:
            self._renew(agent, model)
            return
        occupied.discard(agent.location_key)
        agent.remove()

    def _act(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, occupied: set[object], model: ModelViewProtocol) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Let an agent die, or give birth and remove kin, and return its numbers of new agents and deaths."""
        if self._happens(self.death, agent, model):
            self._die(agent, occupied, model)
            return 0, 1
        born, died = self._give_birth(agent, occupied, model)
        if self._happens(self.cull, agent, model):
            self._remove_kin(agent, model)
        return born, died

    def _give_birth(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, occupied: set[object], model: ModelViewProtocol) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Let an agent give birth, and return its number of new agents and whether it was replaced."""
        born = 0
        events = self._count_births(agent, model)
        if events > 0:
            births = events * int(self._evaluate(self.offspring, agent, model))
            places = self._get_places(agent, births, occupied, model) if births else []
            if places or self.split:
                self._bear(agent, places, model)
            born = len(places)
            for name, value in (self.reset or {}).items():
                setattr(agent, name, value)
            if self.replace:
                occupied.discard(agent.location_key)
                agent.remove()
                return born, 1
        return born, 0

    def _arrive(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> int:
        """Create the agents that arrive without a parent in this step, and return their number."""
        if self.arrival is None:
            return 0
        mean = self.arrival(model) if callable(self.arrival) else self.arrival
        count = int(model.rng.poisson(float(mean)))
        for _ in range(count):
            place = self.placement(None, model) if callable(self.placement) else None
            self._create(None, place, self._get_values(None, model), model)
        return count

    def _live_member(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Run the life cycle of one agent in its own activation."""
        if not agent.alive:
            return
        neighbor = self.placement == 'neighbor'
        occupied = {other.location_key for other in model.agents(self._get_role('target'))} if neighbor else set()
        self._act(agent, occupied, model)

    def _live(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Remove or renew the agents that die and create the offspring of those that give birth, by the schedule."""
        agents = model.agents(self._get_role('target'))
        occupied = {agent.location_key for agent in agents} if self.placement == 'neighbor' else set()
        births = deaths = 0
        order = model.rng.permutation(len(agents)) if self.schedule == 'random-sequential' else range(len(agents))
        for index in order:
            agent = agents[int(index)]
            if not agent.alive:
                continue
            born, died = self._act(agent, occupied, model)
            births, deaths = births + born, deaths + died
        model.report('births', births)
        model.report('deaths', deaths)
        model.report('arrivals', self._arrive(model))

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rule of the life cycle.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rule that removes and creates agents every step.
        """
        if self.schedule == 'member':
            return [RuleLaw(self._live_member, phase=self.phase, members=self._get_role('target'))]
        return [RuleLaw(self._live, phase=self.phase)]

class MapInteraction(Interaction):
    """Map of a state of discrete time, whose next value is a function, or the state plus it.

    In the mode `'replace'` the next value of the state is `f`, and in the mode `'increment'` it is the state plus `f`.
    Under the `'synchronous'` schedule every member of a bound group updates at once, from the states at the start of
    the step. Under the `'sequential'` schedule the members update one after the other, in their order, and under the
    `'random-sequential'` schedule in a new random order every step, each member reading the values the members before
    it set. Under the `'member'` schedule of the agent form, every member updates in its own activation, together with
    the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them.

    In the `'symbolic'` form, `function(namespace)` returns a symbolic expression, or a vector of them for a vector
    state, where `namespace.target` holds the states and parameters of the target, `namespace.sources` the namespaces
    of the sources, and `namespace.t` the time, and may hold draws such as `normal('noise')`. In the `'agent'` form,
    the target is an agent group and `function(agent, model)` returns the value as a number, or as an array of the
    shape of a vector state, so it can read the agent, its neighbours, and the history and storage of the model view.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose state the map sets.

        state:
            The name of the state of the target.

        function:
            The function `f(namespace)` in the symbolic form, or `f(agent, model)` in the agent form.

        sources:
            The paths of the elements, or members of groups such as `cells[0]`, that the function reads.

        mode:
            `'replace'` or `'increment'`.

        schedule:
            `'synchronous'`, `'sequential'`, `'random-sequential'`, or `'member'` for the agent form.

        form:
            `'symbolic'` for update laws of the states of the target, or `'agent'` for a rule over an agent group.

        phase:
            The phase of the step the agent form runs in, or `None` for the default phase.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The mode, the schedule, or the form is unknown, the symbolic form has the schedule `'member'`, the
            function is not callable, or the agent form returns a value that does not match the state, raised by
            `run` of the simulation.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import MapInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.spaces import DiscreteTime
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> from typing import Annotated, SupportsFloat
        >>> class ValueElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.5):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.x = x
        >>> logistic = MapInteraction(
        ...     'map', target='value', state='x', function=lambda s: 3 * s.target.x * (1 - s.target.x)
        ... )
        >>> system = System(elements=[ValueElement('value')], interactions=[logistic], time=DiscreteTime())
        >>> Simulation(system).check().prepare().run(until=2).trajectory_.values('value.x').tolist()
        [0.5, 0.75, 0.5625]
        >>> agents = MapInteraction('map', target='walkers', state='x', function=lambda a, m: a.x + 1, form='agent')
        >>> type(agents.check().prepare().run(SimpleNamespace()).laws_[0]).__name__
        'RuleLaw'
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> class WeightsElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, visual=None, *, w: Annotated[object, StateSpec(vector=True)] = 0.0):
        ...         super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        ...         self.w = w
        >>> group = GroupElement('weights', element=WeightsElement, size=1, values={'w': [1.0, 2.0]})
        >>> doubling = MapInteraction(
        ...     'double', target='weights', state='w', function=lambda a, m: [2 * x for x in a.w], form='agent'
        ... )
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(System(elements=[group], interactions=[doubling])).check().prepare().run(until=2)
        >>> trajectory.trajectory_.agents('weights', 2).values['w'].tolist()
        [[4.0, 8.0]]
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str,
        function: Callable[..., object],
        sources: Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)] = (),
        mode: str = 'replace',
        schedule: str = 'synchronous',
        form: str = 'symbolic',
        phase: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.state = state
        self.function = function
        self.sources = sources
        self.mode = mode
        self.schedule = schedule
        self.form = form
        self.phase = phase

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown mode, schedule, or form, or a function that cannot be called.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The mode, the schedule, or the form is unknown, the symbolic form has the schedule `'member'`, or the
                function is not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        self._check_variant('mode', self.mode, MODES, (BaseSpec,))
        for name, value, variants in (
            ('schedule', self.schedule, SCHEDULES),
            ('form', self.form, FORMS),
        ):
            if value not in variants:
                error_msg = f'The {name} of map {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Use one of {", ".join(variants)}.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.schedule == 'member' and self.form != 'agent':
            error_msg = (
                f'The map {self.label!r} updates every member in its activation, which only the agent form does.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not callable(self.function):
            error_msg = f'The function of map {self.label!r} must be callable, but it is {self.function!r}.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _apply_mode(self, current: Value, value: Value) -> Value:
        """Return the next value of a state from its current value and the value of the function, by the mode."""
        if self.mode == 'increment':
            return current + value
        if self.mode == 'replace':
            return value
        raise self._get_variant_error(self.mode, 'mode', '_apply_mode')

    def _get_vector(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> Value:
        """Return the next value of a vector state of an agent."""
        current = np.asarray(getattr(agent, self.state), dtype=np.float64)
        value = np.asarray(self.function(agent, model), dtype=np.float64)
        if value.shape != current.shape:
            error_msg = (
                f'The function of map {self.label!r} returns the shape {value.shape} for the state {self.state!r} of '
                f'the shape {current.shape}. Return an array of the shape of the state.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        return self._apply_mode(current, value)

    def _get_value(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> Value:
        """Return the next value of the state of an agent, a number or the array of a vector state."""
        if np.ndim(getattr(agent, self.state)) > 0:
            return self._get_vector(agent, model)
        found = self.function(agent, model)
        if not isinstance(found, SupportsFloat):
            error_msg = f'The function of map {self.label!r} returns {found!r} for an agent. Return a number.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        value = float(found)
        return self._apply_mode(float(getattr(agent, self.state)), value)

    def _set_value(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, value: Value) -> None:
        """Set the state of an agent to its next value."""
        setattr(agent, self.state, value)

    def _update_member(self, agent: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Set the state of one member to its next value."""
        if agent.alive:
            self._set_value(agent, self._get_value(agent, model))

    def update(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
        """Set the state of every agent of the target to its next value, by the schedule.

        Args:
            model:
                The model view of the interaction.
        """
        self._update_agents(model, self.schedule, self._get_value, self._set_value)

    def _get_order(self) -> object:
        """Return the order of the members of the symbolic form: none, their own order, or a uniform draw."""
        if self.schedule == 'synchronous':
            return None
        if self.schedule == 'sequential':
            return SR(0)
        return uniform(re.sub(r'\W', '_', f'order_{self.label}'))

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the update of the state to its next value, or the rule of the agent form.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with `namespace.target` and `namespace.sources`.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The update law of the state, or the rule that runs the map of the agents.
        """
        if self.form == 'agent' and self.schedule == 'member':
            return [RuleLaw(self._update_member, phase=self.phase, members=self._get_role('target'))]
        if self.form == 'agent':
            return [RuleLaw(self.update, phase=self.phase)]
        value = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        mapped = cast(Value, self.function(namespace))
        next_value = self._apply_mode(value, mapped)
        return [UpdateLaw(value, next_value, increment=self.mode == 'increment', order=self._get_order())]

class QuotaRegulatorInteraction(FeedbackInteraction[ModelView]):
    """Regulator that halves the quota of cows per herder when the grass runs short and raises it when it recovers.

    The quota is the adaptive parameter `quota` of every herder. It halves, down to one cow, when the grass falls below
    the share `low` of the capacity of the meadow, and grows by one cow when the grass is above the share `high`.
    Without regulation it stays as it is.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the regulator.

        rule:
            Unused, since the regulator overrides `act`.

        phase:
            The phase the regulator acts in.

        regulated:
            One when the regulator changes the quota, zero otherwise.

        low:
            The share of the capacity of the meadow below which the quota halves.

        high:
            The share of the capacity of the meadow above which the quota rises by one cow.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import QuotaRegulatorInteraction
        >>> QuotaRegulatorInteraction('regulator', regulated=1.0).regulated
        1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        rule: Callable[[ModelView], None] | None = None,
        phase: str | None = None,
        regulated: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
        low: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
        high: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.8,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, rule=rule, phase=phase)
        self.regulated = regulated
        self.low = low
        self.high = high

    def act(self, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Change the quota with the share of grass left on the meadow.

        Args:
            model:
                The model view of the regulator.
        """
        if not model.parameter('regulated'):
            return
        pastures = model.agents('meadow', PastureView)
        share = sum(pasture.grass for pasture in pastures) / sum(pasture.capacity for pasture in pastures)
        for herder in model.agents('herders', HerderView):
            if share < model.parameter('low'):
                herder.quota = max(1.0, float(np.floor(herder.quota / 2)))
            elif share > model.parameter('high'):
                herder.quota += 1

docs.title: Von Thünen land use
docs.text:
A square plain around one market at its centre, whose every cell grows the crop of highest bid rent.

  • Name: von_thunen
  • Field: economics/resources
  • Formalism: static solution
  • References: Giordano 2024, arXiv 2407.02181; von Thünen 1826

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='economics/resources',
    tags=('land use', 'bid rent', 'static', 'lattice'),
    references=('Giordano 2024, arXiv 2407.02181', 'von Thünen 1826'),
)
def von_thunen(
    size: int = 41,
    *,
    yields: Sequence[float] = (4.0, 2.0, 1.0),
    prices: Sequence[float] = (3.0, 3.0, 3.5),
    costs: Sequence[float] = (1.0, 0.5, 0.5),
    rates: Sequence[float] = (0.2, 0.2, 0.2),
) -> System:
    """Return a square plain around one market at its centre, whose every cell grows the crop of highest bid rent.

    A crop of a high yield per cell bids most near the market, and its bid falls fastest with distance, so the land use
    forms concentric rings whose boundaries lie where the bids of neighbouring crops are equal (Giordano 2024 §7).

    Args:
        size:
            The side of the plain in cells, one unit of distance each.

        yields:
            The yield of every crop per cell.

        prices:
            The price of every crop at the market.

        costs:
            The cost of every crop per unit of yield.

        rates:
            The transport rate of every crop per unit of yield and of distance.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the states `plain.crop` and `plain.distance`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import von_thunen
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(von_thunen()).check().prepare().run(1.0).trajectory_
        >>> sorted(set(trajectory.values('plain.crop')[0].ravel().tolist()))
        [0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
    """
    centre = (size - 1) / 2
    rows, columns = np.indices((size, size))
    distance = np.hypot(rows - centre, columns - centre)
    plain = FieldElement(
        'plain',
        element=LandCellElement,
        space=LatticeSpace((size, size)),
        values={'distance': distance},
    )
    bid = BidRentInteraction('bid', target='plain', yields=yields, prices=prices, costs=costs, rates=rates)
    return System(elements=[plain], interactions=[bid], time=StaticTime())

class LandCellElement(Element):
    """Cell of a plain that grows one crop, numbered from 1, or lies idle as crop 0.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the cell or the field.

        crop:
            The initial guess of the crop, which the equation replaces.

        distance:
            The distance from the market.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import LandCellElement
        >>> LandCellElement('cell', distance=3.0).distance
        3.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        crop: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        distance: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.crop = crop
        self.distance = distance

class BidRentInteraction(Interaction):
    """Land use of highest bid rent, where crop `i` bids `Y_i (p_i - c_i) - Y_i f_i d` at the distance `d` of a market.

    A cell grows the crop of the highest positive bid, and lies idle as crop 0 when no bid is positive.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        target:
            The path of the field of cells, whose members hold `crop` and `distance`.

        yields:
            The yield `Y_i` of every crop per cell.

        prices:
            The price `p_i` of every crop at the market.

        costs:
            The cost `c_i` of every crop per unit of yield.

        rates:
            The transport rate `f_i` of every crop per unit of yield and of distance.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The four sequences do not have one value per crop, raised by `check`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.economics.resources import BidRentInteraction
        >>> bid = BidRentInteraction('bid', target='plain', yields=(2.0,), prices=(3.0,), costs=(1.0,), rates=(0.1,))
        >>> bid.check().rates
        (0.1,)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        yields: Sequence[float],
        prices: Sequence[float],
        costs: Sequence[float],
        rates: Sequence[float],
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.yields = yields
        self.prices = prices
        self.costs = costs
        self.rates = rates

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for sequences without one value per crop.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The sequences have different lengths.
        """
        super()._check()
        lengths = {len(self.yields), len(self.prices), len(self.costs), len(self.rates)}
        if len(lengths) != 1:
            error_msg = (
                f'The yields, prices, costs, and rates of {self.label!r} have the lengths {sorted(lengths)}. Give one '
                'value per crop.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> Sequence[BasePart]:
        """Return the equation of the crop of highest bid.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The equation of the crop of a cell.
        """
        crop, best = SR(0), SR(0)
        crops = zip(self.yields, self.prices, self.costs, self.rates, strict=True)
        for index, (yield_, price, cost, rate) in enumerate(crops, start=1):
            bid = yield_ * (price - cost) - yield_ * rate * s.target.distance
            crop, best = where(bid > best, index, crop), where(bid > best, bid, best)
        return [EquationLaw(s.target.crop == crop, target=s.target.crop)]

docs.title: Chua double and multiple scrolls
docs.text:
Chua's circuit, whose double-scroll or multiscroll attractor is chaotic.

  • Name: chua
  • Field: engineering/circuits
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Chua, Komuro, and Matsumoto 1986; Tang et al. 2001; Trzaska 2023

Example

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/circuits',
    tags=('circuit', 'chaos', 'ode', 'attractor'),
    references=('Chua, Komuro, and Matsumoto 1986', 'Tang et al. 2001', 'Trzaska 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 0.05},
)
def chua(
    x: float | None = None,
    y: float | None = None,
    z: float = 0.0,
    *,
    nonlinearity: str = 'piecewise-linear',
    alpha: float | None = None,
    beta: float | None = None,
) -> System:
    """Return Chua's circuit, whose double-scroll or multiscroll attractor is chaotic.

    The voltages of the two capacitors and the current of the inductor, in dimensionless form, follow
    `x' = alpha (y - f(x))`, `y' = x - y + z`, and `z' = -β y`. The piecewise-linear diode has
    `f(x) = x + m1 x + (m0 - m1) (|x + 1| - |x - 1|) / 2`, which gives the double scroll. The sine diode has
    `f(x) = -b sin(π x / (2 a))`, continued linearly beyond `|x| = 2 a c`, which gives several scrolls side by side.

    Args:
        x:
            The initial voltage of the first capacitor, or `None` for 0.1 with the piecewise-linear diode and 1 with
            the sine diode.

        y:
            The initial voltage of the second capacitor, or `None` for 0 with the piecewise-linear diode and 1 with the
            sine diode.

        z:
            The initial current of the inductor.

        nonlinearity:
            The characteristic of the diode, `'piecewise-linear'` for the double scroll or `'sine'` for multiple
            scrolls.

        alpha:
            The ratio of the capacitances, or `None` for 15.6 with the piecewise-linear diode and 10.82 with the sine
            diode.

        beta:
            The ratio of the inductance to the second capacitance, or `None` for 28 with the piecewise-linear diode and
            14.286 with the sine diode.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the states `circuit.x`, `circuit.y`, and `circuit.z`.

    Raises:
        ParameterError:
            The nonlinearity is neither `'piecewise-linear'` nor `'sine'`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.circuits import chua
        >>> chua(nonlinearity='sine').elements[0].alpha
        10.82
    """
    if nonlinearity not in CHUA_NONLINEARITIES:
        error_msg = f"Unknown nonlinearity {nonlinearity!r}. Use 'piecewise-linear' or 'sine'."
        raise ParameterError(error_msg)
    element = ChuaCircuitElement if nonlinearity == 'piecewise-linear' else MultiscrollChuaCircuitElement
    initial = {'x': x, 'y': y, 'alpha': alpha, 'beta': beta}
    values: dict[str, float] = {name: value for name, value in initial.items() if value is not None}
    return System(elements=[element('circuit', z=z).set_params(**values)])

class ChuaCircuitElement(Element):
    """Chua circuit with the piecewise-linear current of its diode."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.1,
        y: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        z: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        alpha: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 15.6,
        beta: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 28.0,
        m0: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec()] = -8 / 7,
        m1: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec()] = -5 / 7,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.z = z
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.beta = beta
        self.m0 = m0
        self.m1 = m1

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rates of the states of the circuit."""
        return [
            RateLaw(s.x, s.alpha * (s.y - s.x - s.m1 * s.x - (s.m0 - s.m1) * (abs(s.x + 1) - abs(s.x - 1)) / 2)),
            RateLaw(s.y, s.x - s.y + s.z),
            RateLaw(s.z, -s.beta * s.y),
        ]

docs.title: Circuits under periodic impulses
docs.text:
An RLC circuit driven by a periodic train of current impulses, L C x'' + R C x' + x = A Σ δ(t - k T).

  • Name: impulsive_circuits
  • Field: engineering/circuits
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Trzaska 2023

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/circuits',
    tags=('circuit', 'impulses', 'events', 'hybrid'),
    references=('Trzaska 2023',),
    defaults={'until': 40.0, 'dt': 0.05},
)
def impulsive_circuits(
    x: float = 0.0,
    current: float = 0.0,
    *,
    L: float = 1.0,
    R: float = 0.1,
    C: float = 1.0,
    A: float = 1.0,
    T: float = 2.0,
) -> System:
    """Return an RLC circuit driven by a periodic train of current impulses, `L C x'' + R C x' + x = A Σ δ(t - k T)`.

    Every impulse is an event that raises the rate of change `x'` by `A / (L C)`, and between impulses the circuit
    rings down freely. The response settles on a periodic, non-sinusoidal waveform of period `T`.

    Args:
        x:
            The initial value of the response, the current of the coil.

        current:
            The initial rate of change of the response.

        L:
            The inductance.

        R:
            The resistance.

        C:
            The capacitance.

        A:
            The strength of every impulse.

        T:
            The period of the impulses.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the response `circuit.x` and its rate `circuit.x_d1`, kicked by the impulses `impulse`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.circuits import impulsive_circuits
        >>> impulsive_circuits(T=3.0).interactions[0].period
        3.0
    """
    circuit = KickedCircuitElement('circuit', x=x, x_d1=current, L=L, R=R, C=C, A=A)
    kick = {'x_d1': lambda s: s.target.x_d1 + s.target.A / (s.target.L * s.target.C)}
    impulse = ImpulseInteraction('impulse', target='circuit', reset=kick, period=T)
    return System(elements=[circuit], interactions=[impulse])

class KickedCircuitElement(Element):
    """RLC circuit ringing down freely between the impulses of strength `A` that kick its rate."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[object, StateSpec(order=2)] = 0.0,
        x_d1: float = 0.0,
        L: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        R: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.1,
        C: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        A: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.x_d1 = x_d1
        self.L = L
        self.R = R
        self.C = C
        self.A = A

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the free equation of the circuit between impulses."""
        return [EquationLaw(s.L * s.C * derivative(s.x, 2) + s.R * s.C * derivative(s.x, 1) + s.x == 0)]

class ImpulseInteraction(Interaction):
    """Impulses that set states of the target to new values at given times, or at periodic times.

    The impulses fall at every time of `times` and, with a `period`, at `start + j * period` for `j` from 0, `count`
    times or without end. An impulse at the initial time of a run does not fire. The new values are functions of the
    namespace, which holds `namespace.target`, the states and parameters of the target, and the time `namespace.t`. An
    impulse sets the states of every member of a group at once, and the trajectory records every impulse among its
    events, under the label of the interaction.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose states the impulses set.

        reset:
            A mapping from the name of a state of the target to the function `f(namespace)` of its new value.

        times:
            The times of the impulses.

        period:
            The period of the periodic impulses, or `None` for none.

        start:
            The time of the first periodic impulse.

        count:
            The number of periodic impulses, or `None` for impulses without end.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The impulses set no state, a new value is not a function, the impulses have no time, the period is not
            positive, or the count is not a positive integer.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import ImpulseInteraction
        >>> reset = {'c': lambda s: s.target.c + 1.0}
        >>> dose = ImpulseInteraction('dose', target='body', reset=reset, period=8.0, count=3)
        >>> dose.check().start
        0.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        reset: Mapping[str, Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]],
        times: Sequence[float] = (),
        period: float | None = None,
        start: float = 0.0,
        count: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.reset = reset
        self.times = times
        self.period = period
        self.start = start
        self.count = count

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for impulses without states or times, or with a period or a count they cannot take.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The impulses set no state, a new value is not a function, the impulses have no time, the period is not
                positive, or the count is not a positive integer.
        """
        super()._check()
        if not self.reset or not all(callable(function) for function in self.reset.values()):
            error_msg = (
                f'The impulses {self.label!r} set {self.reset!r}. Map state names to functions of the namespace.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not self.times and self.period is None:
            error_msg = f'The impulses {self.label!r} have no time. Give `times`, or a `period`.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.period is not None and not self.period > 0:
            error_msg = f'The period of the impulses {self.label!r} is {self.period!r}. Give a positive number.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.count is not None and (
            isinstance(self.count, bool) or not isinstance(self.count, int) or self.count < 1
        ):
            error_msg = f'The count of the impulses {self.label!r} is {self.count!r}. Give a positive integer, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_periodic_guard(self, time: Expression, period: float) -> Expression:
        """Return a guard that crosses zero at every periodic impulse and stays away from zero outside them."""
        guard = where(time < self.start - period / 2, -1, sin(pi * (time - self.start) / period))
        if self.count is None:
            return guard
        last = self.count - SR(1) / 2
        return where(time > self.start + last * period, sin(pi * last), guard)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the crossing laws of time at the impulses.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with `namespace.target` and the time `namespace.t`.

        Returns:
            laws:
                One crossing law per given time and one for the periodic impulses.
        """
        reset = {
            getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), name): SR(f(namespace)) for name, f in self.reset.items()
        }
        laws: list[BaseLaw] = [CrossingLaw(namespace.t - time, reset, 1, label=self.label) for time in self.times]
        if self.period is not None:
            laws.append(CrossingLaw(self._get_periodic_guard(namespace.t, self.period), reset, 0, label=self.label))
        return laws

docs.title: Memristor oscillator
docs.text:
The simplest memristor oscillator: a capacitor, an inductor, and a memristor in series.

  • Name: memristor_oscillator
  • Field: engineering/circuits
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Muthuswamy and Chua 2010; Trzaska 2023

Example

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/circuits',
    tags=('circuit', 'memristor', 'chaos', 'ode'),
    references=('Muthuswamy and Chua 2010', 'Trzaska 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 200.0, 'dt': 0.1},
)
def memristor_oscillator(
    v: float = 0.1,
    i: float = 0.0,
    w: float = 0.1,
    *,
    C: float = 1.0,
    L: float = 3.0,
    alpha: float = 0.6,
    beta: float = 1.5,
) -> System:
    """Return the simplest memristor oscillator: a capacitor, an inductor, and a memristor in series.

    The capacitor voltage, the inductor current, and the internal state of the memristor follow `C v' = i`,
    `L i' = -v - β (w^2 - 1) i`, and `w' = -i - alpha w + w i`. The memristor has the memristance `β (w^2 - 1)`, and the
    circuit oscillates chaotically for the default values.

    Args:
        v:
            The initial voltage of the capacitor.

        i:
            The initial current.

        w:
            The initial internal state of the memristor.

        C:
            The capacitance.

        L:
            The inductance.

        alpha:
            The decay rate of the memristor state.

        beta:
            The scale of the memristance.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the states `circuit.v`, `circuit.i`, and `circuit.w`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.circuits import memristor_oscillator
        >>> memristor_oscillator(L=2.0).elements[0].L
        2.0
    """
    return System(elements=[MemristorCircuitElement('circuit', v=v, i=i, w=w, C=C, L=L, alpha=alpha, beta=beta)])

docs.text:
class MemristorCircuitElement(Element):
    """Oscillator built from a memristor, whose current depends on the flux through it."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        v: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.1,
        i: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        w: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.1,
        C: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        L: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 3.0,
        alpha: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.6,
        beta: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.5,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.v = v
        self.i = i
        self.w = w
        self.C = C
        self.L = L
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.beta = beta

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rates of the states of the circuit."""
        return [
            RateLaw(s.v, s.i / s.C),
            RateLaw(s.i, -(s.v + s.beta * (s.w**2 - 1) * s.i) / s.L),
            RateLaw(s.w, -s.i - s.alpha * s.w + s.w * s.i),
        ]

docs.title: Modified Chua with mixed-mode oscillations
docs.text:
A modified Chua circuit on three time scales, whose oscillations mix small and large amplitudes.

  • Name: mixed_mode_chua
  • Field: engineering/circuits
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Krupa, Popović, and Kopell 2008; Trzaska 2023

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/circuits',
    tags=('circuit', 'mixed-mode oscillations', 'canards', 'slow-fast', 'ode'),
    references=('Krupa, Popović, and Kopell 2008', 'Trzaska 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 200.0, 'dt': 0.5, 'solver': ScipyODESolver(method='Radau')},
)
def mixed_mode_chua(
    x: float = 0.01,
    y: float = 0.0,
    z: float = 0.0,
    *,
    epsilon: float = 0.01,
    a: float = 1.5,
    b: float = -1.0,
    alpha: float = 1.0,
    R: float = 0.0,
    beta: float = 0.005,
    c: float = 0.00053,
) -> System:
    """Return a modified Chua circuit on three time scales, whose oscillations mix small and large amplitudes.

    The circuit follows `ε x' = -y + (a + b x) x^2`, `y' = alpha (x - R y - z)`, and `z' = c - β y`. For `ε = 0.01`,
    `a = 1.5`, `b = -1`, and `β = 0.005`, the circuit has small oscillations only for `c = 0`, large ones only for
    `c = 0.00105`, and mixed-mode oscillations for `c = 0.00053`.

    Args:
        x:
            The initial voltage of the first capacitor.

        y:
            The initial current of the inductor.

        z:
            The initial voltage of the second capacitor.

        epsilon:
            The first capacitance, which sets the fast time scale.

        a:
            The quadratic coefficient of the diode.

        b:
            The cubic coefficient of the diode.

        alpha:
            The inverse inductance.

        R:
            The resistance.

        beta:
            The gain of the controlled source over the second capacitance.

        c:
            The offset of the controlled source.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the states `circuit.x`, `circuit.y`, and `circuit.z`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.circuits import mixed_mode_chua
        >>> mixed_mode_chua(c=0.0).elements[0].c
        0.0
    """
    circuit = MixedModeChuaCircuitElement(
        'circuit',
        x=x,
        y=y,
        z=z,
        epsilon=epsilon,
        a=a,
        b=b,
        alpha=alpha,
        R=R,
        beta=beta,
        c=c,
    )
    return System(elements=[circuit])

    """Slow-fast Chua circuit whose oscillations mix small and large amplitudes."""

    def __init__(
        self,

        x: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.01,
        y: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.0,

        epsilon: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.01,
        a: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec()] = 1.5,
        b: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec()] = -1.0,
        alpha: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        R: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
        beta: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.005,
        c: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec()] = 0.00053,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.z = z
        self.epsilon = epsilon
        self.a = a
        self.b = b
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.R = R
        self.beta = beta
        self.c = c

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rates of the states of the circuit."""
        return [
            RateLaw(s.x, (-s.y + (s.a + s.b * s.x) * s.x**2) / s.epsilon),
            RateLaw(s.y, s.alpha * (s.x - s.R * s.y - s.z)),
            RateLaw(s.z, s.c - s.beta * s.y),
        ]

    Args:

class CircuitElement(Element):
    """RLC circuit whose charge follows `L q'' + R q' + q / C = V cos(ω t)`."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        q: Annotated[object, StateSpec(order=2)] = 1.0,
        q_d1: float = 0.0,
        L: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        R: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.1,
        C: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        V: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        omega: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.q = q
        self.q_d1 = q_d1
        self.L = L
        self.R = R
        self.C = C
        self.V = V
        self.omega = omega

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the equation of the charge."""
        return [
            EquationLaw(s.L * derivative(s.q, 2) + s.R * derivative(s.q, 1) + s.q / s.C == s.V * cos(s.omega * s.t)),
        ]

docs.title: Tunnel-diode oscillator
docs.text:
A tunnel-diode oscillator: an inductor and a capacitor in parallel with a negative-resistance diode.

  • Name: tunnel_diode_oscillator
  • Field: engineering/circuits
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: van der Pol 1926; Trzaska 2023

Example

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/circuits',
    tags=('circuit', 'oscillation', 'limit cycle', 'ode'),
    references=('van der Pol 1926', 'Trzaska 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 50.0, 'dt': 0.05},
)
def tunnel_diode_oscillator(
    V: float = 0.1,
    i: float = 0.0,
    *,
    L: float = 1.0,
    C: float = 1.0,
    alpha: float = 1.0,
    gamma: float = 1.0,
) -> System:
    """Return a tunnel-diode oscillator: an inductor and a capacitor in parallel with a negative-resistance diode.

    The diode current is `h(V) = gamma V^3 - alpha V`, so Kirchhoff's laws give `C V' = -h(V) - i` and `L i' = V`,
    which is the van der Pol oscillator with `ε = alpha sqrt(L / C)`. The voltage settles on a limit cycle of
    amplitude near `2 sqrt(alpha / (3 gamma))`.

    Args:
        V:
            The initial voltage.

        i:
            The initial current of the inductor.

        L:
            The inductance.

        C:
            The capacitance.

        alpha:
            The negative conductance of the diode at zero voltage.

        gamma:
            The cubic coefficient of the diode.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the voltage `circuit.V` and the inductor current `circuit.i`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.circuits import tunnel_diode_oscillator
        >>> tunnel_diode_oscillator(alpha=2.0).elements[0].alpha
        2.0
    """
    return System(elements=[TunnelDiodeCircuitElement('circuit', V=V, i=i, L=L, C=C, alpha=alpha, gamma=gamma)])

        *,
        V: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.1,
        i: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        L: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        C: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        alpha: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        gamma: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:

        self.V = V
        self.i = i
        self.L = L
        self.C = C
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.gamma = gamma

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:

        return [
            RateLaw(s.V, -(s.gamma * s.V**3 - s.alpha * s.V + s.i) / s.C),
            RateLaw(s.i, s.V / s.L),
        ]
