docs.title: Swarmtaxis
docs.text:
The swarmtaxis algorithm, which moves a swarm of robots towards a beacon that only some of them see.

  • Name: swarmtaxis
  • Field: engineering/robotics
  • Formalism: agent-based model
  • References: Bjerknes, Winfield, and Melhuish 2007; Varughese et al. 2019

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/robotics',
    tags=('robotics', 'swarms', 'agents', 'taxis'),
    references=('Bjerknes, Winfield, and Melhuish 2007', 'Varughese et al. 2019'),
    defaults={'until': 300},
)
def swarmtaxis(
    n_robots: int = 20,
    *,
    size: float = 100.0,
    spread: float = 3.0,
    speed: float = 0.2,
    radio_range: float = 4.0,
    avoid_illuminated: float = 1.5,
    avoid_shadowed: float = 1.0,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return the swarmtaxis algorithm, which moves a swarm of robots towards a beacon that only some of them see.

    The robots start in a cluster near the left edge of a square arena, with the beacon at the middle of the right edge.
    Each robot keeps radio contact with the swarm by turning around when it loses a connection, and avoids its
    neighbours. Robots that see the beacon avoid at a larger radius than shadowed robots, which moves the centre of the
    swarm towards the beacon.

    Args:
        n_robots:
            The number of robots.

        size:
            The side of the arena.

        spread:
            The standard deviation of the initial positions around the start.

        speed:
            The distance a robot moves per step.

        radio_range:
            The range of the radio pings.

        avoid_illuminated:
            The avoidance radius of illuminated robots.

        avoid_shadowed:
            The avoidance radius of shadowed robots.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the initial positions and headings.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `robots` of headings `heading` and illumination `illuminated`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.robotics import swarmtaxis
        >>> swarmtaxis(5).elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        5
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state)
    start = np.array([size / 5, size / 2])
    points = np.clip(start + rng.normal(0.0, spread, (n_robots, 2)), 0.0, size)
    robots = GroupElement(
        'robots',
        element=SwarmRobotElement,
        size=n_robots,
        values={
            'heading': rng.uniform(0.0, 2 * np.pi, n_robots),
            'speed': speed,
            'radio_range': radio_range,
            'alpha': float(n_robots),
            'avoid_illuminated': avoid_illuminated,
            'avoid_shadowed': avoid_shadowed,
            'beacon_x': size - BEACON_MARGIN,
            'beacon_y': size / 2,
            'arena': size,
        },
        location=[tuple(map(float, point)) for point in points],
    )
    return System(elements=[robots], space=ContinuousSpace(extent=(size, size)))

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
class SwarmRobotElement(Element):
    """Robot of the swarmtaxis algorithm, which keeps in radio contact with the swarm and avoids its neighbours.

    Every step the robot counts the robots within its radio range. When it loses a connection and has fewer than
    `alpha` connections, it turns around to stay with the swarm, and when it gains one it turns at random. A robot
    closer than its avoidance radius to another turns away from it. A robot is shadowed when another robot lies between
    it and the beacon, within the radio range and `shadow_angle` of the bearing to the beacon, and it is illuminated
    otherwise. Illuminated robots avoid at a larger radius than shadowed ones, so they move away from the swarm towards
    the beacon, and the swarm follows. The robot then moves forward at its speed.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        heading:
            The direction of motion.

        connections:
            The number of robots within radio range at the last step.

        illuminated:
            Whether the robot sees the beacon.

        speed:
            The distance moved per step.

        radio_range:
            The range of the radio pings.

        alpha:
            The number of connections below which a robot that loses one turns around.

        avoid_illuminated:
            The avoidance radius of illuminated robots.

        avoid_shadowed:
            The avoidance radius of shadowed robots.

        shadow_angle:
            The half angle of the cone towards the beacon in which another robot casts a shadow.

        beacon_x:
            The horizontal position of the beacon.

        beacon_y:
            The vertical position of the beacon.

        arena:
            The side of the square arena, whose walls stop the robot.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.robotics import SwarmRobotElement
        >>> GroupElement('robots', element=SwarmRobotElement, size=2, location=[(1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 1.0)]).size
        2
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = VisualSpec('agents', {'color_by': 'illuminated', 'color_range': (0.0, 1.0)}),
        *,
        heading: Annotated[float, StateSpec(role='direction')] = 0.0,
        connections: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=NN)] = 0.0,
        illuminated: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=FiniteEnumeratedSet([0, 1]))] = 1.0,
        speed: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.2,
        radio_range: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 4.0,
        alpha: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 20.0,
        avoid_illuminated: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.5,
        avoid_shadowed: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        shadow_angle: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
        beacon_x: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 95.0,
        beacon_y: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 50.0,
        arena: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 100.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.heading = heading
        self.connections = connections
        self.illuminated = illuminated
        self.speed = speed
        self.radio_range = radio_range
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.avoid_illuminated = avoid_illuminated
        self.avoid_shadowed = avoid_shadowed
        self.shadow_angle = shadow_angle
        self.beacon_x = beacon_x
        self.beacon_y = beacon_y
        self.arena = arena

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[SwarmRobotView]:
        """Return the view of the robots, which types their states and parameters."""
        return SwarmRobotView

    def _is_shadowed(self, agent: SwarmRobotView, neighbors: list[AgentView]) -> bool:
        """Return whether a neighbour lies in the cone from the robot towards the beacon."""
        x, y = SwarmRobotElement._position(agent)
        bearing = SwarmRobotElement._bearing(agent.beacon_x - x, agent.beacon_y - y)
        return any(
            SwarmRobotElement._angle_between(
                SwarmRobotElement._bearing(
                    SwarmRobotElement._position(other)[0] - x,
                    SwarmRobotElement._position(other)[1] - y,
                ),
                bearing,
            )
            < agent.shadow_angle
            for other in neighbors
        )

    def _turn(self, agent: SwarmRobotView, model: ModelView, count: int) -> float:
        """Return the new heading: back to the swarm after a lost connection, or at random after a new one."""
        if count < agent.connections and count < agent.alpha:
            return agent.heading + math.pi
        if count > agent.connections:
            return float(model.rng.uniform(0.0, 2 * math.pi))
        return agent.heading

    def _avoid(self, agent: SwarmRobotView, neighbors: list[AgentView], heading: float) -> float:
        """Return the heading away from the nearest neighbour inside the avoidance radius, or the heading unchanged."""
        x, y = SwarmRobotElement._position(agent)
        radius = agent.avoid_illuminated if agent.illuminated else agent.avoid_shadowed
        distances = [
            math.hypot(SwarmRobotElement._position(other)[0] - x, SwarmRobotElement._position(other)[1] - y)
            for other in neighbors
        ]
        close = [(distance, other) for distance, other in zip(distances, neighbors, strict=True) if distance < radius]
        if not close:
            return heading
        _, nearest = min(close, key=lambda pair: pair[0])
        return SwarmRobotElement._bearing(
            x - SwarmRobotElement._position(nearest)[0],
            y - SwarmRobotElement._position(nearest)[1],
        )

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the swarmtaxis rule.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return [RuleLaw(self.move)]

    def move(self, agent: SwarmRobotView, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Update the connections, the shadow, and the heading, and move forward.

        Args:
            agent:
                The robot.

            model:
                The model.
        """
        neighbors = agent.neighbors(agent.radio_range)
        count = len(neighbors)
        agent.illuminated = 0.0 if self._is_shadowed(agent, neighbors) else 1.0
        heading = self._avoid(agent, neighbors, self._turn(agent, model, count))
        agent.connections = count
        agent.heading = heading % (2 * math.pi)
        x, y = SwarmRobotElement._position(agent)
        edge = agent.arena * (1 - EDGE_FRACTION)
        x = min(max(x + agent.speed * math.cos(heading), 0.0), edge)
        y = min(max(y + agent.speed * math.sin(heading), 0.0), edge)
        agent.move_to((x, y))

    @staticmethod
    def _position(agent: AgentView) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """Return the position of an agent in a continuous space."""
        x, y = np.asarray(agent.location, dtype=float)
        return float(x), float(y)

    @staticmethod
    def _bearing(dx: float, dy: float) -> float:
        """Return the angle of a vector."""
        return math.atan2(dy, dx)

    @staticmethod
    def _angle_between(first: float, second: float) -> float:
        """Return the absolute difference of two angles, between 0 and pi."""
        return abs((first - second + math.pi) % (2 * math.pi) - math.pi)

docs.title: Charbonneau traffic
docs.text:
Charbonneau's traffic model, where random braking of single drivers sets off traffic jams.

  • Name: charbonneau_traffic
  • Field: engineering/traffic
  • Formalism: agent-based model
  • References: Charbonneau 2017

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/traffic',
    tags=('traffic', 'jams', 'agents', 'avalanches', 'stochastic'),
    references=('Charbonneau 2017',),
    defaults={'until': 100},
)
def charbonneau_traffic(
    n_cars: int = 100,
    *,
    probability: float = 0.1,
    safe_distance: float = 5.0,
    speed_limit: float = 10.0,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return Charbonneau's traffic model, where random braking of single drivers sets off traffic jams.

    Cars on a one-way road start at rest with random spacings between 3 and 17. Every step, each driver brakes by 3
    when the car ahead is closer than the safe distance and accelerates by 1 otherwise, within the speed limit. A random
    driver brakes with a probability every step, and then every car moves by its speed.

    Args:
        n_cars:
            The number of cars.

        probability:
            The probability that a random driver brakes in a step.

        safe_distance:
            The distance to the car ahead below which drivers brake.

        speed_limit:
            The largest speed.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the initial spacings.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `cars` of positions `x`, speeds `v`, and ranks `rank`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import charbonneau_traffic
        >>> charbonneau_traffic(5).elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        5
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state)
    positions = np.cumsum(rng.uniform(3.0, 17.0, n_cars))
    cars = GroupElement(
        'cars',
        element=MotoristElement,
        size=n_cars,
        values={
            'x': positions,
            'v': np.zeros(n_cars),
            'rank': np.arange(n_cars, dtype=float),
            'safe_distance': safe_distance,
            'speed_limit': speed_limit,
        },
    )
    return System(
        elements=[cars],
        interactions=[CarelessBrakingInteraction('braking', cars='cars', probability=probability)],
    )

class MotoristElement(Element):
    """Car of Charbonneau's traffic model, which brakes when it is closer than a safe distance to the car ahead.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the agent or group.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x:
            The position along the road.

        v:
            The speed.

        rank:
            The order of the car along the road, 0 for the last car.

        safe_distance:
            The distance to the car ahead below which the driver brakes.

        braking:
            The speed lost when braking.

        acceleration:
            The speed gained when accelerating.

        speed_limit:
            The largest speed.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import MotoristElement
        >>> GroupElement('cars', element=MotoristElement, size=3, values={'x': [0.0, 10.0, 20.0]}).size
        3
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = VisualSpec('agents', {'position': 'x', 'color_by': 'v'}),
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec(role='position')] = 0.0,
        v: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo), role='velocity')] = 0.0,
        rank: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=NN)] = 0.0,
        safe_distance: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 5.0,
        braking: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 3.0,
        acceleration: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        speed_limit: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 10.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.v = v
        self.rank = rank
        self.safe_distance = safe_distance
        self.braking = braking
        self.acceleration = acceleration
        self.speed_limit = speed_limit

    @classmethod
    def _get_view(cls) -> type[MotoristView]:
        """Return the view of the cars, which types their states and parameters."""
        return MotoristView

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the speed adjustment rule.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return [RuleLaw(self.adjust)]

    def adjust(self, agent: MotoristView, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Brake when the car ahead is closer than the safe distance and accelerate otherwise.

        The lead car, which has no car ahead, keeps its distance to the car behind it instead.

        Args:
            agent:
                The car.

            model:
                The model.
        """
        cars = model.agents(agent.group, MotoristView)
        ahead = next((car for car in cars if int(car.rank) == int(agent.rank) + 1), None)
        if ahead is None:
            behind = next((car for car in cars if int(car.rank) == int(agent.rank) - 1), None)
            distance = agent.x - behind.x if behind is not None else np.inf
        else:
            distance = ahead.x - agent.x
        change = -agent.braking if distance < agent.safe_distance else agent.acceleration
        agent.v = float(np.clip(agent.v + change, 0.0, agent.speed_limit))

class CarelessBrakingInteraction(Interaction):
    """Model rule of Charbonneau's traffic model: a random driver brakes now and then, and every car moves.

    Every step, with probability `probability`, one random driver brakes by the braking of its group whatever the
    distance to the car ahead. Then every car moves by its speed, but no closer than `gap` to the car ahead.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        cars:
            The path of the group of cars.

        probability:
            The probability that a random driver brakes in a step.

        gap:
            The smallest distance a car keeps to the car ahead.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import CarelessBrakingInteraction
        >>> CarelessBrakingInteraction('bozo', cars='cars').probability
        0.1
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        cars: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        probability: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.1,
        gap: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.cars = cars
        self.probability = probability
        self.gap = gap

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rule of random braking and motion.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        return [RuleLaw(self.drive)]

    def drive(self, model: ModelView) -> None:
        """Make a random driver brake with the interaction's probability, then move every car.

        Args:
            model:
                The model.
        """
        cars = sorted(model.agents('cars', MotoristView), key=lambda car: car.rank)
        if not cars:
            return
        if model.rng.random() < model.parameter('probability'):
            careless = cars[int(model.rng.integers(len(cars)))]
            careless.v = max(careless.v - careless.braking, 0.0)
        gap = model.parameter('gap')
        positions = [car.x for car in cars]
        for index, car in enumerate(cars):
            moved = car.x + car.v
            car.x = min(moved, positions[index + 1] - gap) if index + 1 < len(cars) else moved

docs.text:
A chain of cars that react to the speed difference to the car ahead after a reaction time.

  • Name: delayed_car_following
  • Field: engineering/traffic
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Gros 2015; Chandler, Herman, and Montroll 1958

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/traffic',
    tags=('traffic', 'delay', 'car following', 'instability'),
    references=('Gros 2015', 'Chandler, Herman, and Montroll 1958'),
    defaults={'until': 60.0, 'dt': 0.5},
)
def delayed_car_following(
    n_cars: int = 8,
    *,
    spacing: float = 10.0,
    u: float = 1.0,
    amplitude: float = 0.1,
    omega: float = 0.5,
    reaction: float = 1.0,
    T: float = 1.0,
    power: float = 0.0,
) -> System:
    """Return a chain of cars that react to the speed difference to the car ahead after a reaction time.

    Car `j + 1` follows car `j` as `x''_{j+1}(t) = λ Δv(t - T) / Δx(t - T)^power`, where `Δv` and `Δx` are the speed
    and position differences to the car ahead. The lead car drives at `u (1 - amplitude sin(ω t))`. Oscillations grow
    along the chain when `ω < 2 λ sin(ω T)` for the linear model, `power = 0`.

    Args:
        n_cars:
            The number of cars, the lead car included.

        spacing:
            The initial distance between neighbouring cars.

        u:
            The mean speed of the lead car.

        amplitude:
            The relative amplitude of the speed oscillation of the lead car.

        omega:
            The angular frequency of the speed oscillation of the lead car.

        reaction:
            The reaction constant `λ`.

        T:
            The reaction time.

        power:
            The power of the distance in the reaction, 0 for the linear model.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the lead car `car_0` and the following cars `car_<j>`, each with position `x` and speed `v`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import delayed_car_following
        >>> delayed_car_following(n_cars=3).elements[2].x
        -20.0
    """
    lead = LeadCarElement('car_0', x=0.0, v=u, u=u, amplitude=amplitude, omega=omega)
    followers = [CarElement(f'car_{index}', x=-index * spacing, v=u) for index in range(1, n_cars)]
    interactions = [
        DelayedFollowingInteraction(
            f'follow_{index}',
            target=f'car_{index}',
            leader=f'car_{index - 1}',
            reaction=reaction,
            T=T,
            power=power,
        )
        for index in range(1, n_cars)
    ]
    return System(elements=[lead, *followers], interactions=interactions)

class LeadCarElement(Element):
    """Lead car whose speed swings about a cruising speed `u` with an amplitude and a frequency."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='position')] = 0.0,
        v: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='velocity')] = 1.0,
        u: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        amplitude: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.1,
        omega: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.v = v
        self.u = u
        self.amplitude = amplitude
        self.omega = omega

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the advance of the position and the forced swing of the speed."""
        return [RateLaw(s.x, s.v), RateLaw(s.v, -s.u * s.amplitude * s.omega * cos(s.omega * s.t))]

class CarElement(Element):
    """Car on a road whose position `x` advances at its speed `v`."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='position')] = 0.0,
        v: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='velocity')] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.v = v

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the advance of the position at the speed."""
        return [RateLaw(s.x, s.v)]

class DelayedFollowingInteraction(RateInteraction):
    """Acceleration of a follower car by the speed difference to its leader, both seen a reaction time late.

    The speed of the follower follows the Gazis-Herman-Rothery law
    `v_f'(t) = λ (v_l - v_f)(t - T) / (x_l - x_f)(t - T)^m` of the sensitivity `λ`, the reaction time `T`, and the
    power `m` of the gap.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        target:
            The path of the follower car.

        leader:
            The path of the car ahead of the follower.

        reaction:
            The sensitivity `λ`.

        T:
            The reaction time.

        power:
            The power `m` of the gap.

    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        leader: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        reaction: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        T: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        power: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, state='v')
        self.leader = leader
        self.reaction = reaction
        self.T = T
        self.power = power

    def _get_rate(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the delayed response of the follower to its leader."""
        s, leader, follower = namespace, namespace.leader, namespace.target
        gap = delayed(leader.x, s.T) - delayed(follower.x, s.T)
        return s.reaction * (delayed(leader.v, s.T) - delayed(follower.v, s.T)) / gap**s.power

docs.title: GKT non-local traffic
docs.text:
The gas-kinetic-based traffic model, where drivers brake on the traffic at an interaction point ahead.

  • Name: gkt_traffic
  • Field: engineering/traffic
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Treiber, Hennecke, and Helbing 1999; arXiv:cond-mat/0012229

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/traffic',
    tags=('traffic', 'field', 'conservation law', 'finite volume', 'non-local', 'stop-and-go', 'pde'),
    references=('Treiber, Hennecke, and Helbing 1999', 'arXiv:cond-mat/0012229'),
    defaults={'until': 1.0, 'dt': 1 / 60, 'solver': SSPRKSolver(cfl=0.4)},
)
def gkt_traffic(
    n: int = 200,
    *,
    length: float = 10.0,
    density: float = 35.0,
    amplitude: float = 2.0,
    V0: float = 110.0,
    T: float = 1.8 / 3600,
    tau: float = 35 / 3600,
    rho_max: float = 160.0,
    gamma: float = 1.2,
) -> System:
    """Return the gas-kinetic-based traffic model, where drivers brake on the traffic at an interaction point ahead.

    The density and the flow `Q = rho V` on a ring road follow `rho_t + Q_x = 0` and
    `Q_t + (Q**2 / rho + rho A(rho) V**2)_x = rho (Ve* - V) / tau`, where the dynamic equilibrium speed

        Ve* = V0 (1 - (theta + theta_a) / (2 A(rho_max)) (rho_a T / (1 - rho_a / rho_max))**2 B(dV))

    reads the density `rho_a` and the speed `V_a` at the interaction point `x + gamma (1 / rho_max + T V)`, with the
    variances `theta = A(rho) V**2`, the variance prefactor `A(rho) = A0 + dA (tanh((rho - rho_c) / d_rho) + 1)`, the
    dimensionless speed difference `dV = (V - V_a) / sqrt(theta + theta_a)`, and the Boltzmann factor
    `B(d) = 2 (d phi(d) + (1 + d**2) Phi(d))` of the standard normal density `phi` and distribution `Phi`. Lengths are
    in kilometres and times in hours, and the defaults are the calibrated values of Treiber, Hennecke, and Helbing. The
    flow starts in equilibrium with their dipole perturbation of the density, of height `amplitude`. Homogeneous
    traffic is unstable between about 24 and 51 vehicles per kilometre, where the perturbation grows into stop-and-go
    waves whose downstream fronts move against the traffic.

    Args:
        n:
            The number of cells.

        length:
            The length of the ring road in kilometres.

        density:
            The mean density in vehicles per kilometre.

        amplitude:
            The height of the dipole perturbation in vehicles per kilometre.

        V0:
            The desired speed in kilometres per hour.

        T:
            The safe time headway in hours.

        tau:
            The relaxation time of the speed in hours.

        rho_max:
            The maximum density in vehicles per kilometre.

        gamma:
            The anticipation factor.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the density `road.rho` and the flow `road.Q`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import gkt_traffic
        >>> gkt_traffic(10).elements[0].values['gamma']
        1.2
    """
    centers = (np.arange(n) + 0.5) * length / n
    start, width, wake = 0.3 * length, 0.20125, 0.805
    rho = density + amplitude * (
        np.cosh((centers - start) / width) ** -2 - width / wake * np.cosh((centers - start - 1.00625) / wake) ** -2
    )
    values = {'V0': V0, 'T': T, 'tau': tau, 'rho_max': rho_max, 'gamma': gamma}
    cell = GasKineticTrafficElement('cell', V0=V0, T=T, tau=tau, rho_max=rho_max, gamma=gamma)
    road = FieldElement(
        'road',
        element=GasKineticTrafficElement,
        space=LatticeSpace(n, spacing=length / n),
        values={'rho': rho, 'Q': rho * _gkt_equilibrium_speed(rho, cell), **values},
        discretization='finite-volume',
    )
    vehicles = ConservationInteraction('density', target='road', state='rho', flux=lambda s: s.target.Q)
    momentum = ConservationInteraction(
        'flow',
        target='road',
        state='Q',
        flux=_get_gkt_momentum_flux,
        source=_get_gkt_relaxation,
    )
    return System(elements=[road], interactions=[vehicles, momentum])

class GasKineticTrafficElement(Element):
    """Cell of a road with the traffic density `rho` and the flow `Q` of the gas-kinetic-based traffic model.

    The density and the flow are conserved by conservation interactions, and the flow relaxes to a dynamic equilibrium
    speed that brakes on the density and the speed read ahead at the interaction point. Lengths are in kilometres and
    times in hours, so `T` and `tau` are fractions of an hour.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the cell or the road.

        visual:
            How the cell is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        rho:
            The initial density in vehicles per kilometre.

        Q:
            The initial flow in vehicles per hour.

        V0:
            The desired speed.

        T:
            The safe time headway.

        tau:
            The relaxation time of the speed.

        rho_max:
            The maximum density.

        gamma:
            The anticipation factor, the interaction distance in units of the safe distance `1 / rho_max + T V`.

        A0:
            The variance prefactor of free traffic.

        dA:
            The increase of the variance prefactor from free to congested traffic, halved.

        rho_c:
            The density of the transition of the variance prefactor.

        d_rho:
            The width of the transition of the variance prefactor.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import GasKineticTrafficElement
        >>> GasKineticTrafficElement('cell').gamma
        1.2
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        rho: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 20.0,
        Q: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1800.0,
        V0: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 110.0,
        T: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.8 / 3600,
        tau: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 35 / 3600,
        rho_max: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 160.0,
        gamma: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.2,
        A0: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.008,
        dA: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.02,
        rho_c: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.27 * 160,
        d_rho: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.05 * 160,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.rho = rho
        self.Q = Q
        self.V0 = V0
        self.T = T
        self.tau = tau
        self.rho_max = rho_max
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.A0 = A0
        self.dA = dA
        self.rho_c = rho_c
        self.d_rho = d_rho

class ConservationInteraction(Interaction):
    """Conservation law `du/dt + divergence(flux(ns)) = source(ns)` of a state `u` of a field.

    The flux is one expression for a field of one dimension, or one expression per dimension, of the states of the
    field, and the interaction lowers it to a finite-volume flux law with a slope limiter and a numerical flux, or,
    without a numerical flux, to the rate `-divergence(flux)` that the field discretizes by its own operators, as a
    spectral or finite-difference field does. Without a source the total of the state on a periodic field stays
    constant. The conservation laws of several states of one field form one system, whose numerical flux reads the
    wave speeds of all of them, and a flux may read parameters that vary across the cells. A flux or a source function
    takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespace `target` of the field, the time `t`, and the symbols of
    the parameters a subclass declares.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the field whose state is conserved.

        state:
            The name of the conserved state of the field.

        flux:
            A function of the namespace that returns the flux, or one flux per dimension.

        source:
            A function of the namespace that returns the source, or `None` for none.

        limiter:
            The slope limiter of the reconstruction, `'minmod'`, `'van-leer'`, or `None` for first order.

        riemann:
            The numerical flux of a finite-volume field, `'rusanov'` or `'godunov'`, the exact solver for one state, or
            `None` for the divergence of the flux on a field of another discretization.

        sources:
            The paths of other elements the flux and the source read, as the namespaces `sources`. A field over the
            position lattice of a target on a phase space is read broadcast along the class axes.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The state is not a name, a function is not callable, or the limiter or the numerical flux is unknown.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element, FieldElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import ConservationInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.spaces import LatticeSpace
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> class CellElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, u: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.u = u
        >>> space = LatticeSpace((50,), spacing=0.1, boundary='periodic')
        >>> values = {'u': 1.0 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.arange(50) / 50)}
        >>> volumes = 'finite-volume'
        >>> field = FieldElement('wave', element=CellElement, space=space, values=values, discretization=volumes)
        >>> burgers = ConservationInteraction('burgers', target='wave', state='u', flux=lambda s: s.target.u**2 / 2)
        >>> system = System(elements=[field], interactions=[burgers])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=0.5).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('wave.u')[-1].sum()), 6)
        50.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'u',
        flux: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        source: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        limiter: str | None = 'minmod',
        riemann: str | None = 'rusanov',
        sources: Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)] = (),
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.state = state
        self.flux = flux
        self.source = source
        self.limiter = limiter
        self.riemann = riemann
        self.sources = sources

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, a function that is not callable, or an unknown scheme.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, the state is not a name, a function is not callable, or the limiter or the
                numerical flux is unknown.
        """
        super()._check()
        if not isinstance(self.state, str) or not self.state.isidentifier():
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} conserves the state {self.state!r}, which is no name.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        for name in ('flux', 'source'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and not callable(value):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function of the namespace.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.limiter not in LIMITERS:
            error_msg = f'Unknown limiter {self.limiter!r} of {self.label!r}. Use minmod, van-leer, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.riemann not in RIEMANN_SOLVERS:
            error_msg = f'Unknown numerical flux {self.riemann!r} of {self.label!r}. Use rusanov, godunov, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_flux(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the flux, or `None` for none, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its arguments."""
        return None if self.flux is None else self.flux(namespace)

    def _get_transport_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the laws of the divergence of the flux, the hook a subclass overrides to lower its own flux."""
        flux = self._get_flux(namespace)
        if flux is None:
            return []
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        if self.riemann is None:
            components = list(flux) if isinstance(flux, FreeModuleElement | list | tuple) else [flux]
            return [RateLaw(state, -divergence(components))]
        return [FluxLaw(state, flux, limiter=self.limiter, riemann=self.riemann)]

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the laws of the divergence of the flux and the rate of the source.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespace of the field.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The flux law, and the rate law of the source when there is one.
        """
        laws = self._get_transport_laws(namespace)
        if self.source is not None:
            laws.append(RateLaw(getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state), self.source(namespace)))
        return laws

docs.title: Intelligent driver model
docs.text:
The intelligent driver model of cars on a ring road.

  • Name: intelligent_driver_model
  • Field: engineering/traffic
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Treiber, Hennecke, and Helbing 2000; Chowdhury, Santen, and Schadschneider 2000

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/traffic',
    tags=('traffic', 'jams', 'ode', 'car following'),
    references=('Treiber, Hennecke, and Helbing 2000', 'Chowdhury, Santen, and Schadschneider 2000'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 1.0},
)
def intelligent_driver_model(
    n_cars: int = 20,
    length: float = 500.0,
    *,
    v0: float = 30.0,
    T: float = 1.5,
    a: float = 1.0,
    b: float = 1.5,
    s0: float = 2.0,
    delta: float = 4.0,
    car_length: float = 5.0,
    perturbation: float = 1.0,
) -> System:
    """Return the intelligent driver model of cars on a ring road.

    Car `i` accelerates as `v' = a (1 - (v / v0)^δ - (s* / s)^2)` with the gap `s` to the car ahead and the desired
    gap `s* = s0 + v T + v Δv / (2 sqrt(a b))`, where `Δv` is the speed difference to the car ahead. Cars start at rest.
    The cars are one group, and the car ahead of car `i` is member `i + 1` along the ring.

    Args:
        n_cars:
            The number of cars.

        length:
            The length of the ring road.

        v0:
            The desired speed.

        T:
            The safe time headway.

        a:
            The largest acceleration.

        b:
            The comfortable deceleration.

        s0:
            The jam distance.

        delta:
            The acceleration exponent.

        car_length:
            The length of a car, subtracted from the headway to give the gap.

        perturbation:
            The forward shift of the first car from uniform spacing.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `cars` of positions `cars.x` and speeds `cars.v`, car `i + 1` ahead of car `i`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import intelligent_driver_model
        >>> intelligent_driver_model(n_cars=4).interactions[0].road_length
        500.0
    """
    cars = GroupElement(
        'cars',
        element=CarElement,
        size=n_cars,
        values={'x': _ring_positions(n_cars, length, perturbation), 'v': 0.0},
    )
    following = IntelligentDriverInteraction(
        'follow',
        target='cars',
        v0=v0,
        T=T,
        a=a,
        b=b,
        s0=s0,
        delta=delta,
        length=car_length,
        road_length=length,
    )
    return System(elements=[cars], interactions=[following])

class CarElement(Element):
    """Car on a road whose position `x` advances at its speed `v`."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='position')] = 0.0,
        v: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='velocity')] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.v = v

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the advance of the position at the speed."""
        return [RateLaw(s.x, s.v)]

class IntelligentDriverInteraction(RateInteraction):
    """Acceleration of every car of a ring road by the intelligent driver model of its speed and the car ahead.

    The speed follows `v' = a (1 - (v / v0)^δ - (s*(v, Δv) / (h - l))^2)`, with the desired gap
    `s* = s0 + v T + v Δv / (2 sqrt(a b))`, the approach rate `Δv` to the next car, and the headway `h` less the car
    length `l`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        target:
            The path of the group of cars, in the order they drive.

        v0:
            The desired speed.

        T:
            The safe time headway.

        a:
            The largest acceleration.

        b:
            The comfortable deceleration.

        s0:
            The jam distance.

        delta:
            The acceleration exponent.

        length:
            The length of a car.

        road_length:
            The length of the ring road.

    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        v0: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 30.0,
        T: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.5,
        a: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        b: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.5,
        s0: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 2.0,
        delta: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 4.0,
        length: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 5.0,
        road_length: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 500.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, state='v')
        self.v0 = v0
        self.T = T
        self.a = a
        self.b = b
        self.s0 = s0
        self.delta = delta
        self.length = length
        self.road_length = road_length

    def _get_rate(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the acceleration of the intelligent driver model."""
        s, cars = namespace, namespace.target
        gap = s.s0 + cars.v * s.T + cars.v * (cars.v - shift_member(cars.v, 1)) / (2 * sqrt(s.a * s.b))
        return s.a * (
            1
            - (cars.v / s.v0) ** s.delta
            - (gap / (OptimalVelocityInteraction._headway(cars.x, s.road_length) - s.length)) ** 2
        )

docs.text:
The Kerner-Konhäuser model, where viscous traffic flow forms dense moving clusters.

  • Name: kerner_konhauser
  • Field: engineering/traffic
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Kerner and Konhäuser 1993; Chowdhury, Santen, and Schadschneider 2000

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/traffic',
    tags=('traffic', 'field', 'conservation law', 'finite volume', 'jams', 'pde'),
    references=('Kerner and Konhäuser 1993', 'Chowdhury, Santen, and Schadschneider 2000'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 0.2, 'solver': SSPRKSolver(cfl=0.15)},
)
def kerner_konhauser(
    n: int = 40,
    *,
    length: float = 10.0,
    density: float = 0.25,
    bump: float = 0.1,
    V0: float = 1.0,
    rho_max: float = 1.0,
    tau: float = 1.0,
    c0: float = 0.45,
    mu: float = 0.2,
) -> System:
    """Return the Kerner-Konhäuser model, where viscous traffic flow forms dense moving clusters.

    The density and the flow `q = rho v` on a ring road follow `rho_t + q_x = 0` and
    `q_t + (q^2 / rho + c0^2 rho)_x = (rho V(rho) - q) / τ + μ v_xx`, with the equilibrium speed
    `V(rho) = V0 (1 / (1 + exp((rho / rho_max - 0.25) / 0.06)) - 3.72e-6)`. The flow starts in equilibrium with a
    bump of density, which grows into a cluster at intermediate densities.

    Args:
        n:
            The number of cells.

        length:
            The length of the ring road.

        density:
            The mean density.

        bump:
            The relative height of the density bump.

        V0:
            The scale of the equilibrium speed.

        rho_max:
            The jam density.

        tau:
            The relaxation time of the speed.

        c0:
            The speed of sound of the traffic pressure `c0^2 rho`.

        mu:
            The viscosity.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the density `road.rho` and the flow `road.q`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import kerner_konhauser
        >>> kerner_konhauser(10).elements[0].values['mu']
        0.2
    """
    rho = _density_bump(n, density, bump)
    values = {
        'rho': rho,
        'q': rho * _kerner_konhauser_speed(rho, V0, rho_max),
        'V0': V0,
        'rho_max': rho_max,
        'tau': tau,
        'c0': c0,
        'mu': mu,
    }
    space = LatticeSpace(n, spacing=length / n)
    road = FieldElement(
        'road',
        element=KernerKonhauserElement,
        space=space,
        values=values,
        discretization='finite-volume',
    )
    density = ConservationInteraction('density', target='road', state='rho', flux=lambda s: s.target.q)
    flow = ConservationInteraction(
        'flow',
        target='road',
        state='q',
        flux=lambda s: s.target.q**2 / s.target.rho + s.target.c0**2 * s.target.rho,
    )
    relaxation = RelaxationInteraction(
        'relaxation',
        target='road',
        state='q',
        goal=lambda s: s.target.rho * _get_kerner_konhauser_speed(s.target),
        time=lambda s: s.target.tau,
    )
    viscosity = RateInteraction(
        'viscosity',
        target='road',
        state='q',
        rate=lambda s: s.target.mu * laplacian(s.target.q / s.target.rho),
    )
    return System(elements=[road], interactions=[density, flow, relaxation, viscosity])

<pre><code>class KernerKonhauserElement(Element):
    """Cell of a road with the traffic density `rho` and the flow `q` of the Kerner-Konhäuser model.

    The density and the flow are conserved by conservation interactions, the flow relaxes to the equilibrium flow by a
    relaxation interaction, and the viscosity adds the rate `mu laplacian(q / rho)` to the flow.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        rho: Annotated[object, StateSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.3,
        q: Annotated[object, StateSpec()] = 0.21,
        V0: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        rho_max: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        tau: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
        c0: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.3,
        mu: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.05,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.rho = rho
        self.q = q
        self.V0 = V0
        self.rho_max = rho_max
        self.tau = tau
        self.c0 = c0
        self.mu = mu

class ConservationInteraction(Interaction):
    """Conservation law `du/dt + divergence(flux(ns)) = source(ns)` of a state `u` of a field.

    The flux is one expression for a field of one dimension, or one expression per dimension, of the states of the
    field, and the interaction lowers it to a finite-volume flux law with a slope limiter and a numerical flux, or,
    without a numerical flux, to the rate `-divergence(flux)` that the field discretizes by its own operators, as a
    spectral or finite-difference field does. Without a source the total of the state on a periodic field stays
    constant. The conservation laws of several states of one field form one system, whose numerical flux reads the
    wave speeds of all of them, and a flux may read parameters that vary across the cells. A flux or a source function
    takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespace `target` of the field, the time `t`, and the symbols of
    the parameters a subclass declares.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the field whose state is conserved.

        state:
            The name of the conserved state of the field.

        flux:
            A function of the namespace that returns the flux, or one flux per dimension.

        source:
            A function of the namespace that returns the source, or `None` for none.

        limiter:
            The slope limiter of the reconstruction, `'minmod'`, `'van-leer'`, or `None` for first order.

        riemann:
            The numerical flux of a finite-volume field, `'rusanov'` or `'godunov'`, the exact solver for one state, or
            `None` for the divergence of the flux on a field of another discretization.

        sources:
            The paths of other elements the flux and the source read, as the namespaces `sources`. A field over the
            position lattice of a target on a phase space is read broadcast along the class axes.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The state is not a name, a function is not callable, or the limiter or the numerical flux is unknown.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element, FieldElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import ConservationInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.spaces import LatticeSpace
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> class CellElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, u: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.u = u
        >>> space = LatticeSpace((50,), spacing=0.1, boundary='periodic')
        >>> values = {'u': 1.0 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.arange(50) / 50)}
        >>> volumes = 'finite-volume'
        >>> field = FieldElement('wave', element=CellElement, space=space, values=values, discretization=volumes)
        >>> burgers = ConservationInteraction('burgers', target='wave', state='u', flux=lambda s: s.target.u**2 / 2)
        >>> system = System(elements=[field], interactions=[burgers])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=0.5).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('wave.u')[-1].sum()), 6)
        50.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'u',
        flux: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        source: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        limiter: str | None = 'minmod',
        riemann: str | None = 'rusanov',
        sources: Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)] = (),
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.state = state
        self.flux = flux
        self.source = source
        self.limiter = limiter
        self.riemann = riemann
        self.sources = sources

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, a function that is not callable, or an unknown scheme.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, the state is not a name, a function is not callable, or the limiter or the
                numerical flux is unknown.
        """
        super()._check()
        if not isinstance(self.state, str) or not self.state.isidentifier():
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} conserves the state {self.state!r}, which is no name.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        for name in ('flux', 'source'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and not callable(value):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function of the namespace.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.limiter not in LIMITERS:
            error_msg = f'Unknown limiter {self.limiter!r} of {self.label!r}. Use minmod, van-leer, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.riemann not in RIEMANN_SOLVERS:
            error_msg = f'Unknown numerical flux {self.riemann!r} of {self.label!r}. Use rusanov, godunov, or None.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_flux(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the flux, or `None` for none, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its arguments."""
        return None if self.flux is None else self.flux(namespace)

    def _get_transport_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the laws of the divergence of the flux, the hook a subclass overrides to lower its own flux."""
        flux = self._get_flux(namespace)
        if flux is None:
            return []
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        if self.riemann is None:
            components = list(flux) if isinstance(flux, FreeModuleElement | list | tuple) else [flux]
            return [RateLaw(state, -divergence(components))]
        return [FluxLaw(state, flux, limiter=self.limiter, riemann=self.riemann)]

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the laws of the divergence of the flux and the rate of the source.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespace of the field.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The flux law, and the rate law of the source when there is one.
        """
        laws = self._get_transport_laws(namespace)
        if self.source is not None:
            laws.append(RateLaw(getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state), self.source(namespace)))
        return laws

class RelaxationInteraction(RateInteraction):
    """Relaxation `(goal(ns) - x) / time(ns)` of a state `x` of a target towards a goal, with optional noise.

    With a constant goal and time and an additive noise of amplitude `sigma`, the state follows the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck
    process `dx = (goal - x) / time dt + sigma dW`, whose stationary variance is `sigma**2 time / 2`. Without noise it
    is first-order smoothing, or adaptive expectation, towards the goal. A goal or a time function takes the namespace
    of the interaction, as for `RateInteraction`, and a number stands for a constant. A goal that is a number applies
    to every component of a vector state.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose state relaxes.

        state:
            The name of the state of the target that relaxes.

        goal:
            A function of the namespace that returns the goal, or a number.

        time:
            A function of the namespace that returns the relaxation time, or a positive number.

        noise:
            A function of the namespace that returns the amplitude of the noise, a number, or `None` for no noise.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The state is not a name, or a function is neither callable nor a number.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import CompartmentElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import RelaxationInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> smoothing = RelaxationInteraction('smoothing', target='belief', state='n', goal=10.0, time=0.5)
        >>> system = System(elements=[CompartmentElement('belief', n=0.0)], interactions=[smoothing])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=5.0).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('belief.n')[-1]), 3)
        10.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'x',
        goal: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float = 0.0,
        time: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float = 1.0,
        noise: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, state=state, noise=noise)
        self.goal = goal
        self.time = time

    def _check_functions(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, or a function that is neither callable nor a number."""
        super()._check_functions()
        for name in ('goal', 'time'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if not (callable(value) or isinstance(value, int | float)):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function of the namespace or a number.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_goal(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the goal, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        return self._evaluate(self.goal, namespace)

    def _get_time(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the relaxation time, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        return self._evaluate(self.time, namespace)

    def _get_rate(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the relaxation `(goal - x) / time` of the state.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the rate can use.

        Returns:
            rate:
                The rate of the state.
        """
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        goal = self._broadcast(self._get_goal(namespace), state)
        return (goal - state) / self._get_time(namespace)

class RateInteraction(Interaction):
    """Rate `rate(ns)` and noise `noise(ns) dW` added to the highest time derivative of a state of a target.

    On a state of order 1 the rate is its first derivative, and on a state of order `k` it adds to the `k`-th
    derivative, so rates on one state superpose. With a divisor `d` the rate and the noise are divided by `d`, the name
    of a state or parameter of the target, such as an inertia, a friction, or a capacitance, which backends can read.

    A rate, a noise, or a divisor function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces `target` and
    `sources` of the bound elements, the time `t`, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares. A number
    stands for a constant, and a number on a vector state applies to every component. The noise is a Wiener process per
    component and member by default, a process of a `WienerProcessSpec` to share or correlate it across states and
    members, or a fractional Brownian motion of a Hurst index.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose state the rate changes.

        state:
            The name of the state of the target that the rate changes.

        rate:
            A function of the namespace that returns the rate, or a number.

        sources:
            The paths of the elements or groups the rate and the noise read but do not change.

        noise:
            A function of the namespace that returns the amplitude of the noise, a number, or `None` for no noise.

        divisor:
            The name of the state or parameter of the target that divides the rate and the noise, a function of the
            namespace of the target that returns the divisor, such as a moment of inertia `m l^2`, or `None`.

        process:
            The Wiener processes that drive the noise, or `None` for one independent process per component and member.

        index:
            The process of `process` that drives the noise, or `None` for every process, one per component of a vector
            state.

        convention:
            The stochastic calculus of the noise, `'ito'`, `'stratonovich'`, or `'anti-ito'`.

        hurst:
            The Hurst index in `(0, 1)` of a fractional Brownian motion that drives the noise, a number or a function
            of the namespace that returns a parameter, or `None` for a Wiener process.

        conserved:
            Whether the noise is the divergence of a random flux on the links of the lattice of a field, so it keeps the
            total of the state.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The state is not a name, a function is neither callable nor a number, the convention is unknown, the Hurst
            index is outside `(0, 1)`, or the noise options cannot combine.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import CompartmentElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import RateInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> decay = RateInteraction('decay', target='stock', state='n', rate=lambda s: -0.5 * s.target.n)
        >>> system = System(elements=[CompartmentElement('stock', n=8.0)], interactions=[decay])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=2.0).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('stock.n')[-1]), 3)
        2.943
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'x',
        rate: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float = 0.0,
        sources: Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)] = (),
        noise: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float | None = None,
        divisor: str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        process: Annotated[WienerProcessSpec | None, RoleSpec(noise=True)] = None,
        index: int | None = None,
        convention: str = 'ito',
        hurst: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float | None = None,
        conserved: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.state = state
        self.rate = rate
        self.sources = sources
        self.noise = noise
        self.divisor = divisor
        self.process = process
        self.index = index
        self.convention = convention
        self.hurst = hurst
        self.conserved = conserved

    def _check_functions(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, or a function that is neither callable nor a number."""
        if not isinstance(self.state, str) or not self.state.isidentifier():
            error_msg = (
                f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} changes the state {self.state!r}, which is not a name of a '
                'state.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        for name in ('rate', 'noise'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if not (value is None or callable(value) or isinstance(value, int | float)):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function of the namespace or a number.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not (
            self.divisor is None
            or callable(self.divisor)
            or (isinstance(self.divisor, str) and self.divisor.isidentifier())
        ):
            error_msg = (
                f'The divisor of {self.label!r} is {self.divisor!r}. Give the name of a state or parameter, or a '
                'function of the namespace of the target.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check_noise(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown convention, a Hurst index outside `(0, 1)`, or noise options that conflict."""
        if self.convention not in CONVENTIONS:
            error_msg = f'Unknown noise convention {self.convention!r}. Use one of {", ".join(CONVENTIONS)}.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not (
            self.hurst is None or callable(self.hurst) or (isinstance(self.hurst, int | float) and 0 < self.hurst < 1)
        ):
            error_msg = f'The Hurst index of {self.label!r} is {self.hurst!r}. Give a number in (0, 1) or a function.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.index is not None and self.process is None:
            error_msg = f'{self.label!r} picks the process {self.index!r} but binds no processes. Give `process`.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        options = [
            name
            for name, given in (('hurst', self.hurst), ('process', self.process), ('conserved', self.conserved))
            if given
        ]
        if len(options) > 1:
            error_msg = f'The noise of {self.label!r} takes {" and ".join(options)}. Give at most one of them.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state, functions, or noise options the interaction cannot take.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, the state is not a name, a function is neither callable nor a number, the
                convention is unknown, the Hurst index is outside `(0, 1)`, or the noise options cannot combine.
        """
        super()._check()
        self._check_functions()
        self._check_noise()

    def _evaluate(self, function: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the value of a function of the namespace, or a number as it is."""
        return function(namespace) if callable(function) else function

    def _broadcast(self, value: object, state: object) -> object:
        """Return a value with one component per component of a vector state, repeating a number."""
        if isinstance(state, FreeModuleElement) and not isinstance(value, FreeModuleElement | list | tuple):
            return vector(SR, [value] * len(state))
        if isinstance(value, list | tuple):
            return vector(SR, value)
        return value

    def _divide(self, value: object, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return a value divided by the divisor of the target, or the value without a divisor."""
        if self.divisor is None:
            return value
        divisor = (
            self.divisor(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'))
            if callable(self.divisor)
            else getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.divisor)
        )
        return operator.truediv(value, divisor)

    def _get_rate(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the rate before the divisor, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        return self._evaluate(self.rate, namespace)

    def _get_noise(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the noise amplitude before the divisor, the hook a subclass overrides, or `None` for no noise."""
        return None if self.noise is None else self._evaluate(self.noise, namespace)

    def _get_noise_law(self, state: object, amplitude: object, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> BasePart:
        """Return the noise law of an amplitude, by the process, the convention, and the Hurst index."""
        if self.hurst is not None:
            hurst = self._evaluate(self.hurst, namespace)
            return FractionalNoiseLaw(state, amplitude, hurst=hurst, convention=self.convention)
        process = None
        if self.process is not None:
            handle = self._get_member(namespace, 'process').dW
            process = handle if self.index is None else handle[self.index]
        return NoiseLaw(state, amplitude, convention=self.convention, process=process, conserved=self.conserved)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the rate law of the state and its noise law, both divided by the divisor.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespaces of the target and the sources.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate law, and the noise law when the interaction has noise.
        """
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        rate = self._divide(self._broadcast(self._get_rate(namespace), state), namespace)
        laws: list[BasePart] = [RateLaw(state, rate)]
        noise = self._get_noise(namespace)
        if noise is not None:
            laws.append(self._get_noise_law(state, self._divide(noise, namespace), namespace))
        return laws

docs.title: Langevin car-following toward a density-dependent speed
docs.text:
Cars on a ring road whose speeds relax with noise towards a desired speed set by the local density.

  • Name: langevin_traffic
  • Field: engineering/traffic
  • Formalism: stochastic differential equations
  • References: Bertin 2021

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='engineering/traffic',
    tags=('traffic', 'sde', 'langevin', 'car following'),
    references=('Bertin 2021',),
    defaults={'until': 200.0, 'dt': 1.0, 'solver': EulerMaruyamaSolver(dt=0.01)},
)
def langevin_traffic(
    n_cars: int = 50,
    length: float = 100.0,
    *,
    gamma: float = 3.0,
    u0: float = 1.0,
    rho_max: float = 1.0,
    D1: float = 0.05,
) -> System:
    """Return cars on a ring road whose speeds relax with noise towards a desired speed set by the local density.

    Car `i` follows `dv_i = -gamma (v_i - u(rho_i)) dt + sqrt(2 D(rho_i)) dW` with the desired speed
    `u(rho) = u0 (1 - rho / rho_max)` and the noise intensity `D(rho) = D1 rho`, where the local density `rho_i` is the
    inverse of the headway to the car ahead. Cars start evenly spaced at the speed `u(rho)` of the mean density
    `rho = n_cars / length`. The mean speed stays at `u(rho)`, so the mean flow follows the fundamental diagram
    `rho u(rho)`, and the speeds fluctuate with the variance `D1 rho / gamma`. The uniform flow is linearly stable while
    `u0 rho^2 / rho_max < gamma / 2`, as for the optimal velocity model. Strong noise lets cars pass each other, and the
    headway of a car that has passed the car ahead wraps around the ring.

    Args:
        n_cars:
            The number of cars.

        length:
            The length of the ring road.

        gamma:
            The relaxation rate of the speed.

        u0:
            The desired speed on an empty road.

        rho_max:
            The jam density, at which the desired speed vanishes.

        D1:
            The noise intensity per unit density.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the group `cars` of positions `cars.x` and speeds `cars.v`, car `i + 1` ahead of car `i`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import langevin_traffic
        >>> float(langevin_traffic(n_cars=10, length=20.0).elements[0].values['v'][0])
        0.5
    """
    density = n_cars / length
    positions = np.arange(n_cars) * length / n_cars
    cars = GroupElement(
        'cars',
        element=CarElement,
        size=n_cars,
        values={'x': positions, 'v': np.full(n_cars, u0 * (1 - density / rho_max))},
    )
    driving = LangevinDrivingInteraction(
        'drive',
        target='cars',
        gamma=gamma,
        u0=u0,
        rho_max=rho_max,
        D1=D1,
        road_length=length,
    )
    return System(elements=[cars], interactions=[driving])

class CarElement(Element):
    """Car on a road whose position `x` advances at its speed `v`."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='position')] = 0.0,
        v: Annotated[object, StateSpec(role='velocity')] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.v = v

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the advance of the position at the speed."""
        return [RateLaw(s.x, s.v)]

class LangevinDrivingInteraction(RelaxationInteraction):
    """Relaxation of the speed of every car of a ring road towards the speed of its local density, with noise.

    The speed follows `dv = -gamma (v - u(rho)) dt + sqrt(2 D1 rho) dW`, with the desired speed
    `u(rho) = u0 (1 - rho / rho_max)` of the density `rho`, the inverse of the headway to the next car, an
    Ornstein-Uhlenbeck relaxation over the time `1 / gamma` with a noise that grows with the density.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        target:
            The path of the group of cars, in the order they drive.

        gamma:
            The relaxation rate.

        u0:
            The desired speed on an empty road.

        rho_max:
            The jam density.

        D1:
            The strength of the noise.

        road_length:
            The length of the ring road.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.engineering.traffic import LangevinDrivingInteraction
        >>> LangevinDrivingInteraction('drive', target='cars', gamma=2.0).state
        'v'
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        gamma: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 3.0,
        u0: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        rho_max: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        D1: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.05,
        road_length: Annotated[object, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 100.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, state='v')
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.u0 = u0
        self.rho_max = rho_max
        self.D1 = D1
        self.road_length = road_length

    def _get_goal(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the desired speed of the local density of every car."""
        return LangevinDrivingInteraction._target_speed(
            LangevinDrivingInteraction._local_density(namespace.target.x, namespace.road_length),
            namespace,
        )

    def _get_time(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the relaxation time `1 / gamma`."""
        return 1 / namespace.gamma

    def _get_noise(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the amplitude `sqrt(2 D1 rho)` of the noise of the local density."""
        return sqrt(
            2 * namespace.D1 * LangevinDrivingInteraction._local_density(namespace.target.x, namespace.road_length),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _target_speed(density: Expression, s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the desired speed `u(rho) = u0 (1 - rho / rho_max)` at a density."""
        return s.u0 * (1 - density / s.rho_max)

    @staticmethod
    def _local_density(x: Expression, road_length: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return the density seen by every car of a ring road, the inverse of its headway."""
        return 1 / OptimalVelocityInteraction._headway(x, road_length)
