class VicsekParticleElement(Element):
    """Particle of a Vicsek flock, whose heading becomes the mean heading of its neighbours plus noise every step.

    `HeadingAlignmentInteraction` sets the new heading to the circular mean of the headings within the unit distance,
    itself included, plus a uniform angle in `[-eta pi, eta pi]`. A propulsion step moves the particle along its
    heading.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the particle or the group.

        visual:
            How the particle is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x:
            The initial position.

        theta:
            The initial heading.

        eta:
            The amplitude of the noise, as a fraction of `pi`.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the particle when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.active_matter import VicsekParticleElement
        >>> VicsekParticleElement('bird').eta
        0.1
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[npt.ArrayLike, StateSpec(vector=True, role='position')] = 0.0,
        theta: Annotated[float, StateSpec(period=2 * pi, role='direction')] = 0.0,
        eta: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.1,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.theta = theta
        self.eta = eta

class PropulsionStepInteraction(MapInteraction):
    """Step `x(t + 1) = x + speed (cos theta, sin theta)` of a position in the plane along a heading, in discrete time.

    The step reads the heading at the start of the step, as every map of the step does.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the particle or the group whose positions move.

        speed:
            The distance moved in one step.

        state:
            The name of the vector state that holds the position.

        heading:
            The name of the state that holds the heading.

    Examples:
        >>> from types import SimpleNamespace
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var, vector
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.active_matter import PropulsionStepInteraction
        >>> step = PropulsionStepInteraction('propulsion', target='flock').check().prepare()
        >>> target = SimpleNamespace(x=vector([var('x1'), var('x2')]), theta=var('theta'))
        >>> [law.value for law in step.run(SimpleNamespace(target=target, speed=var('v'))).laws_]
        [(v*cos(theta) + x1, v*sin(theta) + x2)]
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        speed: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        state: str = 'x',
        heading: str = 'theta',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, state=state, function=self._step, mode='increment')
        self.speed = speed
        self.heading = heading

    def _step(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> FreeModuleElement:
        """Return the step `speed (cos theta, sin theta)`."""
        heading = getattr(namespace.target, self.heading)
        return namespace.speed * vector(SR, [cos(heading), sin(heading)])

class HeadingAlignmentInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Vicsek alignment, the turn of every particle to the circular mean heading of its neighbours plus noise.

    Every step the heading `theta` of every particle becomes the circular mean of the headings within the unit
    distance, itself included, plus a uniform angle in `[-eta pi, eta pi]` with the parameter `eta` of the particle.
    With `nematic`, every heading is flipped to the side nearer the particle's own heading first, as for particles
    with an axis rather than a direction. It is the map form of coupling with the circular mean over a radius.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group of particles.

        nematic:
            Whether every heading is flipped to the side nearer the particle's own heading.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.active_matter import HeadingAlignmentInteraction
        >>> HeadingAlignmentInteraction('alignment', target='flock', nematic=True).reduce
        'circular-mean'
    """

    def __init__(self, label: str, *, target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()], nematic: bool = False) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            read='theta',
            write='theta',
            function=self._get_heading,
            reduce='circular-mean',
            weights=self._get_side,
            form='map',
            combine=self._get_noisy,
            neighborhood=RadiusNeighborhood(1.0, center=True),
        )
        self.nematic = nematic

    @staticmethod
    def _get_heading(namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the heading of the neighbour."""
        return namespace.other.theta

    def _get_side(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return -1 for a neighbour heading away from the particle when nematic, and 1 otherwise."""
        if not self.nematic:
            return SR(1)
        return where(cos(namespace.other.theta - namespace.member.theta) >= 0, 1, -1)

    @staticmethod
    def _get_noisy(namespace: SimpleNamespace, reduction: Target) -> Target:
        """Return the mean heading plus a uniform angle in `[-eta pi, eta pi]`."""
        eta = namespace.member.eta
        return reduction + uniform('noise', -eta * math.pi, eta * math.pi)

docs.text:
Bodies in the plane that attract each other pairwise by Newtonian gravity.

  • Name: n_body
  • Field: physics/celestial_mechanics
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Argun et al. 2021; Dilão 2023; Chenciner and Montgomery 2000

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/celestial_mechanics',
    tags=('mechanics', 'ode', 'gravity', 'chaos'),
    references=('Argun et al. 2021', 'Dilão 2023', 'Chenciner and Montgomery 2000'),
    defaults={'until': 6.33, 'dt': 0.01},
)
def n_body(
    preset: str = 'figure_eight',
    *,
    masses: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    positions: Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None = None,
    velocities: Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None = None,
    G: float | None = None,
) -> System:
    """Return bodies in the plane that attract each other pairwise by Newtonian gravity.

    The preset `'figure_eight'` is the periodic orbit of three equal masses found by Chenciner and Montgomery, with
    period 6.3259 for `G = 1`. The preset `'inner_solar_system'` is the Sun with Mercury, Venus, the Earth, and Mars on
    circular orbits, in astronomical units and years, with `G = 4 π²`. Masses, positions, velocities, or `G` given
    explicitly replace those of the preset.

    Args:
        preset:
            `'figure_eight'` or `'inner_solar_system'`.

        masses:
            The masses of the bodies, or `None` for those of the preset.

        positions:
            The initial positions of the bodies, or `None` for those of the preset.

        velocities:
            The initial velocities of the bodies, or `None` for those of the preset.

        G:
            The gravitational constant, or `None` for that of the preset.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the particles `body_<i>` in two dimensions.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The preset is unknown.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import n_body
        >>> len(n_body('inner_solar_system').interactions)
        10
    """
    preset_G, preset_masses, preset_positions, preset_velocities = _preset(preset)
    masses = preset_masses if masses is None else masses
    positions = preset_positions if positions is None else positions
    velocities = preset_velocities if velocities is None else velocities
    G = preset_G if G is None else G
    bodies = [
        MassPointElement(f'body_{index}', x=list(position), x_d1=list(velocity), m=mass)
        for index, (mass, position, velocity) in enumerate(zip(masses, positions, velocities, strict=True))
    ]
    attractions = [
        GravityInteraction(
            f'gravity_{first}_{second}',
            first=f'body_{first}',
            second=f'body_{second}',
            G=G,
        )
        for first, second in itertools.combinations(range(len(bodies)), 2)
    ]
    return System(elements=bodies, interactions=attractions, space=ContinuousSpace(n_dim=2))

class MassPointElement(PointElement):
    """Point mass, a point whose position `x` has order 2, with its velocity `x_d1` and a mass `m`.

    The forces on the point divide by the mass through their divisor `'m'`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the point.

        x:
            The initial position. A number applies to every component.

        x_d1:
            The initial velocity. A number applies to every component.

        visual:
            How the point is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        m:
            The mass.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            Points at the positions.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.particles import MassPointElement
        >>> MassPointElement('ball', x=[0.0, 1.0], m=2.0).m
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        x: npt.ArrayLike = 0.0,
        x_d1: npt.ArrayLike = 0.0,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        m: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, x=x, x_d1=x_d1, visual=visual)
        self.m = m

class GravityInteraction(PotentialEnergyInteraction):
    """Newtonian gravity between two particles.

    The energy is `-G * m_first * m_second / |x_first - x_second|`, and its gradient moves both particles.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        first:
            The path of the first particle.

        second:
            The path of the second particle.

        G:
            The gravitational constant.

        states:
            The name of the vector state that holds the positions of the particles.

        divisor:
            The name of the state or parameter that holds the masses of the particles.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.particles import GravityInteraction
        >>> GravityInteraction('gravity', first='sun', second='earth', G=1.0).G
        1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        first: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        second: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        G: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        states: str = 'x',
        divisor: str = 'm',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=first, states=states, divisor=divisor)
        self.first = first
        self.second = second
        self.G = G

    def _get_potential(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return `-G * m_first * m_second / |x_first - x_second|`.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the energy can use.

        Returns:
            energy:
                The potential energy as a symbolic expression.
        """
        gap = getattr(s.first, self._get_names()[0]) - getattr(s.second, self._get_names()[0])
        masses = getattr(s.first, str(self.divisor)) * getattr(s.second, str(self.divisor))
        return -s.G * masses / sqrt(gap.dot_product(gap))

docs.title: Restricted three-body problem
docs.text:
A light body moving in the plane of two primaries on circular orbits, in the frame that rotates with them.

  • Name: restricted_three_body
  • Field: physics/celestial_mechanics
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Dilão 2023; Szebehely 1967

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/celestial_mechanics',
    tags=('mechanics', 'ode', 'gravity', 'chaos', 'rotating frame', 'hamiltonian'),
    references=('Dilão 2023', 'Szebehely 1967'),
    defaults={'until': 20.0, 'dt': 0.02, 'solver': RK4Solver(), 'invariants': {'body.energy': 1e-6}},
    observables=_get_rotating_frame_observables,
)
def restricted_three_body(
    x: float = 0.5,
    y: float = 0.0,
    vx: float = 0.0,
    vy: float = 1.15,
    *,
    mu: float = 0.01215,
) -> System:
    """Return a light body moving in the plane of two primaries on circular orbits, in the frame that rotates with them.

    The primaries of masses `1 - μ` and `μ` sit at `(-μ, 0)` and `(1 - μ, 0)`, and the light body moves under the
    Hamiltonian `H = (px² + py²) / 2 + y px - x py - (1 - μ) / r1 - μ / r2` of the rotating frame, with the momenta
    `px = x' - y` and `py = y' + x`. Its terms `y px - x py` couple the coordinates and the momenta, so the Hamiltonian
    is not separable. It equals minus half the Jacobi constant `x² + y² + 2 (1 - μ) / r1 + 2 μ / r2 - x'² - y'²`, which
    is conserved. The default `μ` is that of the Earth and the Moon.

    The default start has the Jacobi constant 2.835, below that of the neck towards the Moon, and its orbit is chaotic:
    it passes near the Moon after 3.5 time units and wanders between the two primaries, with a Lyapunov exponent near
    0.2. Starts of a larger constant are confined around the Earth, such as `vy = 0.8` with the constant 3.52, which
    traces a regular precessing rosette.

    Args:
        x:
            The initial first coordinate.

        y:
            The initial second coordinate.

        vx:
            The initial first velocity.

        vy:
            The initial second velocity.

        mu:
            The mass of the lighter primary, as a fraction of the total.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the coordinates `body.x` and `body.y` and the momenta `body.px` and `body.py`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import restricted_three_body
        >>> restricted_three_body(mu=0.1).elements[0].mu
        0.1
    """
    return System(
        elements=[RotatingFrameBodyElement('body', x=x, y=y, px=vx - y, py=vy + x, mu=mu)],
        interactions=[
            HamiltonianInteraction(
                'motion',
                target='body',
                coordinates=('x', 'y'),
                momenta=('px', 'py'),
                hamiltonian=_get_rotating_frame_hamiltonian,
            ),
        ],
    )

class RotatingFrameBodyElement(Element):
    """Light body at `(x, y)` with the canonical momenta `(px, py)` in the frame that rotates with two primaries.

    The states are of order 1, and the momenta are `px = x' - y` and `py = y' + x` for the unit angular velocity of the
    frame. The primaries of masses `1 - mu` and `mu` sit at `(-mu, 0)` and `(1 - mu, 0)`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the body.

        visual:
            How the body is drawn, or `None` for its class visual.

        x:
            The initial first coordinate.

        y:
            The initial second coordinate.

        px:
            The initial first momentum.

        py:
            The initial second momentum.

        mu:
            The mass of the lighter primary, as a fraction of the total.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import RotatingFrameBodyElement
        >>> RotatingFrameBodyElement('body', mu=0.1).mu
        0.1
    """

    visual = VisualSpec('bodies', {'positions': ('x', 'y'), 'trail': None, 'marks': _primaries})

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.5,
        y: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        px: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        py: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.5,
        mu: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.01215,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.px = px
        self.py = py
        self.mu = mu

class HamiltonianInteraction(Interaction):
    """Hamilton's equations `q' = dH/dp` and `p' = -dH/dq` of the canonical pairs `(q, p)` of a Hamiltonian `H(ns)`.

    The coordinates and the momenta are states of order 1, which may be angles, of every role that binds one element or
    group, `target` by default, and the coordinates pair with the momenta in order. Every component of a vector state
    is a coordinate or a momentum. The interaction returns one rate law per coordinate and per momentum, and the rates
    of one state add, so the Hamiltonians of separate interactions sum: a coupling between two oscillators is an
    interaction of its own whose Hamiltonian holds only the coupling energy. Dissipation or forcing is a rate
    interaction on the momenta.

    A Hamiltonian function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces of the roles, the time `t`, and
    the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose states are the canonical pairs.

        coordinates:
            The name of the state of order 1 that is a coordinate, or the names of several states.

        momenta:
            The name of the state of order 1 that is the momentum of the coordinate, or the names of several states in
            the order of the coordinates.

        hamiltonian:
            A function of the namespace that returns the Hamiltonian.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            A state is not a name, the coordinates and the momenta differ in count, the Hamiltonian is not callable,
            or a coordinate and its momentum differ in size or are not of order 1.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import HamiltonianInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> class OscillatorElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, q: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0, p: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.q = q
        ...         self.p = p
        >>> energy = lambda s: (s.target.p**2 + s.target.q**2) / 2
        >>> spring = HamiltonianInteraction('spring', target='mass', hamiltonian=energy)
        >>> system = System(elements=[OscillatorElement('mass')], interactions=[spring])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=3.14159).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('mass.q')[-1]), 3)
        -1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        coordinates: str | Sequence[str] = 'q',
        momenta: str | Sequence[str] = 'p',
        hamiltonian: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.coordinates = coordinates
        self.momenta = momenta
        self.hamiltonian = hamiltonian

    def _get_names(self, names: str | Sequence[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Return the names of the states of one side of the canonical pairs."""
        return (names,) if isinstance(names, str) else tuple(names)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, an unpaired state, or a Hamiltonian that is not callable.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, a state is not a name, the coordinates and the momenta differ in count, or
                the Hamiltonian is not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        for side in ('coordinates', 'momenta'):
            names = self._get_names(getattr(self, side))
            if not names or not all(isinstance(name, str) and name.isidentifier() for name in names):
                error_msg = f'The {side} of {self.label!r} are {getattr(self, side)!r}. Give names of states.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        coordinates, momenta = self._get_names(self.coordinates), self._get_names(self.momenta)
        if len(coordinates) != len(momenta):
            unpaired = coordinates[len(momenta) :] or momenta[len(coordinates) :]
            error_msg = (
                f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} pairs the coordinates {coordinates} with the momenta {momenta}, '
                f'so {", ".join(unpaired)} has no partner. Give one momentum per coordinate.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.hamiltonian is not None and not callable(self.hamiltonian):
            error_msg = f'The hamiltonian of {self.label!r} is {self.hamiltonian!r}. Give a function of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_hamiltonian(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the Hamiltonian, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        if self.hamiltonian is None:
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} has no Hamiltonian. Give a function of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        return self.hamiltonian(namespace)

    def _get_members(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[SimpleNamespace]:
        """Return the namespaces of the members whose states are canonical pairs, those of every role of one path."""
        return [
            getattr(namespace, name)
            for name, spec in self._get_specs().items()
            if isinstance(spec, RoleSpec) and not spec.variadic and not spec.noise
        ]

    def _get_state(self, member: SimpleNamespace, name: str) -> Target:
        """Return a canonical state of a member, after checking that it has order 1."""
        if hasattr(member, f'{name}_d1'):
            error_msg = (
                f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} reads the state {name} of order above 1, but canonical '
                'coordinates and momenta have order 1. Declare it with `StateSpec(order=1)`, or derive the equations '
                'of a coordinate of order 2 with `EulerLagrangeInteraction`.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        state: Target = getattr(member, name)
        return state

    def _get_pairs(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[tuple[Target, Target]]:
        """Return the canonical pairs of every member, after checking that each coordinate matches its momentum."""
        pairs = []
        names = list(zip(self._get_names(self.coordinates), self._get_names(self.momenta), strict=True))
        for member in self._get_members(namespace):
            for coordinate, momentum in names:
                q, p = self._get_state(member, coordinate), self._get_state(member, momentum)
                if len(self._get_components(q)) != len(self._get_components(p)):
                    error_msg = (
                        f'The coordinate {coordinate} and the momentum {momentum} of {self.label!r} differ in size. '
                        'Give a momentum of the size of its coordinate.'
                    )
                    raise ValidationError(error_msg)
                pairs.append((q, p))
        return pairs

    def _get_components(self, state: Target) -> list[Expression]:
        """Return the components of a state, the state itself for a scalar."""
        return list(state) if isinstance(state, FreeModuleElement) else [state]

    def _get_derivative(self, hamiltonian: Expression, state: Target) -> Target:
        """Return the derivative of the Hamiltonian with respect to a state, every component of a vector state."""
        if isinstance(state, FreeModuleElement):
            return vector(SR, [hamiltonian.diff(component) for component in state])
        return hamiltonian.diff(state)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the rate of every coordinate, `dH/dp`, and of every momentum, `-dH/dq`.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespaces of the roles.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate laws of the coordinates and the momenta.
        """
        pairs = self._get_pairs(namespace)
        hamiltonian = SR(self._get_hamiltonian(namespace))
        laws: list[BasePart] = []
        for q, p in pairs:
            laws.append(RateLaw(q, self._get_derivative(hamiltonian, p)))
            laws.append(RateLaw(p, -self._get_derivative(hamiltonian, q)))
        return laws

docs.text:
A light body moving on the axis through the centre of mass of two equal primaries, normal to their orbit.

  • Name: sitnikov
  • Field: physics/celestial_mechanics
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Dilão 2023; Sitnikov 1960

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/celestial_mechanics',
    tags=('mechanics', 'ode', 'second order', 'gravity', 'chaos'),
    references=('Dilão 2023', 'Sitnikov 1960'),
    defaults={'until': 50.0, 'dt': 0.05},
)
def sitnikov(z: float = 0.5, vz: float = 0.0, *, e: float = 0.0) -> System:
    """Return a light body moving on the axis through the centre of mass of two equal primaries, normal to their orbit.

    The primaries of mass 1/2 orbit their centre of mass with unit mean separation and period `2π`, at distance
    `r(t) = (1 - e cos t) / 2` from it to first order in the eccentricity `e`, and the light body follows
    `z'' = -z / (z² + r(t)²)^(3/2)`. For circular primaries the energy `z'²/2 - 1 / √(z² + 1/4)` is conserved and the
    motion is integrable, and eccentric primaries make bounded orbits chaotic.

    Args:
        z:
            The initial height above the plane of the primaries.

        vz:
            The initial vertical velocity.

        e:
            The eccentricity of the primaries' orbits.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the height `body.z` of order 2.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import sitnikov
        >>> sitnikov(e=0.1).elements[0].e
        0.1
    """
    return System(
        elements=[SitnikovBodyElement('body', z=z, z_d1=vz, e=e)],
        interactions=[GradientInteraction('gravity', target='body', states='z', potential=_get_sitnikov_potential)],
    )

docs.text:
class SitnikovBodyElement(Element):
    """Light body at the height `z`, of order 2, on the axis through the centre of mass of two equal primaries.

    The primaries orbit with the eccentricity `e`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the body.

        visual:
            How the body is drawn, or `None` for none.

        z:
            The initial height.

        z_d1:
            The initial vertical velocity.

        e:
            The eccentricity of the primaries' orbits.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import SitnikovBodyElement
        >>> SitnikovBodyElement('body', e=0.1).e
        0.1
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        z: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=2)] = 0.5,
        z_d1: float = 0.0,
        e: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.z = z
        self.z_d1 = z_d1
        self.e = e

class GradientInteraction(Interaction):
    """Motion of states down the gradient of a potential `U(ns)`, as a gradient flow or as Newtonian motion.

    Every state `x` the interaction moves gets the rate `-dU/dx / d` on its highest time derivative, with `d` the
    divisor of its member: a state or parameter of the member, an expression of them such as a moment of inertia
    `m l^2`, or one divisor per state, such as the masses of two coordinates of one element. On a state of order 1
    this is the gradient flow `x' = -dU/dx / d`, with `d` a friction, and on a state of order 2 it is Newton's law
    `x'' = -dU/dx / d`, with `d` an inertia. A vector state gets the gradient of every component, and a tensor state
    the matrix gradient, the projection of the derivative onto the matrices of its symmetry.

    On a field the potential is the density `f` of a functional `F = integral f`, which may read the field, its
    derivatives `partial(x, k)` or `gradient(x)`, and its `laplacian(x)`. A variational interaction moves the field by
    the functional derivative `dF/dx = df/dx - sum_k partial(df/dx_k, k) + laplacian(df/d laplacian(x))`, as in the
    Allen-Cahn equation, and a conserved interaction gives the rate `laplacian(dF/dx) / d` instead, as in the
    Cahn-Hilliard equation, so the total of the field stays constant.

    The interaction moves the states of every role that binds one element or group, `target` by default. A subclass
    may bind several such roles instead, such as both members of a pair potential, and every one of them moves. The
    potential function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces of the roles and of the `sources`,
    the time `t`, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose states move.

        states:
            The name of the state that moves, or the names of several states.

        potential:
            A function of the namespace that returns the potential, or the density of the functional of a field.

        sources:
            The paths of the elements or groups the potential reads but does not move.

        divisor:
            The name of the state or parameter of every moving member that divides its rate, a function of the
            namespace of the member that returns the divisor, a mapping from the name of every moving state to its
            own divisor, or `None`.

        variational:
            Whether the potential is the density of a functional of a field, moved by its functional derivative.

        conserved:
            Whether the rate is the Laplacian of the derivative of the potential, which conserves the total of a field.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            A state or the divisor is not a name, or the potential is not callable.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import CompartmentElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import GradientInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> well = GradientInteraction('well', target='walker', states='n', potential=lambda s: s.target.n**2 / 2)
        >>> system = System(elements=[CompartmentElement('walker', n=1.0)], interactions=[well])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=1.0).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('walker.n')[-1]), 4)
        0.3679
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        states: str | Sequence[str] = 'x',
        potential: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        sources: Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)] = (),
        divisor: (
            str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | Mapping[str, str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]] | None
        ) = None,
        variational: bool = False,
        conserved: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.states = states
        self.potential = potential
        self.sources = sources
        self.divisor = divisor
        self.variational = variational
        self.conserved = conserved

    def _get_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Return the names of the states the interaction moves."""
        return (self.states,) if isinstance(self.states, str) else tuple(self.states)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state or a divisor that is not a name, or a potential that is not callable.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, a state is not a name, a divisor is neither a name nor a function, or the
                potential is not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        names = self._get_names()
        if not names or not all(isinstance(name, str) and name.isidentifier() for name in names):
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} moves the states {self.states!r}. Give names of states.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        divisors = dict(self.divisor) if isinstance(self.divisor, Mapping) else dict.fromkeys(names, self.divisor)
        valid = all(
            item is None or callable(item) or (isinstance(item, str) and item.isidentifier())
            for item in divisors.values()
        )
        if not valid or not set(divisors) <= set(names):
            error_msg = (
                f'The divisor of {self.label!r} is {self.divisor!r}. Give the name of a state or parameter, a function '
                'of the namespace of the member, or a mapping from the moving states to them.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.potential is not None and not callable(self.potential):
            error_msg = f'The potential of {self.label!r} is {self.potential!r}. Give a function of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_potential(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the potential, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        if self.potential is None:
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} has no potential. Give a function of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        return self.potential(namespace)

    def _get_divisor(self, member: SimpleNamespace, name: str) -> object:
        """Return the divisor of a moving state of a member, or `None` for none."""
        divisor = self.divisor.get(name) if isinstance(self.divisor, Mapping) else self.divisor
        if divisor is None:
            return None
        return getattr(member, divisor) if isinstance(divisor, str) else divisor(member)

    def _get_rate_state(self, member: SimpleNamespace, name: str) -> object:
        """Return the state whose highest derivative gets the rate of a moving state, the moving state itself."""
        return getattr(member, name)

    def _walk(self, expression: Expression) -> Iterator[Expression]:
        """Yield an expression and every subexpression of it."""
        yield expression
        for operand in expression.operands():
            yield from self._walk(operand)

    def _get_flux_divergence(
        self,
        fluxes: dict[int, Expression],
        derivatives: dict[int, Expression],
        field: Expression,
    ) -> Expression:
        """Return `sum_k partial(flux_k, k)`, or `c laplacian(x)` when every flux is `c x_k` along every axis read.

        The Laplacian keeps the compact stencil of the field, which nested first derivatives would widen.
        """
        coefficients = [SR(fluxes[axis] / derivatives[axis]) for axis in sorted(fluxes)]
        coefficient = coefficients[0]
        uniform = sorted(fluxes) == list(range(len(fluxes))) and all(
            item.is_trivially_equal(coefficient) for item in coefficients
        )
        constant = not coefficient.has(field) and not any(coefficient.has(item) for item in derivatives.values())
        if uniform and constant:
            return coefficient * laplacian(field)
        return sum((partial(flux, SR(axis)) for axis, flux in fluxes.items()), SR(0))

    def _get_variation(self, density: Expression, field: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return the functional derivative of the integral of a density with respect to a field."""
        derivatives: dict[int, Expression] = {}
        curvature = None
        for item in self._walk(density):
            kind = item.operator()
            if kind == partial and item.operands()[0].is_trivially_equal(field):
                derivatives[int(item.operands()[1])] = item
            elif kind == laplacian and item.operands()[0].is_trivially_equal(field):
                curvature = item
        slots = {item: SR.var(f'_slot_{axis}') for axis, item in derivatives.items()}
        if curvature is not None:
            slots[curvature] = SR.var('_slot_laplacian')
        flat = density.subs(slots)
        back = {symbol: item for item, symbol in slots.items()}
        variation = flat.diff(field).subs(back)
        fluxes = {axis: flat.diff(slots[item]).subs(back) for axis, item in derivatives.items()}
        if fluxes:
            variation -= self._get_flux_divergence(fluxes, derivatives, field)
        if curvature is not None:
            variation += self._get_laplacian(flat.diff(slots[curvature]).subs(back), field)
        return variation

    def _get_laplacian(self, expression: Expression, field: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return the Laplacian of an expression of a field, term by term, with the factors free of the field outside.

        The linear terms of the field, such as `laplacian(x)`, stay apart, so a spectral discretization finds them.
        """
        expanded = SR(expression).expand()
        terms = expanded.operands() if expanded.operator() is add_vararg else [expanded]
        total = SR(0)
        for term in terms:
            factors = term.operands() if term.operator() is mul_vararg else [term]
            constant = prod((factor for factor in factors if not factor.has(field)), start=SR(1))
            varying = prod((factor for factor in factors if factor.has(field)), start=SR(1))
            if varying.has(field):
                total += constant * laplacian(varying)
        return total

    def _get_matrix_derivative(self, potential: Expression, state: Matrix) -> Matrix:
        """Return the matrix gradient of a potential at a tensor state, written in the matrices of its symmetry.

        The derivative with respect to the independent components is the product of the matrices of the components, the
        metric of the state, and the coefficients of the gradient, so the metric gives the coefficients.
        """
        if self.conserved:
            error_msg = f'{self.label!r} conserves the tensor state {state}. Give a scalar state.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        components = sorted(state.variables(), key=str)
        units = [state.derivative(component) for component in components]
        metric = matrix(SR, [[(first.transpose() * second).trace() for second in units] for first in units])
        density = distribute_operators(potential)
        derivatives = [
            self._get_variation(density, component) if self.variational else density.diff(component)
            for component in components
        ]
        coefficients = metric.inverse() * vector(SR, derivatives)
        total = matrix(SR, state.nrows(), state.ncols())
        for coefficient, unit in zip(coefficients, units, strict=True):
            total += coefficient * unit
        return total

    def _get_derivative(self, potential: Expression, state: Target | Matrix) -> Target | Matrix:
        """Return the derivative of the potential with respect to a state, every component of a vector state."""
        if isinstance(state, Matrix):
            return self._get_matrix_derivative(potential, state)
        if isinstance(state, FreeModuleElement):
            if self.variational or self.conserved:
                error_msg = f'{self.label!r} moves the vector state {state} of a field. Give a scalar state.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
            return vector(SR, [potential.diff(component) for component in state])
        if self.variational:
            return self._get_variation(potential, state)
        return potential.diff(state)

    def _get_members(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[SimpleNamespace]:
        """Return the namespaces of the members whose states move, those of every role that binds one path."""
        return [
            getattr(namespace, name)
            for name, spec in self._get_specs().items()
            if isinstance(spec, RoleSpec) and not spec.variadic and not spec.noise
        ]

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the rate of every moving state, minus the derivative of the potential over the divisor.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespaces of the roles.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate laws of the moving states.
        """
        potential = SR(self._get_potential(namespace))
        laws: list[BasePart] = []
        for member in self._get_members(namespace):
            for name in self._get_names():
                state = getattr(member, name)
                derivative = self._get_derivative(potential, state)
                rate = self._get_laplacian(derivative, state) if self.conserved else -derivative
                divisor = self._get_divisor(member, name)
                if divisor is not None:
                    rate = rate / divisor
                laws.append(RateLaw(self._get_rate_state(member, name), rate))
        return laws

docs.title: Störmer charge in a dipole field
docs.text:
A charged particle moving in the magnetic dipole field of a planet, the Störmer problem.

  • Name: stormer_problem
  • Field: physics/celestial_mechanics
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Störmer 1955; Dilão 2023

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/celestial_mechanics',
    tags=('mechanics', 'ode', 'second order', 'magnetism', 'chaos', 'hamiltonian'),
    references=('Störmer 1955', 'Dilão 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 20.0, 'dt': 0.02},
)
def stormer_problem(
    x: float = 1.0,
    y: float = 0.0,
    z: float = 0.0,
    *,
    vx: float = 0.0,
    vy: float = 0.1,
    vz: float = 0.1,
    alpha: float = 1.0,
) -> System:
    """Return a charged particle moving in the magnetic dipole field of a planet, the Störmer problem.

    The charge follows the Euler-Lagrange equations of `|x'|² / 2 + alpha (x y' - y x') / r³`, the kinetic energy and
    the coupling of the velocity to the vector potential of the dipole, whose Lorentz force gives
    `x'' = 3 alpha z (y' z - z' y) / r⁵ - alpha y' / r³`, `y'' = -3 alpha z (x' z - z' x) / r⁵ + alpha x' / r³`,
    and `z'' = 3 alpha z (x' y - y' x) / r⁵`, with `alpha = q M / m` for a dipole of moment `M` along the `z` axis.
    The magnetic force does no work, so the speed is conserved, and the symmetry about the axis conserves
    `x y' - y x' + alpha (x² + y²) / r³`. Bounded orbits near the planet trace the radiation belts, and many of them are
    chaotic.

    Args:
        x:
            The initial first coordinate, in units of the planet's radius.

        y:
            The initial second coordinate.

        z:
            The initial third coordinate, along the dipole.

        vx:
            The initial first velocity.

        vy:
            The initial second velocity.

        vz:
            The initial third velocity.

        alpha:
            The product of the charge and the dipole moment, divided by the mass.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the coordinates `charge.x`, `charge.y`, and `charge.z`, all of order 2.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import stormer_problem
        >>> stormer_problem(alpha=2.0).elements[0].alpha
        2.0
    """
    return System(
        elements=[DipoleChargeElement('charge', x=x, y=y, z=z, x_d1=vx, y_d1=vy, z_d1=vz, alpha=alpha)],
        interactions=[
            EulerLagrangeInteraction(
                'lorentz',
                target='charge',
                states=('x', 'y', 'z'),
                lagrangian=_get_dipole_lagrangian,
            ),
        ],
    )

class DipoleChargeElement(Element):
    """Charge in the magnetic dipole field of a planet, at the position `(x, y, z)` with coordinates of order 2.

    The parameter `alpha` is the product of the charge and the dipole moment, divided by the mass.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the charge.

        visual:
            How the charge is drawn, or `None` for its class visual.

        x:
            The initial first coordinate.

        x_d1:
            The initial first velocity.

        y:
            The initial second coordinate.

        y_d1:
            The initial second velocity.

        z:
            The initial third coordinate, along the dipole.

        z_d1:
            The initial third velocity.

        alpha:
            The product of the charge and the dipole moment, divided by the mass.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import DipoleChargeElement
        >>> DipoleChargeElement('charge', alpha=2.0).alpha
        2.0
    """

    visual = VisualSpec('bodies', {'positions': ('x', 'y', 'z'), 'trail': None, 'marks': [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]})

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=2)] = 1.0,
        x_d1: float = 0.0,
        y: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=2)] = 0.0,
        y_d1: float = 0.0,
        z: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=2)] = 0.0,
        z_d1: float = 0.0,
        alpha: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.x_d1 = x_d1
        self.y = y
        self.y_d1 = y_d1
        self.z = z
        self.z_d1 = z_d1
        self.alpha = alpha

class EulerLagrangeInteraction(Interaction):
    """Equations of motion `d/dt dL/dq' - dL/dq = Q - dR/dq'` of the coordinates `q` of a Lagrangian `L(ns)`.

    The coordinates are states of order 2, and the Lagrangian, the Rayleigh dissipation function `R`, and the
    generalized forcing `Q` read them and their first derivatives `derivative(q, 1)`. The interaction returns one
    equation law per coordinate, which the compiler solves jointly for the second derivatives, so a Lagrangian with a
    mass matrix, such as a double pendulum's, needs no inversion by hand. The equations of one coordinate from several
    interactions add, so their Lagrangians, dissipations, and forcings sum: a coupling, such as a spring between two
    pendulums, is an interaction of its own whose Lagrangian holds only the coupling energy. The coordinates are the
    states of every role that binds one element or group, `target` by default, and every component of a vector state
    is a coordinate.

    A Lagrangian, dissipation, or forcing function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces of the
    roles, the time `t`, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares. The forcing returns one generalized
    force per coordinate, in the order of the roles and of the states, or one expression for a single coordinate.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose states are the coordinates.

        states:
            The name of the state of order 2 that is a coordinate, or the names of several states.

        lagrangian:
            A function of the namespace that returns the Lagrangian.

        dissipation:
            A function of the namespace that returns the Rayleigh dissipation function, or `None` for none.

        forcing:
            A function of the namespace that returns the generalized forces, or `None` for none.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            A state is not a name, or a function is not callable.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import cos
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import EulerLagrangeInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws.utils import derivative
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> class AngleElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, q: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=2)] = 0.1, q_d1: float = 0.0):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.q = q
        ...         self.q_d1 = q_d1
        >>> swing = EulerLagrangeInteraction(
        ...     'swing',
        ...     target='bob',
        ...     states='q',
        ...     lagrangian=lambda s: derivative(s.target.q, 1) ** 2 / 2 + cos(s.target.q),
        ... )
        >>> system = System(elements=[AngleElement('bob')], interactions=[swing])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=3.2).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('bob.q')[-1]), 2)
        -0.1
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        states: str | Sequence[str] = 'x',
        lagrangian: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        dissipation: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        forcing: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.states = states
        self.lagrangian = lagrangian
        self.dissipation = dissipation
        self.forcing = forcing

    def _get_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Return the names of the states that are coordinates."""
        return (self.states,) if isinstance(self.states, str) else tuple(self.states)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, or a function that is not callable.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, a state is not a name, or a function is not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        names = self._get_names()
        if not names or not all(isinstance(name, str) and name.isidentifier() for name in names):
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} reads the states {self.states!r}. Give names of states.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        for name in ('lagrangian', 'dissipation', 'forcing'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and not callable(value):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function of the namespace.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_lagrangian(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the Lagrangian, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        if self.lagrangian is None:
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} has no Lagrangian. Give a function of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        return self.lagrangian(namespace)

    def _get_coordinates(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[Expression]:
        """Return the coordinates, every component of the states of every role that binds one path."""
        coordinates = []
        for name, spec in self._get_specs().items():
            if not isinstance(spec, RoleSpec) or spec.variadic or spec.noise:
                continue
            for state in self._get_names():
                value = getattr(getattr(namespace, name), state)
                coordinates += list(value) if isinstance(value, FreeModuleElement) else [value]
        return coordinates

    def _get_forces(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace, count: int) -> list[Expression]:
        """Return the generalized force of every coordinate, zero without a forcing."""
        if self.forcing is None:
            return [SR(0)] * count
        forces = self.forcing(namespace)
        forces = list(forces) if isinstance(forces, FreeModuleElement | list | tuple) else [forces]
        if len(forces) != count:
            error_msg = f'The forcing of {self.label!r} returns {len(forces)} forces for {count} coordinates.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        return [SR(force) for force in forces]

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the Euler-Lagrange equation of every coordinate.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespaces of the roles.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The equation laws of the coordinates.
        """
        coordinates = self._get_coordinates(namespace)
        velocities = {derivative(q, 1): SR.var(f'_velocity_{index}') for index, q in enumerate(coordinates)}
        back = {symbol: item for item, symbol in velocities.items()}
        slots = list(velocities.values())
        lagrangian = SR(self._get_lagrangian(namespace)).subs(velocities)
        dissipation = SR(0 if self.dissipation is None else self.dissipation(namespace)).subs(velocities)
        forces = self._get_forces(namespace, len(coordinates))
        time = SR(namespace.t)
        laws: list[BasePart] = []
        for q, slot, force in zip(coordinates, slots, forces, strict=True):
            momentum = lagrangian.diff(slot)
            change = momentum.diff(time) + sum(
                momentum.diff(other) * other_slot + momentum.diff(other_slot) * derivative(other, 2)
                for other, other_slot in zip(coordinates, slots, strict=True)
            )
            lhs = (change - lagrangian.diff(q)).subs(back)
            rhs = (force - dissipation.diff(slot)).subs(back)
            laws.append(EquationLaw(lhs == rhs, target=q))
        return laws

docs.title: Two-body orbit
docs.text:
A light planet orbiting a heavy star under Newtonian gravity, as the Kepler problem of their separation.

  • Name: two_body_orbit
  • Field: physics/celestial_mechanics
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Kepler 1609; Newton 1687

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/celestial_mechanics',
    tags=('mechanics', 'ode', 'gravity', 'hamiltonian'),
    references=('Kepler 1609', 'Newton 1687'),
    defaults={'until': 6.0, 'dt': 0.01, 'solver': Yoshida4Solver(), 'invariants': {'planet.energy': 1e-6}},
    observables=_get_kepler_observables,
)
def two_body_orbit(
    eccentricity: float = 0.0,
    *,
    G: float = 1.0,
    mass: float = 1000.0,
    radius: float = 10.0,
) -> System:
    """Return a light planet orbiting a heavy star under Newtonian gravity, as the Kepler problem of their separation.

    The planet moves in the coordinate `(x, y)` relative to the star with the canonical momenta `(px, py)` per unit
    mass, under the Hamiltonian `H = (px² + py²) / 2 - G M / sqrt(x² + y²)`, which is separable. The energy and the
    angular momentum `x py - y px` are conserved, and a bound orbit is an ellipse with the star at a focus.

    Args:
        eccentricity:
            The eccentricity of the orbit, between 0 for a circle and 1 for an escape.

        G:
            The gravitational constant.

        mass:
            The mass of the star.

        radius:
            The distance of the planet from the star at its closest approach.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the coordinates `planet.x` and `planet.y` and the momenta `planet.px` and `planet.py`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import two_body_orbit
        >>> [element.label for element in two_body_orbit().elements]
        ['planet']
    """
    speed = float(np.sqrt(G * mass * (1 + eccentricity) / radius))
    return System(
        elements=[KeplerBodyElement('planet', x=radius, y=0.0, px=0.0, py=speed, G=G, mass=mass)],
        interactions=[
            HamiltonianInteraction(
                'gravity',
                target='planet',
                coordinates=('x', 'y'),
                momenta=('px', 'py'),
                hamiltonian=_get_kepler_hamiltonian,
            ),
        ],
    )

class KeplerBodyElement(Element):
    """Planet at `(x, y)` relative to a heavy star, with the canonical momenta `(px, py)` of the Kepler problem.

    The states are of order 1, and the star of mass `mass` sits at the origin.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the planet.

        visual:
            How the planet is drawn, or `None` for its class visual.

        x:
            The initial first coordinate.

        y:
            The initial second coordinate.

        px:
            The initial first momentum per unit mass.

        py:
            The initial second momentum per unit mass.

        G:
            The gravitational constant.

        mass:
            The mass of the star.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.celestial_mechanics import KeplerBodyElement
        >>> KeplerBodyElement('planet', mass=10.0).mass
        10.0
    """

    visual = VisualSpec('bodies', {'positions': ('x', 'y'), 'trail': None, 'marks': _star})

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 10.0,
        y: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        px: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        py: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 10.0,
        G: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        mass: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1000.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.px = px
        self.py = py
        self.G = G
        self.mass = mass

class HamiltonianInteraction(Interaction):
    """Hamilton's equations `q' = dH/dp` and `p' = -dH/dq` of the canonical pairs `(q, p)` of a Hamiltonian `H(ns)`.

    The coordinates and the momenta are states of order 1, which may be angles, of every role that binds one element or
    group, `target` by default, and the coordinates pair with the momenta in order. Every component of a vector state
    is a coordinate or a momentum. The interaction returns one rate law per coordinate and per momentum, and the rates
    of one state add, so the Hamiltonians of separate interactions sum: a coupling between two oscillators is an
    interaction of its own whose Hamiltonian holds only the coupling energy. Dissipation or forcing is a rate
    interaction on the momenta.

    A Hamiltonian function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces of the roles, the time `t`, and
    the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose states are the canonical pairs.

        coordinates:
            The name of the state of order 1 that is a coordinate, or the names of several states.

        momenta:
            The name of the state of order 1 that is the momentum of the coordinate, or the names of several states in
            the order of the coordinates.

        hamiltonian:
            A function of the namespace that returns the Hamiltonian.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            A state is not a name, the coordinates and the momenta differ in count, the Hamiltonian is not callable,
            or a coordinate and its momentum differ in size or are not of order 1.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import HamiltonianInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> class OscillatorElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, q: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0, p: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.q = q
        ...         self.p = p
        >>> energy = lambda s: (s.target.p**2 + s.target.q**2) / 2
        >>> spring = HamiltonianInteraction('spring', target='mass', hamiltonian=energy)
        >>> system = System(elements=[OscillatorElement('mass')], interactions=[spring])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=3.14159).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('mass.q')[-1]), 3)
        -1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        coordinates: str | Sequence[str] = 'q',
        momenta: str | Sequence[str] = 'p',
        hamiltonian: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.coordinates = coordinates
        self.momenta = momenta
        self.hamiltonian = hamiltonian

    def _get_names(self, names: str | Sequence[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Return the names of the states of one side of the canonical pairs."""
        return (names,) if isinstance(names, str) else tuple(names)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, an unpaired state, or a Hamiltonian that is not callable.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, a state is not a name, the coordinates and the momenta differ in count, or
                the Hamiltonian is not callable.
        """
        super()._check()
        for side in ('coordinates', 'momenta'):
            names = self._get_names(getattr(self, side))
            if not names or not all(isinstance(name, str) and name.isidentifier() for name in names):
                error_msg = f'The {side} of {self.label!r} are {getattr(self, side)!r}. Give names of states.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        coordinates, momenta = self._get_names(self.coordinates), self._get_names(self.momenta)
        if len(coordinates) != len(momenta):
            unpaired = coordinates[len(momenta) :] or momenta[len(coordinates) :]
            error_msg = (
                f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} pairs the coordinates {coordinates} with the momenta {momenta}, '
                f'so {", ".join(unpaired)} has no partner. Give one momentum per coordinate.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.hamiltonian is not None and not callable(self.hamiltonian):
            error_msg = f'The hamiltonian of {self.label!r} is {self.hamiltonian!r}. Give a function of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _get_hamiltonian(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the Hamiltonian, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        if self.hamiltonian is None:
            error_msg = f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} has no Hamiltonian. Give a function of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        return self.hamiltonian(namespace)

    def _get_members(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[SimpleNamespace]:
        """Return the namespaces of the members whose states are canonical pairs, those of every role of one path."""
        return [
            getattr(namespace, name)
            for name, spec in self._get_specs().items()
            if isinstance(spec, RoleSpec) and not spec.variadic and not spec.noise
        ]

    def _get_state(self, member: SimpleNamespace, name: str) -> Target:
        """Return a canonical state of a member, after checking that it has order 1."""
        if hasattr(member, f'{name}_d1'):
            error_msg = (
                f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} reads the state {name} of order above 1, but canonical '
                'coordinates and momenta have order 1. Declare it with `StateSpec(order=1)`, or derive the equations '
                'of a coordinate of order 2 with `EulerLagrangeInteraction`.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        state: Target = getattr(member, name)
        return state

    def _get_pairs(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[tuple[Target, Target]]:
        """Return the canonical pairs of every member, after checking that each coordinate matches its momentum."""
        pairs = []
        names = list(zip(self._get_names(self.coordinates), self._get_names(self.momenta), strict=True))
        for member in self._get_members(namespace):
            for coordinate, momentum in names:
                q, p = self._get_state(member, coordinate), self._get_state(member, momentum)
                if len(self._get_components(q)) != len(self._get_components(p)):
                    error_msg = (
                        f'The coordinate {coordinate} and the momentum {momentum} of {self.label!r} differ in size. '
                        'Give a momentum of the size of its coordinate.'
                    )
                    raise ValidationError(error_msg)
                pairs.append((q, p))
        return pairs

    def _get_components(self, state: Target) -> list[Expression]:
        """Return the components of a state, the state itself for a scalar."""
        return list(state) if isinstance(state, FreeModuleElement) else [state]

    def _get_derivative(self, hamiltonian: Expression, state: Target) -> Target:
        """Return the derivative of the Hamiltonian with respect to a state, every component of a vector state."""
        if isinstance(state, FreeModuleElement):
            return vector(SR, [hamiltonian.diff(component) for component in state])
        return hamiltonian.diff(state)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the rate of every coordinate, `dH/dp`, and of every momentum, `-dH/dq`.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespaces of the roles.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate laws of the coordinates and the momenta.
        """
        pairs = self._get_pairs(namespace)
        hamiltonian = SR(self._get_hamiltonian(namespace))
        laws: list[BasePart] = []
        for q, p in pairs:
            laws.append(RateLaw(q, self._get_derivative(hamiltonian, p)))
            laws.append(RateLaw(p, -self._get_derivative(hamiltonian, q)))
        return laws

docs.title: Budyko-Sellers latitude model
docs.text:
The Budyko-Sellers energy balance of one hemisphere, resolved in the sine of latitude.

  • Name: budyko_sellers
  • Field: physics/climate
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Budyko 1969; Sellers 1969; North 1975; Ghil and Lucarini 2020

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/climate',
    tags=('field', 'pde', 'energy balance', 'ice-albedo feedback', 'snowball'),
    references=('Budyko 1969', 'Sellers 1969', 'North 1975', 'Ghil and Lucarini 2020'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 2.0},
)
def budyko_sellers(
    n_bands: int = 30,
    T: float = 15.0,
    *,
    Q: float = 334.4,
    A: float = 203.3,
    B: float = 2.09,
    D: float = 0.649,
    C: float = 10.0,
) -> System:
    """Return the Budyko-Sellers energy balance of one hemisphere, resolved in the sine of latitude.

    The temperature of a band at `x = sin(latitude)` follows `C dT/dt = Q s(x) (1 - a(x, T)) - (A + B T) +
    D d/dx((1 - x^2) dT/dx)`, with the annual insolation `s(x) = 1 - 0.482 P2(x)`, where `P2(x) = (3x^2 - 1) / 2`.
    The albedo is `0.319 + 0.202 P2(x)` without ice and rises to 0.62 where the temperature falls below -10 °C.
    Bands are centred at `x = (i + 1/2) / n_bands`, with no heat flux across the equator or the pole. Present
    insolation keeps both a climate with polar ice caps and a snowball Earth.

    Args:
        n_bands:
            The number of latitude bands.

        T:
            The initial temperature of every band in °C.

        Q:
            The mean insolation in W m⁻².

        A:
            The outgoing radiation at 0 °C in W m⁻².

        B:
            The increase of outgoing radiation per degree in W m⁻² K⁻¹.

        D:
            The coefficient of meridional heat transport in W m⁻² K⁻¹.

        C:
            The heat capacity in W yr m⁻² K⁻¹, so time is in years.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the temperatures `bands.T` from the equator to the pole.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.climate import budyko_sellers
        >>> budyko_sellers(10).elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        10
    """
    x = (np.arange(n_bands) + 0.5) / n_bands
    bands = FieldElement(
        'bands',
        element=LatitudeBandElement,
        space=LatticeSpace(n_bands, spacing=1 / n_bands),
        boundary={'T': 'zero-flux'},
        values={'T': np.full(n_bands, float(T)), 'x': x, 'Q': Q, 'A': A, 'B': B, 'D': D, 'C': C},
    )
    return System(elements=[bands])

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
class LatitudeBandElement(Element):
    """Latitude band of the Budyko-Sellers energy balance, heated by the sun and exchanging heat with its neighbours.

    The temperature of the band at `x = sin(latitude)` follows `C dT/dt = Q s(x) (1 - a(x, T)) - (A + B T) +
    D d/dx((1 - x^2) dT/dx)`, with the annual insolation `s(x) = 1 + s2 P2(x)`, where `P2(x) = (3x^2 - 1) / 2`. The
    albedo is `albedo_free + albedo_slope P2(x)` without ice and rises to `albedo_ice` where the temperature falls below
    `T_ice`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the band or the field.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        T:
            The initial temperature in °C.

        x:
            The sine of the latitude of the band.

        Q:
            The mean insolation in W m⁻².

        s2:
            The coefficient of the second Legendre polynomial of the insolation.

        A:
            The outgoing radiation at 0 °C in W m⁻².

        B:
            The increase of outgoing radiation per degree in W m⁻² K⁻¹.

        D:
            The coefficient of meridional heat transport in W m⁻² K⁻¹.

        C:
            The heat capacity in W yr m⁻² K⁻¹, so time is in years.

        albedo_ice:
            The albedo of an icy band.

        albedo_free:
            The mean albedo of an ice free band.

        albedo_slope:
            The coefficient of the second Legendre polynomial of the albedo of an ice free band.

        T_ice:
            The temperature in °C below which the band is icy.

        width:
            The width of the transition to ice in kelvin.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.climate import LatitudeBandElement
        >>> LatitudeBandElement('band').albedo_ice
        0.62
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        T: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 15.0,
        x: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.5,
        Q: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 334.4,
        s2: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = -0.482,
        A: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 203.3,
        B: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 2.09,
        D: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.649,
        C: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 10.0,
        albedo_ice: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.62,
        albedo_free: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.319,
        albedo_slope: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.202,
        T_ice: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = -10.0,
        width: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.T = T
        self.x = x
        self.Q = Q
        self.s2 = s2
        self.A = A
        self.B = B
        self.D = D
        self.C = C
        self.albedo_ice = albedo_ice
        self.albedo_free = albedo_free
        self.albedo_slope = albedo_slope
        self.T_ice = T_ice
        self.width = width

    def _get_albedo(self, s: SimpleNamespace, legendre: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return the albedo of the band, which rises smoothly from its ice free value to that of ice as it cools.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

            legendre:
                The second Legendre polynomial of the sine of the latitude.

        Returns:
            albedo:
                The albedo of the band.
        """
        free = s.albedo_free + s.albedo_slope * legendre
        return (s.albedo_ice + free) / 2 - (s.albedo_ice - free) / 2 * tanh((s.T - s.T_ice) / s.width)

    def _get_transport(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the meridional diffusion of heat on the sphere, in the sine of latitude.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            transport:
                The heat the band gains from its neighbours.
        """
        return s.D * ((1 - s.x**2) * laplacian(s.T) - 2 * s.x * gradient(s.T, 1)[0])

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the absorbed insolation, the linearized outgoing radiation, and the meridional diffusion of heat.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate law of the temperature of the band.
        """
        legendre = (3 * s.x**2 - 1) / 2
        insolation = s.Q * (1 + s.s2 * legendre)
        albedo = self._get_albedo(s, legendre)
        transport = self._get_transport(s)
        return [RateLaw(s.T, (insolation * (1 - albedo) - (s.A + s.B * s.T) + transport) / s.C)]

docs.title: Rothman excitable carbon cycle
docs.text:
Rothman's excitable carbon cycle, where a large enough perturbation of the ocean sets off an excursion.

  • Name: carbon_cycle
  • Field: physics/climate
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Rothman 2019; Datseris and Parlitz 2022

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/climate',
    tags=('ode', 'excitability', 'carbon cycle', 'mass extinctions'),
    references=('Rothman 2019', 'Datseris and Parlitz 2022'),
    defaults={'until': 20.0, 'dt': 0.05},
)
def carbon_cycle(
    c: float = 83.58,
    w: float = 2050.0,
    *,
    c_x: float = 55.0,
    nu: float = 0.0,
) -> System:
    """Return Rothman's excitable carbon cycle, where a large enough perturbation of the ocean sets off an excursion.

    The carbonate ion concentration `c` and the dissolved inorganic carbon `w`, in μmol kg⁻¹, follow
    `dc/dt = f(c) (mu (1 - b s(c, c_p) - theta (1 - s(c, c_x)) - nu) + w - w0)` and
    `dw/dt = mu (1 - b s(c, c_p) + theta (1 - s(c, c_x)) + nu) - w + w0`, with the sigmoids
    `s(c, c*) = c^gamma / (c^gamma + c*^gamma)` of burial and respiration and the buffer
    `f(c) = f0 c^beta / (c^beta + c_f^beta)`. The steady state near `c = 83.6` and `w = 2197` is stable, and from a
    dissolved carbon far enough below it the ocean returns only after a large excursion of `c`.

    Args:
        c:
            The initial carbonate ion concentration.

        w:
            The initial dissolved inorganic carbon.

        c_x:
            The crossover carbonate concentration of respiration, which sets the excitability.

        nu:
            The rate of external carbon injection.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the concentrations `ocean.c` and `ocean.w`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.climate import carbon_cycle
        >>> carbon_cycle(nu=0.1).elements[0].nu
        0.1
    """
    return System(elements=[CarbonCycleElement('ocean', c=c, w=w, c_x=c_x, nu=nu)])
