docs.text:
class LogisticNodeElement(Element):
    """Logistic map on a node of a network, with its value, growth rate, and weight of the neighbours.

    `LogisticCouplingInteraction` iterates `x_i(t + 1) = (1 - epsilon) f(x_i) + epsilon mean_j f(x_j)`, where the map
    `f(x) = r x (1 - x)` of the node mixes with the mean of the maps of its neighbours `j` on the network.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the node or the group on the nodes.

        visual:
            How the node is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x:
            The initial value.

        r:
            The growth rate of the logistic map.

        epsilon:
            The weight of the neighbours.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the node when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import LogisticNodeElement
        >>> LogisticNodeElement('node').epsilon
        0.5
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.5,
        r: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 4.0,
        epsilon: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.r = r
        self.epsilon = epsilon

class LogisticCouplingInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Coupled logistic maps, `x_i(t + 1) = (1 - epsilon) f(x_i) + epsilon mean_j f(x_j)` with `f(x) = r x (1 - x)`.

    The map of every node mixes with the mean of the maps of its neighbours `j` on its lattice or network, with the
    parameters `r` and `epsilon` of the node. A node with no neighbours keeps `(1 - epsilon) f(x_i)`. It is the map
    form of coupling, with the mean of the maps of the neighbours combined with the map of the node.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group of maps, on the nodes of a lattice or network.

        state:
            The name of the state that the maps iterate.

    Examples:
        >>> import networkx as nx
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import LatticeElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.spaces import DiscreteTime, NetworkSpace
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import LogisticCouplingInteraction, LogisticNodeElement
        >>> maps = LatticeElement(
        ...     'maps',
        ...     element=LogisticNodeElement,
        ...     space=NetworkSpace(nx.path_graph(2)),
        ...     values={'x': [0.25, 0.5], 'epsilon': 0.5},
        ... )
        >>> coupling = LogisticCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='maps')
        >>> system = System(elements=[maps], interactions=[coupling], time=DiscreteTime())
        >>> Simulation(system).check().prepare().run(until=1).trajectory_.values('maps.x')[-1].tolist()
        [0.875, 0.875]
    """

    def __init__(self, label: str, *, target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()], state: str = 'x') -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            read=state,
            write=state,
            function=self._get_map,
            reduce='mean',
            form='map',
            combine=self._get_mix,
        )
        self.state = state

    @staticmethod
    def _logistic(r: Expression, x: Expression) -> Expression:
        """Return the logistic map `r x (1 - x)`."""
        return r * x * (1 - x)

    def _get_map(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the map of the neighbour, with the growth rate of the node."""
        return self._logistic(namespace.member.r, getattr(namespace.other, self.state))

    def _get_mix(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace, reduction: Target) -> Target:
        """Return the map of the node mixed with the mean map of its neighbours."""
        member = namespace.member
        own = self._logistic(member.r, getattr(member, self.state))
        return (1 - member.epsilon) * own + member.epsilon * reduction

docs.title: Coupled Rössler and the master stability function
docs.text:
Chaotic Rössler oscillators on a ring, diffusively coupled through their second variable.

  • Name: coupled_rossler
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Rössler 1976; Pecora and Carroll 1998; Datseris and Parlitz 2022; Arenas et al. 2008

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'chaos', 'ode', 'master stability function', 'networks'),
    references=('Rössler 1976', 'Pecora and Carroll 1998', 'Datseris and Parlitz 2022', 'Arenas et al. 2008'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 0.1},
)
def coupled_rossler(
    n_oscillators: int = 2,
    *,
    k: float = 0.04,
    mismatch: float = 0.02,
    a: float = 0.2,
    b: float = 0.2,
    c: float = 5.7,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return chaotic Rössler oscillators on a ring, diffusively coupled through their second variable.

    Oscillator `i` follows `x1' = -ω_i x2 - x3`, `x2' = ω_i x1 + a x2 + k sum_j (x2_j - x2_i)`, and
    `x3' = b + x3 (x1 - c)`, summed over its neighbours on the ring. Two oscillators with frequencies `1 ± mismatch`
    pass from no synchronization to chaotic phase synchronization as `k` grows. Identical oscillators, with no mismatch,
    synchronize completely when every nonzero eigenvalue of the ring's Laplacian times `k` falls where the master
    stability function is negative.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators on the ring.

        k:
            The coupling strength.

        mismatch:
            The half width of the interval of natural frequencies around 1.

        a:
            The first Rössler parameter.

        b:
            The second Rössler parameter.

        c:
            The third Rössler parameter.

        seed:
            The seed of the initial states.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the states `oscillator_<i>.x1`, `oscillator_<i>.x2`, and `oscillator_<i>.x3`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import coupled_rossler
        >>> [element.omega for element in coupled_rossler().elements]
        [0.98, 1.02]
    """
    omegas = np.linspace(1 - mismatch, 1 + mismatch, n_oscillators)
    starts = np.random.default_rng(seed).uniform(-1.0, 1.0, (n_oscillators, 2))
    oscillators = [
        RosslerOscillatorElement(
            f'oscillator_{index}',
            x1=float(starts[index, 0]),
            x2=float(starts[index, 1]),
            x3=0.0,
            omega=round(float(omegas[index]), 12),
            a=a,
            b=b,
            c=c,
        )
        for index in range(n_oscillators)
    ]
    links = [(index, index + 1) for index in range(n_oscillators - 1)]
    if n_oscillators > PAIR:
        links.append((n_oscillators - 1, 0))
    couplings = [
        DiffusiveCouplingInteraction(
            f'coupling_{source}_{target}',
            source=f'oscillator_{source}',
            target=f'oscillator_{target}',
            k=k,
        )
        for first, second in links
        for source, target in ((first, second), (second, first))
    ]
    return System(elements=oscillators, interactions=couplings)

class RosslerOscillatorElement(Element):
    """Rössler oscillator `x1' = -omega x2 - x3`, `x2' = omega x1 + a x2`, `x3' = b + x3 (x1 - c)`.

    It is chaotic for `a = b = 0.2` and `c = 5.7`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x1:
            The initial first variable.

        x2:
            The initial second variable.

        x3:
            The initial third variable.

        omega:
            The natural frequency.

        a:
            The first Rössler parameter.

        b:
            The second Rössler parameter.

        c:
            The third Rössler parameter.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import RosslerOscillatorElement
        >>> RosslerOscillatorElement('oscillator').c
        5.7
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x1: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0,
        x2: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        x3: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        a: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.2,
        b: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.2,
        c: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 5.7,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x1 = x1
        self.x2 = x2
        self.x3 = x3
        self.omega = omega
        self.a = a
        self.b = b
        self.c = c

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the Rössler flow.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rates of the three variables.
        """
        s = namespace
        return [
            RateLaw(s.x1, -s.omega * s.x2 - s.x3),
            RateLaw(s.x2, s.omega * s.x1 + s.a * s.x2),
            RateLaw(s.x3, s.b + s.x3 * (s.x1 - s.c)),
        ]

class DiffusiveCouplingInteraction(RateInteraction):
    """Diffusive coupling of a state of one element to the same state of another, `x_t' += k (x_s - x_t)`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        source:
            The path of the element whose state the coupling reads.

        target:
            The path of the element whose state the coupling changes.

        state:
            The name of the coupled state.

        k:
            The coupling strength.

    Examples:
        >>> from types import SimpleNamespace
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import DiffusiveCouplingInteraction
        >>> coupling = DiffusiveCouplingInteraction('coupling', source='a', target='b').check().prepare()
        >>> source, target = SimpleNamespace(x2=var('u')), SimpleNamespace(x2=var('v'))
        >>> [law.value for law in coupling.run(SimpleNamespace(source=source, target=target, k=var('k'))).laws_]
        [k*(u - v)]
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        source: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'x2',
        k: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.1,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, state=state)
        self.source = source
        self.k = k

    def _get_rate(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return `k (x_s - x_t)`.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the rate can use.

        Returns:
            rate:
                The rate of the state of the target.
        """
        return namespace.k * (getattr(namespace.source, self.state) - getattr(namespace.target, self.state))

docs.title: Delayed Kuramoto
docs.text:
Kuramoto phase oscillators coupled all to all through signals that arrive after a delay.

  • Name: delayed_kuramoto
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Yeung and Strogatz 1999; Kuramoto 1984

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'delay', 'oscillators'),
    references=('Yeung and Strogatz 1999', 'Kuramoto 1984'),
    defaults={'until': 50.0, 'dt': 0.1},
)
def delayed_kuramoto(
    n_oscillators: int = 5,
    *,
    K: float = 2.0,
    tau: float = 1.0,
    spread: float = 0.2,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return Kuramoto phase oscillators coupled all to all through signals that arrive after a delay.

    Oscillator `i` follows `theta_i' = omega_i + (K / N) sum_j sin(theta_j(t - tau) - theta_i)`, with natural
    frequencies spread evenly around 1 and initial phases spread around the circle.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

        tau:
            The delay of the coupling.

        spread:
            The width of the interval of natural frequencies around 1.

        seed:
            The seed of the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the phases `oscillator_<i>.theta`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import delayed_kuramoto
        >>> len(delayed_kuramoto(n_oscillators=3).interactions)
        6
    """
    phases = [2 * math.pi * ((seed * 0.618 + index / n_oscillators) % 1.0) for index in range(n_oscillators)]
    omegas = [1.0 + spread * (index / max(n_oscillators - 1, 1) - 0.5) for index in range(n_oscillators)]
    elements = [
        PhaseOscillatorElement(f'oscillator_{index}', theta=phases[index], omega=omegas[index])
        for index in range(n_oscillators)
    ]
    interactions = [
        DelayedCouplingInteraction(
            f'coupling_{source}_{target}',
            source=f'oscillator_{source}',
            target=f'oscillator_{target}',
            K=K / n_oscillators,
            tau=tau,
        )
        for source in range(n_oscillators)
        for target in range(n_oscillators)
        if source != target
    ]
    return System(elements=elements, interactions=interactions)

class PhaseOscillatorElement(Element):
    """Phase oscillator, a phase `theta` that turns at its natural frequency, `theta' = omega`.

    Couplings to other oscillators add to the rate of the phase.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator or the group.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        theta:
            The initial phase.

        omega:
            The natural frequency.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import PhaseOscillatorElement
        >>> system = System(elements=[PhaseOscillatorElement('clock', omega=2.0)])
        >>> float(Simulation(system, dt=0.5).check().prepare().run(until=1.0).trajectory_.values('clock.theta')[-1])
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        theta: Annotated[float, StateSpec(role='phase')] = 0.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.theta = theta
        self.omega = omega

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the turning of the phase at the natural frequency.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate of the phase.
        """
        return [RateLaw(namespace.theta, namespace.omega)]

class DelayedCouplingInteraction(RateInteraction):
    """Delayed sine coupling of one phase oscillator to another, `theta_t' += K sin(theta_s(t - tau) - theta_t)`.

    The target reads the phase of the source as it was a delay `tau` earlier.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        source:
            The path of the oscillator whose delayed phase the coupling reads.

        target:
            The path of the oscillator whose phase the coupling turns.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

        tau:
            The delay.

    Examples:
        >>> from types import SimpleNamespace
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import DelayedCouplingInteraction
        >>> coupling = DelayedCouplingInteraction('coupling', source='a', target='b').check().prepare()
        >>> namespace = SimpleNamespace(source=SimpleNamespace(theta=var('a')), target=SimpleNamespace(theta=var('b')))
        >>> [law.value for law in coupling.run(SimpleNamespace(**vars(namespace), K=var('K'), tau=1)).laws_]
        [K*sin(-b + delayed(a, 1))]
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        source: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        tau: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, state='theta')
        self.source = source
        self.K = K
        self.tau = tau

    def _get_rate(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return `K sin(theta_s(t - tau) - theta_t)`.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the rate can use.

        Returns:
            rate:
                The rate of the phase of the target.
        """
        return namespace.K * sin(delayed(namespace.source.theta, namespace.tau) - namespace.target.theta)

docs.title: Globally coupled systems with heterogeneous time scales
docs.text:
Globally coupled oscillators with heterogeneous time scales, whose fixed point the coupling restabilizes.

  • Name: heterogeneous_global_coupling
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: De Monte, d'Ovidio, and Mosekilde 2003; Bertin 2021

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'amplitude death', 'mean field', 'heterogeneity', 'ode'),
    references=("De Monte, d'Ovidio, and Mosekilde 2003", 'Bertin 2021'),
    defaults={'until': 40.0, 'dt': 0.2},
    observables=lambda system: [
        ObservableSpec('amplitude', _amplitude, group='systems'),
        ObservableSpec('X', group='systems', variable='x'),
        ObservableSpec('Y', group='systems', variable='y'),
        ObservableSpec('V', _time_scale_deviation_x, group='systems'),
        ObservableSpec('W', _time_scale_deviation_y, group='systems'),
    ],
)
def heterogeneous_global_coupling(
    n_systems: int = 100,
    *,
    k: float = 2.0,
    beta: float = 0.1,
    gamma: float = 2.0,
    heterogeneity: float = 0.8,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return globally coupled oscillators with heterogeneous time scales, whose fixed point the coupling restabilizes.

    System `j` follows `x_j' = τ_j g(x_j, y_j) + k (X - x_j)` and `y_j' = τ_j h(x_j, y_j) + k (Y - y_j)`, where `X`
    and `Y` are the population means and `g + ih = (beta + i gamma) z - |z|² z` is the Hopf normal form of
    `z = x + iy`. Its fixed point 0 is an unstable focus with eigenvalues `beta ± i gamma`. The time scales `τ_j` are
    spread evenly over `[1 - heterogeneity, 1 + heterogeneity]`, with mean 1 and variance `sigma²`. The order
    parameters `X`, `Y`, `V = <δτ δx>`, and `W = <δτ δy>` close on four equations. The global fixed point is stable
    when their eigenvalues `nu - k / 2 ± √(k² / 4 + sigma² nu²)`, for `nu = beta ± i gamma`, have negative real parts,
    which holds roughly for `2 beta (1 + sigma) < k < (gamma² - beta²) sigma² / beta`.

    Args:
        n_systems:
            The number of coupled systems.

        k:
            The coupling constant.

        beta:
            The growth rate `β` of the unstable focus.

        gamma:
            The rotation rate `gamma` of the unstable focus.

        heterogeneity:
            The half width of the interval of time scales, below 1.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the states `systems.x` and `systems.y` and the observables `amplitude`, the mean amplitude,
            and the order parameters `X`, `Y`, `V`, and `W`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import heterogeneous_global_coupling
        >>> heterogeneous_global_coupling(4).elements[0].values['tau']
        array([0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6])
    """
    taus = 1 + heterogeneity * (2 * (np.arange(n_systems) + 1 / 2) / n_systems - 1)
    x, y = _spread_on_circle(n_systems, random_state)
    radius = math.sqrt(abs(beta))
    systems = GroupElement(
        'systems',
        element=StuartLandauElement,
        size=n_systems,
        values={'x': radius * x, 'y': radius * y, 'mu': beta, 'omega': gamma, 'tau': taus},
    )
    return System(
        elements=[systems],
        interactions=[
            GlobalCouplingInteraction(f'coupling_{state}', target='systems', state=state, K=k) for state in 'xy'
        ],
    )

class StuartLandauElement(Element):
    """Stuart-Landau oscillator `z' = tau ((mu + i omega) z - kappa (1 + i beta) |z|^2 z)` of `z = x + i y`.

    It is the normal form of a supercritical Hopf bifurcation. For `mu > 0` the oscillator settles on the limit cycle
    of radius `sqrt(mu / kappa)`, which it turns at the frequency `tau (omega - beta mu)`, and for `mu < 0` it decays to
    the fixed point 0. The twist `beta` makes the frequency depend on the amplitude, and the time scale `tau` speeds
    up or slows down the whole flow.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator or the group.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x:
            The initial real part of `z`.

        y:
            The initial imaginary part of `z`.

        mu:
            The growth rate of the fixed point 0, the bifurcation parameter.

        omega:
            The frequency of the linear rotation.

        beta:
            The twist, the shear of the frequency with the amplitude.

        kappa:
            The strength of the cubic saturation.

        tau:
            The time scale.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> import math
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import StuartLandauElement
        >>> system = System(elements=[StuartLandauElement('oscillator', x=0.1, mu=4.0)])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.5).check().prepare().run(until=10.0).trajectory_
        >>> round(math.hypot(trajectory.values('oscillator.x')[-1], trajectory.values('oscillator.y')[-1]), 4)
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0,
        y: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        mu: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        beta: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        kappa: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        tau: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.mu = mu
        self.omega = omega
        self.beta = beta
        self.kappa = kappa
        self.tau = tau

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rates of the real and imaginary parts of `z`.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rates of `x` and `y`.
        """
        s = namespace
        saturation = s.kappa * (s.x**2 + s.y**2)
        return [
            RateLaw(s.x, s.tau * (s.mu * s.x - s.omega * s.y - saturation * (s.x - s.beta * s.y))),
            RateLaw(s.y, s.tau * (s.mu * s.y + s.omega * s.x - saturation * (s.y + s.beta * s.x))),
        ]

class GlobalCouplingInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Diffusive coupling of one state of every member to the mean of the group, `x_i' += K (mean_j x_j - x_i)`.

    The mean runs over every member, the member itself included.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group.

        state:
            The name of the coupled state.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

    Examples:
        >>> from types import SimpleNamespace
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import GlobalCouplingInteraction
        >>> coupling = GlobalCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='oscillators', state='y').check().prepare()
        >>> member, other = SimpleNamespace(y=var('y')), SimpleNamespace(y=var('z'))
        >>> coupling.function(SimpleNamespace(K=var('K'), member=member, other=other))
        -K*(y - z)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'x',
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            read=state,
            write=state,
            function=self._pull,
            reduce='mean',
            mode='group',
            include_self=True,
        )
        self.state = state
        self.K = K

    def _pull(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the pull `K (x_j - x_i)` of one other member."""
        return namespace.K * (getattr(namespace.other, self.state) - getattr(namespace.member, self.state))

docs.title: Kuramoto oscillators with three-body coupling
docs.text:
Kuramoto oscillators coupled in pairs and by three-body interactions on the triangles of a hypergraph.

  • Name: hypergraph_kuramoto
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Skardal and Arenas 2019; Majhi et al. 2022

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'phase', 'hypergraph'),
    references=('Skardal and Arenas 2019', 'Majhi et al. 2022'),
    defaults={'until': 40.0, 'dt': 0.1},
    observables=lambda system: _order_parameter('order', 'oscillators'),
)
def hypergraph_kuramoto(
    n_oscillators: int = 60,
    *,
    K1: float = 0.0,
    K2: float = 8.0,
    width: float = 0.5,
    links: float = 1.0,
    triangles: float = 1.0,
    phases: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return Kuramoto oscillators coupled in pairs and by three-body interactions on the triangles of a hypergraph.

    Oscillator `i` follows `theta_i' = omega_i + (K1 / <k1>) sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i) + (K2 / <k2>) sum_jk
    sin(theta_j + theta_k - 2 theta_i)` over the links `ij` and the triangles `ijk` of a random hypergraph, where `<k1>`
    and `<k2>` are the mean numbers of links and of triangles of a node. All-to-all, the triangle term is the
    three-body coupling of Skardal and Arenas, and the Ott-Antonsen reduction of Lorentzian frequencies of half width
    `width` gives `r' = -width r + K1 (r - r^3) / 2 + K2 (r^3 - r^5) / 2`. Without links, the incoherent state stays
    stable for every `K2`, and for `K2 > 8 width` a synchronized state of `r^2 = (1 + sqrt(1 - 8 width / K2)) / 2`
    coexists with it, so the order parameter depends on the initial phases and sweeps of the coupling show hysteresis.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators, the nodes of the hypergraph.

        K1:
            The pairwise coupling, divided by the mean number of links of a node.

        K2:
            The three-body coupling, divided by the mean number of triangles of a node.

        width:
            The half width of the Lorentzian distribution of the natural frequencies.

        links:
            The probability that a pair of oscillators is a link.

        triangles:
            The probability that a triple of oscillators is a triangle.

        phases:
            The initial phases, or `None` for phases drawn uniformly from the circle.

        seed:
            The seed of the hypergraph, the frequencies, and the phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the phases `oscillators.theta` and the order parameter `order`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import hypergraph_kuramoto
        >>> system = hypergraph_kuramoto(6)
        >>> len(system.elements[0].space.check().prepare().hyperedges_)
        35
    """
    hypergraph = _simplices(n_oscillators, links, triangles, seed)
    space = NetworkSpace(nx.complete_graph(n_oscillators), hyperedges=hypergraph)
    sizes = [len(members) for members in hypergraph.edges.members()]
    mean_links = max(PAIR * sizes.count(PAIR) / n_oscillators, 1.0)
    mean_triangles = max(3 * sizes.count(3) / n_oscillators, 1.0)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1)
    omega = width * stats.cauchy.ppf(rng.uniform(size=n_oscillators))
    theta = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi, n_oscillators) if phases is None else np.asarray(phases, dtype=float)
    oscillators = LatticeElement(
        'oscillators',
        element=PhaseOscillatorElement,
        space=space,
        values={'theta': theta, 'omega': omega},
        visual=VisualSpec('sites', {'states': ['theta'], 'low': 0.0, 'high': 2 * math.pi}),
    )
    coupling = SimplexCouplingInteraction(
        'coupling',
        target='oscillators',
        K1=K1 / mean_links,
        K2=K2 / mean_triangles,
    )
    return System(elements=[oscillators], interactions=[coupling])

class PhaseOscillatorElement(Element):
    """Phase oscillator, a phase `theta` that turns at its natural frequency, `theta' = omega`.

    Couplings to other oscillators add to the rate of the phase.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator or the group.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        theta:
            The initial phase.

        omega:
            The natural frequency.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import PhaseOscillatorElement
        >>> system = System(elements=[PhaseOscillatorElement('clock', omega=2.0)])
        >>> float(Simulation(system, dt=0.5).check().prepare().run(until=1.0).trajectory_.values('clock.theta')[-1])
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        theta: Annotated[float, StateSpec(role='phase')] = 0.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.theta = theta
        self.omega = omega

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the turning of the phase at the natural frequency.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate of the phase.
        """
        return [RateLaw(namespace.theta, namespace.omega)]

class SimplexCouplingInteraction(HyperedgeInteraction):
    """Kuramoto coupling through the simplices of a hypergraph, pairs and triangles.

    On a link, the focal oscillator `i` gets `K1 sin(theta_j - theta_i)`, and on a triangle `K2 sin(theta_j + theta_k -
    2 theta_i)` from its two other members `j` and `k`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group of oscillators on the nodes.

        K1:
            The coupling of every link.

        K2:
            The coupling of every triangle.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import SimplexCouplingInteraction
        >>> SimplexCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='oscillators', K2=0.5).K2
        0.5
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        K1: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        K2: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.K1 = K1
        self.K2 = K2

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the coupling of the focal oscillator to the other members of a link or a triangle."""
        theta = s.member.theta
        others = [other.theta for other in s.others]
        if len(others) + 1 == PAIR:
            return [RateLaw(theta, s.K1 * sin(others[0] - theta))]
        return [RateLaw(theta, s.K2 * sin(sum(others) - len(others) * theta))]

Kuramoto oscillators coupled all to all, theta_i' = omega_i + (K / N) sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i).

  • Name: kuramoto
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Kuramoto 1984; Datseris and Parlitz 2022; Gros 2015; Jensen 2023

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'phase', 'mean field'),
    references=('Kuramoto 1984', 'Datseris and Parlitz 2022', 'Gros 2015', 'Jensen 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 50.0, 'dt': 0.5},
    observables=lambda system: _order_parameter('order', 'oscillators'),
)
def kuramoto(n_oscillators: int = 50, *, K: float = 4.0, sigma: float = 1.0, seed: int = 0) -> System:
    """Return Kuramoto oscillators coupled all to all, `theta_i' = omega_i + (K / N) sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i)`.

    Every oscillator reads the group means of `cos theta` and `sin theta`, so the coupling costs time linear in the
    number of oscillators. The natural frequencies are drawn from a normal distribution of width `sigma`, and the
    phases uniformly from the circle. Above the critical coupling `K_c = 2 sigma sqrt(2 / pi)` a synchronized cluster
    forms, and the order parameter `r`, the modulus of the mean of `exp(i theta)`, grows from about `1 / sqrt(N)`
    towards 1.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

        sigma:
            The standard deviation of the natural frequencies.

        seed:
            The seed of the natural frequencies and the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the phases `oscillators.theta` and the order parameter `order`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import kuramoto
        >>> system = kuramoto(10)
        >>> system.elements[0].size, system.space
        (10, None)
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    oscillators = GroupElement(
        'oscillators',
        element=PhaseOscillatorElement,
        size=n_oscillators,
        values={'theta': _spread_phases(n_oscillators, seed), 'omega': rng.normal(0.0, sigma, n_oscillators)},
    )
    coupling = KuramotoCouplingInteraction(
        'coupling',
        target='oscillators',
        K=K,
        mode='group',
        reduce='mean',
        include_self=True,
    )
    return System(
        elements=[oscillators],
        interactions=[coupling],
    )

class KuramotoCouplingInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Kuramoto coupling `theta_i' += K sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i - alpha)` of the phases of a group.

    The sum, or the mean, runs over the members `j` that the mode selects: the neighbours along the edges of a lattice
    or network, or within a neighbourhood such as `RadiusNeighborhood(r)`, every other member of the group, every member
    of a separate source group, or the next member. With `include_self` it also runs over `j = i`, whose term
    `-K sin(alpha)` slows every phase. Over the whole group without weights or delay, the coupling reads the group sums
    of `sin theta` and `cos theta` once, so it costs time linear in the size of the group.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group of oscillators.

        source:
            The path of the group of oscillators the target couples to in the mode `'group'`, or `None` for the target.

        K:
            The coupling strength of one pair.

        alpha:
            The phase lag.

        state:
            The name of the state that holds the phases.

        reduce:
            `'sum'` or `'mean'`.

        mode:
            `'edges'`, `'group'`, or `'next'`.

        weights:
            The name of the state of the edge group in the mode `'edges'`, a matrix in the mode `'group'`, or `None`.

        include_self:
            Whether the sum also runs over the member itself.

        delay:
            The delay of the phases of the other members, 0 for none.

        neighborhood:
            The neighbourhood of the mode `'edges'`, or `None` for the edges of the lattice or network.

        layer:
            The layer of the network whose edges the interaction runs on, or `None` for the graph of the network.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import (
        ...     KuramotoCouplingInteraction,
        ...     PhaseOscillatorElement,
        ... )
        >>> phases = GroupElement('phases', element=PhaseOscillatorElement, size=4, values={'theta': [0, 1, 2, 3]})
        >>> coupling = KuramotoCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='phases', K=2.0, mode='group', reduce='mean')
        >>> system = System(elements=[phases], interactions=[coupling])
        >>> theta = Simulation(system, dt=1.0).check().prepare().run(until=20.0).trajectory_.values('phases.theta')
        >>> round(float(np.ptp(theta[-1])), 6)
        0.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        source: Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True)] = None,
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        alpha: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        state: str = 'theta',
        reduce: str = 'sum',
        mode: str = 'edges',
        weights: str | npt.ArrayLike | scipy.sparse.sparray | None = None,
        include_self: bool = False,
        delay: float = 0.0,
        neighborhood: BaseNeighborhood | None = None,
        layer: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            source=source,
            read=state,
            write=state,
            function=self._sine,
            reduce=reduce,
            mode=mode,
            weights=weights,
            include_self=include_self,
            delay=delay,
            neighborhood=neighborhood,
            layer=layer,
        )
        self.K = K
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.state = state

    def _sine(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the term `K sin(theta_j - theta_i - alpha)` of one other member."""
        member, other = getattr(namespace.member, self.state), getattr(namespace.other, self.state)
        return namespace.K * sin(other - member - namespace.alpha)

    def _get_group_reduction(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Target:
        """Return the reduction over the group, from the group sums of `sin theta` and `cos theta` when it can."""
        if self.weights is not None or self.delay != 0:
            return super()._get_group_reduction(namespace)
        source, target = namespace.source, namespace.target
        shifted = getattr(target, self.state) + namespace.alpha
        phases = getattr(source, self.state)
        sines, cosines = total(sin(phases), over=source), total(cos(phases), over=source)
        reduction = namespace.K * (sines * cos(shifted) - cosines * sin(shifted))
        if self._excludes_self():
            reduction = reduction + namespace.K * sin(namespace.alpha)
        if self.reduce == 'mean':
            reduction = reduction / (count(over=source) - (1 if self._excludes_self() else 0))
        return reduction

docs.text:
Kuramoto oscillators coupled along the edges of a network, theta_i' = omega_i + K sum_j A_ij sin(...).

  • Name: kuramoto_on_networks
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Arenas et al. 2008; Jensen 2023

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'phase', 'network'),
    references=('Arenas et al. 2008', 'Jensen 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 40.0, 'dt': 0.2},
    observables=lambda system: _order_parameter('order', 'oscillators'),
)
def kuramoto_on_networks(
    n_oscillators: int = 200,
    *,
    network: str = 'watts_strogatz',
    degree: int = 6,
    rewiring: float = 0.1,
    K: float = 1.0,
    sigma: float = 0.5,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return Kuramoto oscillators coupled along the edges of a network, `theta_i' = omega_i + K sum_j A_ij sin(...)`.

    Oscillator `i` follows `theta_i' = omega_i + (K / <k>) sum_j w_ij sin(theta_j - theta_i)` over its neighbours `j`,
    where the weights `w_ij = 1` live on a group on the edges and `<k>` is the mean degree. The coupling runs once per
    edge. The natural frequencies are drawn from a normal distribution of width `sigma`, and the phases uniformly from
    the circle. Above a critical coupling of the order of the all-to-all value `2 sigma sqrt(2 / pi)`, the order
    parameter `r = |<exp(i theta)>|` grows from about `1 / sqrt(N)` towards 1, and small-world shortcuts lower it.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators, the nodes of the network.

        network:
            The generator, `'watts_strogatz'`, `'erdos_renyi'`, or `'barabasi_albert'`.

        degree:
            The mean degree of the network, even for the Watts-Strogatz ring.

        rewiring:
            The probability of rewiring every edge of the Watts-Strogatz ring.

        K:
            The coupling strength, divided by the mean degree.

        sigma:
            The standard deviation of the natural frequencies.

        seed:
            The seed of the network, the frequencies, and the phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the phases `oscillators.theta`, the weights `links.w`, and the order parameter `order`.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            The network is unknown.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import kuramoto_on_networks
        >>> system = kuramoto_on_networks(20, degree=4)
        >>> system.elements[1].check().prepare().size_
        40
    """
    space = _network(network, n_oscillators, degree, rewiring, seed)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1)
    mean_degree = 2 * space.graph.number_of_edges() / n_oscillators
    oscillators = LatticeElement(
        'oscillators',
        element=PhaseOscillatorElement,
        space=space,
        values={'theta': rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi, n_oscillators), 'omega': rng.normal(0.0, sigma, n_oscillators)},
        visual=VisualSpec('sites', {'states': ['theta'], 'low': 0.0, 'high': 2 * math.pi}),
    )
    links = GroupElement('links', element=LinkElement, space=space, on='edges')
    coupling = EdgeCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='oscillators', links='links', K=K / mean_degree)
    return System(elements=[oscillators, links], interactions=[coupling])

docs.title: Kuramoto-Sakaguchi chimera
docs.text:
Two populations of identical phase oscillators with phase lag, where one synchronizes and one drifts.

  • Name: kuramoto_sakaguchi_chimera
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Abrams et al. 2008; Jensen 2023

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'phase', 'chimera'),
    references=('Abrams et al. 2008', 'Jensen 2023'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 1.0},
    observables=lambda system: [*_order_parameter('first_order', 'first'), *_order_parameter('second_order', 'second')],
)
def kuramoto_sakaguchi_chimera(
    n_oscillators: int = 32,
    *,
    A: float = 0.2,
    beta: float = 0.1,
    spread: float = 0.1,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return two populations of identical phase oscillators with phase lag, where one synchronizes and one drifts.

    Oscillator `i` of population `p` follows `theta_i' = sum_q (K_pq / N) sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i - alpha)`, with
    the stronger coupling `mu = (1 + A) / 2` inside a population, the weaker `nu = (1 - A) / 2` between them, and the
    lag `alpha = pi / 2 - beta`. Every population reads the means of `cos theta` and `sin theta` of both populations.
    The first population starts nearly synchronized and the second spread over the circle. The populations settle in a
    chimera, where one is fully synchronized and the other keeps drifting with a partial order parameter, which
    breathes for `A = 0.2`. Which population ends up coherent depends on the initial phases.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators of every population.

        A:
            The disparity of the couplings inside and between the populations.

        beta:
            The distance of the phase lag from `pi / 2`.

        spread:
            The width of the initial phases of the first population.

        seed:
            The seed of the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the phases `first.theta` and `second.theta` and the order parameters `first_order` and
            `second_order`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import kuramoto_sakaguchi_chimera
        >>> len(kuramoto_sakaguchi_chimera(4).interactions)
        4
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    alpha, mu, nu = math.pi / 2 - beta, (1 + A) / 2, (1 - A) / 2
    populations = [
        GroupElement(
            'first',
            element=PhaseOscillatorElement,
            size=n_oscillators,
            values={'theta': rng.normal(0.0, spread, n_oscillators), 'omega': 0.0},
            visual=VisualSpec('phase_ring', {'phase': 'theta'}),
        ),
        GroupElement(
            'second',
            element=PhaseOscillatorElement,
            size=n_oscillators,
            values={'theta': _spread_phases(n_oscillators, seed + 1), 'omega': 0.0},
            visual=VisualSpec('phase_ring', {'phase': 'theta'}),
        ),
    ]
    interactions: list[BaseInteraction] = [
        KuramotoCouplingInteraction(
            f'{target}_from_{source}',
            target=target,
            source=source,
            K=mu if target == source else nu,
            alpha=alpha,
            reduce='mean',
            mode='group',
            include_self=True,
        )
        for target in ('first', 'second')
        for source in ('first', 'second')
    ]
    return System(
        elements=populations,
        interactions=interactions,
    )

class KuramotoCouplingInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Kuramoto coupling `theta_i' += K sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i - alpha)` of the phases of a group.

    The sum, or the mean, runs over the members `j` that the mode selects: the neighbours along the edges of a lattice
    or network, or within a neighbourhood such as `RadiusNeighborhood(r)`, every other member of the group, every member
    of a separate source group, or the next member. With `include_self` it also runs over `j = i`, whose term
    `-K sin(alpha)` slows every phase. Over the whole group without weights or delay, the coupling reads the group sums
    of `sin theta` and `cos theta` once, so it costs time linear in the size of the group.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group of oscillators.

        source:
            The path of the group of oscillators the target couples to in the mode `'group'`, or `None` for the target.

        K:
            The coupling strength of one pair.

        alpha:
            The phase lag.

        state:
            The name of the state that holds the phases.

        reduce:
            `'sum'` or `'mean'`.

        mode:
            `'edges'`, `'group'`, or `'next'`.

        weights:
            The name of the state of the edge group in the mode `'edges'`, a matrix in the mode `'group'`, or `None`.

        include_self:
            Whether the sum also runs over the member itself.

        delay:
            The delay of the phases of the other members, 0 for none.

        neighborhood:
            The neighbourhood of the mode `'edges'`, or `None` for the edges of the lattice or network.

        layer:
            The layer of the network whose edges the interaction runs on, or `None` for the graph of the network.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import (
        ...     KuramotoCouplingInteraction,
        ...     PhaseOscillatorElement,
        ... )
        >>> phases = GroupElement('phases', element=PhaseOscillatorElement, size=4, values={'theta': [0, 1, 2, 3]})
        >>> coupling = KuramotoCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='phases', K=2.0, mode='group', reduce='mean')
        >>> system = System(elements=[phases], interactions=[coupling])
        >>> theta = Simulation(system, dt=1.0).check().prepare().run(until=20.0).trajectory_.values('phases.theta')
        >>> round(float(np.ptp(theta[-1])), 6)
        0.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        source: Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True)] = None,
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        alpha: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        state: str = 'theta',
        reduce: str = 'sum',
        mode: str = 'edges',
        weights: str | npt.ArrayLike | scipy.sparse.sparray | None = None,
        include_self: bool = False,
        delay: float = 0.0,
        neighborhood: BaseNeighborhood | None = None,
        layer: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            source=source,
            read=state,
            write=state,
            function=self._sine,
            reduce=reduce,
            mode=mode,
            weights=weights,
            include_self=include_self,
            delay=delay,
            neighborhood=neighborhood,
            layer=layer,
        )
        self.K = K
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.state = state

    def _sine(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the term `K sin(theta_j - theta_i - alpha)` of one other member."""
        member, other = getattr(namespace.member, self.state), getattr(namespace.other, self.state)

    def _get_group_reduction(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Target:
        """Return the reduction over the group, from the group sums of `sin theta` and `cos theta` when it can."""

docs.title: Mirollo-Strogatz pulse-coupled oscillators
docs.text:
Integrate-and-fire oscillators coupled by pulses, which end up firing in unison.

  • Name: mirollo_strogatz
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Mirollo and Strogatz 1990; Arenas et al. 2008

Example

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'events', 'pulse coupling', 'integrate and fire'),
    references=('Mirollo and Strogatz 1990', 'Arenas et al. 2008'),
    defaults={'until': 20.0, 'dt': 0.1},
)
def mirollo_strogatz(
    n_oscillators: int = 5,
    *,
    S: float = 2.0,
    gamma: float = 1.0,
    epsilon: float = 0.1,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return integrate-and-fire oscillators coupled by pulses, which end up firing in unison.

    Every oscillator of the group charges as `x' = S - gamma x`, a concave rise, and fires when it reaches 1. Firing is
    an event whose guard is the group maximum of the charges, and it resets the most charged oscillators to 0 and lifts
    every other one by `epsilon`. An oscillator lifted to 1 fires at the same instant and is absorbed into the group
    that fired, so the groups merge until all oscillators fire together.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators.

        S:
            The charging input.

        gamma:
            The leak rate, below `S` so that the oscillators fire.

        epsilon:
            The strength of a pulse.

        seed:
            The seed of the initial charges.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the charges `oscillators.x` of the group members and the firings as `fire` events.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import mirollo_strogatz
        >>> mirollo_strogatz(3).elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        3
    """
    charges = np.random.default_rng(seed).uniform(0.0, 1.0, n_oscillators)
    oscillators = GroupElement(
        'oscillators',
        element=IntegrateAndFireOscillatorElement,
        size=n_oscillators,
        values={'x': charges, 'S': S, 'gamma': gamma, 'epsilon': epsilon},
    )
    fire = CrossingInteraction(
        'fire',
        target='oscillators',
        guard=lambda s: maximum(s.target.x) - 1,
        reset={
            'x': lambda s: where(
                s.target.x >= maximum(s.target.x),
                0,
                where(s.target.x + s.target.epsilon >= 1, 0, s.target.x + s.target.epsilon),
            ),
        },
        direction=1,
    )
    return System(elements=[oscillators], interactions=[fire])

class IntegrateAndFireOscillatorElement(Element):
    """Integrate-and-fire oscillator that charges as `x' = S - gamma x`, and sends pulses of strength `epsilon`.

    The oscillator charges towards `S / gamma`. Its firing at 1 is a crossing of the group it belongs to, which resets
    the most charged oscillators to 0 and lifts every other one by `epsilon`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator or the group.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x:
            The initial charge.

        S:
            The charging input.

            The leak rate.

        epsilon:

    Attributes:

            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import IntegrateAndFireOscillatorElement
        >>> IntegrateAndFireOscillatorElement('oscillator').epsilon
        0.1
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        S: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 2.0,

        self.S = S
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.epsilon = epsilon

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the charging of the oscillator.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate of the charge.
        """
        s = namespace
        return [RateLaw(s.x, s.S - s.gamma * s.x)]

class CrossingInteraction(Interaction):
    """Event at the crossing of zero by a guard, which sets states of the target to new values or ends the run.

    The guard and the new values are functions of the namespace, which holds `namespace.target`, the states and
    parameters of the target, and the time `namespace.t`. A guard that reads the members of a group gives every member
    its own event, which sets the states of that member alone. Solvers locate the crossing within their tolerance, and
    the trajectory records every crossing among its events, under the label of the interaction and with the member.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose states the guard reads and the event sets.

        guard:
            The function `guard(namespace)` of the expression whose crossing of zero triggers the event.

        reset:
            A mapping from the name of a state of the target to the function `f(namespace)` of its new value, applied
            all at once, or `None` to keep the states.

        direction:
            `1` for crossings from negative to positive, `-1` for the opposite, and `0` for both.

        terminal:
            Whether the crossing ends the run.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The direction is not -1, 0, or 1, or the guard or a new value is not a function.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import Element
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import CrossingInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.laws import RateLaw
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.specs import StateSpec
        >>> class ClockElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.x = x
        ...
        ...     def _get_laws(self, s):
        ...         return [RateLaw(s.x, 1.0)]
        >>> wrap = CrossingInteraction(
        ...     'wrap', target='clock', guard=lambda s: s.target.x - 1, reset={'x': lambda s: 0}, direction=1
        ... )
        >>> system = System(elements=[ClockElement('clock')], interactions=[wrap])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.5).check().prepare().run(until=2.2).trajectory_
        >>> [round(event.time, 6) for event in trajectory.events]
        [1.0, 2.0]
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        guard: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object],
        reset: Mapping[str, Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object]] | None = None,
        direction: int = 0,
        terminal: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.guard = guard
        self.reset = reset
        self.direction = direction
        self.terminal = terminal

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a direction that is not -1, 0, or 1, or a guard or a new value that is not a function.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The direction is not -1, 0, or 1, or the guard or a new value is not a function.
        """
        super()._check()
        if self.direction not in DIRECTIONS:
            error_msg = f'The direction of crossing {self.label!r} is {self.direction!r}. Use -1, 0, or 1.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not callable(self.guard) or not all(callable(function) for function in (self.reset or {}).values()):
            error_msg = f'The guard and the new values of crossing {self.label!r} must be functions of the namespace.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    @staticmethod
    def _get_law_value(value: object) -> object:
        """Return what a function of the namespace returned: a function as it is, or a symbolic expression."""
        return value if BaseLaw._is_function(value) else SR(value)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the crossing law of the guard with the new values of the states.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with `namespace.target`.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The crossing law.
        """
        reset = {
            getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), name): self._get_law_value(f(namespace))
            for name, f in (self.reset or {}).items()
        }
        return [
            CrossingLaw(
                self._get_law_value(self.guard(namespace)),
                reset or None,
                self.direction,
                self.terminal,
                label=self.label,
            ),
        ]

docs.title: Nonlocal ring chimera
docs.text:
Identical phase oscillators on a ring, each coupled to its R nearest neighbours on both sides.

  • Name: nonlocal_ring_chimera
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Kuramoto and Battogtokh 2002; Datseris and Parlitz 2022

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'phase', 'chimera', 'nonlocal coupling'),
    references=('Kuramoto and Battogtokh 2002', 'Datseris and Parlitz 2022'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 1.0},
    observables=lambda system: _order_parameter('order', 'ring'),
)
def nonlocal_ring_chimera(
    n_oscillators: int = 100,
    *,
    R: int = 14,
    alpha: float = 1.46,
    omega: float = 0.0,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return identical phase oscillators on a ring, each coupled to its `R` nearest neighbours on both sides.

    Oscillator `i` follows `phi_i' = omega - (1 / 2R) sum_{j = i - R}^{i + R} sin(phi_i - phi_j + alpha)`, where the sum
    includes the oscillator itself. Near `alpha = pi / 2`, coherent and incoherent domains coexist on the ring as a
    chimera state, which is a long transient on small rings.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators on the ring.

        R:
            The range of the coupling.

        alpha:
            The phase lag.

        omega:
            The natural frequency.

        seed:
            The seed of the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the phases `ring.theta` and the places of the oscillators `ring.x`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import nonlocal_ring_chimera
        >>> nonlocal_ring_chimera(20, R=3).interactions[0].neighborhood.radius
        3.5
    """
    weight = 1 / (2 * R)
    ring = GroupElement(
        'ring',
        element=SitedOscillatorElement,
        size=n_oscillators,
        values={
            'theta': _spread_phases(n_oscillators, seed),
            'omega': omega,
            'x': np.arange(n_oscillators, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1),
        },
        visual=VisualSpec('phase_ring', {'phase': 'theta', 'position': 'x'}),
    )
    return System(
        elements=[ring],
        interactions=[
            KuramotoCouplingInteraction(
                'coupling',
                target='ring',
                K=weight,
                alpha=alpha,
                include_self=True,
                neighborhood=RadiusNeighborhood(R + 0.5),
            ),
        ],
        space=ContinuousSpace((float(n_oscillators),), boundary='periodic'),
    )

docs.text:
class SitedOscillatorElement(PhaseOscillatorElement):
    """Phase oscillator with a place `x` in a continuous space, which couplings within a distance or swarming read.

    The phase turns at the natural frequency, and the place changes only by the rates of interactions.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator or the group.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        theta:
            The initial phase.

        omega:
            The natural frequency.

        x:
            The initial place. A number applies to every component.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import SitedOscillatorElement
        >>> SitedOscillatorElement('unit', x=[0.0, 1.0]).x
        [0.0, 1.0]
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        theta: float = 0.0,
        omega: float = 1.0,
        x: Annotated[npt.ArrayLike, StateSpec(vector=True, role='site')] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual, theta=theta, omega=omega)
        self.x = x

class KuramotoCouplingInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Kuramoto coupling `theta_i' += K sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i - alpha)` of the phases of a group.

    The sum, or the mean, runs over the members `j` that the mode selects: the neighbours along the edges of a lattice
    or network, or within a neighbourhood such as `RadiusNeighborhood(r)`, every other member of the group, every member
    of a separate source group, or the next member. With `include_self` it also runs over `j = i`, whose term
    `-K sin(alpha)` slows every phase. Over the whole group without weights or delay, the coupling reads the group sums
    of `sin theta` and `cos theta` once, so it costs time linear in the size of the group.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group of oscillators.

        source:
            The path of the group of oscillators the target couples to in the mode `'group'`, or `None` for the target.

        K:
            The coupling strength of one pair.

        alpha:
            The phase lag.

        state:
            The name of the state that holds the phases.

        reduce:
            `'sum'` or `'mean'`.

        mode:
            `'edges'`, `'group'`, or `'next'`.

        weights:
            The name of the state of the edge group in the mode `'edges'`, a matrix in the mode `'group'`, or `None`.

        include_self:
            Whether the sum also runs over the member itself.

        delay:
            The delay of the phases of the other members, 0 for none.

        neighborhood:
            The neighbourhood of the mode `'edges'`, or `None` for the edges of the lattice or network.

        layer:
            The layer of the network whose edges the interaction runs on, or `None` for the graph of the network.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import (
        ...     KuramotoCouplingInteraction,
        ...     PhaseOscillatorElement,
        ... )
        >>> phases = GroupElement('phases', element=PhaseOscillatorElement, size=4, values={'theta': [0, 1, 2, 3]})
        >>> coupling = KuramotoCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='phases', K=2.0, mode='group', reduce='mean')
        >>> system = System(elements=[phases], interactions=[coupling])
        >>> theta = Simulation(system, dt=1.0).check().prepare().run(until=20.0).trajectory_.values('phases.theta')
        >>> round(float(np.ptp(theta[-1])), 6)
        0.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        source: Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec(optional=True)] = None,
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        alpha: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        state: str = 'theta',
        reduce: str = 'sum',
        mode: str = 'edges',
        weights: str | npt.ArrayLike | scipy.sparse.sparray | None = None,
        include_self: bool = False,
        delay: float = 0.0,
        neighborhood: BaseNeighborhood | None = None,
        layer: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            source=source,
            read=state,
            write=state,
            function=self._sine,
            reduce=reduce,
            mode=mode,
            weights=weights,
            include_self=include_self,
            delay=delay,
            neighborhood=neighborhood,
            layer=layer,
        )
        self.K = K
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.state = state

    def _sine(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the term `K sin(theta_j - theta_i - alpha)` of one other member."""
        member, other = getattr(namespace.member, self.state), getattr(namespace.other, self.state)
        return namespace.K * sin(other - member - namespace.alpha)

    def _get_group_reduction(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Target:
        """Return the reduction over the group, from the group sums of `sin theta` and `cos theta` when it can."""
        if self.weights is not None or self.delay != 0:
            return super()._get_group_reduction(namespace)
        source, target = namespace.source, namespace.target
        shifted = getattr(target, self.state) + namespace.alpha
        phases = getattr(source, self.state)
        sines, cosines = total(sin(phases), over=source), total(cos(phases), over=source)
        reduction = namespace.K * (sines * cos(shifted) - cosines * sin(shifted))
        if self._excludes_self():
            reduction = reduction + namespace.K * sin(namespace.alpha)
        if self.reduce == 'mean':
            reduction = reduction / (count(over=source) - (1 if self._excludes_self() else 0))
        return reduction

docs.title: Globally coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators with frequency spread
docs.text:
Globally coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators, whose oscillations all die for strong coupling and spread.

  • Name: oscillator_death
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Ermentrout 1990; Mirollo and Strogatz 1990; Bertin 2021

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'amplitude death', 'mean field', 'ode'),
    references=('Ermentrout 1990', 'Mirollo and Strogatz 1990', 'Bertin 2021'),
    defaults={'until': 20.0, 'dt': 0.2},
    observables=lambda system: [
        ObservableSpec('amplitude', _amplitude, group='oscillators'),
        ObservableSpec('X', group='oscillators', variable='x'),
        ObservableSpec('Y', group='oscillators', variable='y'),
        ObservableSpec('order', _order),
    ],
)
def oscillator_death(
    n_oscillators: int = 100,
    *,
    K: float = 3.0,
    width: float = 1.5,
    distribution: str = 'lorentzian',
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return globally coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators, whose oscillations all die for strong coupling and spread.

    Oscillator `j` follows `z_j' = (1 + iω_j) z_j - |z_j|² z_j + (K / N) Σ_k (z_k - z_j)` for `z_j = x_j + i y_j`.
    Alone it settles on the unit circle. The frequencies are the midpoint quantiles of a density of width `ω0`, the
    Lorentzian `ω0 / (π (ω² + ω0²))` or the quartic `g0 / (ω⁴ + ω0⁴)`. For many oscillators, the common fixed point
    `z = 0` is stable for `K > 1` and `ω0` above a critical width, 1 for the Lorentzian and
    `(1 + √(2K - 1)) / √2` for the quartic density, and every amplitude then decays to zero. For the Lorentzian, the
    slowest perturbation decays at the rate `ω0 - 1`.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

        width:
            The width `ω0` of the density of frequencies.

        distribution:
            The density of frequencies, `'lorentzian'` or `'quartic'`.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the states `oscillators.x` and `oscillators.y` and the observables `amplitude`, the mean
            amplitude, `X` and `Y`, the mean field, and `order`, its modulus.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The distribution is neither `'lorentzian'` nor `'quartic'`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import oscillator_death
        >>> oscillator_death(4, distribution='quartic').elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        4
    """
    omegas = _frequency_quantiles(n_oscillators, width, distribution)
    x, y = _spread_on_circle(n_oscillators, random_state)
    oscillators = GroupElement(
        'oscillators',
        element=StuartLandauElement,
        size=n_oscillators,
        values={'x': x, 'y': y, 'mu': 1.0, 'omega': omegas, 'tau': 1.0},
    )
    return System(
        elements=[oscillators],
        interactions=[
            GlobalCouplingInteraction(f'coupling_{state}', target='oscillators', state=state, K=K) for state in 'xy'
        ],
    )

class StuartLandauElement(Element):
    """Stuart-Landau oscillator `z' = tau ((mu + i omega) z - kappa (1 + i beta) |z|^2 z)` of `z = x + i y`.

    It is the normal form of a supercritical Hopf bifurcation. For `mu > 0` the oscillator settles on the limit cycle
    of radius `sqrt(mu / kappa)`, which it turns at the frequency `tau (omega - beta mu)`, and for `mu < 0` it decays to
    the fixed point 0. The twist `beta` makes the frequency depend on the amplitude, and the time scale `tau` speeds
    up or slows down the whole flow.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator or the group.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        x:
            The initial real part of `z`.

        y:
            The initial imaginary part of `z`.

        mu:
            The growth rate of the fixed point 0, the bifurcation parameter.

        omega:
            The frequency of the linear rotation.

        beta:
            The twist, the shear of the frequency with the amplitude.

        kappa:
            The strength of the cubic saturation.

        tau:
            The time scale.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> import math
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import StuartLandauElement
        >>> system = System(elements=[StuartLandauElement('oscillator', x=0.1, mu=4.0)])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.5).check().prepare().run(until=10.0).trajectory_
        >>> round(math.hypot(trajectory.values('oscillator.x')[-1], trajectory.values('oscillator.y')[-1]), 4)
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0,
        y: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        mu: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        beta: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        kappa: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        tau: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.mu = mu
        self.omega = omega
        self.beta = beta
        self.kappa = kappa
        self.tau = tau

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rates of the real and imaginary parts of `z`.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rates of `x` and `y`.
        """
        s = namespace
        saturation = s.kappa * (s.x**2 + s.y**2)
        return [
            RateLaw(s.x, s.tau * (s.mu * s.x - s.omega * s.y - saturation * (s.x - s.beta * s.y))),
            RateLaw(s.y, s.tau * (s.mu * s.y + s.omega * s.x - saturation * (s.y + s.beta * s.x))),
        ]

class GlobalCouplingInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Diffusive coupling of one state of every member to the mean of the group, `x_i' += K (mean_j x_j - x_i)`.

    The mean runs over every member, the member itself included.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group.

        state:
            The name of the coupled state.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

    Examples:
        >>> from types import SimpleNamespace
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import GlobalCouplingInteraction
        >>> coupling = GlobalCouplingInteraction('coupling', target='oscillators', state='y').check().prepare()
        >>> member, other = SimpleNamespace(y=var('y')), SimpleNamespace(y=var('z'))
        >>> coupling.function(SimpleNamespace(K=var('K'), member=member, other=other))
        -K*(y - z)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'x',
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            read=state,
            write=state,
            function=self._pull,
            reduce='mean',
            mode='group',
            include_self=True,
        )
        self.state = state
        self.K = K

    def _pull(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the pull `K (x_j - x_i)` of one other member."""
        return namespace.K * (getattr(namespace.other, self.state) - getattr(namespace.member, self.state))
