docs.title: Ott-Antonsen reduction
docs.text:
The Ott-Antonsen equation for the order parameter of infinitely many Kuramoto oscillators.

  • Name: ott_antonsen
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Ott and Antonsen 2008; Bick et al. 2020

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'ode', 'mean field', 'dimension reduction'),
    references=('Ott and Antonsen 2008', 'Bick et al. 2020'),
    defaults={'until': 30.0, 'dt': 0.1},
)
def ott_antonsen(
    r: float = 0.1,
    *,
    K: float = 2.0,
    Delta: float = 0.5,
    omega: float = 0.0,
) -> System:
    """Return the Ott-Antonsen equation for the order parameter of infinitely many Kuramoto oscillators.

    For natural frequencies with a Lorentzian distribution of center `omega` and half width `Delta`, the complex order
    parameter `z = x + i y` follows exactly `z' = (i omega - Delta) z + (K / 2)(1 - |z|²) z`, a Stuart-Landau
    oscillator with the growth rate `K / 2 - Delta` and the saturation `K / 2`. Its modulus settles at
    `sqrt(1 - 2 Delta / K)` above the critical coupling `K_c = 2 Delta`, and at 0 below it.

    Args:
        r:
            The initial modulus of the order parameter.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

        Delta:
            The half width of the distribution of natural frequencies.

        omega:
            The center of the distribution of natural frequencies.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the real part `field.x` and the imaginary part `field.y` of the order parameter.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import ott_antonsen
        >>> ott_antonsen(K=3.0).elements[0].kappa
        1.5
    """
    return System(elements=[StuartLandauElement('field', x=r, y=0.0, mu=K / 2 - Delta, omega=omega, kappa=K / 2)])

            The growth rate of the fixed point 0, the bifurcation parameter.

        omega:
            The frequency of the linear rotation.

        beta:
            The twist, the shear of the frequency with the amplitude.

        kappa:
            The strength of the cubic saturation.

        tau:
            The time scale.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> import math
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import StuartLandauElement
        >>> system = System(elements=[StuartLandauElement('oscillator', x=0.1, mu=4.0)])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.5).check().prepare().run(until=10.0).trajectory_
        >>> round(math.hypot(trajectory.values('oscillator.x')[-1], trajectory.values('oscillator.y')[-1]), 4)
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        x: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0,
        y: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        mu: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        beta: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        kappa: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        tau: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.mu = mu
        self.omega = omega
        self.beta = beta
        self.kappa = kappa
        self.tau = tau

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the rates of the real and imaginary parts of `z`.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rates of `x` and `y`.
        """
        s = namespace
        saturation = s.kappa * (s.x**2 + s.y**2)
        return [
            RateLaw(s.x, s.tau * (s.mu * s.x - s.omega * s.y - saturation * (s.x - s.beta * s.y))),
            RateLaw(s.y, s.tau * (s.mu * s.y + s.omega * s.x - saturation * (s.y + s.beta * s.x))),
        ]

docs.title: Swarmalators
docs.text:
Swarmalators, identical oscillators whose phases set their attraction and whose positions their coupling.

  • Name: swarmalators
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: O'Keeffe, Ceron, and Petersen 2017; te Vrugt and Wittkowski 2024

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('swarmalators', 'synchronization', 'swarming', 'pair interaction', 'ode'),
    references=("O'Keeffe, Ceron, and Petersen 2017", 'te Vrugt and Wittkowski 2024'),
    defaults={'until': 100.0, 'dt': 1.0, 'solver': RK4Solver(dt=0.1)},
)
def swarmalators(
    n_units: int = 100,
    *,
    J: float = 1.0,
    K: float = 0.0,
    A: float = 1.0,
    B: float = 1.0,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = 0,
) -> System:
    """Return swarmalators, identical oscillators whose phases set their attraction and whose positions their coupling.

    Every swarmalator `i` moves by `(1 / N) sum_j [(x_j - x_i) / |x_j - x_i| (A + J cos(theta_j - theta_i)) -
    B (x_j - x_i) / |x_j - x_i|^2]` and turns by `(K / N) sum_j sin(theta_j - theta_i) / |x_j - x_i|`. With `J > 0`
    like phases attract. With `K = 0` and `J = 1` the swarm settles into a static phase wave, a disk whose phase winds
    once around its center, so one of the order parameters `S± = |mean(exp(i (phi ± theta)))|` of the spatial angle
    `phi` and the phase approaches 1. With `K > 0` the phases synchronize into a uniform disk, and with `K < 0` and
    small `J` they stay asynchronous.

    Args:
        n_units:
            The number of swarmalators `N`.

        J:
            The influence of the phase similarity on the attraction.

        K:
            The phase coupling.

        A:
            The strength of the attraction.

        B:
            The strength of the repulsion.

        random_state:
            The seed or generator of the initial positions in the square of side 2 and of the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the positions `units.x` and the phases `units.theta`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import swarmalators
        >>> swarmalators(10, K=-0.1).interactions[0].K
        -0.1
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state)
    units = GroupElement(
        'units',
        element=SwarmalatorElement,
        size=n_units,
        values={'x': rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, (n_units, 2)), 'theta': rng.uniform(-np.pi, np.pi, n_units), 'omega': 0.0},
        visual=VisualSpec('points', {'position': 'x', 'color_by': 'theta', 'radius': 0.03}),
    )
    coupling = SwarmalatorCouplingInteraction(
        'coupling',
        first='units',
        second='units',
        A=A,
        B=B,
        J=J,
        K=K,
        n_units=n_units,
    )
    return System(elements=[units], interactions=[coupling], space=ContinuousSpace(n_dim=2))

docs.text:
class SwarmalatorElement(SitedOscillatorElement):
    """Phase oscillator whose place `x` is a position that moves by the rates of interactions.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the swarmalator or the group.

        visual:
            How the swarmalator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        theta:
            The initial phase.

        omega:
            The natural frequency.

        x:
            The initial position. A number applies to every component.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import SwarmalatorElement
        >>> SwarmalatorElement('unit', x=[0.0, 1.0]).x
        [0.0, 1.0]
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        theta: float = 0.0,
        omega: float = 1.0,
        x: Annotated[npt.ArrayLike, StateSpec(vector=True, role='position')] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual, theta=theta, omega=omega, x=x)

class SwarmalatorCouplingInteraction(PairCouplingInteraction):
    """Coupling of two swarmalators through their separation `r` and their phase difference `dtheta`.

    Each swarmalator moves toward the other at the speed `(A + J cos(dtheta)) / N`, away from it at `B / (N |r|)`, and
    turns its phase toward the other's at the rate `K sin(dtheta) / (N |r|)`, as in O'Keeffe, Ceron, and Petersen. It
    is a pair coupling of the positions and the phases jointly.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        first:
            The path of the group of the first members.

        second:
            The path of the group of the second members.

        cutoff:
            The distance beyond which pairs do not interact, large for the all-to-all model.

        position:
            The name of the vector state that holds the positions of the members.

        A:
            The strength of the attraction.

        B:
            The strength of the repulsion.

        J:
            The influence of the phase similarity on the attraction.

        K:
            The phase coupling, synchronizing when positive.

        period:
            The side of a periodic box, for minimum image distances, or `None` for an open space.

        n_units:
            The number of swarmalators `N` that normalizes the coupling.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import SwarmalatorCouplingInteraction
        >>> SwarmalatorCouplingInteraction('coupling', first='units', second='units', J=0.5).J
        0.5
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        first: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        second: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        cutoff: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1000000.0,
        position: str = 'x',
        *,
        A: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        B: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        J: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        period: float | None = None,
        n_units: int = 1,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            first,
            second,
            cutoff=cutoff,
            position=position,
            write=(position, 'theta'),
            function=self._get_terms,
            period=period,
        )
        self.A = A
        self.B = B
        self.J = J
        self.K = K
        self.n_units = n_units

    def _get_terms(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> tuple[Target, Target]:
        """Return the move and the phase turn of the first member of a pair toward the second."""
        separation = getattr(s.second, self.position) - getattr(s.first, self.position)
        r = sqrt(separation.dot_product(separation))
        difference = s.second.theta - s.first.theta
        move = ((s.A + s.J * cos(difference)) / r - s.B / r**2) * separation / self.n_units
        return move, s.K * sin(difference) / (self.n_units * r)

docs.title: Winfree model
docs.text:
The Winfree model, theta_i' = omega_i + (K / N) sum_j P(theta_j) R(theta_i), with the sum over all j.

  • Name: winfree
  • Field: physics/synchronization
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Winfree 1967; Ariaratnam and Strogatz 2001; Bick et al. 2020

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/synchronization',
    tags=('synchronization', 'oscillators', 'phase', 'oscillator death'),
    references=('Winfree 1967', 'Ariaratnam and Strogatz 2001', 'Bick et al. 2020'),
    defaults={'until': 50.0, 'dt': 0.5},
    observables=lambda system: _order_parameter('order', 'oscillators'),
)
def winfree(n_oscillators: int = 50, *, K: float = 0.5, spread: float = 0.1, seed: int = 0) -> System:
    """Return the Winfree model, `theta_i' = omega_i + (K / N) sum_j P(theta_j) R(theta_i)`, with the sum over all `j`.

    The influence `P(theta) = 1 + cos(theta)` and the sensitivity `R(theta) = -sin(theta)` make every oscillator respond
    to the mean influence of the population, which every oscillator reads as a group mean. The natural frequencies are
    spread evenly over `[1 - spread, 1 + spread]`. Weak coupling leaves the oscillators incoherent, moderate coupling
    locks them to one frequency, and strong coupling stops them, which is oscillator death.

    Args:
        n_oscillators:
            The number of oscillators.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

        spread:
            The half width of the interval of natural frequencies around 1.

        seed:
            The seed of the initial phases.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the phases `oscillators.theta` and the order parameter `order`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import winfree
        >>> len(winfree(5).interactions)
        1
    """
    oscillators = GroupElement(
        'oscillators',
        element=PhaseOscillatorElement,
        size=n_oscillators,
        values={
            'theta': np.random.default_rng(seed).uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, n_oscillators),
            'omega': np.linspace(1 - spread, 1 + spread, n_oscillators),
        },
    )
    return System(
        elements=[oscillators],
        interactions=[WinfreeMeanFieldInteraction('coupling', target='oscillators', K=K)],
    )

class PhaseOscillatorElement(Element):
    """Phase oscillator, a phase `theta` that turns at its natural frequency, `theta' = omega`.

    Couplings to other oscillators add to the rate of the phase.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the oscillator or the group.

        visual:
            How the oscillator is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        theta:
            The initial phase.

        omega:
            The natural frequency.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            The visual of the oscillator when it sets none.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.oscillators import PhaseOscillatorElement
        >>> system = System(elements=[PhaseOscillatorElement('clock', omega=2.0)])
        >>> float(Simulation(system, dt=0.5).check().prepare().run(until=1.0).trajectory_.values('clock.theta')[-1])
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        theta: Annotated[float, StateSpec(role='phase')] = 0.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.theta = theta
        self.omega = omega

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the turning of the phase at the natural frequency.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate of the phase.
        """
        return [RateLaw(namespace.theta, namespace.omega)]

class WinfreeMeanFieldInteraction(CouplingInteraction):
    """Winfree coupling `theta_i' += K mean_j P(theta_j) R(theta_i)` over every member `j` of the group.

    The influence `P(theta) = 1 + cos(theta)` that an oscillator sends and the sensitivity `R(theta) = -sin(theta)` with
    which it responds make every oscillator respond to the mean influence of the group.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the group of oscillators.

        K:
            The coupling strength.

    Examples:
        >>> from types import SimpleNamespace
        >>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import var
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.synchronization import WinfreeMeanFieldInteraction
        >>> coupling = WinfreeMeanFieldInteraction('coupling', target='oscillators')
        >>> member, other = SimpleNamespace(theta=var('a')), SimpleNamespace(theta=var('b'))
        >>> coupling.function(SimpleNamespace(K=var('K'), member=member, other=other))
        -K*(cos(b) + 1)*sin(a)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        K: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            label,
            target=target,
            read='theta',
            write='theta',
            function=self._response,
            reduce='mean',
            mode='group',
            include_self=True,
        )
        self.K = K

    def _response(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the response `K P(theta_j) R(theta_i)` of a member to one other member."""
        return namespace.K * (1 + cos(namespace.other.theta)) * -sin(namespace.member.theta)

docs.title: Schrödinger equation minimally coupled to an electromagnetic potential
docs.text:
A Gaussian wave packet of a charge in a prescribed electromagnetic potential, after Schwichtenberg 4.3.

  • Name: charged_schrodinger
  • Field: physics/waves
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Schwichtenberg 2020

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/waves',
    tags=('quantum', 'gauge field', 'electromagnetism', 'wave packet', 'spectral', 'pde'),
    references=('Schwichtenberg 2020',),
    defaults={'until': 8.0, 'dt': 0.1},
)
def charged_schrodinger(
    n_sites: int = 256,
    *,
    length: float = 80.0,
    D: float = 0.5,
    q: float = 1.0,
    momentum: float = 0.0,
    width: float = 2.0,
    A_x: float = 0.0,
    A_t: float = 0.0,
    E: float = 1.0,
    duration: float = 2.0,
) -> System:
    """Return a Gaussian wave packet of a charge in a prescribed electromagnetic potential, after Schwichtenberg 4.3.

    The wave function follows the Schrödinger equation with the covariant derivatives `d - i q A`,
    `(d_t - i q A_t) psi = i D (d_x - i q A_x)^2 psi`, on a periodic line with spectral derivatives. A mode of wave
    number `k` turns at the frequency `D (k - q A_x)^2 - q A_t`, so the packet moves at the group velocity
    `2 D (k - q A_x)`. A constant `A_x` is a pure gauge that only shifts the canonical momentum, while the electric
    field `E` switched on for `duration` changes `A_x` and accelerates the packet at the rate `2 D q E`.

    Args:
        n_sites:
            The number of sites of the periodic lattice.

        length:
            The length of the periodic line, centered on 0.

        D:
            The coefficient of the Laplacian, `ħ / (2 m)`.

        q:
            The electric charge.

        momentum:
            The mean wave number `k` of the packet.

        width:
            The width of the packet.

        A_x:
            The vector potential at time 0.

        A_t:
            The scalar potential.

        E:
            The electric field.

        duration:
            The time the electric field is on.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the real part `packet.u` and the imaginary part `packet.w` of the wave function.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import charged_schrodinger
        >>> charged_schrodinger(64, E=0.5).elements[0].values['E']
        0.5
    """
    spacing = length / n_sites
    positions = spacing * np.arange(n_sites) - length / 2
    envelope = np.exp(-(positions**2) / (4 * width**2)) / (2 * np.pi * width**2) ** 0.25
    psi = envelope * np.exp(1j * momentum * positions)
    values = {
        'u': psi.real,
        'w': psi.imag,
        'D': D,
        'q': q,
        'A_x': A_x,
        'A_t': A_t,
        'E': E,
        'duration': duration,
    }
    space = LatticeSpace(n_sites, spacing=spacing)
    return System(
        elements=[
            FieldElement(
                'packet',
                element=ChargedWaveFunctionElement,
                space=space,
                values=values,
                discretization='spectral',
            ),
        ],
    )

class ChargedWaveFunctionElement(Element):
    """Wave function `psi = u + i w` of a charge `q` in a uniform electromagnetic potential.

    The wave function follows `(d_t - i q A_t) psi = i D (d_x - i q A_x)^2 psi`. The vector potential
    `A_x(t) = A_x - E min(t, duration)` holds a uniform electric field `E` from time 0 to `duration`, and the scalar
    potential `A_t` is constant. Expanded, the equation is
    `psi_t = i D psi_xx + 2 D q A_x psi_x + i (q A_t - D q^2 A_x^2) psi`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the site or the field.

        visual:
            How the element is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        u:
            The initial real part.

        w:
            The initial imaginary part.

        D:
            The coefficient of the Laplacian, `ħ / (2 m)`.

        q:
            The electric charge.

        A_x:
            The vector potential at time 0.

        A_t:
            The scalar potential.

        E:
            The electric field.

        duration:
            The time the electric field is on.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import ChargedWaveFunctionElement
        >>> ChargedWaveFunctionElement('site').q
        1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        u: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        w: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        D: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
        q: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 1.0,
        A_x: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        A_t: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        E: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        duration: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.u = u
        self.w = w
        self.D = D
        self.q = q
        self.A_x = A_x
        self.A_t = A_t
        self.E = E
        self.duration = duration

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the minimally coupled Schrödinger equation for the real and imaginary parts.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The laws of the component.
        """
        potential = s.A_x - s.E * ramp(s.t, 0, s.duration, s.duration)
        drift = 2 * s.D * s.q * potential
        phase = s.q * s.A_t - s.D * s.q**2 * potential**2
        return [
            RateLaw(s.u, -s.D * laplacian(s.w) + drift * gradient(s.u, 1)[0] - phase * s.w),
            RateLaw(s.w, s.D * laplacian(s.u) + drift * gradient(s.w, 1)[0] + phase * s.u),
        ]

docs.title: Schrödinger equation as real and imaginary fields
docs.text:
A Gaussian wave packet that follows the Schrödinger equation, as its real and imaginary parts.

  • Name: schrodinger
  • Field: physics/waves
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Schrödinger 1926; Schwichtenberg 2020

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/waves',
    tags=('waves', 'field', 'pde', 'quantum', 'spectral'),
    references=('Schrödinger 1926', 'Schwichtenberg 2020'),
    defaults={'until': 4.0, 'dt': 0.1, 'solver': ETDRK4Solver(dt=0.01)},
)
def schrodinger(
    n_sites: int = 256,
    *,
    length: float = 40.0,
    D: float = 0.5,
    momentum: float = 2.0,
    width: float = 1.0,
    omega: float = 0.0,
    formulation: str = 'fields',
    gamma: float = 0.0,
) -> System:
    """Return a Gaussian wave packet that follows the Schrödinger equation, as its real and imaginary parts.

    The wave function `psi = u + i w` follows `psi_t = i D laplacian(psi) - i V psi`, written as `u_t = -D laplacian(w)
    + V w` and `w_t = D laplacian(u) - V u`, on a periodic lattice with spectral derivatives. In units with `ħ = 1`,
    `D = 1 / (2 m)`. The potential is the harmonic well `V = omega² x² / (4 D)`, or zero for a free packet. A free
    packet of momentum `k` moves at the group velocity `2 D k` and spreads, and its norm `sum(u² + w²)` is conserved.

    The operator formulation builds the same particle as one quantum subsystem whose basis states are the sites, with
    the Hamiltonian `-D laplacian + V` of the same spectral Laplacian, normalised so that `|psi|²` is the probability of
    every site. It runs with the quantum solvers, and it accepts position dephasing at the rate `gamma`, which turns
    the state into a density matrix.

    Args:
        n_sites:
            The number of sites of the periodic lattice.

        length:
            The length of the periodic box, centered on 0.

        D:
            The coefficient of the Laplacian, `ħ / (2 m)`.

        momentum:
            The mean wave number of the packet.

        width:
            The width of the packet.

        omega:
            The angular frequency of the harmonic well.

        formulation:
            `'fields'` for two real fields, or `'operators'` for a particle on the sites of the lattice.

        gamma:
            The rate of position dephasing of the operator formulation.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the real part `packet.u` and the imaginary part `packet.w` of the wave function, or the
            quantum state `schrodinger.state` of the operator formulation.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The formulation is unknown, or the field formulation has a dephasing rate.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import schrodinger
        >>> schrodinger(64).elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        64
    """
    spacing = length / n_sites
    positions = spacing * np.arange(n_sites) - length / 2
    envelope = np.exp(-(positions**2) / (4 * width**2)) / (2 * np.pi * width**2) ** 0.25
    psi = envelope * np.exp(1j * momentum * positions)
    potential = omega**2 * positions**2 / (4 * D)
    space = LatticeSpace(n_sites, spacing=spacing)
    if formulation not in FORMULATIONS or (formulation == 'fields' and gamma):
        error_msg = (
            f'Unknown formulation {formulation!r}, or dephasing in the field formulation. Use one of '
            f'{", ".join(FORMULATIONS)}, and gamma > 0 only with the operator formulation.'
        )
        raise ValidationError(error_msg)
    if formulation == 'operators':
        amplitudes = psi / np.linalg.norm(psi)
        interactions: list[BaseInteraction] = [
            LatticeHamiltonianInteraction('kinetic', target='packet', D=D),
        ]
        if gamma > 0:
            interactions.append(
                PositionDephasingInteraction('dephasing', target='packet', gamma=gamma, n_sites=n_sites),
            )
        return System(
            'schrodinger',
            elements=[SiteElement('packet', amplitudes, hilbert=site_space(space, potential, projectors=gamma > 0))],
            interactions=interactions,
        )
    packet = FieldElement(
        'packet',
        element=WaveFunctionElement,
        space=space,
        values={'u': psi.real, 'w': psi.imag, 'D': D, 'V': potential},
        discretization='spectral',
    )
    return System(elements=[packet])

class WaveFunctionElement(Element):
    """Site of the wave function `psi = u + i w` of a particle with the potential `V`, by its real and imaginary parts.

    The parts follow the Schrödinger equation `i psi' = -D laplacian(psi) + V psi`, so
    `u' = -D laplacian(w) + V w` and `w' = D laplacian(u) - V u`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the site.

        visual:
            How the site is drawn, or `None` for none.

        u:
            The initial real part.

        w:
            The initial imaginary part.

        D:
            The coefficient of the kinetic energy, `hbar / (2 m)`.

        V:
            The potential at the site.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import WaveFunctionElement
        >>> WaveFunctionElement('site', V=1.0).V
        1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        u: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        w: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0,
        D: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 0.5,
        V: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.u = u
        self.w = w
        self.D = D
        self.V = V

    def _get_laws(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BaseLaw]:
        """Return the Schrödinger equation of the real and imaginary parts.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate laws of the two parts.
        """
        return [
            RateLaw(s.u, -s.D * laplacian(s.w) + s.V * s.w),
            RateLaw(s.w, s.D * laplacian(s.u) - s.V * s.u),
        ]

docs.text:
Masses joined in a row by springs of zero rest length between two anchors, a discrete string.

  • Name: spring_chain
  • Field: physics/waves
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Argun et al. 2021

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/waves',
    tags=('waves', 'ode', 'springs', 'normal modes', 'mechanics'),
    references=('Argun et al. 2021',),
    defaults={'until': 20.0, 'dt': 0.05, 'solver': VelocityVerletSolver(dt=0.01)},
)
def spring_chain(
    n_masses: int = 15,
    *,
    length: float = 1.0,
    k: float = 1.0,
    mass: float = 0.01,
    pluck: float = 0.05,
    pluck_at: float = 0.5,
    amplitude: float = 0.0,
    omega: float = 2.0,
) -> System:
    """Return masses joined in a row by springs of zero rest length between two anchors, a discrete string.

    The masses start evenly spaced between the anchors at `0` and `length`, stretched, so the chain carries tension.
    With `pluck`, the masses start on a triangle of that height peaking at the fraction `pluck_at` of the length, the
    pluck of a guitar string. With `amplitude`, the left anchor moves transversally as `amplitude sin(omega t)` and
    sends a transverse wave along the chain. Springs of zero rest length are linear, so the transverse modes are
    independent, with frequencies `2 sqrt(k / m) sin(n pi / (2 (N + 1)))`.

    Args:
        n_masses:
            The number of masses between the anchors.

        length:
            The distance between the anchors.

        k:
            The stiffness of every spring.

        mass:
            The mass of every mass.

        pluck:
            The initial transverse displacement of the plucked point.

        pluck_at:
            The plucked point, as a fraction of the length.

        amplitude:
            The amplitude of the transverse motion of the left anchor.

        omega:
            The angular frequency of the left anchor.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the masses `mass_<i>` and their positions `mass_<i>.x` in two dimensions.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import spring_chain
        >>> len(spring_chain(4).interactions)
        5
    """
    spacing = length / (n_masses + 1)
    positions = spacing * np.arange(1, n_masses + 1)
    heights = _pluck(positions, length, pluck, pluck_at) if pluck else np.zeros(n_masses)
    masses = [
        MassPointElement(f'mass_{index}', x=[float(positions[index]), float(heights[index])], x_d1=[0.0, 0.0], m=mass)
        for index in range(n_masses)
    ]
    springs = [
        SpringInteraction(f'spring_{index}', first=f'mass_{index}', second=f'mass_{index + 1}', k=k)
        for index in range(n_masses - 1)
    ]
    anchors = [
        DrivenAnchorInteraction('left_end', target='mass_0', k=k, center=[0.0, 0.0], amplitude=amplitude, omega=omega),
        DrivenAnchorInteraction('right_end', target=f'mass_{n_masses - 1}', k=k, center=[length, 0.0]),
    ]
    return System(elements=masses, interactions=[*anchors, *springs], space=ContinuousSpace(n_dim=2))

class MassPointElement(PointElement):
    """Point mass, a point whose position `x` has order 2, with its velocity `x_d1` and a mass `m`.

    The forces on the point divide by the mass through their divisor `'m'`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the point.

        x:
            The initial position. A number applies to every component.

        x_d1:
            The initial velocity. A number applies to every component.

        visual:
            How the point is drawn, or `None` for `default_visual_`.

        m:
            The mass.

    Attributes:
        default_visual_:
            Points at the positions.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.particles import MassPointElement
        >>> MassPointElement('ball', x=[0.0, 1.0], m=2.0).m
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        x: npt.ArrayLike = 0.0,
        x_d1: npt.ArrayLike = 0.0,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        m: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, x=x, x_d1=x_d1, visual=visual)
        self.m = m

class DrivenAnchorInteraction(HarmonicPotentialInteraction):
    """Spring that ties a particle to an anchor point, which oscillates transversally as `amplitude sin(omega t)`.

    The energy is `k |x - center - (0, amplitude sin(omega t))|² / 2`, and a zero amplitude gives a fixed anchor.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        target:
            The path of the particle.

        k:
            The stiffness of the spring.

        center:
            The rest position of the anchor.

        amplitude:
            The amplitude of the transverse motion of the anchor.

        omega:
            The angular frequency of the anchor.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import DrivenAnchorInteraction
        >>> DrivenAnchorInteraction('end', target='mass_0', center=[0.0, 0.0], amplitude=0.1).amplitude
        0.1
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        k: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        center: Annotated[npt.ArrayLike, ParameterSpec(vector=True)] = 0.0,
        amplitude: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()] = 0.0,
        omega: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=target, k=k, center=center)
        self.amplitude = amplitude
        self.omega = omega

    def _get_center(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return the position `center + (0, amplitude sin(omega t))` of the anchor."""
        return s.center + vector(SR, [0, s.amplitude * sin(s.omega * s.t)])

class SpringInteraction(PotentialEnergyInteraction):
    """Spring between two particles.

    The energy is `k * (|x_first - x_second| - length)**2 / 2`, and its gradient moves both particles.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction.

        first:
            The path of the first particle.

        second:
            The path of the second particle.

        k:
            The stiffness.

        length:
            The rest length.

        states:
            The name of the vector state that holds the positions of the particles.

        divisor:
            The name of the state or parameter that holds the masses of the particles.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.common.particles import SpringInteraction
        >>> SpringInteraction('spring', first='a', second='b', k=3.0, length=1.0).length
        1.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        first: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        second: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        k: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
        length: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.closed_open(0, oo))] = 0.0,
        states: str = 'x',
        divisor: str = 'm',
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, target=first, states=states, divisor=divisor)
        self.first = first
        self.second = second
        self.k = k
        self.length = length

    def _get_potential(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
        """Return `k * (|x_first - x_second| - length)**2 / 2`.

        Args:
            s:
                The namespace of the symbols the energy can use.

        Returns:
            energy:
                The potential energy as a symbolic expression.
        """
        gap = getattr(s.first, self._get_names()[0]) - getattr(s.second, self._get_names()[0])
        return s.k * (sqrt(gap.dot_product(gap)) - s.length) ** 2 / 2

docs.title: Standing waves on a string
docs.text:
A string with fixed ends on [-length / 2, length / 2] that vibrates as a standing wave.

  • Name: standing_waves
  • Field: physics/waves
  • Formalism: ordinary differential equations
  • References: Starkovich 2021

docs.title: Factory
docs.text:
@register_model(
    field='physics/waves',
    tags=('waves', 'field', 'pde', 'normal modes'),
    references=('Starkovich 2021',),
    defaults={'until': 4.0, 'dt': 0.05},
)
def standing_waves(
    n_sites: int = 99,
    *,
    length: float = 2.0,
    c: float = 1.0,
    mode: int = 1,
    amplitude: float = 1.0,
) -> System:
    """Return a string with fixed ends on `[-length / 2, length / 2]` that vibrates as a standing wave.

    The displacement follows the wave equation `u'' = c² u_xx`, written as `u' = v` and `v' = c² laplacian(u)` on a
    lattice whose edges hold the string at zero. The string starts at rest in the mode
    `amplitude sin(mode pi (x + length / 2) / length)`, which oscillates in place with the period
    `2 length / (mode c)`, up to the discretization.

    Args:
        n_sites:
            The number of sites inside the string.

        length:
            The length of the string.

        c:
            The speed of the waves.

        mode:
            The number of half wavelengths along the string.

        amplitude:
            The initial amplitude.

    Returns:
        system:
            The model, with the displacement `string.u` and the velocity `string.v`.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import standing_waves
        >>> standing_waves(9).elements[0].check().prepare().size_
        9
    """
    spacing = length / (n_sites + 1)
    positions = spacing * np.arange(1, n_sites + 1)
    shape = amplitude * np.sin(mode * math.pi * positions / length)
    space = LatticeSpace(n_sites, spacing=spacing)
    edges = ('fixed', 0.0)
    string = FieldElement(
        'string',
        element=WaveStringElement,
        space=space,
        boundary={'u': edges},
        values={'u': shape, 'c': c},
    )
    tension = RateInteraction(
        'tension',
        target='string',
        state='u',
        rate=lambda s: s.target.c**2 * laplacian(s.target.u),
    )
    return System(elements=[string], interactions=[tension])

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
class WaveStringElement(Element):
    """Site of a string, with the transverse displacement `u` of order 2 and the wave speed `c`.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the site.

        visual:
            How the site is drawn, or `None` for none.

        u:
            The initial displacement.

        u_d1:
            The initial transverse velocity.

        c:
            The wave speed.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.models.physics.waves import WaveStringElement
        >>> WaveStringElement('site', c=2.0).c
        2.0
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        visual: VisualSpec | None = None,
        *,
        u: Annotated[float, StateSpec(order=2)] = 0.0,
        u_d1: float = 0.0,
        c: Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=RealSet.open(0, oo))] = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label, visual=visual)
        self.u = u
        self.u_d1 = u_d1
        self.c = c

class RateInteraction(Interaction):
    """Rate `rate(ns)` and noise `noise(ns) dW` added to the highest time derivative of a state of a target.

    On a state of order 1 the rate is its first derivative, and on a state of order `k` it adds to the `k`-th
    derivative, so rates on one state superpose. With a divisor `d` the rate and the noise are divided by `d`, the name
    of a state or parameter of the target, such as an inertia, a friction, or a capacitance, which backends can read.

    A rate, a noise, or a divisor function takes the namespace of the interaction, with the namespaces `target` and
    `sources` of the bound elements, the time `t`, and the symbols of the parameters a subclass declares. A number
    stands for a constant, and a number on a vector state applies to every component. The noise is a Wiener process per
    component and member by default, a process of a `WienerProcessSpec` to share or correlate it across states and
    members, or a fractional Brownian motion of a Hurst index.

    Args:
        label:
            The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

        target:
            The path of the element or group whose state the rate changes.

        state:
            The name of the state of the target that the rate changes.

        rate:
            A function of the namespace that returns the rate, or a number.

        sources:
            The paths of the elements or groups the rate and the noise read but do not change.

        noise:
            A function of the namespace that returns the amplitude of the noise, a number, or `None` for no noise.

        divisor:
            The name of the state or parameter of the target that divides the rate and the noise, a function of the
            namespace of the target that returns the divisor, such as a moment of inertia `m l^2`, or `None`.

        process:
            The Wiener processes that drive the noise, or `None` for one independent process per component and member.

        index:
            The process of `process` that drives the noise, or `None` for every process, one per component of a vector
            state.

        convention:
            The stochastic calculus of the noise, `'ito'`, `'stratonovich'`, or `'anti-ito'`.

        hurst:
            The Hurst index in `(0, 1)` of a fractional Brownian motion that drives the noise, a number or a function
            of the namespace that returns a parameter, or `None` for a Wiener process.

        conserved:
            Whether the noise is the divergence of a random flux on the links of the lattice of a field, so it keeps the
            total of the state.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            The state is not a name, a function is neither callable nor a number, the convention is unknown, the Hurst
            index is outside `(0, 1)`, or the noise options cannot combine.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.elements import CompartmentElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.interactions import RateInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.system import System
        >>> from skcomplex.engine.runtime import Simulation
        >>> decay = RateInteraction('decay', target='stock', state='n', rate=lambda s: -0.5 * s.target.n)
        >>> system = System(elements=[CompartmentElement('stock', n=8.0)], interactions=[decay])
        >>> trajectory = Simulation(system, dt=0.01).check().prepare().run(until=2.0).trajectory_
        >>> round(float(trajectory.values('stock.n')[-1]), 3)
        2.943
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        label: str,
        *,
        target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
        state: str = 'x',
        rate: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float = 0.0,
        sources: Annotated[Sequence[str], RoleSpec(variadic=True)] = (),
        noise: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float | None = None,
        divisor: str | Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | None = None,
        process: Annotated[WienerProcessSpec | None, RoleSpec(noise=True)] = None,
        index: int | None = None,
        convention: str = 'ito',
        hurst: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float | None = None,
        conserved: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(label)
        self.target = target
        self.state = state
        self.rate = rate
        self.sources = sources
        self.noise = noise
        self.divisor = divisor
        self.process = process
        self.index = index
        self.convention = convention
        self.hurst = hurst
        self.conserved = conserved

    def _check_functions(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state that is not a name, or a function that is neither callable nor a number."""
        if not isinstance(self.state, str) or not self.state.isidentifier():
            error_msg = (
                f'{type(self).__name__} {self.label!r} changes the state {self.state!r}, which is not a name of a '
                'state.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        for name in ('rate', 'noise'):
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if not (value is None or callable(value) or isinstance(value, int | float)):
                error_msg = f'The {name} of {self.label!r} is {value!r}. Give a function of the namespace or a number.'
                raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not (
            self.divisor is None
            or callable(self.divisor)
            or (isinstance(self.divisor, str) and self.divisor.isidentifier())
        ):
            error_msg = (
                f'The divisor of {self.label!r} is {self.divisor!r}. Give the name of a state or parameter, or a '
                'function of the namespace of the target.'
            )
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check_noise(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for an unknown convention, a Hurst index outside `(0, 1)`, or noise options that conflict."""
        if self.convention not in CONVENTIONS:
            error_msg = f'Unknown noise convention {self.convention!r}. Use one of {", ".join(CONVENTIONS)}.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if not (
            self.hurst is None or callable(self.hurst) or (isinstance(self.hurst, int | float) and 0 < self.hurst < 1)
        ):
            error_msg = f'The Hurst index of {self.label!r} is {self.hurst!r}. Give a number in (0, 1) or a function.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        if self.index is not None and self.process is None:
            error_msg = f'{self.label!r} picks the process {self.index!r} but binds no processes. Give `process`.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)
        options = [
            name
            for name, given in (('hurst', self.hurst), ('process', self.process), ('conserved', self.conserved))
            if given
        ]
        if len(options) > 1:
            error_msg = f'The noise of {self.label!r} takes {" and ".join(options)}. Give at most one of them.'
            raise ValidationError(error_msg)

    def _check(self) -> None:
        """Raise an error for a state, functions, or noise options the interaction cannot take.

        Raises:
            ValidationError:
                The type declares states, the state is not a name, a function is neither callable nor a number, the
                convention is unknown, the Hurst index is outside `(0, 1)`, or the noise options cannot combine.
        """
        super()._check()
        self._check_functions()
        self._check_noise()

    def _evaluate(self, function: Callable[[SimpleNamespace], object] | float, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the value of a function of the namespace, or a number as it is."""
        return function(namespace) if callable(function) else function

    def _broadcast(self, value: object, state: object) -> object:
        """Return a value with one component per component of a vector state, repeating a number."""
        if isinstance(state, FreeModuleElement) and not isinstance(value, FreeModuleElement | list | tuple):
            return vector(SR, [value] * len(state))
        if isinstance(value, list | tuple):
            return vector(SR, value)
        return value

    def _divide(self, value: object, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return a value divided by the divisor of the target, or the value without a divisor."""
        if self.divisor is None:
            return value
        divisor = (
            self.divisor(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'))
            if callable(self.divisor)
            else getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.divisor)
        )
        return operator.truediv(value, divisor)

    def _get_rate(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the rate before the divisor, the hook a subclass overrides to derive it from its parameters."""
        return self._evaluate(self.rate, namespace)

    def _get_noise(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> object:
        """Return the noise amplitude before the divisor, the hook a subclass overrides, or `None` for no noise."""
        return None if self.noise is None else self._evaluate(self.noise, namespace)

    def _get_noise_law(self, state: object, amplitude: object, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> BasePart:
        """Return the noise law of an amplitude, by the process, the convention, and the Hurst index."""
        if self.hurst is not None:
            hurst = self._evaluate(self.hurst, namespace)
            return FractionalNoiseLaw(state, amplitude, hurst=hurst, convention=self.convention)
        process = None
        if self.process is not None:
            handle = self._get_member(namespace, 'process').dW
            process = handle if self.index is None else handle[self.index]
        return NoiseLaw(state, amplitude, convention=self.convention, process=process, conserved=self.conserved)

    def _get_laws(self, namespace: SimpleNamespace) -> list[BasePart]:
        """Return the rate law of the state and its noise law, both divided by the divisor.

        Args:
            namespace:
                The namespace of the symbols the laws can use, with the namespaces of the target and the sources.

        Returns:
            laws:
                The rate law, and the noise law when the interaction has noise.
        """
        state = getattr(self._get_member(namespace, 'target'), self.state)
        rate = self._divide(self._broadcast(self._get_rate(namespace), state), namespace)
        laws: list[BasePart] = [RateLaw(state, rate)]
        noise = self._get_noise(namespace)
        if noise is not None:
            laws.append(self._get_noise_law(state, self._divide(noise, namespace), namespace))
        return laws

docs.title: Cooperation
docs.text:
• Iterated prisoner's dilemma tournament: The evolution of strategies of the iterated prisoner's dilemma from random genomes.
  • Public goods game: The spatial public goods game in groups of five neighbours, with Fermi imitation.
  • Public goods game on hypergraphs: The public goods game on a hypergraph, played in every hyperedge, with Fermi imitation.
  • Spatial prisoner's dilemma with best-neighbour and Fermi imitation: The spatial prisoner's dilemma of Nowak and May, with best-neighbour or Fermi imitation.
  • Two-player games on links and three-body games on 2-simplices: The social dilemmas of Guo et al. on the links and the 2-simplices of a simplicial complex.

docs.title: Crowds
docs.text:
• Criminality and security: The kinetic model of criminality in a society and the security forces that act against it.
  • Crowd dynamics and evacuation: The kinetic model of the evacuation of a building whose rooms form a network.
  • Social force pedestrians: Two crowds walking in opposite directions along a periodic corridor, which form lanes.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: • Mandelbrot least-effort word frequencies: The word frequencies that minimise the mean cost of a language over its entropy, a power law of rank.

docs.title: Opinion dynamics
docs.text:
• Axelrod culture dissemination: Axelrod's culture dissemination model on a full grid with von Neumann neighbourhoods.
  • Belief diffusion with influentials: The belief diffusion model with influentials who care passionately and weigh more with their neighbours.
  • Coevolving voter: The coevolving voter model, which fragments into consensual components when rewiring is fast.
  • Cognitive consistency agents: Agents whose attitudes spread by conversation and settle in a belief network that seeks consistency.
  • Complex agents with internal states and standardization: Complex agents whose interactions make them standardized, all showing one characteristic, and ordered.
  • Deffuant bounded confidence: The Deffuant bounded confidence model, whose opinions settle into about 1 / (2 * confidence) clusters.
  • Galam majority: The Galam majority model, where random groups adopt their majority until one opinion wins.
  • Hegselmann-Krause: The Hegselmann-Krause model, whose opinions freeze within a few steps into clusters about 2 ε apart.
  • Join-a-club spins: Join-a-club spins, agents who join a club with their acquaintances while acquaintances follow the club.
  • Kinetic opinion formation: The kinetic model of opinion formation over a discrete grid of opinions.
  • Majority rule automaton: Voters that take the majority opinion of their neighbourhood, which coarsens into domains.
  • Naming game: The minimal naming game, where agents with empty inventories agree on one word.
  • Nonlinear three-body consensus on temporal hypergraphs: The nonlinear three-body consensus model on a random hypergraph of triangles that switch on and off.
  • Social impact theory: The social impact model on a full grid, with random persuasiveness and supportiveness.
  • Sznajd: The Sznajd model, where agreeing pairs of agents convince their neighbours.
  • Threshold adoption: The threshold adoption model in social circles, started by the 2.5% of agents with the lowest thresholds.
  • Voter model: A voter model with one voter per node of a network.
  • Voter variants: Voter model variants on a network, with threshold voters and a share of contrarians.

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text:
• Barabási priority queues: The Barabási priority queue, whose waiting times follow a power law as the choice becomes greedy.
  • Bonabeau hierarchies: The Bonabeau model, where a hierarchy of strengths emerges above a critical density of agents.
  • Brothel movement model: The brothel movement model, where victims moved between brothels leave traces in bills and train trips.
  • Employment takeover: The employment takeover model on a periodic checkerboard, with half of each kind coloured at random.
  • Escalation: Meadows' escalation trap, two parties that each want to exceed the other's stock by a margin.
  • Gravity interaction model of urban scaling: The residents of a city at uniform positions in a disc, each interacting with the others as r^-gamma.
  • Insider sabotage: The insider sabotage model of employees whose risk of sabotage builds up over the days of a year.
  • Obesity model: The obesity model of adults who eat near home and work, one step per day.
  • Shifting the burden: Meadows' shifting the burden trap, a quick fix that relieves a symptom and erodes the system's capability.
  • Success to the successful: Meadows' success to the successful trap, two competitors that share a budget by their past success.

docs.title: Segregation

  • Stochastic Schelling: The stochastic Schelling model of agents moving between blocks, which segregates above beta = 2.
